supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the offsets are or that excess is forfeited.

value_domain: Dollar refundable tax offset entitlement, company return item 12 label J
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 12. National rental affordability scheme
variable_description: What the firm was entitled to receive for renting dwellings below market rent under the National Rental Affordability Scheme. The ATO instruction is to "Write at J the company's entitlement to a tax offset under the National Rental Affordability Scheme (NRAS). Show cents", and the entitlement exists only where "the secretary of the Department of Social Services has issued a certificate under the NRAS". The scheme pays providers of new dwellings rented "to low and moderate income households at 20% below market rates".
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents refundable tax offset entitlement, reported at item 12 and claimed in the refundable tax offsets total of the calculation statement.
limitation: The certificate covers an NRAS year running 1 May to 30 April, which does not align with the income year, so the entitlement in a return does not correspond to a financial year of renting. It records money, not housing: no dwelling count, tenure or location sits behind it, so it cannot be used to locate affordable housing supply.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 12 label J, and the ATO page defines the entitlement, the certificate requirement and the NRAS year it relates to.
evidence_quote: The refundable tax offset is only available when the secretary of the Department of Social Services has issued a certificate under the NRAS.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the entitlement follows a certificate on an offset year that does not match the income year.

value_domain: Dollar reconciliation add-back, company return item 7 label B
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Assessable income the firm did not show as income in its accounts, added in at the reconciliation. The ATO instruction is to "Write at B the total of the amounts that form part of assessable income if you have not included them as income at item 6 or at item 7 at A Net capital gain, J Franking credits or C Australian franking credits from a New Zealand company, for example, attributed foreign income of a CFC, and timing adjustments such as that which reconciles interest receivable to assessable interest income." It is where accounting income and tax income part company on the income side.
value_definition: A whole-dollar add-back at item 7, sitting between the accounting profit at item 6 and the taxable income at item 7.
limitation: It is a catch-all with no breakdown: attributed foreign income from a controlled foreign company, assessable foreign exchange gains, balancing adjustments on asset disposals and R&D clawback amounts all sit in one number, so a movement in it cannot be attributed to any one cause. It is also an adjustment, so it is not comparable with any item 6 income label.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label B, and the ATO reconciliation page defines it and lists the classes of amount that fall into it.
evidence_quote: Write at B the total of the amounts that form part of assessable income if you have not included them as income at item 6 or at item 7 at A Net capital gain, J Franking credits or C Australian franking credits from a New Zealand company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other Assessable Income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which read like an income category rather than a reconciliation adjustment.

value_domain: Dollar reconciliation subtraction, company return item 7 label P
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The adjustment that brings an offshore banking unit's income down to the fraction that is actually taxed. The ATO restricts the label: "Only use P if the company has been declared to be an offshore banking unit (OBU) by the minister under subsection 128AE(2) of the ITAA 1936, otherwise disregard P." The mechanism is a rate concession delivered through the tax base, because "section 121EG of the ITAA 1936 reduces the assessable income and allowable deductions from OB activities so that an OBU's taxable income includes only the 'eligible fraction'", giving an effective rate of 10 per cent.
value_definition: A whole-dollar subtraction at item 7 for the income year, applied after the gross income and expenses of offshore banking activities have gone through the other gross income and all other expenses labels at item 6.
limitation: Only ministerially declared offshore banking units complete it, so a non-zero value identifies a closed and very small set of financial firms rather than any general offshore activity. Because the figure is a net adjustment, it is not the size of the offshore banking business: the gross income and expenses sit inside the item 6 residual labels and cannot be recovered from here.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label P, and the ATO reconciliation page defines who may use it, how the eligible fraction works and where the underlying income and expenses are reported.
evidence_quote: Only use P if the company has been declared to be an offshore banking unit (OBU) by the minister under subsection 128AE(2) of the ITAA 1936, otherwise disregard P.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Offshore banking unit adjustment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the label is restricted to declared OBUs or what the adjustment achieves.

value_domain: Dollar value of trading stock at the start of the year, company return item 8 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
variable_description: The tax value of the trading stock the firm held at the start of the income year. The ATO instruction is to "Write at A the total value of all trading stock on hand at the beginning of the income year or accounting period for which the company tax return is being prepared", valued under section 70-40 or, for small business entities, the simplified trading stock rules. It is anchored to the year before: "The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous income year."
value_definition: A whole-dollar stock value at a point in time, calculated for tax purposes rather than lifted from the accounts, and including motor vehicle floor plan stock and work in progress on manufactured goods.
limitation: A small business entity using the simplified trading stock rules need not account for a change in value, in which case closing equals opening and a firm whose inventory actually moved shows no movement at all. Service firms hold no trading stock, so a zero carries no information about their size, and stock allocated to a business that commenced during the year is directed to the purchases label instead.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 8 label A, and the ATO page defines the value, its legislative basis and the continuity rule linking it to the prior year.
evidence_quote: The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Opening stock' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a tax value or that the simplified rules can freeze it.

value_domain: Dollar accounting profit or loss, company return item 6 bottom line
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: The firm's accounting bottom line for the year, before any tax adjustment. The ATO defines the item 6 result as follows: "Total profit or loss is the amount written at Income, S Total income, less the amount written at Expenses, Q Total expenses. If this amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at T." The label wording here is the older form's, which the current company return calls total profit or loss.
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual for the income year, equal to the item 6 income total less the item 6 expense total, on the company's own accounting basis.
limitation: It is not taxable income and should never be used as a tax base: every adjustment happens afterwards at item 7, and a firm can be profitable here and in loss for tax, or the reverse. The sign is carried by an indicator box rather than by the number, so a loss extracted without the indicator reads as a profit of the same size.
rationale: The label describes the item 6 result of a business income tax return, and the ATO expenses page defines that result and how a loss is marked. The mapping of the older operating profit wording to the current total profit or loss label is inferred from the arithmetic rather than published.
evidence_quote: Total profit or loss is the amount written at Income, S Total income, less the amount written at Expenses, Q Total expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Operating profit or loss' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the sign lives in a separate indicator or that the figure is not taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar cost of assets, company return item 9 label B
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 9. Capital allowances
variable_description: The cost of the tangible assets the firm began depreciating for the first time this year. The ATO instruction is to "Write at B the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the company is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time", and it is the counterpart of the intangible column beside it. Assets costing under $1,000 that went into a low-value pool are included, and the cost is not reduced for expected private or other non-taxable use.
value_definition: A whole-dollar cost for the income year, including amounts written off immediately under temporary full expensing.
limitation: Cost at first deduction is not the year's capital expenditure: an asset bought earlier but first installed ready for use now appears now, and an asset never used for a taxable purpose never appears. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules report their depreciation as tax values through the pooling labels instead, so this column is not a comparable investment series across firm sizes.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 9 label B, and the ATO capital allowances page defines the amount, the low-value pool inclusion and the no-reduction rule.
evidence_quote: Write at B the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the company is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the intangible assets column or warn against reading it as investment.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label R
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Income
variable_description: Every source of income that does not fit one of the named income labels at item 6. The ATO lists what belongs here: "royalties, insurance recoveries, bad debt recoveries, life insurance premiums, non-government subsidies, assessable non-government assistance from all sources, profit on sale of depreciating assets", TOFA gains not shown elsewhere, and extraordinary revenue from events outside the ordinary operations of the company. It can be negative, and the form marks that with an indicator letter.
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual income line for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, excluding everything already reported at the named labels.
limitation: The contents are heterogeneous, so a recurring royalty stream and a one-off gain on selling a machine are indistinguishable, and the column cannot be used to identify a business model. For a declared offshore banking unit the entire gross income from offshore banking activities is directed here, so for a handful of financial firms this residual label is the whole business.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 income label R, and the ATO income page enumerates what falls into it.
evidence_quote: Write at R the total amount of other gross income. Do not show at R amounts you included above at Income, from B to J item 6.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other gross income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the residual contains or that it can be negative.

value_domain: Dollar reconciliation subtraction, company return item 7 label X
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Deductions the firm was allowed for tax but did not show as expenses in its accounts. The ATO instruction is to "Write at X expense-related adjustments that are subtracted from T Total profit or loss item 6 to reconcile with T Taxable income or loss item 7", and it is the mirror image of the non-deductible expenses add-back. It is where timing differences that favour the taxpayer are recorded.
value_definition: A whole-dollar subtraction at item 7, excluding any amount already reported at the named subtraction labels between C and P of the same item.
limitation: Like its mirror label, it is a residual that cannot be decomposed: deductible foreign exchange losses, carbon sink forest establishment costs, R&D balancing adjustment catch-up deductions, a life insurer's listed investment company deduction and pure timing reversals all land in one number. A large value therefore identifies a gap between book and tax, not a tax concession.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label X, and the ATO reconciliation page defines the subtraction and lists the specific items it collects.
evidence_quote: Write at X expense-related adjustments that are subtracted from T Total profit or loss item 6 to reconcile with T Taxable income or loss item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other deductible expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read like an expense category rather than a reconciliation subtraction.

value_domain: Dollar total of eligible credits, company return calculation statement label H
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, calculation statement label H, eligible credits
variable_description: The credits the firm set against its tax bill other than its instalments, aggregated across the eligible credits block of the calculation statement. That block holds credit for interest on early payments, credit for tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, credit for foreign resident withholding and the other withholding credits. Credits sit after tax payable in the calculation, so they reduce the amount due or turn it into a refund.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total for the income year, aggregating the individual eligible credit labels of the calculation statement.
limitation: It is not the tax the firm paid. Pay as you go instalments have their own separate label and must not be added to this one as if both were payments, and a withholding credit can arise for a firm that ends the year with no liability at all. The aggregate also hides which credit produced it, so a firm that failed to quote an ABN and one with foreign resident withholding look the same.
rationale: The BLADE label names eligible credits, which is the title of the calculation statement's H block, and the ATO page for that block sets out the credits it holds and how they enter the amount due or refundable.
evidence_quote: Write at H1 only the calculated interest amount of 50 cents or more for early payment. Do not show actual payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label 'Eligible credits' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which credits it aggregates or that instalments are elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 6 label S
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 6. Expenses
variable_description: Every expense that does not fit one of the named expense labels at item 6. The ATO instruction is to "Write at S the total of all other expenses including losses on the disposal of depreciating assets (including assets used in R&D activities subject to the R&D tax incentive)", together with TOFA losses not already shown and "any extraordinary expenses, that is, expenses or losses from events outside the ordinary operations of the company and not of a recurring nature". For many small companies it is the largest single expense line.
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual expense line for the income year on the accounting basis used at item 6, excluding amounts already reported at the named expense labels.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed, so it defeats any attempt to build a cost structure from the return: accounting and legal fees, doubtful debt provisions, extraordinary losses and losses on asset disposals all land together. Non-deductible parts of it are added back at item 7, so it is also not a deduction.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 6 expense label S, and the ATO expenses page defines the residual and names what is directed into it.
evidence_quote: Write at S the total of all other expenses including losses on the disposal of depreciating assets (including assets used in R&D activities subject to the R&D tax incentive).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'All other expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the residual contains or how large a share of costs it typically is.

value_domain: Dollar reconciliation subtraction, company return item 7 label Q
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: Income the firm booked in its accounts that is not assessable for tax, subtracted at the reconciliation. The ATO instruction is to "Write at Q income-related adjustments that have to be subtracted from T Total profit or loss item 6 to reconcile with T Taxable income or loss item 7" and adds that "Generally, the amounts that are included at Q are income for accounting purposes, but not assessable for income tax purposes". Exempt income has its own label, so this one holds the non-assessable non-exempt residue.
value_definition: A whole-dollar subtraction at item 7, excluding anything already reported at the labels between the flow-on dividend deduction and exempt income.
limitation: It is not exempt income and should not be read as a tax concession: accounting capital profits that are dealt with as capital gains, non-assessable non-exempt foreign income, unfranked distributions that are conduit foreign income and cash flow boost receipts all sit in the same number. A large value therefore says the accounts and the tax law measure income differently, not that the firm was favoured.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label Q, and the ATO reconciliation page defines the subtraction, separates it from exempt income and lists what falls into it.
evidence_quote: Write at Q income-related adjustments that have to be subtracted from T Total profit or loss item 6 to reconcile with T Taxable income or loss item 7.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other Income not included in assessable Income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and nothing separated it from the exempt income label.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company return, overseas interests question
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, overseas transactions, interests or thin capitalisation (items 26 to 30)
variable_description: Whether the firm holds offshore structures, meaning an overseas branch or an interest in a foreign entity. The company return asks it as one question: "Did you have overseas branch operations or a direct or indirect interest in a foreign trust, foreign company, controlled foreign entity or transferor trust?" The ATO adds that a company must answer yes if it derived income treated as non-assessable non-exempt under the branch profits and participation exemption provisions, and a yes generally pulls an International dealings schedule with it.
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes and N for no, with any other value meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: Despite the variable name, this is not about interest income. It is an ownership and branch question and does not cover ordinary cross-border trade with related parties, which is asked separately. It also carries no country, no count of entities and no value, so the scale of a firm's offshore footprint cannot be read from it.
rationale: The BLADE label matches the company return's overseas interests question, and the ATO page states the question, defines overseas branch operations and lists the interests that require a yes.
evidence_quote: Did you have overseas branch operations or a direct or indirect interest in a foreign trust, foreign company, controlled foreign entity or transferor trust?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Overseas interest indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited a reader to take it for interest income received from overseas.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 8 label Q
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
variable_description: What a private company paid to its own people and their associates. The ATO instruction is to "Write at Q the amounts, including salaries, wages, commissions, superannuation contributions, allowances and payments in consequence of retirement or termination of employment, paid by a private company to associated persons", and it defines an associated person as "a current or former shareholder or director of the company, or an associate of such a person". The label exists because excessive amounts may be non-deductible and treated as unfranked dividends.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year, drawn from the same payroll figures as the total salary and wage expense label at item 8.
limitation: The amounts here are also inside the total salary and wage expense column, so adding the two double counts the same payroll. Only private companies complete it, and it does not record whether any part was in fact treated as excessive remuneration or reclassified as a dividend, so it cannot identify a Division 7A or section 109 outcome.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 8 label Q, and the ATO page defines the payments, defines an associated person and states the overlap with the salary and wage label.
evidence_quote: Also include the amounts of salaries and wages paid to associated persons at D Total salary and wage expenses item 8.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Payments to associated persons' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing defined an associated person or warned about the double count with payroll.

value_domain: Whole-number percentage, company return item 15 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 15. Licensed clubs only
variable_description: For a licensed club, the share of its income that came from people who are not members, which is the share that is taxable. The ATO instruction is to "Write at A the percentage, in whole figures, of total income attributable to non-members." The principle behind it is mutuality: a club's dealings with its own members are not income-producing for tax, so only the non-member share reaches taxable income.
value_definition: An integer percentage from 0 to 100 for the income year, self-assessed by the club from its own income records.
limitation: It is a ratio with no dollar value behind it, so the taxable income implied cannot be recovered without the club's income total at item 6. The label is only completed by licensed clubs, so it is empty or zero for every other company and cannot be used to compare mutuality across not-for-profit forms. The apportionment itself is the club's own estimate rather than an audited figure.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 15 label A, and the ATO page defines the percentage and points to the mutuality principle that gives it meaning.
evidence_quote: Write at A the percentage, in whole figures, of total income attributable to non-members.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Licensed clubs: percentage of non-member income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained mutuality or that the figure is a self-assessed whole-number ratio.

value_domain: Dollar reconciliation subtraction, company return item 7 label H
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 7. Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The year's write-off of capital expenditure the firm pooled against a project. The ATO instruction is to "Write at H the total amount of the company's deductions for project pools", and it includes the closing write-off: "If a project is abandoned, sold or otherwise disposed of, the company can deduct the project pool value at that time." The expenditure itself is added back at the non-deductible expenses label to the extent it went through item 6.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, spread over the project life under the uniform capital allowance rules.
limitation: It is the deduction taken, not the pool balance or the expenditure allocated, so a firm halfway through a long project and one that has just finished can show the same figure. A spike can mean a project was abandoned or sold, which brings the whole remaining pool into deduction at once, and nothing in the column distinguishes that from a project growing.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 7 label H, and the ATO reconciliation page defines the deduction, the disposal write-off and the matching add-back.
evidence_quote: Write at H the total amount of the company's deductions for project pools.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deduction for project pool' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the deduction is spread over the project life or that abandonment accelerates it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company return, item 8 label S
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 8. Financial and other information
variable_description: What the firm spent on the direct materials it turned into sales. The ATO instruction is to "Write at S the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business. This amount includes freight inwards." It sits in the tax-value block of item 8, alongside opening and closing stock, so the three together give a materials-based cost of goods for the year.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year calculated for tax purposes, excluding input tax credit entitlements.
limitation: It is not the accounting cost of sales, which is a separate item 6 label and includes external labour and other costs that this one excludes, so the two will not agree and should not be used interchangeably. A firm that continued to use the former simplified tax system accounting method writes only the costs it has paid, so the figure is on a cash basis for those firms.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 8 label S, and the ATO page defines the amount, its tax-value basis and the cash-basis exception.
evidence_quote: Write at S the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business. This amount includes freight inwards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Purchases and other costs' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and nothing separated it from the accounting cost of sales at item 6.

value_domain: Dollar total of pay as you go instalments, company return calculation statement label K
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, calculation statement labels I, K and S
variable_description: The instalments the firm reported on its activity statements through the year, credited against its final tax. The ATO instruction is to "Write at K the total of the company's PAYG instalments reported for the income year of the tax return" and to "Include in K the amounts the company reported at 5A on its activity statements, reduced by any credits it claimed at 5B." It is the link between the firm's within-year activity statement reporting and its annual return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total for the income year of monthly, quarterly or annual instalments raised, net of instalment credits claimed at 5B.
limitation: Instalments raised are not tax paid: the ATO states that "The company is entitled to a credit for its PAYG instalments even if it has not actually paid a particular instalment", so a firm in arrears shows the same figure as one that paid on time. Wash-up and residual payments are excluded, so this column plus the final balance does not reconcile to cash remitted.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's calculation statement label K, and the ATO page defines the total, its activity statement source and the credit-without-payment rule.
evidence_quote: The company is entitled to a credit for its PAYG instalments even if it has not actually paid a particular instalment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'PAYG instalments raised' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is raised rather than paid.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, company return item 9 label D
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 9. Capital allowances
variable_description: Whether the firm revised the effective life it uses to depreciate any of its assets this year. The ATO instruction is that "If you have recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets this income year, print X in the Yes box at D", and a recalculation is permitted where the life in use is no longer accurate and required in some circumstances. It sits beside a separate flag recording whether the firm self-assesses effective life rather than adopting the Commissioner's determination.
value_definition: A single character, Y for yes and N for no, with any other value meaning an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It triggers on any asset, so one revision on one machine records the same yes as a review of an entire fleet, and no count or value is attached. It also does not say which way the revision went, so it cannot be signed against a change in the depreciation deduction: a shortened life raises deductions and a lengthened life lowers them, and both read as yes.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 9 label D, and the ATO capital allowances page states the question and when a recalculation may or must be made.
evidence_quote: If you have recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets this income year, print X in the Yes box at D.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is any-asset and unsigned.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset, company return item 21 label A
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 21. Research and development tax incentive
variable_description: The R&D tax offset a company earned this year in the form that reduces tax but is not refunded. The ATO instruction is to "Write at A the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset. This is the amount calculated in the Research and development tax incentive schedule 2022 at Part E, A Non-refundable R&D tax offset item 3." Claiming an amount here obliges the company to lodge the R&D tax incentive schedule with its return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax offset earned in the income year, calculated on the R&D tax incentive schedule and rolled into the non-refundable carry forward offsets total of the calculation statement.
limitation: It is the offset earned, not the benefit received: whether any of it reduced tax this year is at the utilisation label, and the unused balance goes to the carry-forward label, so summing this column across years overstates what firms actually got. The offset also depends on the entity's aggregated turnover being above the refundable threshold, so it is the large-claimant form of the incentive.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 21 label A, and the ATO page defines it, states its source on the R&D schedule and shows how it flows to the calculation statement.
evidence_quote: Write at A the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset. This is the amount calculated in the Research and development tax incentive schedule 2022 at Part E, A Non-refundable R&D tax offset item 3.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Non-refundable R&D tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish the offset earned from the offset used or carried forward.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset carried forward, company return item 21 label D
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 21. Research and development tax incentive
variable_description: The part of the firm's R&D offset entitlement it could not use this year and takes into the next one. The ATO gives the arithmetic: "Write at D the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset carried forward to next year. This amount is calculated by adding the amounts at A and B item 21 and then subtracting the amount at C item 21." It is therefore a closing balance of unused entitlement, not a claim.
value_definition: A whole-dollar closing balance at the end of the income year, equal to the offset earned plus the offset brought forward less the offset utilised.
limitation: It is an entitlement, not an asset the firm is certain to realise. Division 65 requires the balance to be applied against net exempt income before it can reduce tax, and a company that fails both the continuity of ownership test and the business continuity test after a change of control cannot use it at all, so the balance can vanish without ever appearing as a benefit.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 21 label D, and the ATO page defines the balance, its arithmetic and the Division 65 and continuity restrictions that govern its later use.
evidence_quote: Write at D the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset carried forward to next year. This amount is calculated by adding the amounts at A and B item 21 and then subtracting the amount at C item 21.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the balance can be extinguished by a change of control.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset utilised, company return item 21 label C
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 21. Research and development tax incentive
variable_description: How much of the firm's R&D offset actually reduced its tax this year. The ATO instruction is to "Write at C the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset utilised in the current year. The non-refundable R&D tax offset can be utilised to reduce your tax payable to zero, but cannot go below zero, that is, not into a negative." It is the only R&D label at item 21 that measures a benefit received rather than an entitlement.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the income year, bounded above by the tax remaining after the non-carry-forward offsets have been applied.
limitation: Because it is bounded by the year's tax, a small value can reflect a loss-making or low-profit year rather than a small R&D claim, so it is a poor measure of R&D activity. It also does not separate the offset earned this year from the offset brought forward, both of which feed it, so the vintage of the benefit cannot be recovered.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 21 label C, and the ATO page defines the amount, the zero floor and its dependence on the calculation statement subtotals.
evidence_quote: Write at C the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset utilised in the current year. The non-refundable R&D tax offset can be utilised to reduce your tax payable to zero, but cannot go below zero, that is, not into a negative.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the amount is capped by the year's tax.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset brought forward, company return item 21 label B
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 21. Research and development tax incentive
variable_description: The unused R&D offset the firm brought into this year from earlier ones. The ATO instruction is to "Write at B the amount of non-refundable R&D tax offset carried forward from the previous year", drawn directly from the prior return: "You can obtain the amount to include at B from your previous year's company tax return at D Non-refundable R&D tax offset carried forward to next year item 21." It is an opening balance and reflects no new R&D at all.
value_definition: A whole-dollar opening balance for the income year, which should equal the prior year's closing carry-forward balance.
limitation: A non-zero value is history, not current research, so treating it as R&D activity in the year double counts spending already recorded in an earlier return. Where it does not match the prior year's closing balance the cause is an amendment or a Division 65 restriction rather than new expenditure, and the ATO directs a company blocked by the continuity tests to leave it blank.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 21 label B, and the ATO page defines it, ties it to the prior year's closing label and states when it must not be completed.
evidence_quote: You can obtain the amount to include at B from your previous year's company tax return at D Non-refundable R&D tax offset carried forward to next year item 21 in the Company tax return 2021.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the value reflects prior years rather than current research.

value_domain: Dollar tax amount, company return calculation statement label M
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, calculation statement labels A, T1, M and B
variable_description: Extra tax charged where a firm received a government grant for R&D it had already claimed a notional deduction for. The ATO restricts the label sharply: "Only for use by early balancing entities with a substitute accounting period. Write at M the extra tax required on your recoupment as calculated under Subdivision 355-G of the ITAA 1997." The charge is capped, so "the extra tax payable cannot exceed the amount of the grant you received", and it is added into gross tax.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of extra income tax for the income year, added to tax on taxable income to give gross tax.
limitation: This label captures only early balancers with a substituted accounting period. For every other company the same clawback is delivered as additional assessable income at item 21 and item 7 instead, so the column is near-empty and cannot be used to measure grant clawback across the population of R&D claimants.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's calculation statement label M, and the ATO page defines the recoupment tax, the restriction to early balancers and the cap at the grant amount.
evidence_quote: Only for use by early balancing entities with a substitute accounting period. Write at M the extra tax required on your recoupment as calculated under Subdivision 355-G of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'R&D recoupment tax' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the label is restricted to a small group of filers.

value_domain: Dollar refundable tax offset, company return item 21 label U
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions, 21. Research and development tax incentive
variable_description: The R&D tax offset a smaller company receives as cash where it has no tax to pay. The ATO instruction is to "Write at U the amount of refundable R&D tax offset. This amount is calculated in Part E, U Refundable R&D tax offset item 2 of the Research and development tax incentive schedule 2022", and it is claimed in the refundable tax offsets total of the calculation statement. Because it is refundable, it reaches loss-making research firms that a deduction would never help.
value_definition: A whole-dollar refundable tax offset for the income year, calculated on the R&D tax incentive schedule and lodged with it.
limitation: The refundable form applies only below an aggregated turnover threshold, so the column truncates at the larger end of the size distribution and the non-refundable offset at item 21 takes over there. Reading it as R&D intensity therefore mixes a size cut-off with research behaviour, and it also says nothing about whether the underlying activities were later found ineligible on registration review.
rationale: The BLADE label is the company return's item 21 label U, and the ATO page defines the amount, its source on the R&D schedule and where it is claimed.
evidence_quote: Write at U the amount of refundable R&D tax offset. This amount is calculated in Part E, U Refundable R&D tax offset item 2 of the Research and development tax incentive schedule 2022.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Refundable R&D tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the refundable form is reserved for smaller claimants.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: What the company paid as a tenant to rent land and buildings it used to earn income during the year. The ATO instruction for the label is "Write at H the expenditure incurred as a tenant on rental of land and buildings used in the production of income". It is an item 6 figure, so it is the accounting expense from the financial statements before any tax adjustment at item 7, and it sits beside separate lease, interest and repairs columns.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label H of the company return. Item 6 amounts are accounting system amounts that correspond to the company's financial statements, not tax values.
limitation: It is not a firm's premises cost. Leases of plant, equipment and vehicles go to the lease expense labels, a company that owns its premises reports nothing here despite occupying space, and rent paid to a related entity is indistinguishable from rent paid at arm's length.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 rent expense label, and the ATO instruction page for item 6 gives the label wording and the rule that item 6 amounts are accounting figures.
evidence_quote: Write at H the expenditure incurred as a tenant on rental of land and buildings used in the production of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word return label 'Rent expenses' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is an accounting figure or what it excludes.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Spending on keeping the company's existing plant, machinery and premises working, as expensed in its accounts. The ATO instruction is "Write at Z the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises". Anything of a capital nature that a company puts here has to be added back at the non-deductible expenses label at item 7, so the column can carry more than the tax law allows as a repair.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label Z of the company return, taken from the accounts rather than calculated for tax.
limitation: It is not a measure of capital renewal or asset condition. Alterations, additions and improvements are capital and belong in depreciation, and remedying defects that existed when an asset was bought is capital too, so a firm that replaces rather than repairs shows a small figure here while spending heavily.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 repairs and maintenance label, and the ATO instruction page gives both the label wording and the capital add-back rule that bounds what the number means.
evidence_quote: Write at Z the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Repairs and maintenance' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and never distinguished repairs from capital improvements.

value_domain: Dollar amount of refundable tax offsets claimed
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
variable_description: The total refundable tax offsets the company claimed for the year, the refundable research and development offset being the largest of them for most firms. The ATO says these offsets "are refundable, although they must first be offset against gross tax, if there is any gross tax to be paid after C and D have been applied", and that any excess is recorded at the remainder label. The instruction is also to write "the total of actual tax offsets available (in dollars and cents) and not the amounts giving rise to those tax offsets".
value_definition: Dollars and cents at calculation statement label E. It is the entitlement available in the year, before it is applied against tax, and it feeds the subtotal 3 step.
limitation: It is not a refund. A profitable company absorbs the whole amount against tax and receives no cash, so only reading this column together with the remainder of refundable tax offsets separates a claim from a payment.
rationale: The DIL label is calculation statement label E, and the ATO's label page defines what goes in it, states the order of application and distinguishes the offset from the expenditure that generates it.
evidence_quote: The tax offsets shown at E are refundable, although they must first be offset against gross tax, if there is any gross tax to be paid after C and D have been applied to gross tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Refundable tax offsets' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving a reader unable to tell this from the amount actually refunded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of refundable tax offsets not absorbed by tax
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels I, K and S
variable_description: The part of the company's refundable tax offsets left over once tax had been reduced to zero, which is the amount that becomes a credit to the company. The ATO instruction is "Write at I the remaining amount (if any) of refundable tax offsets from E", and the label is mandatory, so a zero is a real answer rather than a skipped question. Read against the refundable tax offsets column, this is the split between an offset that saved tax and one that paid cash out.
value_definition: Dollars and cents at calculation statement label I, being label E less whatever was absorbed at subtotal 2. It cannot be negative and is written as zero when the offsets were fully used.
limitation: It is not the cash the company received. Label S nets this against PAYG instalments, withholding credits and the section 102AAM interest charge before any payment or refund is worked out, so a firm with a large figure here can still owe tax.
rationale: The DIL label matches calculation statement label I, and the ATO page defines it as the remainder from label E and sets out where it goes in the final balance.
evidence_quote: Write at I the remaining amount (if any) of refundable tax offsets from E.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing tied it to label E or explained that a zero means the offsets were fully absorbed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Royalties the company paid to Australian residents during the year, typically for the use of intellectual property, trademarks or resources. The ATO instruction is "Write at W the royalty expenses paid during the income year to Australian residents". Its pair on the same return is the overseas royalty label, and the split between the two is the only thing on the return that says whether a company's licensing costs stay onshore.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label W of the company return. The Australian label is on a paid basis, while the overseas label is on an incurred basis.
limitation: It cannot identify what was licensed or from whom. A company licensing from an Australian subsidiary of a foreign group reports here, not at the overseas label, so this column understates payments that ultimately leave the country.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 domestic royalty label and the ATO instruction page states its scope and the record-keeping it requires.
evidence_quote: Write at W the royalty expenses paid during the income year to Australian residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Royalty expenses in Australia' with the generic sentence printed twice, and never contrasted it with the overseas royalty label it exists to separate.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: Royalties the company incurred to non-residents, the classic channel for paying a foreign parent for intellectual property. The ATO instruction is "Write at U the royalty expenses incurred during the income year to non-residents", and reporting an amount here triggers a further form: "If an amount is reported at U, complete and attach an International dealings schedule". Royalty withholding tax is generally deducted from these payments, so an amount here implies a withholding obligation the return does not show.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label U of the company return, measured on an incurred rather than a paid basis.
limitation: It says nothing about who was paid or whether the price was arm's length; only the international dealings schedule carries the counterparty and country detail. Thin capitalisation and transfer pricing adjustments happen at item 7, so a large figure here is not necessarily a large deduction.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 overseas royalty label; the ATO instruction page gives the wording, the schedule trigger and the withholding consequence.
evidence_quote: Write at U the royalty expenses incurred during the income year to non-residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Royalty expenses overseas' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without noting the international dealings schedule trigger that makes the label a marker of related-party dealings.

value_domain: Country by country reporting entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: Whether the company self-assessed itself as a country by country reporting entity, which in practice marks it as part of a very large multinational group. The ATO instruction is "Print X at G2 if the entity was a Country by country reporting entity (CBC reporting entity) for the income year", an entity being one if it is "a country by country reporting parent, or a member of a country by country reporting group, and one of the other group members is a CBC reporting parent with an annual global income of A$1 billion or more". The flag sits beside the significant global entity flag at the same item and the two tests are not identical.
value_definition: A coded flag at item 3 label G2: 5 marks a CBC reporting entity and every other value is an invalid response or no response, so it reads as yes against not-stated rather than yes against no.
limitation: The label does not appear on older company returns - it is absent from the 2013 form and present from 2020 - so an empty run of years is a change in the form, not evidence that a group was small. It is also a self-assessment, and misapplying the investment entity exception changes the answer without changing the group.
rationale: The BLADE valid-response text names the country by country reporting entity, which is item 3 label G2 of the company return; the ATO status page defines the term and distinguishes it from the significant global entity test.
evidence_quote: Print X at G2 if the entity was a Country by country reporting entity (CBC reporting entity) for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw code text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is self-assessed, recent, or different from the significant global entity flag beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 6 Income
variable_description: The company's ordinary trading revenue: gross sales of trading stock, manufactured goods and services. The ATO requires it before netting, saying "Gross income is to be shown before any legal set off or other netting off between amounts", and excludes payments where an ABN was not quoted or where foreign resident withholding applied, which have their own labels. For most operating companies this is the closest single column to turnover, but total income is the correct measure of the whole income side.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 6 label C of the company return, on an accounting basis and gross of any offsetting amounts.
limitation: It is not turnover and not aggregated turnover. Dividends, interest, rent, government industry payments and gains on asset sales sit at other labels, so a finance or property company can report almost nothing here while running a large business.
rationale: The DIL label is the company return's item 6 other sales of goods and services label; the ATO income page lists what belongs in it and what must be reported elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Gross income is to be shown before any legal set off or other netting off between amounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Other sales of goods and services' with the generic sentence twice, and gave no warning against reading the column as turnover.

value_domain: Dollar amount of accelerated depreciation deductions claimed
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Depreciation claimed this year on assets that were first written down under the Backing business investment measure in an earlier year. The ATO instruction is "If you are an entity that used the Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation in a previous year for one or more assets, write at N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2021-22 for these assets". The first-year claim, which was half the asset's cost plus ordinary depreciation on the rest, sits at a different label, so this column is the tail of a stimulus measure rather than the take-up of it.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 9 label N of the company return, covering only assets already inside the Backing business investment measure.
limitation: It is not an investment measure. New assets stopped entering the measure once temporary full expensing took over from October 2020, so the column decays for reasons that have nothing to do with a firm's capital spending, and the opt-out labels mean some eligible assets never appear at all.
rationale: The DIL label names the subsequent year Backing business investment deduction, which is item 9 label N; the ATO instruction page for item 9 defines the label and its relationship to the first-year claim.
evidence_quote: If you are an entity that used the Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation in a previous year for one or more assets, write at N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2021–22 for these assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label as its description with the generic sentence twice, and never separated the subsequent-year tail from the first-year claim.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deduction claimed on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: A deduction for unfranked non-portfolio dividends that an Australian company passed straight through to its foreign parent. The ATO explains that the deduction "is allowable in certain cases where a non-portfolio dividend that is not fully franked is on-paid by a resident company to its non-resident parent", and that claiming it obliges the company to keep an unfranked non-portfolio dividend account under section 46FB. An amount here also forces an international dealings schedule.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a reconciliation deduction at item 7 label C of the company return, subtracted from accounting profit in arriving at taxable income.
limitation: The column is almost always zero and a zero carries no information about foreign ownership, since only a resident subsidiary that on-paid an unfranked non-portfolio dividend can use it. The section 46FB account balance that makes the deduction meaningful is on a separate schedule.
rationale: The DIL label names the section 46FA deduction for flow-on dividends, which is item 7 label C; the ATO reconciliation page gives the label's scope and the account it requires.
evidence_quote: This deduction is allowable in certain cases where a non-portfolio dividend that is not fully franked is on-paid by a resident company to its non-resident parent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the statutory label with the generic sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know what circumstance produces a non-zero value.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deduction claimed on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 7 Reconciliation to taxable income or loss
variable_description: The company's claim under section 40-880, the provision that lets business capital expenditure with no other home be written off in equal parts over five years. The ATO instruction is "Write at Z the total of the company's deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997", and the same expenditure has to be added back at the non-deductible expenses label to the extent it was already expensed at item 6. Because the write-off is spread, an entry here signals costs such as business establishment, restructure or cessation expenses that were incurred in this year or in any of the four before it.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a reconciliation deduction at item 7 label Z of the company return, being the current year's slice of expenditure spread over five income years.
limitation: It cannot be read as this year's capital spending: in a typical case it is one fifth of the underlying amount and mixes slices from up to five separate years of expenditure. The column also does not say what the expenditure was for, so start-up costs and wind-up costs look identical.
rationale: The DIL label names the section 40-880 deduction, item 7 label Z, and the ATO reconciliation page gives the instruction and the interaction with the non-deductible expenses add-back.
evidence_quote: Write at Z the total of the company’s deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the section number as the description with the generic sentence twice, and never said the deduction is spread over five years.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: Whether the company worked out the effective life of any depreciating asset itself rather than adopting the Commissioner's determination. The ATO puts the choice plainly: a taxpayer may "work out the effective life yourself (self-assess), or use an effective life determined by the Commissioner", and prints X in the Yes box "If you have self-assessed the effective life of any of your depreciating assets". A shorter self-assessed life brings deductions forward, so the flag marks firms taking a position on their own depreciation rates.
value_definition: A yes or no flag at item 9 label C of the company return, with Y and N coded and anything else an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is an any-asset flag, so a company that self-assessed one asset out of a thousand is indistinguishable from one that self-assessed the lot, and the flag does not say whether the chosen life was shorter or longer than the Commissioner's. It is a separate question from recalculating effective life, which has its own label.
rationale: The DIL label is the exact wording of the company return's item 9 self-assessment question; the ATO instruction page defines the two alternatives and how the box is completed.
evidence_quote: If you have self-assessed the effective life of any of your depreciating assets, print X in the Yes box at C.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic sentence twice, and never explained that a yes can rest on a single asset.

value_domain: Dollar amount of shareholders funds from the company's balance sheet
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The company's shareholders funds: the equity left on its balance sheet after liabilities, reported beside total assets and total liabilities. The ATO's rule for that block is that amounts from trade debtors to total liabilities are taken from the accounts "as these amounts relate to accounting values", so this is book equity rather than anything computed for tax. The current company return no longer asks for it, so the column belongs to the earlier years of the Business Income Tax file.
value_definition: A dollar amount and a stock measured at the end of the income year, drawn from the financial statements rather than from tax values.
limitation: A blank is a form change, not a company without equity: the label is absent from recent company returns, so a series built across the change breaks. Book equity is also not market value and can be negative for a solvent firm carrying accumulated losses.
rationale: The label sits with the other balance sheet items of the company return's financial information block, and the ATO page for that block states that those amounts are accounting values. No fetchable ATO page carries the shareholders funds label itself, which is why this is guessed.
evidence_quote: Include amounts taken from the company’s financial statements at C Trade debtors to H Total liabilities, and N Loans to shareholders and their associates as these amounts relate to accounting values.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Shareholders funds' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say the figure is an accounting balance or that the label has been dropped from the return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the SME income component of a pooled development fund
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 18 Pooled development funds
variable_description: The small and medium sized enterprises income component of a pooled development fund, which is the part of the fund's taxable income attributed to its SME investments. The ATO defines it as "its SME assessable income, less deductions allowable to the PDF for the income year, whether those deductions relate to the SME assessable income or not", and notes that deductions hit this class first before touching unregulated investment income. It only makes sense read against the unregulated investment income column, because the two components together exhaust the fund's taxable income.
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 18 label G of the company return, a flow over the income year that already has deductions and the relevant capital gains and losses applied within the SME class.
limitation: It is not a measure of SME income in the economy: only companies registered as pooled development funds complete item 18, so the column is empty for essentially every other business. The deduction ordering rule also means the figure falls when unrelated deductions rise.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 18 label G of the company return, and the ATO page defines the SME income component, its assessable income base and the deduction ordering.
evidence_quote: A pool development fund's (PDF) SME income component is its SME assessable income, less deductions allowable to the PDF for the income year, whether those deductions relate to the SME assessable income or not.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Small and medium sized enterprises income' with the generic sentence twice, which invited a reader to treat it as an SME income measure for ordinary companies.

value_domain: Business status code: ceased, commenced or continuing
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2022 instructions, items P2 to P6
variable_description: Whether the business ceased, commenced or continued during the income year, as the lodger answered it on the return. The ATO asks the same question on its business schedules by exception rather than by choice: a box is marked "If you ceased your main business during 2021-22" and another "If you commenced a new business", with both left blank when the business simply continued. That construction matters for BLADE, because the continuing category is the default state and therefore also collects every lodger who did not answer.
value_definition: A three-way code: 5 ceased, 10 commenced and 15 continuing, with anything else an invalid response or no response given.
limitation: It is the lodger's own account of the business, not an ABS Business Register event or an ASIC deregistration, so a shell that keeps lodging stays continuing for years after it stops trading, and a business that ceased late in the year still reports a full set of income and expense labels.
rationale: The three states in the BLADE valid-response text are exactly the ATO's business status question, and the business and professional items page defines how the ceased and commenced boxes work and what a blank means. The company return page carrying this label is not fetchable, so the entry is marked guessed.
evidence_quote: If you ceased your main business during 2021–22, enter X at C1 item P4 on page 2 of your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw code list with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that continuing is a residual category rather than a positive answer.

value_domain: Tax consolidation status of the company
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: Whether the company lodged as the head company of a tax consolidated group, or as a subsidiary member reporting a period when it sat outside one. The ATO instruction is to "Select Z1 Consolidated head company if the company was a head company of a consolidated or MEC group at any time during the income year", and Z2 only "if Z1 does not apply and the company was a subsidiary member of a consolidated or MEC group that had a period when it was not a member of the group". A head company's income, expenses and balance sheet cover the whole group, so this flag decides how to read every dollar figure on the row.
value_definition: A coded status at item 3 label Z: 5 consolidated head company, 10 consolidated subsidiary member, with anything else an invalid or absent response. Only one of the two can be selected.
limitation: It cannot be used to count group members or measure group size. A subsidiary inside a consolidated group does not lodge a return at all, so it is absent from the data rather than coded, and a subsidiary that does appear is there because of a non-membership period, meaning its figures cover part of a year.
rationale: The two BLADE categories are the company return's Z1 and Z2 boxes at item 3, and the ATO page defines each and the exclusivity between them.
evidence_quote: Select Z1 Consolidated head company if the company was a head company of a consolidated or MEC group at any time during the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text with the generic sentence twice, and never said that consolidated subsidiaries are missing from the file rather than coded, which is the trap this column sets.

value_domain: Company residency status for tax
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 3 Status of company
variable_description: The company's residency for tax, split into resident, non-resident without an Australian permanent establishment and non-resident with one. The ATO's rule for the third box is "Complete C3 if the company is a non-resident company carrying on a business in Australia through a permanent establishment (PE)". The distinction drives the income base itself: a resident is taxed on income from all sources while a non-resident is taxed on Australian-sourced income, so the same taxable income label means different things across the three categories.
value_definition: A coded status at item 3 label C: 15 resident, 20 non-resident with no permanent establishment, 25 non-resident with a permanent establishment, and 5 for a blank answer.
limitation: Tax residency is not ownership or incorporation. An Australian-incorporated subsidiary of a foreign group is a resident here, so this column cannot be used to identify foreign-owned firms - the ultimate holding company country code is the label for that.
rationale: The BLADE categories map one to one onto the company return's C1, C2 and C3 residency boxes at item 3, and the ATO page defines the permanent establishment condition that separates the two non-resident states.
evidence_quote: Complete C3 if the company is a non-resident company carrying on a business in Australia through a permanent establishment (PE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the codes with the generic sentence twice, and left a reader likely to treat residency as a proxy for foreign ownership.

value_domain: Dollar amount of immediate write-off deductions for cheap depreciating assets
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
variable_description: The deduction a small business claimed by writing off cheap depreciating assets immediately instead of pooling and depreciating them. It is the first label of the simplified depreciation item, whose current wording is a deduction for assets "costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold"; the sts in the variable name points to the Simplified Tax System, the pre-2007 name for these small business concessions, when the same line was described as low cost assets. The threshold that defines cheap has moved repeatedly, so the label's meaning is anchored to the year.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 10 label A of the company return, available only to a small business entity that has chosen the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: The series is not comparable across years, because the amount depends as much on where the write-off threshold sat as on the firm's spending, and for 2021-22 the ATO directed small businesses to write zero here and use temporary full expensing instead. A zero therefore does not mean the firm bought no cheap assets.
rationale: The label is the immediate write-off line of the company return's simplified depreciation item, and the ATO page states its current scope and the instruction to report zero while temporary full expensing applied. The reading of sts as the Simplified Tax System is inferred from the variable name.
evidence_quote: A small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules must insert 0 at A because, in 2021–22, you do not hold an asset meeting the criteria to claim instant asset write-off.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Deduction for low cost assets' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing recorded that the threshold moves or that the label was forced to zero in the temporary full expensing years.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the general small business pool deduction
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
variable_description: The depreciation a small business claimed on its general pool, the single pool holding the assets that were too dear for the immediate write-off. The ATO instruction is "Write at B the total amount the company claimed at item 6 relating to the general small business pool", and it adds that a company which has already written the pool balance off in a previous year inserts zero. The custodian's description is truncated to 'Deduction for general'; the full label is deduction for general small business pool, and the sts in the variable name is the Simplified Tax System, the older name for the same concessions.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the income year, at item 10 label B of the company return, calculated from the pool balance at a fixed statutory rate rather than asset by asset.
limitation: It lags investment rather than measuring it: a pool deduction is driven by the accumulated balance, so it keeps running for years after the last purchase and falls to zero the moment the pool is written off, even though the firm still holds and uses the assets.
rationale: The truncated DIL label matches item 10 label B of the company return, and the ATO page gives the instruction and the write-off condition that produces zeros.
evidence_quote: Write at B the total amount the company claimed at item 6 relating to the general small business pool.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the truncated wording 'Deduction for general' as its whole description with the generic sentence twice, so the column did not even name the pool it belongs to.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
variable_description: The first of the three running subtotals in the calculation statement: tax left after the non-refundable, non-carry-forward offsets are applied to gross tax. The ATO instruction is "Write at T2 the amount of tax payable after C has been offset against B Gross tax" and "T2 cannot be less than zero". It is the step where offsets such as the foreign income tax offset are used or lost.
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T2, floored at zero, being gross tax less the label C offsets.
limitation: Because the subtotal floors at zero, it cannot show the value of the offsets that were wasted: offsets at label C that exceed gross tax are neither refunded nor carried forward, and nothing on the statement records the excess.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 1' is calculation statement label T2, and the ATO label page defines the arithmetic and the zero floor.
evidence_quote: Write at T2 the amount of tax payable after C has been offset against B Gross tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 1' and printed the generic sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about which offsets had been applied by that point.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels C, T2, D and T3
variable_description: The second running subtotal: tax left after the non-refundable carry forward offsets are applied to subtotal 1. The ATO instruction is "Write at T3 the amount of tax payable after D has been offset against T2", and it cannot be less than zero. The offsets applied at this step are the ones that survive an unprofitable year, since "Any excess offsets can be carried forward to a later income year".
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T3, floored at zero, being subtotal 1 less the label D offsets.
limitation: It hides the carry-forward that gives these offsets their value: where label D exceeds subtotal 1, the unused part moves to a later year and no column on this row records how much left. Comparing T2 and T3 gives offsets used, not offsets held.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 2' is calculation statement label T3, and the ATO label page defines the step and the carry-forward treatment that distinguishes it from subtotal 1.
evidence_quote: Write at T3 the amount of tax payable after D has been offset against T2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 2' with the generic sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the other two subtotal columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount at a calculation statement subtotal
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels E, T4 and F
variable_description: The third running subtotal: tax left after the refundable tax offsets are applied to subtotal 2. The ATO instruction is "Write at T4 the amount of tax payable after E has been offset against T3", and it cannot be less than zero. This is the step at which a company with a large refundable research and development offset drops to nil tax and starts generating a refund at the remainder label.
value_definition: Whole dollars and cents at calculation statement label T4, floored at zero, being subtotal 2 less the label E refundable offsets.
limitation: A zero here is ambiguous on its own: it covers both a company with no tax to pay before offsets and a company whose refundable offsets more than covered its tax. Only the remainder of refundable tax offsets column separates the two.
rationale: The DIL label 'Subtotal 3' is calculation statement label T4, and the ATO label page defines the step and its relationship to the refundable offsets and the remainder label.
evidence_quote: Write at T4 the amount of tax payable after E has been offset against T3.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Subtotal 3' with the generic sentence twice, and the three subtotal columns were interchangeable on the page.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax payable on the company tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2022 instructions, Calculation statement labels T5 and G
variable_description: The company's tax payable for the year, the end of the offset sequence: "Write at T5 the amount of tax payable after F has been offset against T4". The ATO makes the label mandatory and requires a zero rather than a blank when no tax is payable, so it is the closest thing on the return to a headline company tax liability.
