value_definition: A non-negative integer count of grant events in one financial year, counting rights rather than applicants' shares.
limitation: Filed and granted counts in the same year do not form a success rate, because the grants relate to earlier cohorts of applications; a firm can show zero filings and several grants, or the reverse, without any change in behaviour. The lag varies with examination and with whether the applicant requested certification, so it is not a fixed offset either.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the granted event stream and the enforceable-status terminology inherited from IPGOD, which is what a grant means in this column.
evidence_quote: Gained Enforceable Status is used in the IPGOD dataset to describe when a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned against reading filings and grants in one year as a conversion rate.

value_domain: Fractional count of design applications granted in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights granted in the financial year, split evenly among co-applicants. It applies the same weighting rule as the filing column, which IP Australia introduced so that "accurate numbers of applications" are "preserved in aggregate for each IP right type". Use it rather than the plain granted count when adding grants across firms or industries.
value_definition: A non-negative rational number for one financial year, equal to the plain granted count for sole owners and fractional where a right is jointly held.
limitation: Ownership can change between filing and grant, through assignment or a change in the applicant list, so a firm's weighted grant share need not match its weighted filing share for the same design. Differencing the two columns as a measure of attrition will therefore pick up ownership transfers as well as failed applications.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary states the joint-applicant weighting rule and its purpose, and defines the granted event stream to which it is applied here.
evidence_quote: The inclusion of weighted count variables allows for accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's phrase about a fraction granted and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said ownership can shift between the filing and grant streams.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas among granted designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different Locarno product areas the business obtained design rights in during the financial year. It is the granted counterpart of the filing scope column, and IP Australia gives the trade marks analogue to show the reading: "an applicant with a trademark granting scope of 20 in 2019/20 would have had trademark applications granted with classifications in 20 different trademark areas". For designs the corresponding ceiling is 32 areas.
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 for one financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories among the rights granted that year.
limitation: The rights counted here were filed in earlier years, so a change in granted scope is evidence about past strategy, not this year's; using it as a contemporaneous diversification measure will date the firm's decisions wrongly by the length of the examination lag.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables with a worked granting example and fixes the number of design classification areas that bound this column.
evidence_quote: For example, an applicant with a trademark granting scope of 20 in 2019/20 would have had trademark applications granted with classifications in 20 different trademark areas (of the possible 45 in the Nice system).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the granted scope reflects earlier filing decisions.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value among granted designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that most of the business's design grants fell into during the financial year. Assigning one area per right is possible because multiple classification is rare in designs: IP Australia notes that "While in designs, multiple classification types for a single Right are possible, they are rare." That makes the design mode cleaner than the equivalent for patents or trade marks, where a single right routinely carries several classifications.
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories among the year's grants, with 99 meaning unknown.
limitation: It can differ from the filed modal class in the same year without meaning anything, because the two streams describe different cohorts of designs. Reading a divergence between them as a pivot in product focus would confuse the examination queue with a business decision.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables, the granted event stream and the rarity of multiple classification in designs, which is what makes a single modal area meaningful here.
evidence_quote: While in designs, multiple classification types for a single Right are possible, they are rare.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished the granted mode from the filed mode.

value_domain: Stock of legally enforceable design rights at end of financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many design rights the business could actually enforce at the end of the financial year, which is a stock rather than a flow. IP Australia defines the stream as "Enforceable - Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year" and states that "Filings do not affect the stockpile", so only grants and retirements move it. The BLADE column name uses le for legally enforceable where the public IPLoRD release calls the same stream enforceable.
value_definition: A non-negative integer standing at the last day of the financial year, counting rights held rather than events during the year.
limitation: Because it is a stock, it must not be summed across years the way the filed, granted and retired counts can be; adding twenty years of stockpiles counts the same right twenty times. It also counts rights, not their commercial value or whether the design is still in production.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the enforceable stockpile, states what moves it and what does not, and the naming convention that maps the BLADE le prefix onto that stream.
evidence_quote: Enforceable - Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said this is a stock that cannot be summed over time.

value_domain: Fractional stock of legally enforceable design rights at end of financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights it could enforce at the end of the financial year, with jointly held rights split evenly among owners. It applies the same one-over-n rule as the flow columns, so it is the column to use when aggregating portfolios across firms without double counting shared rights. IP Australia describes the underlying quantity as the applicant's stockpile of "applications fractions owned and legally enforceable" at year end.
value_definition: A non-negative rational number standing at the last day of the financial year, equal to the plain enforceable count for sole owners and fractional where rights are jointly held.
limitation: Enforcement is not divisible the way the count is. A joint owner with a 0.5 share can generally still act on the whole right, so this column understates what the firm can do while the plain stock column overstates the national total; neither is the right answer to a question about litigation capacity.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines both the weighted count rule and the enforceable stockpile, whose combination is what this column holds; the enforcement consequence is an inference from how joint ownership works rather than a published statement.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about fractions owned and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the fraction does not correspond to a fraction of enforcement rights.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas in the enforceable design portfolio
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Across how many Locarno product areas the business's live design portfolio was spread at the end of the financial year. It is the stock counterpart of the filed and granted scope columns, so it accumulates the breadth of past grants net of retirements rather than describing this year's activity. IP Australia builds all scope variables on the same idea of "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity".
value_definition: An integer from 0 to 32 measured at the last day of the financial year, counting distinct Locarno high-level categories represented in the enforceable stockpile.
limitation: It moves slowly and lags: a firm that abandons a product area keeps the area in its scope until the last right there is retired, which for a design can be years. Treating a fall in this column as the moment the firm exited a market will therefore date the exit far too late.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the scope metric and the enforceable event stream that this column combines, and states that the stockpile changes only through grants and retirements.
evidence_quote: The enforceable stockpile is affected by flows from the granted and retired applications.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that portfolio scope lags behind business decisions.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value in the enforceable design portfolio
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that dominates the business's live design portfolio at the end of the financial year. Unlike the filed and granted modes on the same row, this one describes accumulated holdings rather than a year's events, so it is the closest thing IPLoRD offers to a design-based industry marker for a firm. IP Australia's simplified classification is deliberately coarse, being intended "as a table for high-level economic analysis of an organisation's IP right filing activity across time".
value_definition: A character code identifying one of the 32 Locarno high-level categories, measured over the enforceable stockpile at year end, with 99 meaning unknown.
limitation: The portfolio mode is set by whichever product line the firm registered most heavily in the past, so it can keep pointing at a discontinued product long after the firm has moved on. It is a poor instrument for current activity and should be read against the filed modal class, which responds immediately.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables, the enforceable stockpile and the intended level of analysis, which together determine what this column can support.
evidence_quote: As IPLoRD is intended as a table for high-level economic analysis of an organisation's IP right filing activity across time, a simpler classification system is required for some rights.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the portfolio mode lags the firm's current product focus.

value_domain: Count of design rights retired in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many of the business's design rights ceased during the financial year, which IP Australia calls the retired event stream. The dictionary defines the stream as "Retired - rights retired during the financial year", one of the two flows that move the enforceable stockpile on the same row. A retirement is the end of protection for that design, whatever the reason.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of retirement events in one financial year, counting rights rather than owners' shares.
limitation: It cannot separate a deliberate lapse from an expiry. A firm that stops paying renewal fees because a product line closed and a firm whose right simply reached the end of its maximum term both appear here identically, so a spike in retirements is not by itself evidence of retrenchment.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the retired event stream and its role in moving the enforceable stockpile, which is what this count records.
evidence_quote: Retired - rights retired during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that retirement conflates lapse with expiry.

value_domain: Fractional count of design rights retired in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the design rights retired during the financial year, split evenly where the right was jointly held. It closes the weighted accounting on the row: weighted filings, grants, retirements and stock all use the same one-over-n rule, so the weighted stock moves by weighted grants less weighted retirements. IP Australia frames the column as the fraction of applications the applicant "has allowed to retire" that year.
value_definition: A non-negative rational number for one financial year, equal to the plain retired count for sole owners and fractional where the retired right was jointly held.
limitation: A joint right retires as a whole, so the co-owners' fractions retire together whether or not each of them wanted it to. The column therefore attributes to a firm a decision it may not have made, which matters for any analysis reading retirement as a signal about that firm's product strategy.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count rule and the retired event stream that this column combines; the joint-retirement consequence follows from how a single right is held rather than from a published statement.
evidence_quote: Weighted count variables consider the number of applicants associated with an IP Right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about fractions allowed to retire and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said a co-owner cannot retire its share alone.

value_domain: Count of distinct Locarno classification areas among retired designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different Locarno product areas the business let design rights lapse in during the financial year. It is the retirement counterpart of the filed and granted scope columns, and reading it against the enforceable scope on the same row shows whether a firm is narrowing its portfolio or merely refreshing it. IP Australia builds every scope variable from the same set of "32 high-level categories (classification areas)" for designs.

Comparing the raw scope across firms therefore ranks past diversity, not the extent of the withdrawal.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables, the retired event stream and the fixed set of design classification areas that bounds this column.
evidence_quote: The Locarno system for designs has 32 high-level categories (classification areas).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the measure is bounded by the firm's own portfolio breadth.

value_domain: Locarno classification area, modal value among retired designs
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The Locarno product area that most of the business's retired design rights came from in the financial year. IP Australia names such columns by right type, event stream and metric, giving as its own worked example "the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class"; this is the design equivalent. It answers what the firm is giving up, not what it is pursuing.

A firm with a single legacy product line will show the same retirement mode for years as that stock winds down.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary gives the naming convention with the retired modal class as its worked example, and defines the modal metric and the design classification areas it draws on.
evidence_quote: Similarly, the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and a pointer to WIPO literature, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that the retirement mode reflects an old portfolio rather than current choices.

value_domain: Deferred GST on imported goods, activity statement label 7A (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Deferred GST scheme
variable_description: The GST on the business's imports that it deferred to its activity statement instead of paying at the border, reported at label 7A. The ATO explains the mechanism: "The DGST scheme allows the GST payable on taxable imports to be paid via your monthly business activity statement (BAS) rather than to the Australian Border Force (ABF) at the time of importation." It is a tax amount, roughly one eleventh of the taxable value of the imports, not the value of the goods themselves.

The amount is also usually claimed straight back at label 1B, so it is cash-neutral and must not be read as a cost or a tax burden.

value_domain: Count of distinct employees paid in the calendar month
value_source: ATO, What STP is (Single Touch Payroll)
variable_description: How many distinct people the employer paid during the calendar month, counted from its Single Touch Payroll reports. STP is real-time payroll reporting: "With STP you report employees' payroll information to us each time you pay them through STP-enabled software", so the count is assembled from pay events rather than from an annual return. It is a headcount of payees, which is the only employment measure in BLADE available at monthly frequency.
value_definition: A non-negative integer for one calendar month, counting distinct payees rather than jobs, hours or full-time equivalents.
limitation: It cannot distinguish a casual paid once from a full-time employee, so a month with heavy casual turnover looks larger than a month with the same wage bill on permanent staff, and headcount will move without any change in labour input. Coverage also begins with the STP rollout, which the ATO dates to "1 July 2018 for employers with 20 or more employees and 1 July 2019 for employers with 19 or fewer employees", so earlier months carry no payee count even where the BLADE module is listed as starting in 2001-02.
rationale: The ATO page defines what STP reporting is, when it happens and when each employer size class was brought in, which fixes both the meaning of the count and the period over which it exists.
evidence_quote: STP started on 1 July 2018 for employers with 20 or more employees and 1 July 2019 for employers with 19 or fewer employees and is a mandatory obligation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the count is a headcount of payees or that it starts with the STP phase-in.

value_domain: Date a variation to a federal enterprise agreement takes effect
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The day a variation to a federal enterprise agreement starts to operate, which is not the day it was agreed, lodged or approved. DEWR records the database's span as "wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997", so a variation date sits inside the life of an agreement already on file. One agreement can be varied several times, so a business can carry several of these dates.
value_definition: A calendar date written dd/mm/yyyy, one row per variation rather than one per agreement.
limitation: The date alone does not say what changed. A pay rise, a change to shift arrangements and a technical correction all stamp this one field, so the variation has to be read against the agreement's own conditions items. WAD also covers federal enterprise agreements only, so award-reliant and individually contracted workplaces never generate a variation date at all.
rationale: The DEWR page is the custodian's description of the database this column comes from, giving its coverage, what it records about each agreement and that variations are tracked alongside agreements.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished the effect date from the approval date or noted the federal-only coverage.

value_domain: Deidentified Customs Client Identifier
value_source: ABS, Characteristics of Australian Importers methodology, 2020-21
variable_description: A deidentified Customs Client Identifier, which is who the exporter was on the customs declaration when it did not quote an ABN. The ABS defines it as "a unique identifier, administered by ABF, to represent importing persons and organisations that do not report an ABN", and the same registration system covers exporters. It is the fallback identity on a trade record, so its presence marks a party that Australian Border Force could not tie to the business register.
value_definition: A 10-digit alphanumeric identifier, deidentified for BLADE, with 9999999999 meaning unknown.
limitation: A row keyed on this identifier cannot be joined to the BLADE business spine: the ABS states that "CCIDs, which cannot be linked to the ABSBR, are treated as statistical units", so trade attributed to a CCID is missing from any ABN-based firm analysis and will look like a hole in industry or size aggregates. A single entity can also hold both an ABN and a CCID, so counting distinct identifiers overcounts traders.
rationale: The ABS methodology for a BLADE-based trade release defines the Customs Client Identifier, explains why it exists and states that it cannot be linked to the business register, which is the decisive fact about this column.
evidence_quote: CCIDs, which cannot be linked to the ABSBR, are treated as statistical units.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviation as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what a CCID is or that it does not link to the business spine.

value_domain: ABS internal integration version reference
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Which build of the ABS Dealroom integration produced the row, a processing marker rather than a fact about the business. Dealroom is a commercial database of startup and venture activity that the Department of Industry, Science and Resources brings into BLADE, and the ABS lists it as a requestable module for 2025 only. Use this column to tell two extracts apart, not to describe a firm.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string following an internal ABS naming convention, of the form shown in the data item list as an integration reference. No code list is published.
limitation: It carries no information about the business, so a change in the string between two files is a change in ABS processing, not a change in the firm. Because BLADE holds Dealroom for a single reference year, the version cannot be used as a time dimension either.
rationale: The BLADE data page confirms Dealroom is a requestable BLADE module and gives its single-year coverage, which bounds what a version marker on those rows can mean; the ABS does not publish the internal version convention.
evidence_quote: Dealroom: 2025
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's parenthetical note and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said the field is a processing marker with no business content.

value_domain: Date an intellectual property right or application is deemed no longer in force
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The date from which IP Australia treats a right or application as no longer in force, on the IPRAPID applications table. IP Australia uses retirement as the general term for a right leaving the live register, and treats it as one of the two flows that move a holder's enforceable stock: "Retired - rights retired during the financial year". The word deemed matters, because the date is set by rule rather than by an event on the day.
value_definition: A calendar date written dd/mm/yyyy, applying to one application or right rather than to the applicant.
limitation: It is backdated. When a lapse is recognised later, for example after renewal fees stop, the deemed date is the day protection is treated as having ended, which can be well before the register was updated, so it cannot be used to date the administrative decision. It also does not distinguish a deliberate abandonment from expiry at the end of the maximum term, and it is never a date about the business, only about the right.
rationale: The IP Australia data dictionary for the sister longitudinal product defines retirement of a right and its place in the lifecycle, which is the concept this IPRAPID column dates; IP Australia does not publish a column-level dictionary for IPRAPID.
evidence_quote: Retired - rights retired during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never explained that a deemed date is backdated and set by rule.

value_domain: Diversified company indicator
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Whether the Department of Industry, Science and Resources classed the company as diversified rather than concentrated on a single emerging industry. It sits in the Emerging Industries module, which the ABS lists as a requestable BLADE addition for 2024-25 alone. The flag is an assessment made by the department for its own industry programmes, not a derivation from ANZSIC or from turnover by product.
value_definition: An indicator whose only documented value is YES, so the affirmative case is populated and everything else is blank or absent. No negative code and no full code list is published.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as not diversified, because it is equally consistent with never assessed, and any regression that treats missing as zero will attribute the department's coverage decisions to the firms. With a single reference year in BLADE there is also nothing to compare against, so the flag cannot support a before-and-after design.
rationale: The BLADE data page confirms Emerging Industries is a departmental module in BLADE and gives its single-year coverage, which bounds what the flag can support; the department does not publish the diversification criterion.
evidence_quote: Emerging Industries: 2024-25
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's question wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that only the affirmative value is documented.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains the business made on non-active assets under the indexation method, measured after capital losses have been applied. The old CGT schedule reaches this figure in a part headed "Part E Current year capital gains (CYCG) after applying capital losses", where non-active assets occupy the first row and the indexation method the first column. The ATO restricts that method to "capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999", so the column follows a closing stock of pre-1999 assets. Non-active means the gain does not qualify for the small business concessions, either because the asset is not used in the business or because the entity is not entitled.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label A of the schedule, a flow over the income year. It is struck after current year and prior year capital losses but before the CGT discount at Part F and the small business concessions at Part G.
limitation: The schedule dropped Part E after 2011-12, so the column stops rather than falls to zero and a series that spans the change is not continuous. Nor can the figure be read as a share of gains: an entity that chose the discount method for an eligible pre-1999 asset reports nothing here for that asset even though indexation was available.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the row and column headings of Part E of the pre-2013 CGT schedule, and the variable prefix e_ matches that part. The form itself carries the wording, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define the indexation method.
evidence_quote: Part E Current year capital gains (CYCG) after applying capital losses
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets worked out under the CGT discount method, after capital losses have been applied. It is the second column of the non-active row in Part E of the old CGT schedule, sitting beside the indexation and other-method columns for the same assets. The discount method covers assets owned at least twelve months, and the ATO notes that it "does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies", so for most BLADE units the column is structurally empty.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label B, gross of the discount itself: the schedule applies the discount percentage later, at Part F, so this figure is the full gain and not the halved one.
limitation: A zero does not mean the firm made no long-held gains. A company reports all of them in the indexation and other columns because it cannot use the discount at all, so the column mainly separates trusts, funds and life companies from ordinary companies rather than measuring holding periods.
rationale: The DIL label is the non-active discount-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions state which entities may use the discount method.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets that fall under neither the indexation nor the discount method, after capital losses. The ATO defines the residual as the "'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)", which in practice means assets bought after 21 September 1999 and sold within twelve months, plus every gain of a company that cannot use the discount. For an ordinary trading company this is normally the largest of the three non-active columns in Part E.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label C, a flow over the income year, carrying no concession or discount of any kind: the other method is the full gain with no reduction applied at any later part.
limitation: Two different situations collapse into this one figure - a short-held asset and a company that is simply barred from the discount - and nothing on the row separates them, so the column cannot be used as evidence of short holding periods or asset churn.
rationale: The DIL label is the non-active other-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define the other method as the residual of the three.
evidence_quote: 'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: Capital gains on the firm's active assets under the other method, after capital losses, and only where a small business concession applies. Active assets are the ones used in running the business: "Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business)". The active columns are narrower than that, though, because the ATO says to include a gain there only if it "qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions" - the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label F, a flow over the income year, struck after losses but before the concessions at Part G that are the reason the gain was put in the active column in the first place.
limitation: It is not a measure of business asset disposals. A firm too large for the concessions reports the sale of its own goodwill in the non-active columns instead, and a gain covered by the 15-year exemption never reaches Part E at all, so the column tracks concession entitlement more than it tracks what was sold.
rationale: The DIL label is the active-asset other-method cell of Part E, and the ATO CGT schedule instructions define an active asset and restrict what may be shown in the active columns.
evidence_quote: At Active assets in the CGT summary worksheet (and the CGT schedule), you should only include a capital gain from an active asset that qualifies for one or more of the following 3 small business CGT concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's indexation-method capital gains left standing after capital losses, active and non-active added together. The schedule computes it rather than collecting it: "Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below." It is the indexation-method entry point into the final calculation, since Part H subtracts the discount and concession totals from exactly this figure to reach the net capital gain.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label G, equal to the non-active and active indexation cells on the same row. It is a derived total, so it carries the rounding and the reporting errors of both components.
limitation: Adding G, H and I does not give the net capital gain: the CGT discount and the small business concessions are still to come off at Parts F to H, and only after that does an amount reach the return. The total also cannot be split back into active and non-active if the component columns are missing.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the totals row of Part E, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines the cell.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's discount-method capital gains surviving capital losses, active and non-active combined. The schedule builds it by addition: "Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below." This is the only one of the three totals that then meets the CGT discount, which Part F applies separately to the non-active and active parts of it.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label H, equal to the non-active and active discount cells on the same row, and still gross of the discount percentage itself.
limitation: For a company the total is normally zero because the discount is closed to companies, so a cross-entity comparison of this column measures legal form rather than investment behaviour. It is also not the amount that will be taxed: the discount comes off afterwards.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the discount-method cell of the Part E totals row, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines it.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), Part E
variable_description: All of the firm's other-method capital gains surviving capital losses, active and non-active combined. The schedule sets it out as an addition: "Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below." For a company this is usually the largest of the three totals, because a company cannot use the discount and few of its assets predate September 1999.
value_definition: Whole dollars at Part E label I, equal to the non-active and active other-method cells on the same row, and reduced only by capital losses.
limitation: The column ends with the old form after 2011-12, and the replacement schedule records a single current year capital gain with no method split, so a firm's other-method total cannot be reconstructed for later years and a break in the series is a form change, not a change in behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the other-capital-gains cell of the Part E totals row, and the schedule prints the addition rule that defines it.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which part of the CGT schedule the column comes from or that the part no longer exists.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
variable_description: The first day this intellectual property right was filed anywhere in the world, which need not be the day IP Australia saw the file. It differs from application_date on the same row whenever the right reached Australia through an international route: a Patent Cooperation Treaty case or a Madrid Protocol trade mark is filed abroad first and arrives in Australia months or years later. For firm-level work it is the better date for asking when a business first sought protection, and the worse date for asking when it engaged with the Australian system.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, drawn from IP Australia's rights registers, which IPGOD publishes as the open version of the same data. The domain is open and runs back over a century of registry records.
limitation: It is not the priority date and it is not evidence of invention. A filing can claim priority from an earlier application that is itself not in this table, and a firm that files a provisional and then abandons it leaves a filing date attached to a right that never existed.
rationale: IPRAPID is IP Australia's own analytical product built on the rights registers that IPGOD releases publicly, so the IPGOD collection and its data dictionary are the authority for the filing dates the registers hold.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never distinguished this date from the three other dates on the same row.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
variable_description: The day from which the firm could actually sue on this right, as opposed to the day it was granted. IP Australia backdates protection: a granted patent and a registered trade mark are enforceable from the filing date, so this field usually sits well before gained_registration_status_date and gained_enforceable_status_date on the same row. It is the date to use when asking from when a competitor was excluded, and it is the anchor for the term of the right.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY. It is populated only for rights that reached a protected status, so it is missing by design for applications that lapsed, were withdrawn or were refused.
limitation: A right being enforceable from a date does not mean it was enforceable on that date. Protection is conferred retrospectively when the right is granted, so at any point between filing and grant the register showed no enforceable right at all, and using this field to date market power will overstate how early the firm held it.
rationale: IPRAPID is built on IP Australia's rights registers, which IPGOD releases publicly with a data dictionary covering the status and date fields of each right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said that the date is backdated or how it relates to the registration date beside it.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
variable_description: The day a party - an applicant, owner, agent or inventor - took up its role on this IP right. The Party table holds one row per party per role, so this date opens an episode and effective_to_date closes it; a change of owner after an assignment or an acquisition shows up as a new row starting here rather than as an edit to the old one. It is what makes it possible to attribute a patent or trade mark to the firm that held it at a given moment rather than to whoever holds it now.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, one per party-role episode. Read with party_role and party_role_category, which say what the party was doing, and with is_founding, which marks the earliest party in that role.
limitation: It dates the record, not the transaction. A party change takes effect at IP Australia only when it is notified, so an assignment recorded late will place the transfer after the commercial deal, and an unnotified change never appears at all.
rationale: The IPRAPID Party table mirrors the party and ownership records IP Australia keeps for each right, which IPGOD publishes with a data dictionary for the party tables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the field opens an episode in an ownership history.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Government Open Data (IPGOD)
variable_description: The day a party stopped holding its role on this IP right, closing the episode that effective_from_date opened. A populated value marks a hand-over - an assignment of ownership, a change of attorney, the death of the right itself - while a missing value means the party was still in the role when the extract was taken, which is what p_is_current on the same row records.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, or empty for an open episode. Emptiness is meaningful here and should not be recoded to a far-future date without saying so.
limitation: An open end date is a statement about the extract, not about the future, so a panel built at one vintage will show ownership continuing past dates when it had in fact ended. The field also cannot distinguish an owner who sold the right from one whose right simply expired.
rationale: The IPRAPID Party table mirrors IP Australia's party records, released publicly through IPGOD with a data dictionary for each party table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained what a missing end date means.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Total allowances the employer paid its workers over the month, on top of ordinary wages. The ATO defines allowances as "payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses" and keeps them out of the wages figure: "You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments." The row is one ABN and branch in one month, so this is the sum across every payee reported in that month.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, aggregated by the ABS from the year-to-date allowance amounts employers report for each payee through STP.
limitation: It does not say which allowances. A tool allowance, a car allowance and a shift allowance land in one figure, and a living-away-from-home allowance is excluded entirely, so the column cannot be read as the cost of any particular working condition.
rationale: The BLADE field is the STP carry-over of the payment summary's total allowances field, and the ATO instruction for that field defines what an allowance is and how it sits against gross payments.
evidence_quote: Allowances are payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out as lump sum A, which the ATO limits to older accruals and to leave paid alongside a redundancy. Its instruction covers "unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", unused holiday pay accrued before 18 August 1993, and post-1993 leave paid in connection with a genuine redundancy, an early retirement scheme or an invalidity segment. In an employer-month total a non-zero value is a marker of separations rather than of ordinary pay, and it is deliberately excluded from the gross payments column.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees. Lump sum A carries a type code of R for redundancy or T for any other reason on the payment summary; the code is not in this table, only the amount.
limitation: It cannot separate a redundancy from an ordinary resignation, because the distinguishing type code is absent. Leave accrued after 17 August 1993 and paid on an ordinary resignation goes into gross payments instead, so the column understates leave paid out on separation.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum A box carried into STP from the individual non-business payment summary, and the ATO instruction for that box lists exactly which payments belong in it.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused long service leave from before 16 August 1978, paid out during the month. The ATO reserves the box for "amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978", and it is separated from lump sum A because only a small fraction of it is assessable to the worker. In an employer-month row a non-zero value marks the departure of someone whose service reaches back nearly fifty years.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across the employer's payees, and reported outside gross payments like the other lump sums.
limitation: The column is close to structurally empty and shrinking as pre-1978 service leaves the workforce, so a zero says nothing about how much long service leave the firm paid out; almost all of it will be in the lump sum A column or in gross payments.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum B box of the payment summary carried into STP, and the ATO instruction defines the accrual period that qualifies.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax-free part of genuine redundancy and early retirement scheme payments the employer made in the month, despite a field name that suggests leave. The ATO defines lump sum D as "the tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", so it is the closest thing in this table to a direct redundancy signal: it exists only where the redundancy conditions are met. It is the one lump sum the ATO leaves out of the employer's gross payments total.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees. The tax-free component is capped by a base amount plus a per-year-of-service amount that the ATO resets each income year.
limitation: Because of that cap the figure tracks the number of redundancies and the length of service far better than the money the departing workers received; anything above the cap becomes an employment termination payment and is reported outside this column.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum D box carried into STP from the payment summary, and the ATO instruction gives its definition in one sentence.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done in earlier years, paid out during the month and reported as lump sum E. The ATO defines it as "amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments", which is why it is taken out of ordinary wages: the worker is taxed on it with an offset that recognises it belongs to another year. A spike in an employer-month is usually a settlement, a back-dated agreement or a correction of underpaid wages.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across payees, and excluded from the gross payments column on the same row.
limitation: It cannot date the work it pays for. One lump sum E can cover several past years at once, so using the column to reconstruct historical wage bills, or to date when an underpayment happened, will put the money in the wrong year.
rationale: The BLADE field is the lump sum E box of the payment summary carried into STP, and the ATO instruction defines which payments belong there.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Gross pay the employer reported under the foreign employment income stream, earned by Australian tax residents working overseas. The ATO describes the income type as telling it about "the income an Australian tax resident has earned while working overseas where the qualifying period for foreign employment income is met", and instructs that it be used only where tax was withheld in the foreign country. A non-zero value therefore identifies a firm with staff posted abroad under a foreign tax obligation.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, summed across the employer's payees and reported apart from the ordinary salary and wages gross column.
limitation: It is not a count of overseas postings. Where no foreign tax is withheld the ATO directs the same worker's pay to the ordinary salary and wages stream, so the column sees only the postings that attracted foreign withholding and misses staff sent to countries that did not tax them.
