value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: A withholding amount that is narrower than the total PAYG withholding column sitting beside it on the same row. Because the row already carries an employer total, this second column is best read as withholding attached to one part of the payroll rather than to the firm as a whole, most likely the ordinary salary and wages stream. The item list gives only the word withheld and does not say which part.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, aggregated for one ABN and branch, and expressed on the same basis as the total PAYG withholding column.
limitation: Do not add it to the total PAYG withholding column, and do not use it as the firm's withholding. Compare the two columns across many rows first: if one is always the smaller, it is a component of the other and the difference is what the named income streams withheld.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instruction establishes that total tax withheld is a single employer-level figure, which is what the neighbouring column holds; the item list does not define this second withholding field.
evidence_quote: Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported through Single Touch Payroll
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: The second working holiday maker amount on the row, pairing with the working holiday maker gross column and reading as the tax withheld from backpacker pay. Registered working holiday maker employers withhold at a concessional flat rate on the first band of a backpacker's earnings, so the ratio between these two columns is both a check on the reading and a way of telling registered employers from unregistered ones. The item list gives only the word total.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a flow over the reference month, aggregated across the backpackers on the employer's books that month and reported apart from ordinary wages withholding.
limitation: The implied rate mixes registered and unregistered employers, who withhold at very different rates, and it mixes workers above and below the concessional threshold, so a firm-level ratio cannot be read as a tax rate on any individual backpacker.
rationale: The ATO income types page establishes the working holiday maker stream and that its pay is taxed differently; the two-amount structure comes from the payment summaries STP carried over, but the item list does not name this field.
evidence_quote: the employee's income may be taxed differently (such as for working holiday makers)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name as its whole description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the amount covers or that the row is an employer-month rather than a person.

value_domain: Deidentified customs export declaration number
value_source: Australian Border Force, Export declaration
variable_description: The customs export declaration that this shipment line belongs to, deidentified - one declaration is one consignment from one consignor to one consignee. The Australian Border Force sets the rule directly: "You should lodge one export declaration for each consignment of goods that you export. A consignment for the purposes of an export declaration is defined as goods sent from one consignor to one consignee." Rows sharing an EDN are commodity lines on the same declaration, which is why the table also carries a transaction identifier for the individual line.
value_definition: A ten character alphanumeric code, deidentified for BLADE. It is issued by the Department of Home Affairs when a declaration is accepted, and is not a business identifier: the exporting business is on the same row as bn.
limitation: It is neither a shipment nor a firm. Goods worth less than AUD2,000 need no declaration at all, so small consignments never generate one; and a declaration may be lodged up to six months before the goods leave, so the number cannot date the departure.
rationale: The Australian Border Force page for the export declaration defines what a declaration covers, when it is lodged and what it is issued against, which is what the deidentified number stands for.
evidence_quote: You should lodge one export declaration for each consignment of goods that you export.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase and the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so it never said what a declaration covers or that rows share one.

value_domain: Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: ASIC, How to interpret ASIC's corporate insolvency statistics
variable_description: The day the insolvency appointment over this company took effect, which is the closest thing in BLADE to a dated corporate failure. ASIC's own description of the underlying records lists the "start date of the appointment and relevant financial year" among the details it holds for all external administration and controller appointments. Read it with appointment_type on the same row, because a company can hold more than one appointment and can move between them, and each brings its own effective date.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, one per appointment rather than one per company, drawn from the form lodgements behind ASIC's Series 1 and Series 2 statistics.
limitation: It is not the day the business stopped trading, and the column is not a full record of company exits: ASIC's series "exclude members' voluntary liquidations", which are solvent wind-ups, and a company that simply deregisters without an administrator never generates a row at all.
rationale: ASIC publishes what its insolvency series contain, what the raw appointment records hold and what they exclude, which is exactly the ambiguity a reader of a bare appointment date faces.
evidence_quote: Series 1 and 2 statistics exclude members' voluntary liquidations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase 'Effective date of insolvency appointment' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that there can be several appointments per company or what the series leaves out.

value_domain: Binary indicator (0 = no, 1 = yes)
value_source: Austrade, What's changed in the Export Market Development Grant (EMDG) program
variable_description: Marks a financial year in which the business had qualifying expenditure behind a successful grant under the original EMDG reimbursement scheme. Under that scheme a firm spent its own money on export marketing first and claimed part of it back afterwards, which Austrade describes as the arrangement it left behind: "In 2021-22, the EMDG program shifted from a reimbursement scheme to an eligibility-based, demand-driven program." The flag therefore identifies exporters who were already spending, not firms that were given money to start.
value_definition: A binary flag on the entity-by-financial-year panel: 1 where the entity had qualifying expenditure for a successful EMDG1 application in that year, 0 otherwise.
limitation: The year is the year of the qualifying expenditure, not of the payment, so pairing this flag with a cash amount in the same year will misalign the two by up to a year; and the scheme is closed, so the flag stops being available rather than falling to zero.
rationale: Austrade's page on what changed states that the program was a reimbursement scheme until 2021-22, which is what distinguishes EMDG1 from the EMDG2 flag beside it.
evidence_quote: In 2021-22, the EMDG program shifted from a reimbursement scheme to an eligibility-based, demand-driven program.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Binary indicator (0 = no, 1 = yes)
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: Marks a financial year in which the business had qualifying expenditure behind a successful grant under the redesigned EMDG program that began in 2021-22. The redesign replaced claiming back past spending with a forward grant agreement in one of three tiers, so an EMDG2 year says the firm entered an agreement with Austrade and committed to future marketing activity. Where emdg1 marks a firm reimbursed for what it had already done, emdg2 marks a firm funded for what it intended to do.
value_definition: A binary flag on the entity-by-financial-year panel: 1 where the entity had qualifying expenditure for a successful EMDG2 application in that year, 0 otherwise. It runs from 2021-22 and overlaps the closing years of the EMDG1 flag.
limitation: The two flags are not two versions of the same treatment, so pooling them creates a treated group with two different mechanisms and two different selection rules; a firm can carry both in the overlap years.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG page describes the current program, its tiers and its grant agreement structure, which is what the EMDG2 flag records participation in.
evidence_quote: The EMDG program provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: EMDG grant tier assessed by Austrade
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: Which tier of the redesigned EMDG program Austrade assessed the business into, which is a statement about its export maturity. Austrade sets the tiers out as "Tier 1 - small and medium enterprises ready to export", "Tier 2 - small and medium enterprises exporting within existing markets", "Tier 3 - small and medium enterprises exporting to new key markets", and representative bodies that support member businesses. The item list is explicit that this is the assessed tier and not necessarily the tier the applicant asked for.
value_definition: A short character code taking Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, Rep Body, or blank where the entity has no EMDG2 grant in the year. It applies to the EMDG2 program only.
limitation: The tier is an administrative judgement about readiness, not a measured export status, and it is capped by rule rather than by the firm: a business may hold Tier 1 for only two years and Tier 2 for only four, so a move up the tiers can be a time limit expiring rather than a business advancing.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG program page defines each tier in its own words, which is what the assessed tier code records.
evidence_quote: Tier 2 - small and medium enterprises exporting within existing markets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Dollar amount of grant approved
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: The grant Austrade agreed to give the business for the financial year, which is a commitment rather than a payment. Under the current program the grant agreement fixes the total available amount per year in advance, which is the change Austrade made so that businesses "will know how much they will receive over the life of their grant agreement". It is the natural denominator for the amount received column beside it.
value_definition: Whole dollars for one entity in one financial year, set by the grant agreement or, under the older scheme, by the assessment of the claim.
limitation: An approved amount is not money that moved. Payments are released against milestone reports and a grantee that does not spend or does not report keeps an approval it never draws, so approved minus received is a real and common gap rather than a data error.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG page and its account of the program changes establish that grant amounts are set in advance in an agreement and paid separately, which is the distinction the approved and received columns carry.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Dollar amount of grant paid
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: The grant money that actually reached the business in the financial year. Under the current program some of it can arrive before the activity happens - Austrade notes grantees "may receive some of their grant at the start of the grant year, before they begin their grant activity" - while the rest follows milestone reports. This, not the approved column, is the cash a firm had to spend.
value_definition: Whole dollars received by one entity in one financial year, which may be a part payment against a larger approved amount and may relate to activity in a different year.
limitation: It cannot be matched to the activity it funded. Payments run ahead of and behind the marketing they support, so lining this column up against the same year's exports will attribute effects to the wrong period.
rationale: Austrade's page on the program changes describes when grant money is paid relative to the activity, which is what separates the received amount from the approved amount.
evidence_quote: They may receive some of their grant at the start of the grant year, before they begin their grant activity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Grant identifier issued by Austrade
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: Identifies the particular EMDG grant behind the row, across both the old reimbursement scheme and the current program. It is a grant key, not a business key: the entity is identified by bn on the same row, and a business with several grants over the years carries several of these numbers. It is what allows the approved, received, expenditure and tier columns to be tied to one grant rather than to a firm-year in general.
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned by Austrade to a grant. The domain is open and the numbering spans both the EMDG1 and EMDG2 programs, so the number itself does not say which scheme applied.
limitation: It is not a stable panel key. Numbers issued under the two schemes are drawn from the same field with no scheme indicator, so a jump in the number does not mean a new firm and the same firm's grants cannot be ordered by it reliably; use the emdg1 and emdg2 flags to tell the schemes apart.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG page establishes that grants are made under agreements to individual entities, which is what a grant number identifies; the numbering scheme itself is not published.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Binary indicator (0 = no, 1 = yes)
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: Marks the entity as an industry representative body rather than an exporting business. Austrade funds these separately from the enterprise tiers, describing them as "representative bodies - that support small and medium business members to achieve export success", so the grant pays for member services and not for the body's own exports. The flag matters because a representative body sitting undetected in a sample of grant recipients will look like an exporter with no exports.
value_definition: A binary flag on the entity-by-financial-year panel, covering representative bodies under either the EMDG1 or the EMDG2 program.
limitation: It says nothing about how many members the body has or which of them benefited, so the grant cannot be attributed to any business the money eventually helped; the beneficiaries are outside the row entirely.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG page lists representative bodies as one of the four things the program funds and says what they do, which is what the flag records.
evidence_quote: Representative bodies - that support small and medium business members to achieve export success.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: Dollar amount of expenditure related to the grant
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants (EMDG)
variable_description: What the business spent on the marketing, promotion or training the grant relates to, as opposed to what the grant paid. It is the base figure the two schemes work from in opposite directions: the old reimbursement scheme paid a share of expenditure already incurred, and the current program requires a firm to be able to spend its own money alongside the grant. Against the received amount it gives a rough co-contribution ratio for the firm.
value_definition: Whole dollars of expenditure attached to a grant in a financial year. It is expenditure the program recognised, not the firm's total marketing spend.
limitation: The rules defining eligible expenditure differ between the two schemes and changed within them, so comparing this column across the 2021-22 break measures a rule change as much as a spending change.
rationale: Austrade's EMDG pages describe the reimbursement basis of the old scheme and the own-money spending requirement of the current one, which bound what expenditure attached to a grant means.
evidence_quote: Capacity to spend at least $20,000 on marketing and promotional activities. This must be exclusive of the grant amount. It must be the applicant's own money.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Austrade field description alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing explained the two EMDG schemes or what the number can support.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Records which ABS integration run produced the emerging industries row, and says nothing about the business itself. It is the module's own vintage stamp, sitting alongside the same kind of stamp on every other BLADE module, and it changes when the ABS rebuilds the integration rather than when a firm changes. Use it to keep two extracts apart, not as a variable in an analysis.
value_definition: A short internal code of the form in260_v1, naming the integration and its version number. The domain is open and grows by one entry each time the module is rebuilt.
limitation: It cannot date the data. The version identifies the run, not the reference period of what the run produced, so two rows with different versions may describe the same year and two rows with the same version may not.
rationale: No public document describes this internal ABS field; the BLADE overview page is cited as the authority for the asset it belongs to, and the reading follows the pattern of the version stamps on the other BLADE modules.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned a reader off using the field as data.

value_domain: Emerging industry category in the DISR taxonomy
value_source: Glass.AI, The Australian Government (DISR) uses Glass.AI to research emerging industries
variable_description: Which of seven emerging industries the business has been placed in, on the basis of what its website says it does. The classification comes from the Department of Industry, Science and Resources work that combined web-scale text analysis with government microdata: Glass.AI describes the exercise as combining "web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata" to measure industries that standard classifications miss. The example value in the item list is Artificial Intelligence, and the row also carries whether the firm is core or peripheral to that industry.
value_definition: A character label naming one of seven emerging industries, alongside the finer theme, sector and sector_group fields on the same row. The full list of seven is not published with the item list.
limitation: It is not an ANZSIC industry and does not replace one: a firm classified into an emerging industry here also carries an ANZSIC code, and the two answer different questions. Because the classification is read off web text, a firm with a thin or dated website is invisible to it regardless of what it actually does.
rationale: Glass.AI's account of the DISR emerging industries database explains how the classification was built and what it was for, which is the method behind this field; the seven categories themselves are not published there.
evidence_quote: web-scale research algorithms with econometric methods and government microdata
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's question-shaped description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said where the classification comes from or that it is derived from web text.

value_domain: Count of employees covered by an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database dataset
variable_description: How many workers the enterprise agreement covered when it was lodged, which is the agreement's reach rather than the employer's size. The database records the "number of employees covered by agreement, including (where provided) a breakdown into" women, part time, casual, mature age, young, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, non-English-speaking background and employees with disability. It is coded from the agreement document and its lodgement papers, not from a payroll.
value_definition: A count of persons at the date of lodgement, one figure per agreement. The breakdown categories are coded only where the agreement or its papers supply them.
limitation: It is a headcount frozen on one day and never revised, so across a three or four year agreement it drifts from real employment; and an employee covered by two agreements is counted in both, so summing the column across agreements overstates coverage.
rationale: The DEWR introduction to the WAD dataset lists the employer detail fields and defines the employees field with the breakdown it can carry.
evidence_quote: Number of employees covered by agreement, including (where provided) a breakdown into
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line custodian description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so nothing said the count is fixed at lodgement or that it double counts across agreements.

value_domain: Coded agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Records that the enterprise agreement puts new employees on a probationary period, coded by reading the agreement text. The Workplace Agreements Database is a content database: departmental staff code the clauses of every federal agreement lodged, so a Y here means a probation clause was found in the document rather than that a firm has a probation practice. The item list is explicit that the field "should only be coded in agreements made prior to 1/1/2011".
value_definition: A single character taking Y for yes and otherwise left blank. There is no explicit N: absence is the second state, and it carries two very different meanings.
limitation: Coding stopped at 1 January 2011, so a blank in a later agreement means the clause was not looked for, not that there is no probation; the column therefore cannot be used to test whether probation clauses became more or less common over time.
rationale: The DEWR page for the Workplace Agreements Database establishes that the database codes the content of lodged federal agreements, which is what the flag records; the coding window comes from the item list itself.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never warned that a blank after 2011 is uncoded rather than negative.

value_domain: Percentage of salary contributed to superannuation
value_source: DEWR, Introduction to the Workplace Agreements Database dataset
variable_description: The superannuation contribution rate an agreement commits the employer to, where that rate differs from the legislated minimum. The database field is defined as covering an agreement that "states that the employer must pay a certain percentage of the employee's salary which is different [can be either lower or higher] than the superannuation guarantee ... as a superannuation contribution", and adds that "the percentage amount is recorded". It is one of the few agreement-level measures of superannuation above the floor.
value_definition: A number expressed as a percentage of salary. The value 111111111 is a dump code meaning the agreement varies the rate or the quantity could not be determined, not a rate.
limitation: The dump code must be removed before any average, since left in a single agreement will dominate the mean. The figure is also what the agreement promises, not what was paid, and a rate below the guarantee in the document does not lower the employer's statutory obligation.
rationale: The DEWR introduction to the WAD dataset defines this superannuation field in the same words the item list carries, and the dump code is documented with the field.
evidence_quote: The agreement states that the employer must pay a certain percentage of the employee's salary which is different [can be either lower or higher] than the superannuation guarantee
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing flagged the dump code that will wreck any average taken from the column.

value_domain: Coded agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Records that the agreement states employment security as a core principle, which is a commitment in the document rather than an observed employment outcome. Coders read each lodged federal agreement and mark the clause where it appears, so the field measures the language of bargaining. The item list restricts it to agreements "made prior to 1/1/2008", which makes it one of the shortest-lived fields in the database.
value_definition: A single character taking Y for yes and otherwise blank, coded from the agreement text for agreements made before 2008.
limitation: The seven-year gap between this field closing in 2008 and the rest of the database continuing means it cannot be used in any analysis spanning the global financial crisis; a blank from 2008 onwards is an uncoded field, and reading it as an absence of job security clauses will invent a decline that is purely administrative.
rationale: The DEWR page for the Workplace Agreements Database establishes that the database codes clause content from lodged federal agreements, which is the nature of this flag; the closing date comes from the item list.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the field stops in 2008.

value_domain: Deidentified ATO employer identifier
value_source: ATO, JobMaker Hiring Credit scheme
variable_description: The employer that registered and claimed under the JobMaker Hiring Credit, deidentified, and not necessarily the same unit as the ABN beside it on the row. JobMaker was a COVID-19 wage subsidy: "Eligible employers could access the JobMaker Hiring Credit for each eligible additional employee they hired between 7 October 2020 and 6 October 2021." The claim was made by the entity the ATO held as the employer, so this key is the one that ties the eight claim periods on the row together.
value_definition: A thirty character alphanumeric identifier, deidentified for BLADE. It is a claimant key rather than a business key: bn on the same row carries the deidentified ABN.
limitation: It cannot be used to count employers in the economy or to join to anything outside JobMaker. Only registered claimants have one at all, so absence means the firm did not claim, which is not the same as being ineligible or having hired nobody.
rationale: The ATO's JobMaker Hiring Credit page describes who could claim, over what window and on what basis, which is what an employer identifier in this table stands for.
evidence_quote: Eligible employers could access the JobMaker Hiring Credit for each eligible additional employee they hired between 7 October 2020 and 6 October 2021.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Deidentified emplr_id' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never distinguished the claimant from the ABN on the same row.

value_domain: Collapsed state and territory grouping for funded agencies
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Where a funded family violence agency operates, expressed as one collapsed geography for the whole organisation rather than as an address. The codes mix a national category with single jurisdictions and one pairing: national and multi-state presence, ACT and NSW together, then NT, SA, QLD, VIC, TAS and WA separately. It describes the service footprint of the funded body, not the place any client was helped.
value_definition: A single character code from 1 to 8, where 1 is a national or multi-state presence and 2 to 8 are jurisdictions with ACT and NSW sharing code 2.
limitation: It cannot be crossed with state-level data. ACT and NSW are inseparable, a national provider has no state at all, and a multi-state agency's activity in any one jurisdiction is invisible, so counts of agencies by state built from this field will be wrong in both directions.
rationale: No public documentation of the National Family Violence Funded Agencies collection could be found, so the reading rests on the code labels in the item list; the BLADE overview page is cited as the authority for the asset the table sits in.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's field name as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the geography is collapsed and cannot be used as a state variable.

value_domain: Service type grouping for funded family violence agencies
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: What kind of family violence service the funded agency provides, in three broad groups. The first gathers the direct response services - crisis intervention, case management, emergency accommodation, victim survivor support, advocacy and counselling; the second is services for First Nations people and multicultural communities; the third is everything else. It sits under the coarser entity_organisation_type on the same row.
value_definition: A single character code taking 1, 2 or 3, one per funded agency rather than one per service delivered.
limitation: The groups are not mutually exclusive in practice, so an agency running crisis accommodation specifically for First Nations clients has to be forced into one of them, and which one it lands in is a coding decision rather than a fact about the service. Category 3 is a residual that absorbs whatever the first two do not describe.
rationale: No public documentation of this collection could be found, so the reading rests on the category labels in the item list; the BLADE overview page is cited as the authority for the asset that carries the table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's field name as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never spelled out what the three groups contain.

value_domain: Two-way flag for a specialist against a non-specialist family violence funded agency
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Whether the funded agency on this row is a specialist family violence organisation or a general service provider that also delivers funded family violence work. It is an attribute of the funded organisation rather than of a client or a service event, so it splits the funded agency population into the two groups that dominate family violence service delivery. Read it as a characteristic of the whole funding relationship, not of a particular year's activity, unless a year column on the same row says otherwise.
value_definition: A one-character code taking 1 for a specialist organisation and 2 for a non-specialist organisation, with no third category and no separate missing code documented in the data item list.
limitation: It does not say what the agency actually does. A generalist community or health provider coded 2 may deliver most of the family violence hours in its region, and a specialist coded 1 may be very small, so the flag carries no information about scale, caseload or service type.
rationale: No published dictionary for the National Family Violence Funded Agencies collection could be fetched, so the meaning is read from the code labels in the BLADE data item list and from the standard specialist against non-specialist split used across Australian family and domestic violence service reporting.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, 'Entity Organisation Type', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the unit is a funded agency rather than a client.

value_domain: Lodging entity type on the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: Which kind of taxpayer lodged the capital gains tax schedule this row comes from, which decides what concessions the rest of the row can contain. The distinction is not cosmetic: the ATO states that "Companies can't claim the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business", and that the discount rate is "33 1/3% for complying superannuation entities" and "50% for individuals and trusts". In BLADE the business-relevant codes are C for company, S for superannuation fund and T for trust; an I row is an individual, typically a sole trader.
value_definition: A single character: C company, I individual, S super fund, T trust. Anything else is recorded as an invalid or absent response rather than as a further entity category.
limitation: It is the lodging entity on the schedule, not the legal form of the operating business. A family business run through a trust with a corporate trustee produces T rows, and a sole trader's business and private asset disposals both land in an I row, so the code cannot be used on its own to classify the firm.
rationale: The CGT schedule instructions set out which returns the schedule attaches to (company, trust, fund and self-managed super fund returns) and make the discount entitlement depend on the entity type, which is exactly what this column selects.
evidence_quote: Companies can't claim the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label 'Entity Type' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why the entity type changes how the rest of the schedule reads.

value_domain: Dollar amount from the capital gains tax schedule, non-active assets under the discount method on the old form and total CGT discount on the new form
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: A dollar figure whose meaning changed with the schedule: discount-method gains on non-active assets on the old form, the total CGT discount on the new. The old-form split exists only for the small business concessions - "You'll only need to differentiate your capital gains between active and non-active assets if you're going to apply the small business concessions" - so a non-zero old-form figure marks the gains that are outside the concession pool. The new-form quantity is a reduction rather than a gain, at "33 1/3% for complying superannuation entities" and "50% for individuals and trusts".

value_domain: Nominal expiry date of the enterprise agreement (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Nominal expiry date
variable_description: The date the enterprise agreement covering this employer nominally expires, which is when bargaining may reopen rather than when the agreement stops applying. The Fair Work Commission is explicit that "Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated by the Commission", and that the old terms "are fully enforceable and must be applied, even if the nominal expiry date was several years before". For a firm it therefore marks the earliest date a wage bargain can be reopened, not the end of the wage bargain.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY. Under the Fair Work Act the nominal expiry date can be at most four years after the Commission approves the agreement, so the value is bounded relative to the approval date on the same record.
limitation: A past expiry date does not mean the agreement is gone. Treating an expired agreement as no longer covering the firm overstates how often employers move off agreements, since many operate for years past nominal expiry.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page defines the nominal expiry date and states what happens after it, which is the fact that decides how this column should be read for a firm.
evidence_quote: Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated by the Commission.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would take nominal expiry for the end of the agreement.

value_domain: Flag for an enterprise agreement operating in Australia's external territories
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework

It sits with the state and territory coverage fields, which the collection framework records as "State/Territories coverage", and separates agreements whose geographic reach goes beyond the states and mainland territories. A 1 marks a very small group of employers, so it is more useful as an exclusion than as a population.

value_domain: Count of female employees covered by the enterprise agreement at lodgement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework

It is a point-in-time stock at lodgement, not an average over the agreement's life.

value_domain: Flag for an agreement restricting the use of fixed-term employment

The item is coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2010, so it is a historical field rather than a current one.

value_domain: Flag for an individual flexibility term allowing the whole agreement to be varied
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework

value_domain: Export sales reported at BAS label G2 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Completing your BAS for GST: Step 1 Sales
variable_description: The value of GST-free export sales the business reported on its activity statement at label G2 for the period. The ATO requires that "At G2 you need to report the free-on-board value of export goods (that is, the value used for Home Affairs purposes)" where the sale is GST-free, and that "All amounts reported at G2 should also have been reported at G1", so it is a component of total sales rather than an addition to them. For a firm it is the closest thing in the BAS to a self-reported export turnover, available at the same frequency as the statement.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the activity statement period, on a free on board basis and excluding the freight and insurance amounts reported separately at G3.
limitation: It is not the firm's exports. Only goods exported within the 60-day GST-free rule belong at G2, services and other GST-free international supplies do not, and quarterly reporters can straddle a shipment across periods, so a G2 series will diverge from the same firm's customs export declarations.
rationale: The ATO instruction for completing the BAS defines exactly what belongs at label G2, on what valuation basis, and how it relates to G1 and G3.
evidence_quote: At G2 you need to report the free-on-board value of export goods (that is, the value used for Home Affairs purposes) if the export sale is GST-free
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, 'Export sales*', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is also inside G1 or that only goods qualify.

value_domain: De-identified farm business unit identifier in the Farm Level Analytical Dataset
value_source: ABARES, Agricultural Data Integration Project
variable_description: The de-identified key for a farm business in the Farm Level Analytical Dataset, which is what makes a farm followable across agricultural collections. ABARES describes FLAD as combining "farm-level micro-data from all ABS Agricultural surveys and census' undertaken between 2000-01 and 2017-18", and says the dataset "was integrated with the BLADE for the period 2005-06 to 2016-17, predominantly through simple matching of Australian Business Numbers (ABNs)". So this identifier is the agricultural spine, and the ABN is the bridge to the tax and business columns.
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier, opaque by construction and unique to a farm business within FLAD.
limitation: It is not the BLADE business identifier and does not join directly to the tax tables; the link runs through the ABN match, which fails for farms whose ABN changed or was never held. A farm that restructures can also acquire a new identifier and appear as an exit and an entry.
rationale: The ABARES project page is the custodian's description of the dataset this control table belongs to, and states both what FLAD covers and how it reaches BLADE.
evidence_quote: For this project FLAD was integrated with the BLADE for the period 2005-06 to 2016-17, predominantly through simple matching of Australian Business Numbers (ABNs).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, 'De-identified Ag unit', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said how the farm unit reaches the rest of BLADE.

value_domain: Australian financial year, four-digit year of the ending June (YYYY)
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: The Australian financial year this IPLORD row describes, written as the calendar year in which the year ends, so 2016 means 2015-16. It is the panel dimension of the Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data, which the ABS lists in BLADE as "Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD): 2001-02 to latest available". Because IP events are dated by day but firms are observed by financial year, this column is what puts a filing or a grant into the same period as the firm's tax and survey data.
value_definition: A four-digit numeric year giving the final year of the financial year, on the standard Australian July to June basis.
limitation: It is not a calendar year and the two are out by six months, so a series read as calendar years will misplace every event filed between January and June. IPLORD's own coverage begins at 2001-02, which is later than the IP RAPID history in BLADE, so early filings have no IPLORD year at all.
rationale: The ABS BLADE data page names IPLORD and its coverage, and the data item list gives the year convention used in this column.
evidence_quote: Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD): 2001-02 to latest available
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the four digits are the ending year of a July to June period.

value_domain: De-identified business identifier on the business income tax records
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment, BLADE
variable_description: The scrambled business identifier that ties a firm's income tax return rows to the rest of BLADE, and the column you group by to build a firm-level panel. The ABS says "The BLADE microdata contains businesses that have been active at one time in the Australian economy since 2001-02 and are in the scope of the ABS's Business Register", so the identifier is a business register unit rather than a raw ABN. It appears on several business income tax tables at once - company, individual, partnership and trust - which is how a group's returns are brought together.
value_definition: An opaque alphanumeric key, unique to a business unit and stable within a BLADE integration version but not meaningful outside it.
limitation: It is not an ABN and will not join to anything outside BLADE. It is also a statistical unit rather than a legal entity, so a corporate group can resolve to one identifier while a business that restructures can break into two, which shows up in a panel as a spurious exit and entry.
rationale: The ABS microdata page defines the BLADE population and the unit the microdata is built on, which is what this identifier keys.
evidence_quote: The BLADE microdata contains businesses that have been active at one time in the Australian economy since 2001-02 and are in the scope of the ABS's Business Register.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, 'fn - deidentified scrambled business identifier (SBID)', with no valid-response text and the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what the identifier links.

value_domain: Free on board value of an export consignment line (Australian dollars)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
variable_description: The value of the goods on this export declaration line at the moment they were loaded for export from Australia, the standard basis for Australian export statistics. The ABS defines it so: "A FOB price at the customs frontier includes the transaction value of the goods, the value of outside packaging (other than international containers used for containerised cargo), and related distributive services used, up to and including loading the goods onto the carrier at the customs frontier of the exporting country." It excludes international freight and insurance, which is why a firm's export revenue on this basis is lower than the price its overseas customer pays on delivery.
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for one consignment line, on a free on board basis at the Australian border. Foreign currency values are converted using an indicative Reserve Bank reference rate for the day.
limitation: The declaration threshold truncates the column: export consignments below $2,000 are treated as out of scope, so a small or occasional exporter can have real overseas sales and no row here at all. Exports are also recorded on a date of shipment basis, not when the firm was paid.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the FOB valuation used for Australian export statistics and the currency conversion applied to reported values.
evidence_quote: A FOB price at the customs frontier includes the transaction value of the goods, the value of outside packaging (other than international containers used for containerised cargo), and related distributive services used, up to and including loading the goods onto the carrier at the customs frontier of the exporting country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the $2,000 threshold that removes small exporters was never stated.

value_domain: Free on board value of an import consignment (Australian dollars)
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Trade system, valuation and time of recording
variable_description: The value of an imported consignment at the exporting country's border, before international freight and insurance are added. The ABS uses a free on board type value for imports as well as exports, and notes that "The CIF price is equal to the FOB transaction value, plus the cost of freight and merchandise insurance involved in transporting the goods beyond the place of export to the customs frontier of the importing country." Unlike the export column, this figure sits at the foreign border, so the difference between the two is the whole international leg.
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for the whole consignment, converted by the Integrated Cargo System from any reported foreign currency at the rate applying on the date of export from the place of export.
limitation: It is not the landed cost. Freight, insurance, duty and the import processing charge all sit outside this value, so using it as the firm's input cost understates what the goods cost to get onto an Australian loading dock. Imports below the $1,000 threshold are also out of scope.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the FOB and CIF valuation points for imports and the currency conversion applied.
evidence_quote: The CIF price is equal to the FOB transaction value, plus the cost of freight and merchandise insurance involved in transporting the goods beyond the place of export to the customs frontier of the importing country.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long sentence about consignment values and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the contrast with a landed CIF cost was not drawn.

value_domain: Type of import declaration lodged with Customs (Nature 10, 20 or 30)
value_source: Australian Border Force, Import declarations
variable_description: Which kind of import declaration the business lodged, which tells you whether the goods entered the Australian economy on this row or only entered a bonded warehouse. The Australian Border Force explains that declarations clear goods "into: the commerce of Australia/home consumption - via an Import Declaration or Self-Assessed Clearance Declaration, or a licensed warehouse - via a Warehouse Declaration", so Nature 10 is a direct entry into home consumption, Nature 20 puts goods into a warehouse and Nature 30 releases them from it. A firm that warehouses stock therefore produces two rows for the same goods, months apart.
value_definition: A character value taking Nature 10, Nature 20 or Nature 30, corresponding to the Import Declaration, Warehouse Declaration and ex-warehouse declaration lodged through the Integrated Cargo System.

The column also does not record whether the exempt amount was paid into superannuation, which the exemption can require.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the retirement exemption with its lifetime limit and states that it is shown at labels O to Q of part G of the capital gains tax schedule, the label on this column.
evidence_quote: the amount of your entity's small business retirement exemption (SBRE) at O to Q
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF and NF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so the lifetime cap and the superannuation condition were never mentioned.

value_domain: Date an intellectual property right became legally enforceable (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, Policy register: address confusion around registered and certified designs and the two-step examination process
variable_description: The day the right on this application became something the business could actually enforce against an infringer. For a design that is later than registration, because Australia examines designs only on request: IP Australia states that "If the design is found to have met the substantive requirements of the Act it will be certified and only then is it enforceable". Read against gained_registration_status_date on the same row, the gap between the two is the period in which the firm held a registered but unenforceable right.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, present only for applications that reached an enforceable status with IP Australia.
limitation: A missing date is usually a fact rather than a gap: a registered but uncertified design, or an application that lapsed, was withdrawn or was refused, never acquires one. The date also does not start the term of protection, which for a patent or a trade mark runs from the filing date, so it cannot be used to compute expiry.
rationale: IP Australia's policy register states directly that certification, not registration, is what makes a design right enforceable, which is the distinction this column exists to record and the reason it differs from the registration date.
evidence_quote: If the design is found to have met the substantive requirements of the Act it will be certified and only then is it enforceable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's own one-line wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained why a right can be registered and not yet enforceable.

value_domain: Date an intellectual property right entered the register (DD/MM/YYYY)
value_source: IP Australia, How to renew my IP right
variable_description: The day the right on this application was entered on IP Australia's register. It marks the end of the application process and the point from which the business appears as an owner on the public register, which is what administrative and renewal correspondence keys off: for a trade mark IP Australia says "Renewal is due every 10 years". It is not the same event as the right becoming enforceable, which for designs comes later and is carried by gained_enforceable_status_date.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, present only for applications that reached registered status with IP Australia.
limitation: The term of protection is generally measured from the filing date, not from this one, so building an expiry or a right-age series on this column shortens every right by the length of its examination. It also says nothing about whether the right is still in force, since a registered right lapses if renewal fees are not paid.
rationale: IP Australia's renewal guidance sets out the renewal cycles and the consequence of not renewing, which is what fixes registration as an administrative milestone distinct from the start of the protection term.
evidence_quote: If you don't renew or pay the fee within this period, your rights will lapse and your IP will no longer be protected.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated IP Australia's one-line wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that protection is measured from filing rather than registration.

value_domain: Geocode precision level for a business location (1 to 3)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: How precisely the business location on this row could be placed on the ground: to a single address record, to a mesh block, or only to an SA2. The ABS assigns each address on the Address Register "a latitude and longitude coordinate known as a 'geocode'", and where the business's address could not be matched to one, the location falls back to a coarser statistical area. A 1 means an address-level match, a 3 means the row is only good for SA2 and larger geography.
value_definition: A one-digit code from 1 to 3, ordered from finest to coarsest: 1 accepted at the address register identifier level, 2 at the mesh block level, 3 at the SA2 level.
limitation: Ignoring this column silently mixes precise and imprecise rows in the same map or mesh-block aggregate, and a 3 cannot be improved by joining to a finer geography later. It is also a statement about the address match, not about the site: a precisely geocoded registered office may be an accountant's address rather than anywhere the business operates.
rationale: The ABS Address Register information guide defines the geocode and the statistical geography codes carried with an address, which are the three levels this indicator grades a business location against.
evidence_quote: a latitude and longitude coordinate known as a 'geocode'
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase about a precision indicator with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said what happens to an analysis that ignores the level.

value_domain: Go Global Toolkit first registration indicator
value_source: business.gov.au, Exporting and your business
variable_description: Whether the business first opened a Go Global Toolkit account, Austrade's free online export service, in this financial year. The toolkit is the entry point to government export help: "Austrade's Go Global Toolkit has tools, market insights and guidance to help you expand into new markets", so a first sign-up is a reasonable marker of a firm starting to look seriously at exporting. It fires once in a business's history, in the year of first registration.
value_definition: A binary indicator, 0 for no and 1 for yes, in each financial year. Note that the custodian's label describes a financial year while the recorded domain is binary.
limitation: The label and the value domain disagree, so check the actual values before treating the column as a year rather than a flag; a numeric year read as a flag, or the reverse, will misclassify every business. A sign-up is also only an account, not use of the toolkit or any export activity, so it cannot stand in for export readiness.
rationale: business.gov.au describes the Go Global Toolkit and what it offers Australian businesses, which is the service this registration indicator refers to; the recording convention comes from the custodian's own label and valid response.
evidence_quote: Austrade's Go Global Toolkit has tools, market insights and guidance to help you expand into new markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and did not flag that the label describes a year while the domain is binary.

value_domain: Go Global Toolkit webinar attendance indicator (0/1)
value_source: business.gov.au, Exporting and your business
variable_description: Whether anyone from the business attended a Go Global Toolkit webinar in the financial year, either live or by watching a recording. It is the lightest touch of engagement recorded in the exporter panel, one step beyond simply holding an account, and it sits on top of the toolkit that business.gov.au describes as having "tools, market insights and guidance to help you expand into new markets". Unlike the sign-up indicator it can be set in more than one year.
value_definition: A binary indicator, 0 for no and 1 for yes, per financial year, covering both online check-in at a live session and access to a session recording.
limitation: Live attendance and a recording view are pooled, so the column cannot separate a scheduled commitment from an incidental click, and it counts the business once no matter how many staff attended or how many sessions. A zero includes firms that got export advice through a TradeStart adviser or another channel entirely.
rationale: business.gov.au identifies the Go Global Toolkit and its role in Austrade's export support, which is the service whose webinars this indicator records; the pooling of live and recorded attendance comes from the custodian's own label.
evidence_quote: Austrade's Go Global Toolkit has tools, market insights and guidance to help you expand into new markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Austrade's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said that a recording view and live attendance are counted alike.

value_domain: Declared gold assay concentration, grams per tonne
value_source: Australian Border Force, Export declaration supplementary page (form B957a), hosted by the ABS
variable_description: The gold grade the exporter declared for this consignment of ore or concentrate, in grams of gold per tonne. It comes from the assay details on the export declaration, which the form defines as "A chemical test to determine the content of a particular element" and requires "Only input details if goods are minerals requiring an assay"; gold's prescribed unit on that form is GPT, grams per tonne. It is a property of the shipment, not of the exporting business.
value_definition: A non-negative number in grams per tonne, declared against the assay element AU on the export declaration supplementary page, and present only on mineral lines that require an assay.
limitation: It cannot be averaged into a firm-level ore grade, because it is populated only on qualifying mineral lines and is weighted by nothing: a large low-grade shipment and a small high-grade one carry equal-looking numbers. Nor is it a reserve or resource grade, since it describes what left the wharf after processing rather than what is in the ground.
rationale: The export declaration supplementary page defines the assay fields, states when they must be completed, and prescribes grams per tonne as the unit for gold, which is exactly what this column carries.
evidence_quote: A chemical test to determine the content of a particular element. Only input details if goods are minerals requiring an assay.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Grams of gold per tonne of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the field is consignment-level and conditional on the goods requiring an assay.

value_domain: Gross shipping weight of an export consignment, kilograms
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
variable_description: The shipped weight of the goods the business exported on this line, including the packaging that went with them. The ABS states that "Gross weight is recorded for each commodity on a customs export declaration", which makes the export side of this pair usable at commodity level, unlike its import counterpart. It is a flow for one declaration line, not an annual total for the firm.
value_definition: A weight in kilograms in ABS output, covering the goods plus wrapping, crates, boxes and outside packages, but excluding the shipping container itself.
limitation: It is not the traded quantity: the comparable measure is the net quantity in the unit prescribed by the AHECC, and a change in packaging moves this number with no change in what was sold. Weight is also a poor proxy for value, since one tonne of ore and one tonne of medical devices are the same number here.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods publication defines gross weight for exports, states that it is recorded per commodity, and sets the unit used in ABS output.
evidence_quote: Gross weight is recorded for each commodity on a customs export declaration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's definition of gross weight with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished gross weight from the AHECC net quantity.

value_domain: Gross shipping weight of an import declaration, kilograms
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Quantity measurement
variable_description: The shipped weight of an import declaration, which the ABS reports for the whole declaration rather than for each commodity on it. This is why the custodian warns against commodity or country use: "For imports, gross weight is not recorded at the individual commodity level but total gross weight is reported for all the commodities on a customs import declaration", and the ABS then assigns that whole weight to one line so commodity estimates can be produced. The line carrying the weight is therefore arbitrary within the declaration.
value_definition: A weight in kilograms covering the goods plus their immediate packaging on the entire import declaration, attached to a single line of it rather than apportioned.
limitation: Summing this column by commodity or by country produces a nonsense result, because a mixed consignment's entire weight sits on whichever line the ABS attached it to. ABS advises that import gross weight is only reliable when aggregated at the port or state level, so a firm-level weight of imports built from it is not safe either.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods publication states plainly that import gross weight is a declaration-level figure and explains the assignment to one line, which is exactly the caution attached to this column.
evidence_quote: For imports, gross weight is not recorded at the individual commodity level but total gross weight is reported for all the commodities on a customs import declaration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's warning without explaining it, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Count of Austrade general service events in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade recorded delivering any kind of general service to the business during the financial year. It is the total that the more specific general service counts on the same row sit under, and it is drawn from Austrade's client records rather than from the business. Austrade describes this work as advisory: "We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections".
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of service events in one financial year, covering all general service types including those recorded with an unknown type.
limitation: It counts events, not effort, value or duration, so ten short email introductions outrank one sustained market entry engagement. It also does not add up to Austrade's whole relationship with the firm, since grants and named programmes are recorded in their own columns rather than here.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the trade services and adviser network that generate the service events this column tallies, and the ABS project register confirms Austrade's client records are the source integrated into BLADE.
evidence_quote: We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's one-line label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the number counts events rather than effort.

value_domain: Count of Austrade international contact identification services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade identified relevant overseas contacts for the business during the financial year. This is the introductions component of Austrade's general services, the part that draws on its in-market posts to put a firm in front of possible buyers, distributors or partners. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the international contacts type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: An introduction is not a relationship: the column records that contacts were identified, not that the business pursued them or that anything followed. It also gives no market, so a firm's introductions cannot be traced to the countries in its merchandise trade records.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the in-market adviser network that makes these introductions, which is the activity this service-type count records.
evidence_quote: We have advisers in Australia and in our international offices who provide information, insights, support and connections.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing distinguished an introduction from an outcome.

value_domain: Count of Austrade market selection and assessment services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade helped the business choose and assess overseas markets during the financial year. It is the earliest stage of the export journey among the general service types, coming before market entry work, so a firm showing counts here and nowhere else is still deciding where to go. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the market selection and assessment type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: The column cannot show which markets were assessed or whether any was chosen, so it will not explain a later change in a firm's export destinations. A count here is also compatible with a business that never exported, since assessment often concludes against entry.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the information and insight services its advisers provide, which is the activity behind this market selection count.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing placed the service in the sequence of export support.

value_domain: Count of Austrade market entry and expansion services in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many times Austrade assisted the business with entering or expanding in an overseas market during the financial year. It is the operational end of the general services, and it usually follows market selection work rather than preceding it, so counts here suggest a firm already committed to a market. It is a subset of gsallservices on the same row.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of general service events of the market entry and expansion type in a financial year, one of the components of gsallservices.
limitation: Entry and expansion are pooled in one count, so a first shipment to a new country cannot be told apart from deepening an existing trade relationship. The column also has no dollar value, so it cannot be used to weight the assistance a firm received.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes trade services aimed at helping businesses expand in overseas markets, which is the activity this service-type count records.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Austrade's service-type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said that entry and expansion are pooled.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at GST on sales on the business activity statement
value_source: business.gov.au, Business activity statement
variable_description: The goods and services tax the business reported as payable on its sales for the period, or its GST instalment amount where it uses that option. The activity statement is the vehicle: "Your BAS helps you to report on taxes like: goods and services tax (GST), pay as you go (PAYG) withholding, PAYG instalments, fringe benefits tax (FBT) instalments, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax". Because it is roughly one-eleventh of taxable sales, it is often used as a high-frequency proxy for a firm's turnover.
value_definition: A dollar amount reported for a business activity statement period, which may be monthly, quarterly or annual depending on the firm's reporting cycle.
limitation: It is GST on sales, not GST paid: net GST is this amount less the credits claimed on purchases, so reading it as the firm's tax bill overstates it. The column also mixes two different quantities, because an instalment payer reports a pre-set amount rather than a measured one, and businesses under the GST registration turnover threshold report nothing at all.
rationale: business.gov.au sets out what a business activity statement reports and its reporting cycles, which fixes the period, the form and the tax this column comes from; the label itself names GST on sales or the GST instalment.
evidence_quote: Your BAS helps you to report on taxes like: goods and services tax (GST), pay as you go (PAYG) withholding, PAYG instalments, fringe benefits tax (FBT) instalments, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing separated GST on sales from net GST or flagged the instalment payers pooled into the same column.

value_domain: Count of Austrade general services of unrecorded type in a financial year
value_source: Austrade, Programs and services
variable_description: How many general service events Austrade recorded for the business without capturing what kind of service it was. It is a data quality residual within the general services block, and its size sets how much of gsallservices the named service-type columns actually account for. A firm with a large count here received help that cannot be characterised from this panel.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of service events in a financial year whose service type was not recorded, forming the unspecified remainder of the general services total.
limitation: It is not a kind of service and must not be modelled as one; doing so treats an administrative recording failure as a business experience. Because recording practice varies with the office and the year, movements in this column can reflect changes in Austrade's own systems rather than in what firms received.
rationale: The Austrade programs and services page describes the service delivery whose records generate these counts, which is what makes an unknown-type count a completeness measure for the block rather than a service in its own right.
evidence_quote: Trade services can help eligible Australian businesses expand in overseas markets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Austrade's unknown service type label with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned against treating it as a substantive category.

value_domain: Net capital gain, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The part of the business entity's net capital gain that came from assets worked out under the discount method, after losses, the discount and the small business concessions. The ATO restricts the method by holding period, applying it "for assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method", so this column is the long-held end of the entity's disposals. The OF prefix marks it as an old-form label; the new form no longer splits the net gain by method.
value_definition: A dollar amount at the net capital gain step of the capital gains tax schedule, after part D losses, the part F discount and the part G concessions have all been applied.
limitation: For most companies this column is empty as a matter of law rather than of business behaviour: the ATO states that "Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business". Reading a zero as an absence of long-held asset sales is therefore wrong for the great majority of company filers.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the discount method and its twelve-month holding requirement, and states which entities are eligible for the discount, which together fix what this method column can and cannot contain.
evidence_quote: the discount method (see note 3 of the worksheet) for assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained that companies cannot use the discount at all.

value_domain: Net capital gain, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The part of the entity's net capital gain that came from assets worked out under the indexation method, after all losses and concessions. Indexation is closed to new assets: the ATO allows it only "for capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11.45am (by legal time in the ACT) on 21 September 1999 and owned for at least 12 months", so this column is a window on a firm's oldest holdings. The OF prefix marks the old-form label, which the new form dropped when it stopped splitting the net gain by method.
value_definition: A dollar amount at the net capital gain step of the schedule, restricted to gains on assets acquired before 21 September 1999 and worked out with cost base indexation.
limitation: The column thins out mechanically across the panel as pre-1999 assets are sold, so a downward trend measures asset vintage rather than any change in business behaviour. A zero in a later year is close to uninformative, and the column should not be summed with the discount and other-method columns as if the three were comparable measures.
rationale: The ATO guide defines the indexation method and states the acquisition date and holding period that qualify an asset for it, which is what makes this column a declining series by construction.
evidence_quote: the indexation method (see note 2 of the worksheet) for capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11.45am (by legal time in the ACT) on 21 September 1999 and owned for at least 12 months
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the raw OF label text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the method is closed to assets acquired after 1999.

value_domain: Net capital gain, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
