value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Expenses label N, split into primary and non-primary production columns, with the calculation method recorded in the adjacent type box column.
limitation: The number's meaning depends on the method code beside it. A cents-per-kilometre claim is a statutory rate applied to distance and does not measure what the vehicle cost, while a logbook claim is a business-use share of actual outlays, so pooling the two compares two different constructions rather than two levels of spending.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction defines the label, states the depreciation, lease and interest exclusions, includes ride-sourcing, and sets out the method codes that qualify the amount.
evidence_quote: Don't include depreciation, finance leasing charges or interest paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Motor vehicle expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not tie the amount to the method code that determines how it was constructed.

value_domain: Motor vehicle expense calculation method code
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: How the business worked out the motor vehicle amount beside it, or a marker that the vehicle sits outside the car substantiation rules. The current schedule offers two methods — "S if you used the 'cents per kilometre' method" and "B if you used the 'logbook' method" — plus code N for a motorcycle, a taxi taken on hire, or a vehicle carrying a tonne or more or nine or more passengers. Where a taxpayer has more than one code, only the one covering the largest claim is kept.
value_definition: A coded response with five values in the BLADE frame: 5 for S cents per kilometre, 15 for O one-third of actual expenses, 20 for B logbook, 30 for T 12 per cent of original value and 35 for N vehicles outside the car rules. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: The one-third of actual expenses and 12 per cent of original value methods were withdrawn after 2014-15, so codes 15 and 30 appear only in earlier years and a method series spanning the change is not continuous. The largest-claim rule also means the code describes part of the amount, not all of it.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction lists the current method letters, the N category and the largest-claim tie-break, and the presence of the O and T codes in the BLADE frame dates the column to the earlier four-method regime.
evidence_quote: S if you used the ‘cents per kilometre’ method
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the five-value code list with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that two of the five methods were abolished, which is what breaks the series.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The farming business's own result for the year, before any losses deferred from earlier years are brought in. The ATO's instruction for this step says plainly: "Don't include any non-commercial business loss deferred from a prior year." That makes it the cleanest available measure of current-year primary production performance, and it is not the figure that reaches the tax return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount for the income year, printed with an L beside it when it is a loss. It is total primary production business income less total primary production expenses, after the income and expense reconciliation adjustments.
limitation: Using this column as farm income overstates it for any business carrying deferred non-commercial losses, because those are subtracted afterwards to produce the figure that is transferred to the return. It also aggregates every primary production activity the person runs, so a profitable enterprise and a loss-making one cancel inside it.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines this step, excludes deferred non-commercial losses from it, and shows the later step that applies them, which is what separates this column from the final net primary production figure.
evidence_quote: Don't include any non-commercial business loss deferred from a prior year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net income or loss from business this year - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it could not be told apart from the post-deferral net primary production column in the same table.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The non-farm business result that actually reaches the tax return, after deferred non-commercial losses have been applied. The ATO flags the difference from the current-year figure directly: "This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year." It is transferred to the income question in the individual's supplementary return, so it is the number the tax system acts on.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 label Z, with an L printed beside it when it is a loss, carried to label C of question 15 in the supplementary return.
limitation: A loss here triggers a further reporting obligation for business loss activity details, so a loss is a year with consequences rather than simply a bad year, and the reporting itself may shape what is declared. The figure also pools every non-primary business the person runs and cannot be attributed to one activity.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines this label as the post-deferral figure, gives its transfer to the supplementary return and states the loss reporting consequence.
evidence_quote: This amount takes into account non-commercial losses deferred from a prior year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Net income/loss from business other than PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not distinguish it from the current-year non-primary net income column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The farming business result that reaches the tax return, after deferred non-commercial losses have been applied. The ATO closes the step by moving it off the schedule: "Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) question 15 in your supplementary tax return." It is the primary production twin of the post-deferral non-primary column, and differs from the current-year primary production figure by exactly the deferred loss applied.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 label Y, flagged with an L when it is a loss, and transferred to label B of question 15 in the supplementary return.
limitation: Primary production income is subject to income averaging and to farm management deposits elsewhere in the individual's return, so this column is not the amount the farmer is finally assessed on. A farm that moved activities between the primary and non-primary columns also breaks its own series here without any change in operations.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the post-deferral primary production label and its transfer to the supplementary return, which is what separates it from the current-year primary production figure.
evidence_quote: Step 4: Transfer the amounts at Y and Z to B and C (respectively) question 15 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net income/loss - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which is indistinguishable from the current-year primary production column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Non-farm income paid to the business with tax withheld because it did not quote an ABN to the payer. The ATO defines the pair of labels as "the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN". A non-zero value is a compliance signal rather than an income type: it says the business traded without a quoted ABN with at least one payer, which typically happens around registration or lapse.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label D, gross of the tax withheld, taken from payment summaries with an N in the type box for non-primary production activities.
limitation: The column cannot tell you how much tax was withheld — that is a separate label on the supplementary return — and it names no payer, so the exposure cannot be traced. It is also not a measure of cash economy activity: a payer who withholds is reporting the payment to the ATO.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines both no-ABN labels, ties them to the payment summary schedule and distinguishes the primary from the non-primary production column.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels C and D is the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what a value signals about the firm.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Farm income paid to the business with tax withheld because no ABN was quoted. The ATO builds it from the taxpayer's own payer documents: "Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box." It is the primary production twin of the non-primary no-ABN column.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P8 Income label C, gross of tax withheld, in the primary production column.
limitation: Farm output is usually sold to processors, agents and saleyards that hold an ABN on file, so this label is sparse and a value is more often a new or lapsed registration than a persistent pattern. It also cannot separate one large payment from many small ones, so it is a poor basis for inferring how a farm sells.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the primary production label and its payment summary type-box construction, which is what distinguishes it from the non-primary label.
evidence_quote: Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and offered no way to distinguish it from its non-primary twin.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Reconciliation items P8
variable_description: The non-farm business result for the year in its own right, before deferred non-commercial losses are applied. It pools every non-primary activity the sole trader runs, and the ATO uses a loss in it as a trigger for further disclosure: a loss in any one activity means "you need to complete P3 Number of business activities and P9 Business loss activity details". The number of activities behind the figure is therefore only recoverable from a separate item.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount for the income year, the non-primary production counterpart of the current-year primary production figure, printed with an L when it is a loss.
limitation: A profitable business and a loss-making one net off inside this single number, so it cannot be used to count failing activities. It is also not the figure carried to the tax return, which is the post-deferral non-primary net income column, so the two must not be used interchangeably.
rationale: The ATO reconciliation instruction defines the current-year net income step, excludes deferred losses from it and states the multi-activity disclosure trigger that reveals its aggregation.
evidence_quote: If the amount at label B or C includes details from more than one business activity, and any one of these activities resulted in a net loss, you need to complete P3 Number of business activities and P9 Business loss activity details.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Net income or loss from business this year - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, indistinguishable from the post-deferral non-primary column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: The tax value of trading stock the business held at the start of the income year. It is not an independent observation: the ATO ties it to the previous return, since "The value of your stock on hand at the start of the income year is the same value as the closing value shown in your schedule in the previous year." Stock of a business that commenced during the year is excluded, so a first-year business reports nothing here.
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at 1 July, equal by rule to the prior year's closing stock for the same items, and split into primary and non-primary production columns before being totalled.
limitation: Because it is defined as last year's closing value, it inherits last year's valuation method and any small business election not to account for a stock movement, so a difference between opening and closing stock measures a reported change rather than a physical one. It also cannot be used to check the previous return, since the two are the same number by construction.
rationale: The ATO expenses instruction defines opening stock by reference to the previous year's closing value and excludes stock of a business that commenced during the year.
evidence_quote: The value of your stock on hand at the start of the income year is the same value as the closing value shown in your schedule in the previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Opening stock' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that it is last year's closing value by rule rather than a fresh measurement.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Ordinary trading income of the farming business — despite the name, this is the main revenue line for most farms. The ATO's list starts with "gross sales of trading stock" and "gross sales from produce", and then reaches non-cash items including goods taken from stock for own use, the "value of livestock killed for rations" and livestock exchanged for other goods or services. Everything already reported at the withholding, government payment and labour hire labels is excluded from it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 Income label I; a loss is possible and is flagged with an L. Primary producers build it from the gross income from primary production worksheet before entering it.
limitation: Treating this as miscellaneous income understates farm turnover badly, because it is where sales land. It also mixes cash sales with imputed non-cash amounts such as rations and own use, so it is not a receipts figure and cannot be reconciled to a bank statement.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists what other business income comprises, states the exclusions against the other income labels and gives the primary production worksheet route into this label.
evidence_quote: Other business income includes: gross sales of trading stock, gross sales from produce, goods taken from stock for your own use, value of livestock killed for rations
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Other business income - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, inviting a reader to treat the largest revenue line on a farm return as a residual.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Income P8
variable_description: Ordinary trading income of the non-farm business, which for most sole traders is nearly all of their turnover. It reaches beyond invoiced sales to platform work: the ATO includes "income earned through the sharing economy, or other marketplace, where you're carrying on a business", along with rent from a renting business, royalties, insurance recoveries and profit on selling a depreciating asset. It excludes everything shown at the withholding, government payment and labour hire labels.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P8 Income label J, the non-primary production counterpart of label I, with a loss flagged by an L.
limitation: It absorbs one-off items — insurance payouts, gains on selling equipment, foreign exchange gains — alongside recurring sales, so a single year's figure is a poor measure of trading and a spike may be an asset disposal. Ride-sourcing and taxi income may sit here or at the personal services income item depending on the taxpayer, so the column is not a stable definition of gig work.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists what other business income comprises, including sharing economy earnings and one-off recoveries, and states the exclusions against the other income labels.
evidence_quote: income earned through the sharing economy, or other marketplace, where you're carrying on a business
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other business income - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing signalled that this is the main turnover line and that it carries one-off gains.

value_domain: Dollar cost of tangible depreciating assets first deducted
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Depreciating assets P17 to P20
variable_description: The cost of tangible assets the business began depreciating this year — plant, vehicles, equipment and fit-out. The ATO defines the label as "the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time". Because it is cost rather than deduction, it is the closest the schedule comes to gross fixed capital formation by a sole trader.
value_definition: Whole dollars of cost at P18 label J, not reduced for estimated private use, and including assets under $1,000 allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules do not complete the label, so the column is systematically missing for the smallest firms and thins out further in years when the instant asset write-off threshold was high. It also counts assets first deducted, so a second-hand asset already depreciated by its previous owner still appears as new investment here.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label as first-year cost of non-intangible depreciating assets, excludes simplified-depreciation taxpayers and states the low-value pool inclusion and the no-reduction-for-private-use rule.
evidence_quote: At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other depreciating assets first deducted' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no warning that small business entities are absent from the column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Expenses P8
variable_description: Everything the business spent that no named expense line covers, which for most sole traders includes the wages bill. The ATO defines it as "the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses", and lists wages, accounting and professional fees, advertising, office supplies, foreign exchange losses and any book loss on selling a depreciating asset. It is usually the largest single expense line on a services return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting expense at P8 Expenses label P, split into primary and non-primary production columns; business gifts and donations and fees paid to professionals for the business's tax affairs also belong here rather than in the individual's personal deductions.
limitation: Because wages are buried inside it, the column is not comparable across firms with different mixes of employed and contracted labour; the separate total salary and wage expenses item is the only way to pull wages back out. Capital and other non-deductible items are also reported here and removed later at the reconciliation label, so it is not a deduction total.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label as the residual expense line, lists what belongs in it, and directs non-deductible amounts inside it to the reconciliation label.
evidence_quote: This is the total of all other expenses that you incur in deriving your profit or loss and you haven't already shown elsewhere at P8 Expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'All other expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned a reader that wages sit inside the residual line.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the individual business and professional items schedule
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Payments to associated persons P16
variable_description: What the business paid relatives and related partnerships during the year. The ATO defines the item as "amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives", and adds that "These also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives." It is a disclosure item that supports the excessive payment test, so a value marks a family-staffed business rather than a separate category of spending.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P16 label H, aggregated across the taxpayer's businesses. The salary and wage portion is also inside the total salary and wage expenses item, so the two items overlap by design.
limitation: Adding this column to the expense lines double counts, because the same payments already sit in wages or other expenses. It says nothing about how many relatives were paid or what work they did, and payments the ATO later treats as excessive and disallows still appear here at their full amount.
rationale: The ATO instruction for P16 defines what the item covers, requires the same amounts to be included in total salary and wages, and states the excessive payment rule that gives the disclosure its purpose.
evidence_quote: These are amounts, including salary, wages, commissions or allowances, paid to your relatives. These also include super contributions paid for the benefit of your relatives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Payments to associated persons' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the amounts are also counted inside the expense lines.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income received with tax withheld because the taxpayer did not quote an ABN to the payer. The ATO defines it as "your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld". It is one of the four gross labels that feed the net personal services income calculation, and it reports the same withholding event as the business no-ABN labels but for a different population.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label N, gross of tax withheld, taken from payment summaries with an N in the type box.
limitation: Income reaches P1 only where the personal services income rules apply, so a contractor moves between this column and the business no-ABN columns as their personal services business status changes, and the two sets must never be added. It also does not show the tax withheld, which is reported at the supplementary return.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines this label, states that it is gross of tax withheld, ties it to the payment summary type box and places it among the labels summed to reach net personal services income.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label N is your total PSI from which an amount is withheld because you didn't quote your ABN, including the amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'PSI where Australian Business Number not quoted' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never distinguished it from the identically named business income labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income earned under a labour-hire arrangement or as a specified payment, gross of tax withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld", and specified payments here mean Indigenous tutorial services, translating and interpreting work, and promotional appearances by performing artists. Employment income from a labour-hire business is excluded and goes to the salary question on the individual return instead.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label O, built from payment summaries with an S in the type box, and one of the four gross personal services income labels added before deductions.
limitation: The three specified payment types are pooled with genuine labour hire and cannot be separated, so a rise in the column is not necessarily a rise in labour hire. A taxpayer can report labour hire at this label and other labour hire at the business income labels in the same year, so neither column alone measures the firm's labour-hire exposure.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, states that it is gross of withholding, lists the specified payments and excludes labour-hire employees.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label O is the total income you receive from labour hire or other specified payments, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'PSI labour hire or other specified payments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the specified payments or the employment exclusion.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Net personal services income for the year: the four gross personal services income labels less the two personal services income deduction labels. The ATO's arithmetic is explicit — "Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1" — and the result is carried to the personal services income question on the supplementary return. A populated value means the personal services income rules applied to at least some of the taxpayer's income.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at P1 label A, printed with an L beside it when it is a loss, and transferred to label A of question 14 in the supplementary return.
limitation: The column identifies a tax status, not an occupation: the personal services income rules turn on the results, unrelated clients, employment and business premises tests, so two people doing the same work can sit on opposite sides of it. Income earned through a personal services business is reported at the business income item instead, so a nil here does not mean the person sells no personal services.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the net personal services income calculation step by step, its label, the loss convention and the transfer to the supplementary return, and elsewhere sets out the tests that decide whether income reaches P1 at all.
evidence_quote: Step 3: Subtract the amount calculated at step 2 from the amount calculated at step 1. Write your answer at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Net PSI' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing told a reader that presence in the column is a legal test rather than a description of the work.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: Personal services income that had no tax withheld at source, which is the residual of the four gross personal services income labels. The instruction is short and self-assessed: "Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) - label J." For a contractor invoicing clients directly with an ABN quoted and no voluntary agreement, this is where nearly all of their income lands.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label J, excluding GST for a taxpayer registered or required to be registered, and added to the three withholding labels to give gross personal services income.
limitation: It is the only personal services income label with no payment summary behind it, so it rests entirely on the taxpayer's own records and cannot be cross-checked against payer reporting the way the withholding labels can. A large value therefore carries a different evidential weight from the same amount at the withholding labels.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, gives the GST exclusion and places it among the labels summed in step 1 of the net personal services income calculation, which is what makes it the unreconciled residual.
evidence_quote: Work out the total amount of other PSI and write this amount at P1 Personal services income (PSI) – label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'PSI other' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never said that this is the one personal services income label with no payer document behind it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income item
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, Personal services income P1
variable_description: All deductions claimed against personal services income other than payments to associates for principal work. The ATO folds prior-year losses into it: "Add up the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI." With the associates label, it is one of the two amounts subtracted from gross personal services income to reach the net figure.
value_definition: Whole dollars at P1 label L, excluding anything already shown at the associates label and excluding amounts relating to input tax credit entitlements for a GST-registered taxpayer.
limitation: The personal services income rules deny many ordinary business deductions, including home occupancy costs and payments to associates for non-principal work, so this column shows what survived the rules rather than what the person spent. Deferred non-commercial losses from earlier years sit inside it, so it is not a clean current-year expense figure either.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, states that deferred non-commercial losses are included, excludes the associates amounts and the GST component, and places it in the net personal services income calculation.
evidence_quote: Add up the total amount of all other expenses (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) that you can deduct from your PSI.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total amount of other deductions against PSI' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not flag that prior-year deferred losses are mixed into the total.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the personal services income voluntary agreement label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Personal services income - P1
variable_description: Personal services income the entity reported as paid under a PAYG voluntary agreement, gross of the tax the payer withheld. The ATO defines the label as "the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld", and defines the income itself as "income that is mainly a reward for an individual's personal efforts or skills". A voluntary agreement is an arrangement where a contractor who has quoted an ABN asks the payer to withhold anyway, so a non-zero figure marks a business whose earnings are one person's labour sold under contract.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one income year, reported in the personal services income section of the return rather than in business income, and reported gross of the amounts withheld by the payer.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the personal services income rules bit. Deduction restrictions turn on the results test, the other personal services business tests or a Commissioner's determination, none of which this column carries. A zero is also not an absence of personal services income: income earned without a voluntary agreement sits at the labour hire, ABN-not-quoted or other personal services income labels instead.
rationale: The BLADE Business Income Tax module carries income tax return items. The ATO's business and professional items instructions define the voluntary agreement label directly and define personal services income in the same document.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at label M is the total income you receive that is subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement, including amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the purchases and other costs expense label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business spent during the year on trading stock and the direct materials that went into what it sold. The ATO defines the label as "the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business", and says it "includes inwards freight and the cost of stock acquired when starting or acquiring a business during the year". It is one component of cost of sales, which also moves with opening and closing stock reported beside it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount for one income year, entered separately for primary production and non-primary production and totalled, and reported net of any input tax credit entitlement where the entity is registered for GST.
limitation: It is not the cost of the goods actually sold. Cost of sales adds opening stock and subtracts closing stock, so a firm that built up inventory shows purchases well above the cost of what it sold that year. The boundary with contractor expenses also moves with the firm's own bookkeeping: the ATO tells lodgers that contract labour recorded in the cost of sales account belongs here rather than at contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses.
rationale: The purchases and other costs label is defined verbatim in the ATO business and professional items expense instructions, including the treatment of inwards freight, start-up stock and contract labour.
evidence_quote: Purchases and other costs represent the direct cost of materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the income reconciliation adjustments label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items - P8
variable_description: The net adjustment that carries the business from the income in its accounts to the income assessable for tax. The ATO says these adjustments "reconcile your business operating profit or loss with your business taxable income", and that "your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions". Add-backs are assessable amounts not in the accounts, such as balancing adjustments on disposing of depreciating assets; subtractions are accounting income that is not assessable, such as exempt income and book profit on the sale of a depreciating asset.
value_definition: A signed whole-dollar amount for one income year. The return carries a separate loss indicator for a negative value, so the sign is held outside the number itself.
limitation: Read without the sign flag, a large negative adjustment looks like a large positive one. The column is also a residual: exempt income, cash flow boost amounts, balancing adjustments and plain omissions all net off inside one figure, so a movement cannot be attributed to any of them, and the expense-side adjustment is a separate column that must be read with it.
rationale: The reconciliation items instructions define what an income reconciliation adjustment is, how it is built from add-backs and subtractions, and what it is for.
evidence_quote: These adjustments reconcile your business operating profit or loss with your business taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the rent expenses label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business paid as a tenant to rent the land and buildings it used to earn income. The ATO defines the label as "expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income" and tells lodgers to "include the cost of leasing real estate". Equipment and vehicle leasing is a different label, so this column is premises cost alone.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount for one income year, split between primary production and non-primary production columns and totalled, and net of input tax credits for a GST-registered entity.
limitation: A nil value is a fact about tenure, not about premises cost. A business that owns its site reports nothing here while carrying the same occupancy cost through interest, capital works and rates, so rent cannot be used as a proxy for the cost of space, and comparisons across firms of different tenure are misleading.
rationale: The rent expenses label is defined in one sentence in the ATO business and professional items expense instructions, and the company return carries the same expense line at item 6 label H.
evidence_quote: This is expenditure you incur as a tenant for rental of land and buildings used for producing assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the repairs and maintenance expense label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: What the business spent keeping its premises, plant and equipment in working order, as the figure appears in its accounts. The ATO defines it as "expenditure shown in your accounts for repairs and maintenance of premises, plant, machinery, implements, utensils, rolling stock or articles associated with the production of income". It is an accounts figure rather than a deduction: the same instruction tells lodgers that capital items or private-use amounts included here must be reversed at the expense reconciliation adjustment.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense amount for one income year, entered in the primary production and non-primary production columns of the business expenses item and totalled.
limitation: It overstates deductible repairs by design, because improvements of a capital nature and private-use portions stay in the number and are removed elsewhere on the return. It also cannot separate maintenance of buildings from maintenance of machinery, so it will not support a capital-stock story about which assets a firm is looking after.
rationale: The ATO expense instruction defines the label and states explicitly that non-deductible amounts inside it are handled through the expense reconciliation adjustment, which is the fact a reader needs.
evidence_quote: This is expenditure shown in your accounts for repairs and maintenance of premises, plant, machinery, implements, utensils, rolling stock or articles associated with the production of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ATO label wording from the BLADE data item list as its whole description, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the business actually reported, on which return item, or how the figure behaves.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the section 40-880 deduction label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Reconciliation items - P8
variable_description: The deduction the business claimed under section 40-880 for business-related capital costs, mostly start-up and cessation expenses. These are costs no other provision allows, and the ATO states that the section "allows for certain start-up costs to be immediately deductible" for small business entities, and otherwise "allows you to deduct in equal proportions over a 5-year period certain capital expenditure" at 20 per cent a year. Eligible costs include advice on setting up a structure, government fees, feasibility studies, and the cost of winding a business up.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for one income year, reported among the reconciliation items rather than among business expenses, and split between primary production and non-primary production.
limitation: A non-zero amount is not this year's spending. value_domain: Self-reported business status code on the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2022 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 to 2
variable_description: The tick box the entity used to say whether its business ceased, commenced or continued during the income year. The boxes are not identical across return types: the trust return asks the lodger to "Print X at label B1 Multiple business, B2 Ceased business, or B3 Commenced business to represent the appropriate description for the status of the business", and only one box may be used, because "If more than one selection applies, select the first applicable option". The continuing category in the BLADE code list is therefore the residual left when no cessation or commencement was ticked, rather than a box the lodger chose.
value_definition: A coded response taking 5 for ceased business, 10 for commenced business and 15 for continuing business, with anything else recorded as an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It cannot date entry or exit, and it cannot show both in one year: a business that opened and closed within the year reports only the first applicable option. value_domain: Dollar amount of simplified depreciation deducted from the general small business pool
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation
variable_description: The depreciation the business deducted this year from its general small business pool. The pool holds the assets that cost at or above the instant asset write-off limit, and the ATO describes it as one that "has simplified calculations to work out the depreciation deduction", written down at "a 15% deduction in the year you start to use them or have them installed ready for use" and "a 30% deduction each year after the first year". It sits beside the immediate write-off column, and the two together cannot exceed the depreciation expense reported in the profit and loss item.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for one income year. It is a deduction, not a pool balance, and it is reported only by entities that chose the small business simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: A blank means outside the regime at least as often as it means no depreciation: only small business entities with aggregated turnover under the threshold, currently $10 million, may use simplified depreciation, and everyone else depreciates under the general rules with no entry here. The series also breaks for years ended between 6 October 2020 and 30 June 2023, when the whole pool balance had to be written off under temporary full expensing.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the instant asset write-off claimed under simplified depreciation
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 10 Small business entity simplified depreciation

You therefore need to insert 0 at this label." It pairs with the general pool deduction column, which takes the assets above the limit.

limitation: The level is driven by the threshold as much as by investment: the limit has moved between $1,000, $20,000, $30,000, $150,000 and no limit at all, so a jump between years can be entirely legislative. value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the superannuation expenses label of the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 6 Expenses
variable_description: The superannuation the business expensed for its workers over the income year. The company return instruction is direct - "Write at label D the superannuation expenses incurred for the income year" - and the sole trader schedule adds that the figure excludes the owner's own contributions, which are claimed in the personal part of the return. Employers deduct contributions to a complying fund or retirement savings account in the year the contributions are made.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the termination value of intangible depreciating assets label
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: What the business received for intangible depreciating assets it stopped holding or using during the year. In-house software with expenditure in a software development pool is excluded.

The assessable and deductible balancing adjustments are separate labels, so a large termination value can sit against either. value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the termination value of other depreciating assets label
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: What the business received for its tangible depreciating assets - vehicles, plant and equipment - that it stopped holding or using during the year. The ATO defines the label as "the termination value of each balancing adjustment event occurring for depreciating assets, including assets allocated to a low-value pool", and lists what to leave out: intangibles, assets already in a general small business pool, buildings deductible under the capital works rules, R&D assets and Australian film investments. A balancing adjustment event covers assets "sold, lost or destroyed", so an insurance recovery is a termination value too.

Destroyed and written-off assets enter it through insurance and deemed amounts, and the exclusions carve out pooled small business assets and buildings, so a firm that sold its factory and its pooled plant shows very little here. Read with the asset first-deducted labels, it cannot be netted to a capital expenditure figure.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductions claimed under temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: What the business wrote off under temporary full expensing, the COVID-era immediate deduction for the full cost of eligible assets. The ATO tells lodgers to "Show the total amount of any deduction under temporary full expensing you claimed at Depreciation expenses", so the amount is a subset of the depreciation expense already reported, not an addition to it. The measure ran from 7:30 pm AEDT on 6 October 2020 and "Temporary full expensing ended on 30 June 2023".

The window also makes an investment series discontinuous: a firm's capital spending looks to collapse after 2022-23 when what actually ended was the concession, and second-hand assets were eligible only for firms under $50 million of aggregated turnover.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many assets the business claimed temporary full expensing on that year - a count of assets, not an amount of money. The ATO instruction for the label is to "Show the total number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", and it sits directly beside the deduction amount, so the two together give an average cost per asset written off. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules do not complete it, since their assets go through the pool.
value_definition: An integer count for one income year, held as up to five characters in the data item list, reported at item P11 on the sole trader schedule and the matching labels of the other returns.
limitation: The count is not comparable between firms in different depreciation regimes: a small business using simplified depreciation writes off the same investment through the pool and reports nothing here, so a zero count with a positive deduction is expected rather than an error. Asset improvements as well as acquisitions can carry the concession, so the count is not a count of purchases.
rationale: The ATO label guide gives the instruction for the count label and states that entities using simplified depreciation leave the related temporary full expensing labels blank.

value_domain: Coded choice to opt out of temporary full expensing for some, all or no eligible assets
value_source: ATO, Opting out of temporary full expensing
variable_description: Whether the business chose to keep some, all or none of its eligible assets out of temporary full expensing that year. The ATO states that "You can make a choice to opt out of temporary full expensing for an income year on an asset-by-asset basis if you are not using the simplified depreciation rules", and that from 1 July 2021 the tax return is how the choice is notified: "The choice is unchangeable and you must notify us by the day you lodge your tax return for the income year to which the choice relates." The number and value of the assets opted out sit in the two columns beside it.

value_domain: Count of eligible assets the entity opted out of temporary full expensing for
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many eligible assets the business chose to keep out of temporary full expensing, so that they depreciate under the ordinary rules instead. It is the count that goes with the opt-out choice code and the opt-out value on the same row, and the ATO limits who can report it: "You cannot opt out of temporary full expensing for assets that the simplified depreciation rules apply to." A positive count therefore identifies a firm outside simplified depreciation that actively declined an immediate write-off.

value_domain: Dollar value of eligible assets opted out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: The value of the assets the business chose to keep out of temporary full expensing, which it then depreciates under the general rules. It is the money counterpart of the opt-out count and opt-out choice columns on the same row, and it exists only where the firm was outside the simplified depreciation rules, since the ATO states "You cannot opt out of temporary full expensing for assets that the simplified depreciation rules apply to." A firm typically opts out to spread deductions into later years rather than take them all in a loss year.

The choice was also unchangeable once the return was lodged, so a later amendment of the underlying asset position leaves this figure standing.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at total business income on the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Income - P8
variable_description: The entity's total business income for the year as reported on the return. It is the primary production and non-primary production columns added together, built by instruction rather than definition: "Add up the amounts at TOTAL BUSINESS INCOME in the Primary production and Non-primary production columns and write the total in the adjacent Totals box." It is gross income before any expense, and a loss is flagged with a separate code rather than a minus sign.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one income year, equal to the sum of the two column totals reported beside it and of the individual income labels that feed them.
limitation: It is not the entity's income. Interest, dividends, distributions from partnerships and trusts, net capital gains, foreign income and - on a sole trader's schedule - personal services income are all reported elsewhere on the return and are excluded here by instruction, so business income can be small for an entity with substantial receipts.
rationale: The ATO income instruction sets out exactly which labels are added to reach total business income and which income types must not be shown in the item.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total business income, non-primary production column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Income - P8

Adding it to the primary production column gives total business income on the same row.

limitation: The split is a tax classification of income, not an industry code. A farm with a contracting or agistment sideline reports in both columns, so a non-zero value here cannot exclude an agricultural business, and an ANZSIC-based industry population cannot be built from the split.
rationale: The ATO income instruction lists the specific labels summed into the non-primary production column, which is what distinguishes it from the primary production column beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of total business income, primary production column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Income - P8
variable_description: The primary production half of the entity's business income - what it earned from farming, fishing or forestry activity. The ATO builds it from a smaller set of labels than the non-primary production column: "Add up the primary production amounts shown at P8 Income - labels C, E, G and I", and primary producers are directed to a separate worksheet that brings in livestock and produce accounts before the column is filled. Farm household and averaging concessions turn on income being classified this way.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at total expenses on the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Expenses - P8
variable_description: Everything the entity reported as a business expense for the year, from cost of sales through to all other expenses. The ATO builds it by instruction: "Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses", then the same for non-primary production, then the two together. Subtracting it from total business income gives the net business profit or loss before any reconciliation item.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one income year, being the sum of the individual expense labels reported above it, and able to be negative where an expense account is in credit, in which case the return carries a loss code.
limitation: It is an accounting total, not deductions. The reconciliation items - the section 40-880 deduction, project pool, landcare and the expense reconciliation adjustment - all sit outside it, so total business income less total expenses is not taxable income and cannot be treated as it.
rationale: The ATO expense instruction states which labels are added to form the total and how a negative total is flagged, and the company return carries the same total at item 6 label Q.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at total salary and wage expenses on the income tax return
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2025 instructions, item 8 Financial and other information
variable_description: The entity's total wage bill for the year, including directors' remuneration and the wage component buried inside cost of sales. It is reported as a memorandum item, not as one of the expense labels that add to total expenses.

limitation: It is not total labour cost and not a deduction. Superannuation, contractors and labour hire are excluded by instruction, so a firm that outsources its workforce looks to have almost no labour; and payments made without meeting PAYG withholding obligations remain in this accounts figure while being denied as deductions.
rationale: The company return item 8 instruction defines the label, lists what is included and excluded, and describes the accompanying code box; the sole trader schedule gives the same inclusions and exclusions at P15.

value_domain: Code identifying which expense line the salary and wage expenses were reported in
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, Total salary and wage expenses - P15
variable_description: Which expense line of the return the entity's wage bill was reported in - cost of sales, all other expenses, both, or somewhere else. The ATO asks the lodger to "Select the letter that matches the description of the expense component where the salary and wage expenses have been wholly or predominantly reported", with C for cost of sales, A for all other expenses, B for both and O for other expense components. It exists because the salary and wage total is a memorandum figure that is already counted inside one or more of the expense labels.

limitation: It cannot be used to strip wages out of cost of sales. The code marks where the wage bill was wholly or predominantly reported, not how it was split, so a B row gives no basis for apportioning the total between the two lines. It also says nothing about the workforce itself - headcount, hours and composition are absent.

value_domain: De-identified BLADE business unit identifier
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment, BLADE
variable_description: The de-identified business this row belongs to, and the key that joins a firm's records across every BLADE module. The ABS says BLADE "combines taxation and other administrative data at the ABS Economics Model Unit level", so the unit behind the identifier is a statistical business rather than a legal entity: for the non-profiled population "one ABN equates to one business", while large and complex groups are represented by type of activity units the ABS maintains itself. The ID to BN key table is the crosswalk that ties this identifier to the business number key used elsewhere in the asset.
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier with no meaning in its digits, stable for a unit across years and modules within an extract, and not derived from the ABN in any recoverable way.
limitation: It is not an ABN and cannot be taken back to a named business, and it is not a company: counting distinct identifiers counts ABS statistical units, so a corporate group that the ABS has profiled contributes several units while a group of related private companies that it has not contributes one per ABN. Identifiers also need not be comparable across extract vintages.
rationale: The ABS microdata page states the unit level BLADE is built at, and the counts methodology defines the two-population model that decides whether a unit is an ABN or a type of activity unit; no published page names this column directly.
evidence_quote: For the non-profiled population, one ABN equates to one business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Identifier - deidentified unit_id' from the data item list with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what unit the identifier stands for or what joining on it does.

value_domain: De-identified customs import declaration number
value_source: ABS, International Trade in Goods methodology, June 2026
variable_description: The customs import declaration this row came from, de-identified - one lodgement, not one business and not one shipment. The declarations go to the Department of Home Affairs, and the ABS states that it "compiles import and export declarations, as lodged with The Department of Home Affairs", and that merchandise trade statistics are "primarily compiled from customs declarations submitted by exporters and importers or their agents". Rows sharing this number are commodity lines of a single declaration, so it is the natural key for collapsing an import event.
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric de-identified number, unique to a declaration within the imports collection, with no meaning in its digits and no relationship to the importing business identifier on the same row.
limitation: A declaration is a customs event, not a purchase: it may be lodged by a broker or agent on the importer's behalf, it can be amended and relodged, and one declaration can cover many commodity lines and several suppliers. Counting declarations therefore counts paperwork, and the ABS itself warns that most transactions are as reported to Customs and that care is needed with detailed estimates.
rationale: The ABS trade in goods methodology states where import declarations come from, who lodges them and what quality caveats attach, which is what a reader of a declaration-level identifier needs.

value_domain: Dealroom sports industry tag flag
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Industries and sub-industries
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tagged this business to its sports industry, meaning firms in athletic performance, fan engagement or fitness technology. value_definition: A binary flag: 1 where the tag applies, 0 where it does not, and . where Dealroom holds no industry information for the ABN. It is one of about thirty industry tags in the Dealroom taxonomy, which are not mutually exclusive and do not form an exhaustive classification.
limitation: It is not an industry code and cannot be reconciled with the firm's ANZSIC division: a wearables maker, a stadium ticketing platform and a gym app all carry the same flag, while a sporting goods manufacturer outside Dealroom's tracked population carries none. A 0 therefore means untagged, which for most Australian businesses means unobserved rather than not in sport.
rationale: The Dealroom knowledge base publishes the industry taxonomy behind these flags and gives the sports definition in the same words the BLADE data item list carries, which confirms the tag is Dealroom's and not the ABS's.
evidence_quote: Sports startups create technology, products, and services that improve athletic performance, fan engagement, and fitness experiences.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the data item list wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said who assigns the tag, that the tags overlap, or that coverage is limited to firms Dealroom tracks.
