value_domain: Self-reported Indigenous control of the company, R&D Tax Incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether the company said its board or management committee is majority Indigenous, answered when it registered R&D activities for the tax incentive. The application asks "Is the company Indigenous controlled (where at least 51% of the organisation's board or management committee are Indigenous)?" with the options Yes, No and Prefer not to answer, and the department explains the question is asked because "Indigenous ownership and Indigenous controlled details are required as part of policy and program development, review and evaluation". Control is about who governs the company, which is why it sits beside indigenousowned, the question about who holds the shares.
value_definition: A categorical response taking Yes, No, N/A or Prefer not to answer. It is a registration-form answer for one income year rather than a verified register entry, and there is no partial or percentage response.
limitation: The population is companies that registered R&D activities, so the field says nothing about Indigenous control of Australian business generally, and it can only be observed in the years a company registered. Prefer not to answer is a real and non-random category, so treating anything other than Yes as No understates Indigenous-controlled firms.
rationale: The published R&D Tax Incentive application form questions carry this exact question, its 51 per cent board threshold and its response options, which is the instrument that generates the BLADE column.
evidence_quote: Is the company Indigenous controlled (where at least 51% of the organisation's board or management committee are Indigenous)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form's wording as the description and used the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the answer is self-reported at registration, that the population is R&D claimants, or how the non-response option behaves.

value_domain: Self-reported Indigenous ownership of the company, R&D Tax Incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive application form questions (business.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether the company said its members or proprietors are majority Indigenous, answered on its R&D Tax Incentive registration. The form asks "Is the company Indigenous owned (where at least 51% of the organisation's members or proprietors are Indigenous)?", with Yes, No and Prefer not to answer as the choices. Ownership and control are asked separately and can differ: a company can be majority Indigenous owned while its board is not, which is why the answer here need not match indigenouscontrolled on the same row.
value_definition: A categorical response of Yes, No, N/A or Prefer not to answer, recorded once per registration. The 51 per cent test is applied by the company itself when it answers, not by the department.
limitation: It is a claim about equity held at registration and carries no evidence: no supporting documentation, Supply Nation certification or Indigenous Business Register check stands behind the answer. It also cannot be read as a business count, since only companies that register R&D activities are asked at all.
rationale: The published application form questions give this question, its 51 per cent ownership threshold and its options, and set out why the department collects it, which is the origin of the BLADE column.
evidence_quote: Is the company Indigenous owned (where at least 51% of the organisation's members or proprietors are Indigenous)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form wording as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not distinguish ownership from control or warn that the answer is unverified.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering both product and process innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter was classified as both a new product and a new way of making or doing something. It is the overlap of the two flags beside it, so a row with innovation_both set to 1 should also be readable as product and process together rather than as a third, separate kind of invention. The classification attaches to the patent application, not to the firm, so a business-level measure has to be built by aggregating its applications.
value_definition: A numeric flag taking 0 or 1 on the IPRAPID applications table. It is a derived variable rather than an IP Australia register field, and it applies only to patents, so trade mark and design rows carry no meaningful value.
limitation: How the classification was made is not published in the IP RAPID data dictionary, so the reader cannot check whether it came from patent claim text, the IPC marks or a model, and cannot judge its error rate. Nor does it say anything about commercialisation: a patent classified as both is a description of the document, not evidence that the firm brought either innovation to market.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary documents the applications table this column sits in but contains no product or process innovation field, so the derivation is unpublished and the meaning is read from the label, from the pair of flags beside it and from the standard product against process distinction used in innovation statistics.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label 'Whether the patent relates to both a process and product innovation' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record that the flag is derived, undocumented and defined on the application rather than the firm.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering a process innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter is a method or process - a new way of making, treating or doing something - rather than an artefact. Process patents are the ones usually read as evidence of production or efficiency improvement, which is why they are separated from product patents in productivity research. The flag sits on the application row in IPRAPID and is not mutually exclusive with innovation_product, since a single specification can claim both.
value_definition: A numeric 0 or 1 flag on the IPRAPID applications table, defined for patents. It is derived rather than reported by the applicant, and there is no accompanying strength or confidence score.
limitation: A process patent is a claim to a method, not proof that the firm adopted it: patents are frequently filed defensively or licensed out, so the flag cannot stand in for process innovation as the Oslo-style business surveys measure it. Because the derivation is not documented in IP Australia's IP RAPID dictionary, misclassification cannot be bounded.
rationale: No published IP Australia or ABS documentation for this derived column could be fetched, so the description rests on the label, on the neighbouring product and both flags, and on the settled meaning of process innovation in patent research.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Whether the patent relates to a process innovation' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, and gave no warning that the flag is an undocumented derivation.

value_domain: Derived flag for a patent covering a product innovation
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: A derived flag marking a patent application whose subject matter is a thing - an apparatus, device, compound or composition - rather than a method. Product patents are usually treated as the closer proxy for new goods reaching a market, and the split from innovation_process is what allows a firm's patent portfolio to be read as output-facing or production-facing. The flag is defined on the application, so a firm with many applications carries many rows.
value_definition: A numeric 0 or 1 flag on the IPRAPID applications table, meaningful only for patent rows. It is a derived classification of the specification, not a field an applicant supplies.
limitation: It says nothing about whether the product exists: an application can be abandoned, refused or never worked, and the flag is set from the document regardless of the status column beside it. Filing strategy also differs by technology, so a rise in product-flagged patents can reflect drafting practice rather than a change in what firms are inventing.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary covers the applications table but not this flag, so no fetchable source defines it; the meaning is assembled from the label, the sibling flags and the standard product against process reading of patent claims.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Whether the patent relates to a product innovation' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate the document-level classification from any statement about commercialisation.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause flag, non work-related illness or injury insurance
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 Data Collection Framework
variable_description: Whether the federal enterprise agreement on this row contains an insurance scheme covering absence from work for illness or injury that did not happen at work. The DEWR framework defines the field as covering an agreement that "provides for an insurance scheme covering absence from work due to a non work-related illness or injury", notes that employees may have to "cash in" part of their sick leave to pay the premiums, and states that it "also covers 'Income Protection Insurance' that relates to non work-related injury or illness". The framework keeps it strictly apart from the redundancy income protection field, which is a different clause type. The unit is the agreement, coded by departmental analysts from the approved document, not the employer or the employee.
value_definition: A presence flag written as Y when the clause is found. There is no explicit N: an agreement without the provision is simply left blank, and the field is one of about two hundred conditions items coded per agreement.
limitation: Blank is ambiguous and is the trap here - it can mean no such clause, or a year in which the item was not part of the coding framework, since DEWR reviews the conditions collected each year and codes conditions only for agreements approved from 1 January 1997. A Y also says nothing about the premium, the benefit or how many of the covered employees ever used the scheme.
rationale: The WAD 2021 Data Collection Framework, published by DEWR as the introduction to the dataset, carries this field with the exact description the BLADE data item list reproduces, and the department's WAD page states the 1997 start for conditions coding and the annual review of the fields.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides for an insurance scheme covering absence from work due to a non work-related illness or injury.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the framework text as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence used as both definition and limitation, so it did not say that the unit is the agreement, that only Y is recorded, or that conditions coding begins in 1997.

value_domain: Currency code of the export invoice
value_source: ABS, Export and Import Invoice Currencies, 2023-24
variable_description: The currency the exporter billed this consignment in, before the value was converted to Australian dollars. The ABS defines an invoice currency as "the currency in which an invoice for exported or imported goods is denominated, prior to conversion to Australian Dollar (AUD)", and on the export side it is the ABS that does the conversion, "using Reserve Bank of Australia daily exchange rates, based on the date of departure of the goods". The code is reported to the Department of Home Affairs on the export declaration, so it is administrative rather than survey data, and it describes one shipment rather than the firm's usual practice.
value_definition: A short character currency code from the code list at Appendix 8 of the data item list, using the standard three-letter abbreviations such as USD, AUD, JPY and CNY. It is a categorical attribute of the transaction line, carried alongside the AUD value on the same row.
limitation: There is almost no variation to exploit: the ABS reports that 88.9 per cent of merchandise exports by value were invoiced in United States dollars in 2023-24 and 8.8 per cent in Australian dollars, and the mix is driven by commodity composition, with metalliferous ores invoiced in USD for more than 99 per cent of value. It is also not a measure of currency exposure, because exporters that hedge value the transaction at the hedged rate rather than the prevailing one.
rationale: The ABS article defines invoice currency, states that Home Affairs collects it and passes it to the ABS with the rest of the merchandise trade information, sets out the export-side conversion method, and publishes the currency shares and the hedging caveat.
evidence_quote: An invoice currency is the currency in which an invoice for exported or imported goods is denominated, prior to conversion to Australian Dollar (AUD).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'A code to indicate the currency of the invoice' and pointed at an appendix, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say who converts the value, at what rate, or how concentrated the codes are.

value_domain: Currency code of the import invoice
value_source: ABS, Export and Import Invoice Currencies, 2023-24
variable_description: The currency the overseas supplier billed this import in, recorded on the import declaration before conversion to Australian dollars. Imports differ from exports in who converts: the ABS states that "For imports, the Department of Home Affairs converts values reported in foreign currencies to the AUD using exchange rates applicable on the date of departure of the goods from the overseas country", and that the ABS receives the invoice currency together with the transaction value already denominated in AUD. The import currency mix is far more varied than the export one, so this column carries more information about a firm's trading relationships than its export counterpart does.
value_definition: A short character currency code taken from the Appendix 8 code list, in the usual three-letter form such as USD, AUD, RMB and EUR, attached to the import transaction line rather than to the business as a whole.
limitation: The foreign-currency amount is unrecoverable from BLADE: only the converted AUD value arrives with the code, so the original invoice value cannot be reconstructed and firm-level exchange rate pass-through cannot be measured from this column alone. Australian dollar invoicing is also common on imports, 31.9 per cent of value in 2023-24, so an AUD code does not mean a domestic transaction.
rationale: The ABS article defines the invoice currency concept, describes the import-side conversion performed by Home Affairs before the data reach the ABS, and publishes the 2023-24 import currency shares.
evidence_quote: The ABS is provided details of the invoice currency, combined with the value of the import transaction denominated in the AUD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the one-line label and the appendix reference with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the import conversion from the export one or warn that the foreign-currency value is not carried.

value_domain: IP right sub-type on the IP RAPID application table
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
variable_description: Which kind of patent or trade mark the application is, within the broader right type. IP Australia lists the patent sub-types as "standard_complete", "provisional", "innovation (phasing out)" and "petty (no longer a current type)", and the trade mark sub-types as "trade_mark", "collective_trade_mark", "certification_trade_mark" and "defensive_trade_mark", noting that "Designs and PBRs do not have sub-types". The distinction carries most of the economic content of a patent filing: a provisional is a cheap twelve-month priority claim, while a standard complete application is the one that can be examined and granted.
value_definition: A categorical string from the fixed sub-type list above, populated for patent and trade mark rows and empty for design and plant breeder's right rows. It qualifies ip_right_type on the same row rather than replacing it.
limitation: Counting sub-types will double count one invention: a firm typically files a provisional and then a standard complete application for the same idea, and both are rows here. The innovation patent has also been closed to new filings, so a fall in that sub-type after 2021 is the end of a scheme rather than a fall in inventive activity.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary is IP Australia's own documentation for the source of this BLADE module, and Table 1 defines the field and enumerates its permitted values.
evidence_quote: Patents and trade marks have specific sub-types of right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the sentence 'Patents and trade marks have specific sub-types of right' with a pointer to an appendix, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the actual sub-types and their economic meaning were missing.

value_domain: IP right type: trade mark, design, patent or plant breeder's right
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
variable_description: Which of IP Australia's registers the application belongs to, and half of the key that identifies it. The dictionary sets the permitted values as trade_mark, design, patent and pbr, and states that "The primary key for the application table is both the application_number and the ip_right_type", so an application number is only unique within a right type. It repeats on the party, events and classification tables for the same reason, which is why it appears many times across the IPRAPID module.
value_definition: A categorical string with four permitted values - trade_mark, design, patent and pbr - although the BLADE data item list shows design, patent and trade_mark for the tables it carries. It is one half of a composite key, not a descriptive attribute.
limitation: The four rights are not comparable units and must not be pooled into an IP count: a trade mark protects a brand indefinitely on renewal, a standard patent protects an invention for twenty years, and a design protects appearance for up to ten. Joining on application_number alone without this column silently mixes unrelated filings.
rationale: IP Australia's IP RAPID data dictionary defines the field, lists its values and states its role in the composite primary key of the application table and in every joined table.
evidence_quote: The primary key for the application table is both the application_number and the ip_right_type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Type of IP right' and listed the codes with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it missed that the column is part of the join key and that the four rights are not a single countable unit.

value_domain: BLADE integration version identifier for the IPLORD module
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data row, an internal reference rather than anything about the IP right. IPLORD is IP Australia's applicant-centred view of Australian filings, supplied to BLADE alongside IPRAPID, and this code pins the linkage run in which the applicant was matched to an ABN and then to the BLADE spine. It describes vintage, not content: two rows with different values can be the same filing seen through two integrations.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric code identifying the integration, with no ordering, date component or published code list.
limitation: It is not a date and cannot be ordered, so it will not serve as a data vintage or a reference period, and it says nothing about the IP right's own timing, which comes from the filing and event dates. Stacking two versions of the same module without filtering on this column duplicates filings, because the linkage is redone rather than appended.
rationale: No published ABS documentation of the BLADE integration version codes could be fetched; the reading rests on the data item list label, on the same column appearing across IP modules, and on the ABS BLADE overview page, which names IPLORD as one of the IP Australia inputs to the asset.
evidence_quote: Intellectual Property Australia: Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD) and Intellectual Property Refreshed Automated Product for Information (IPRAPID)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not warn against reading the code as a vintage or against pooling versions.

value_domain: BLADE integration version identifier for the IPRAPID module
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this IPRAPID row. The code is carried on every table of the module, so applications, parties, events and classifications can be held to one consistent run. The data item list shows a single observed value, in285_v1, which is what a stable code looks like while only one integration has been loaded. IP RAPID is refreshed weekly at IP Australia and re-resolves parties by name and address matching, so the run a row came from matters more here than in a static source.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric categorical code. It is constant within an integration and shared across all IPRAPID tables, which makes it a filter rather than an analytical variable.
limitation: Because party identifiers are rebuilt at each refresh, the same applicant can carry different party groupings in two versions, so mixing them breaks firm-level portfolio counts rather than merely adding rows. The code also carries no extract date, so it cannot tell you how current the IP records on a row are.
rationale: No ABS documentation of the version codes could be fetched, so the reading comes from the data item list, from the column recurring on six IPRAPID tables, and from IP Australia's dictionary statement that party identifiers are resolved by name and address matching at each build.
evidence_quote: Unique ID for a given party. Calculated using the resolved group of raw applicants based on name and address matching.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Integration version of dataset (internal ABS reference)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice and did not explain why the column exists on every IPRAPID table.

value_domain: Boolean flag for the earliest party in a role on an IP right
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether this business was the first party recorded in its role on the IP right, which is how an original applicant is told apart from a later owner. IP Australia describes it as "A Boolean flag that indicates if the party was the earliest party on record in that role" and says why it is there: "Many economic analyses are interested in the parties who originally engaged with the IP Right system to apply for a right." Filtering on it gives the firm that filed, where the is_current flag beside it gives the firm that holds the right at extract, and for an assigned or sold right those are different businesses.
value_definition: A boolean stored as 0 for No and 1 for Yes, defined per party role on the party table, with effective_from_date and effective_to_date bounding the role episode.
limitation: Founding is per role, not per right, so more than one party can be flagged on the same application - an original applicant and an original agent both qualify - and counting flagged rows is not counting filings. It also records the earliest party on record, so a transfer done before IP Australia's records begin, or a right filed by a related entity, shows as founding for the wrong business.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary defines this exact field on the party table and states the analytical purpose it was built for, alongside the is_current flag it should be read against.
evidence_quote: A Boolean flag that indicates if the party was the earliest party on record in that role. Many economic analyses are interested in the parties who originally engaged with the IP Right system to apply for a right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the dictionary's first sentence alone and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say the flag is per role or how it differs from is_current.

value_domain: Boolean flag for whether an IP right event still officially stands
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary (data.gov.au)
variable_description: Whether the event on this row is still officially part of the IP right's history, or has been retroactively undone. IP Australia keeps events that no longer have legal force so the administrative story stays readable, and explains that "Only events which have TRUE for this field are legal events for the purposes of IP Australia history", with the plain instruction: "if the record it is standing, you can trust it. If the record no longer stands, you should use it with caution." Revocations, court-ordered expungements and migrations between IP Australia's record systems are what set it to FALSE.
value_definition: A boolean stored as 0 for FALSE and 1 for TRUE on the IPRAPID events table, defined per event row rather than per application.
limitation: Ignoring the flag inflates event counts and can create impossible sequences, such as a revocation with no acceptance before it, because a superseded history is present in the same table as the live one. It is also not the same thing as being on the register or as being current, so it cannot be used to work out whether a firm holds a right today.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary defines the field on the events table and devotes a section, 'What is is_standing?', to why retroactively removed events are retained and how they should be treated.
evidence_quote: This field defines whether a history record remains something which is officially recorded as having happened to the IP right (TRUE) or if a business process has retroactively made the event to have never happened (FALSE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the dictionary sentence as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never told a reader that unfiltered event counts include histories IP Australia has withdrawn.

value_domain: Count of accelerator investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many of the business's known backers are accelerators, the fixed-term programs that take a small stake in return for seed money, mentoring and a demo day. A non-zero count marks a firm that went through a structured early-stage program rather than one that simply raised money, which is why it is kept apart from investors_inc_n for incubators. Like every Dealroom field in BLADE it is time invariant and written on every year of the ABN, so it dates nothing.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of distinct investors carrying the accelerator type, with . for missing. An investor can hold more than one type, so the type counts overlap and do not add to investors_n.
limitation: It carries no dollars and no date, so two accelerators can mean less capital than none, and a firm accelerated in 2015 looks identical in 2012. It also cannot say whether the program was finished or the equity still held.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the investor concept and the tracked company population behind the count, but publishes no separate accelerator definition, so the type's meaning is read from the data item list wording and general knowledge of accelerator programs.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Dealroom's paragraph as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the count is undated, overlapping and limited to firms Dealroom tracks.

value_domain: Count of advisor investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many of the business's recorded investors are investment banks or financial advisory firms, which Dealroom counts as an investor type in their own right. Advisors usually appear on larger or more complicated rounds, so a non-zero count is a weak signal of deal complexity rather than of a new source of capital. The count is an attribute of the ABN, repeated unchanged across its years in BLADE.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investors tagged advisor. Investor types are not exclusive, so an entity counted here can also be counted in another investors_ column.
limitation: An advisor is normally paid a fee to run a transaction rather than committing its own money, so adding this column to the others overstates how many parties actually funded the firm. Dealroom also tags advisory businesses as service providers elsewhere in its taxonomy, so the same firm can be recorded twice under two different ideas of what it did.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page establishes what an investor record is and how the tracked population is drawn, but does not publish an advisor definition, so the description is assembled from the data item list text and standard practice in advised rounds.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not flag that an advisor is usually a paid intermediary rather than a capital provider.

value_domain: Count of individual angel investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many named individuals are recorded as investing their own money in the business. Dealroom builds this from its people records: "A people entity that makes various investments into companies is considered as an Individual Angel investor." It counts individuals only, so an angel who invests through a syndicate vehicle is counted in investors_angelfund_n instead, and the two columns cannot be added without double counting the same person's money.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of distinct individuals tagged as angels, with . for missing. It counts people rather than legal entities, which is what separates it from every other investors_ column.
limitation: Angel participation is the least completely recorded part of any private-market database, since individuals are often unnamed in round announcements, so a zero is at least as likely to mean undisclosed as to mean none. The count also says nothing about how much each angel put in, and it never falls when an angel sells out.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the individual angel investor as a people entity that invests, which is the record type this count is built from, and sets out the tracked company population that bounds it.
evidence_quote: A people entity that makes various investments into companies is considered as an Individual Angel investor.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's paragraph and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the count is of people, that it overlaps angel funds, or that undisclosed angels read as zero.

value_domain: Count of angel fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many angel funds - vehicles through which individual angels invest collectively - are recorded as backing the business. Dealroom treats the angel fund as a sub-type of investment fund and attributes the investment to the fund rather than to the individuals inside it. That makes this column the pooled counterpart of investors_angel_n, which counts named individuals investing in their own right.
value_definition: A non-negative integer, . where missing, counting distinct entities tagged angel fund. Because angel funds sit inside the investment fund family, the same entity can also be counted in investors_inv_n.
limitation: One vehicle is one investor no matter how many people stand behind it, so a syndicate of thirty angels adds 1 here while the same thirty investing directly would add 30 to investors_angel_n. Adding the two columns to measure angel involvement therefore mixes two incompatible units.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines investment funds and the investor concept but does not publish a separate angel fund definition, so the meaning comes from the data item list text and the fund-of-individuals structure it describes.
evidence_quote: According to Investopedia : " An investment fund is a supply of capital belonging to numerous investors used to collectively purchase securities while each investor retains ownership and control of his own shares".
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the entity and the individual counts are on different units.

value_domain: Count of operating company investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many ordinary companies, as opposed to funds or individuals, are recorded as having invested in this business. It is the broadest of the company-shaped investor tags and sits above the narrower corporate and corporate venture fund tags rather than beside them. In BLADE the count is fixed for the ABN, so it describes the firm's investor register over its whole recorded life, not a particular year.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investor entities that are companies. Investor types overlap, so a single backer can appear in this count and in investors_corporate_n at the same time.
limitation: It does not separate a strategic backer from a founder's own holding company or a parent funding its subsidiary, so a high count can be a group structure rather than external support. Summing it with investors_corporate_n and investors_cvf_n counts the same corporate group up to three times.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page explains how companies become investor records once they invest, but publishes no standalone company investor-type definition, so the description is built from that page, the data item list wording and the neighbouring corporate columns.
evidence_quote: Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies, for example .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line Dealroom text with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it did not explain the overlap with the corporate columns or the group-structure confusion.

value_domain: Count of corporate investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many established companies backed this business directly, as distinct from through a venture arm. Dealroom's tag turns on founding date, not size: "Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies", while companies founded before 1990 are labelled mature as well. Read against investors_cvf_n, this column is the parent investing off its own balance sheet rather than through a fund.
value_definition: A non-negative integer, . where missing, counting distinct investor entities tagged corporate. The tag is applied by Dealroom when a company first invests, so the count reflects the investor's status rather than the recipient's.
limitation: The date-based rule hides the largest backers: a bank or miner founded before 1990 is tagged mature, so corporate venture money from Australia's oldest firms need not raise this count at all. It is also silent on strategy - a supplier taking a small stake and an acquirer building a position look the same.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page states the rule that produces the corporate tag, including the founding-date condition and the mature label that applies instead to older companies, which is what governs when this count moves.
evidence_quote: Companies founded after 1990 are labeled as 'corporate' (without the 'mature' tag, given their founding date) as soon as they make investments in other companies, for example .
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's descriptive paragraph and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the founding-date rule that decides which corporates are counted was missing.

value_domain: Count of equity crowdfunding platform investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many equity crowdfunding platforms are recorded as an investor in this business. Dealroom scopes the category tightly to "Platforms for equity crowdfunding", so the entity counted is the platform that ran the raise, not the retail investors who subscribed. A count of 1 can therefore sit behind hundreds of new shareholders, which matters for any reading of ownership dispersion.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct crowdfunding platform entities. Platforms are counted once regardless of how many raises or how many subscribers passed through them.
limitation: Reward and donation platforms are outside the definition, so a firm that raised on a pre-sales platform reads zero here even though it raised money from a crowd. The column also cannot show the amount raised or the number of subscribers, which is the part of crowdfunding a reader usually wants.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines crowdfunding entities as equity crowdfunding platforms, which fixes both what is counted and what is excluded from this column.
evidence_quote: Platforms for equity crowdfunding. Example Seedrs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Dealroom paragraph and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not make clear that the unit is the platform rather than the crowd.

value_domain: Count of corporate venture fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many corporate venture funds - the dedicated investment arms of larger companies - are recorded as backing this business. The fund and its parent are separate investor records in Dealroom, which is why this column exists alongside investors_corporate_n rather than inside it. A non-zero count usually marks strategic money with an industrial parent behind it, as opposed to a purely financial venture fund.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged corporate venture fund. As a fund type it also falls within the broader investment fund family that investors_inv_n counts.
limitation: One corporate group can raise two columns at once, because a filter on the parent company in Dealroom also picks up the investments made by its venture arm, so this count and investors_corporate_n are not additive. It also cannot tell you whether the strategic relationship survived, since the count never falls when a corporate parent winds up its fund.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page documents the investor and fund concepts and the relationship between corporates and their venture arms, but publishes no standalone corporate venture fund definition, so the description leans on the data item list text as well.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, and did not warn that the parent and its fund can both be counted.

value_domain: Count of family office investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many family offices - the wealth vehicles of very wealthy individuals or families - are recorded as investors in this business. Dealroom names family offices as one of the investor entity types, and they matter here because they behave differently from funds: no fixed life, no limited partners to report to, and often a longer horizon. The count is fixed for the ABN and does not identify the family behind the office.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged family office. Some family offices also invest through funds they back, in which case the fund rather than the office is the counted investor.
limitation: Family offices disclose selectively and many prefer not to be named at all, so this count is a floor rather than a measure, and a zero cannot be read as no private wealth backing. It is also silent on size, and a single office writing the largest cheque in a round counts the same as one taking a token stake.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page lists family offices within its definition of an investor but publishes no separate family office definition, so the meaning is taken from the data item list wording and from how family offices operate in private markets.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Dealroom paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record that family office coverage is selective and the count is a lower bound.

value_domain: Count of fund of funds investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many funds of funds are recorded as investors in this business, a vehicle that normally allocates to other funds rather than to companies. Because their usual role is one step removed, a non-zero count here is unusual and generally means either a direct co-investment or an attribution of a backed fund's deal to its own investors. The column is written on every year of the ABN and does not date the commitment.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged fund of funds. It is one of the specialised fund types that also sit within the broader investment fund category.
limitation: A non-zero value should not be read as an extra financing round, since the vehicle's normal exposure to the firm is indirect through the funds it backs. Treating it as a distinct capital source alongside investors_vc_n therefore risks counting the same money twice.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines investment funds and the investor record generally but gives no fund of funds definition, so the description rests on the data item list text and on the standard structure of a fund of funds.

value_domain: Count of government investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities

It is the equity channel only, which is what separates it from the grant and tax-offset support recorded elsewhere in BLADE.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct investor entities tagged government. It sits inside the wider government and non-profit grouping that investors_govtnp_n counts.
limitation: It understates public support badly, because the money that reaches most Australian firms arrives as a grant, a loan or an R&D tax offset rather than as equity, and none of those raise this count. The RDTI columns in BLADE catch a different and much larger slice of the same idea.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the government and non-profit entity group that this tag is drawn from, and the entities page also fixes the tracked company population within which the count is observed.

value_domain: Count of combined government and non-profit investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many investors sit in Dealroom's combined public and philanthropic category, which it describes as "Government agencies and non-profit organisations". This is the parent tag of the two narrower columns beside it, so it is the one to use when the question is whether any non-commercial money backed the firm at all. Its value is fixed for the ABN and repeated on every year of the record.

rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the combined government and non-profit entity group in its own words, which is exactly what this tag counts.
evidence_quote: Government agencies and non-profit organisations.

value_domain: Count of incubator investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many incubators are recorded as supporting this business. A non-zero count therefore usually marks a young company with institutional hand-holding rather than one that has raised capital. The value belongs to the ABN and is repeated across its years.

value_domain: Count of investment fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many pooled investment funds are recorded as investors in this business. Dealroom takes the definition from Investopedia: "An investment fund is a supply of capital belonging to numerous investors used to collectively purchase securities while each investor retains ownership and control of his own shares", and it tracks fund types including venture capital, private equity, growth equity, life sciences, renewables and corporate. This is the parent category of the specialised fund columns rather than a leftover bucket beside them.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged investment fund. Angel funds, venture funds and corporate venture funds are sub-types, so those entities are counted here as well as in their own columns.
limitation: It cannot be used as an other-funds residual: subtracting the venture, private equity and angel fund columns from it will not leave a meaningful category, because the same entities are inside it. The count is also of vehicles, not of commitments, so a fund that led four rounds still adds 1.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page gives the investment fund definition it applies and lists the fund types it tracks, which establishes that this tag is the parent of the specialised fund tags.
evidence_quote: According to Investopedia : " An investment fund is a supply of capital belonging to numerous investors used to collectively purchase securities while each investor retains ownership and control of his own shares".

value_domain: Total count of investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many investors Dealroom has recorded in this business in total, across every investor type. Dealroom defines an investor as "An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels)", so the total mixes institutions and individuals in one number. It is the denominator for the type columns, but those columns overlap because one investor can carry several types, so they will usually sum to more than this figure.

Coverage is the deeper limit, since Dealroom tracks only companies it judges venture-backable, so a zero for most Australian ABNs means unobserved rather than unfunded.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page gives the investor definition this total is built from and sets out the criteria for the company population it tracks, which is what bounds the column's coverage.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Count of investors in the business' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say that the total is cumulative, that it says nothing about amounts, or how it relates to the type columns.

value_domain: Count of non-profit investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many not-for-profit organisations are recorded as investors in this business, the philanthropic half of Dealroom's combined public and non-profit group. Foundations and mission-driven funds are the usual entities, and they show up most often in health, education and clean energy firms. Because Dealroom records the tag on the investor rather than on the deal, the count says who backed the firm at some point, not when or on what terms.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged non-profit. It is a subset of the combined government and non-profit group counted by investors_govtnp_n.
limitation: Most charitable support reaches firms as a grant or a prize rather than as equity, and none of that appears here, so a zero is compatible with substantial philanthropic funding. An entity can also be tagged both government and non-profit, which means a firm's non-profit count can move with a tagging decision rather than with a financing.
rationale: Dealroom's entities page defines the government and non-profit entity group this tag comes from, but does not separate the non-profit half, so the split reading is inferred from the sibling columns and the data item list wording.
evidence_quote: Government agencies and non-profit organisations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the same Dealroom paragraph as the government and combined columns with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not identify which slice of the group this column holds.

value_domain: Count of private equity investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many private equity investors are recorded as holding a stake in this business. Private equity is one of the fund types Dealroom tracks - "In addition to Venture Capital funds, we also track Private Equity, Growth Equity, Corporate, Life Sciences, Renewables, and Other fund types" - and it is the type most often associated with control positions and restructuring rather than with early-stage growth capital. Growth equity is a separate fund type in the taxonomy, so this column is narrower than a general later-stage measure.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged private equity. As a fund type it is also inside the investment fund category counted by investors_inv_n.
limitation: A private equity investment often changes who owns the firm rather than adding capital to it, and this column cannot separate a growth investment from a change of control; BLADE's own ownership and ABN continuity information is needed for that. It also gives no entry date, so a buyout in the last observed year looks the same as one at the firm's founding.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page names private equity among the fund types it tracks and defines the investment fund concept the tag sits inside, which is what this count is drawn from.
evidence_quote: In addition to Venture Capital funds, we also track Private Equity, Growth Equity, Corporate, Life Sciences, Renewables, and Other fund types.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that a private equity investor can mark a change of ownership rather than new money.

value_domain: Count of pension fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many pension or superannuation funds are recorded as investing directly in this business. Their normal role in private markets is as a limited partner in someone else's fund, so a direct holding is unusual and generally signals a large, late-stage transaction. The count is a fixed attribute of the ABN in BLADE and carries neither the size of the stake nor the year it was taken.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged pension fund. Only direct investments produce a count; money reaching the firm through a fund the pension backs is attributed to that fund instead.
limitation: A zero is the normal case even for firms heavily backed by institutional money, because superannuation capital usually arrives through a venture or private equity manager rather than in the fund's own name. Reading this column as superannuation exposure to the firm therefore understates it by most of the actual amount.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the investor record and the fund types it tracks but publishes no pension fund definition, so the description rests on the data item list wording and on how pension capital ordinarily reaches private companies.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that pension funds normally invest as limited partners and therefore rarely appear.

value_domain: Count of service provider investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many service providers hold an investor record against this business. Dealroom defines a service provider as "A company providing services to other companies on a project basis" and lists consulting, digital services, financial advisory, legal services and recruitment as the industries involved, so a count here usually reflects a supplier that took equity rather than a financier that wrote a cheque. That makes it the least monetary of the investor type columns.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged service provider that also carry an investor record. The tag describes what the entity sells, not how it invested.
limitation: Equity taken in place of fees is not an arm's-length financing, so including this column in a count of investors overstates the capital raised and can make a bootstrapped firm look funded. The column also cannot say which service was supplied, so it will not identify, for example, firms that used a particular adviser.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the service provider entity type and lists the industries it covers, which is what this investor tag is drawn from.
evidence_quote: A company providing services to other companies on a project basis.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the Dealroom paragraph and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not flag that the entity is defined by what it sells rather than by an investment.

value_domain: Count of sovereign wealth fund investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many sovereign wealth funds - state-owned investment vehicles managing national reserves - are recorded as investors in this business. They appear almost exclusively in very large late-stage rounds, so the column functions as a marker of a firm that reached international institutional scale. The count is time invariant on the ABN, so it does not date the investment or say whether the stake is still held.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged sovereign wealth fund. There are few such investors worldwide, so realised values are almost always 0 or 1.
limitation: Because so few Australian firms have this backing, a non-zero value is close to identifying the business, which makes the column disclosive in small cells rather than analytically useful. It also cannot distinguish a direct stake from participation alongside a fund the sovereign investor backs.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the investor record and the tracked population but publishes no sovereign wealth fund definition, so the description is built from the data item list wording and the known behaviour of these investors.
evidence_quote: An entity or individual investing capital in companies (including investment funds (angel funds, VC. PE), Family offices, CVC, Corporates, Angels).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning about how rare and identifying a non-zero value is.

value_domain: Count of university investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many universities hold an investor record against this business. Dealroom's entity type is simply "Educational institutions", and in practice the investing entity is usually a university's commercialisation company or venture fund rather than the university itself. A non-zero count is the clearest Dealroom marker of a spin-out relationship, which is why it is worth reading against the IPRAPID applicant columns elsewhere in BLADE.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct educational institution entities recorded as investors. Whether a university's separate commercialisation arm is recorded under this tag or as a fund is Dealroom's editorial decision.
limitation: It counts equity, not origin: a firm founded on university research that licensed the technology without giving up shares reads zero, so this column will not enumerate spin-outs. It also says nothing about ongoing collaboration, staff involvement or research funding.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines universities as an entity type in its own words, which is the tag this count is built from.
evidence_quote: Educational institutions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the Dealroom text with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it did not distinguish an equity stake from the licensing and collaboration relationships a reader would assume it covers.

value_domain: Count of venture capital investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many venture capital firms are recorded as investors in this business, the single most used signal in the Dealroom module. Venture capital is the first of the fund types Dealroom tracks, and it describes a venture-backed company as one that "has received venture-style equity backing from venture capital or private equity firms, typically in exchange for ownership stakes and accompanied by active investor involvement such as board participation, strategic guidance, and growth oversight". The count is cumulative over the firm's recorded life, so it tallies venture firms ever recorded rather than those on the register today.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged venture capital. Venture funds also sit inside the broader investment fund category, so they are counted in investors_inv_n as well.
limitation: It is a count of firms, not of rounds or dollars, so a company with one investor across a large Series B can outrank a company with four small backers on money while ranking below it here. Corporate venture arms are often tagged corporate venture fund instead, so a well-funded firm can show a surprisingly low venture count.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page names venture capital among the fund types it tracks and defines what venture backing means in its taxonomy, which fixes what this count includes.
evidence_quote: A company that has received venture-style equity backing from venture capital or private equity firms, typically in exchange for ownership stakes and accompanied by active investor involvement such as board participation, strategic guidance, and growth oversight.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried Dealroom's paragraph with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the count is cumulative, unit-free of dollars, or split from corporate venture arms.

value_domain: Count of workspace provider investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many workspace providers hold an investor record against this business. Dealroom defines a workspace as "A company that provides a working environment", so the entity counted supplies desks and facilities, occasionally taking equity in the tenants it hosts. It is a different idea from investors_workl_n, which attributes an investment to a precinct or cluster rather than to a specific provider.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct entities tagged workspace. The tag identifies what the entity provides, so a count can arise from a tenancy arrangement rather than a financing.
limitation: Desk space is not capital, so a firm can show a workspace investor while having raised nothing at all, and including this column in a funding measure overstates support. It also cannot say whether the firm was ever a tenant, since the tag describes the investor and not the relationship.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the workspace entity type in its own words, which is what this investor tag counts.
evidence_quote: A company that provides a working environment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the one-line Dealroom text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate a workspace relationship from an actual investment.

value_domain: Count of workspace location investors recorded against the business
value_source: Dealroom.co Knowledge Base, Entities
variable_description: How many innovation precincts or clusters are recorded as investing in this business through association with it. The unit is a place rather than a company, which is what separates this column from investors_work_n and its named workspace providers. A non-zero count is best read as evidence that the firm was located in or affiliated with a precinct, not that the precinct wrote it a cheque.
value_definition: A non-negative integer with . for missing, counting distinct workspace location entities recorded as investors. Values are almost always 0 or 1, since a firm is normally associated with one precinct at a time.
limitation: Attribution runs through location, so the count can change when a precinct is re-tagged or a firm moves address, with no financing event behind the change. It should not be used as a geography either, because the ABN's address fields elsewhere in BLADE are the proper source for where the firm operates.
rationale: The Dealroom entities page defines the workspace entity but has no separate workspace location definition, so this reading comes from the data item list wording about investment through association with innovation precincts.
evidence_quote: A company that provides a working environment.
