It is only meaningful on lines classified to ores, slag and concentrates, so it is empty for a firm exporting refined metal or anything else.
value_definition: A number expressed as a percentage, recorded against an export transaction classified by the AHECC, the eight-digit Australian extension of the World Customs Organisation Harmonized System. The AHECC edition in force changes with each HS revision, most recently HS2022.
limitation: It is a grade, not a quantity and not a value, so it cannot be summed or averaged across shipments without weighting by tonnage. It also says nothing about the lead a firm sold: an exporter of a polymetallic concentrate reports several metal percentages on the same line, and the revenue split between them is not in the data.
rationale: The AHECC page establishes the classification that governs Australian export lines, including the ore and concentrate classes this column qualifies; no fetchable page was found that defines the metal-percentage field itself, so the reading of it is inferred.
evidence_quote: The Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC) is the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Percentage of lead in shipment of ore' with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never said the column is a grade that has to be combined with weight to mean anything.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag, Y where present
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement covering this employer contains a training leave clause, coded from the agreement text by DEWR. The framework defines the field, numbered 200 and titled "Leave for training purposes (including study/exam)", as one where "The agreement provides for leave (whether paid or unpaid) to attend training." Paid and unpaid provisions are coded the same way, so the flag measures the existence of an entitlement in a document, not its generosity and not what employees took up.
value_definition: A single character, Y where the clause was found. Absence is recorded as a blank rather than an N, so the column is a presence indicator over the agreements DEWR has coded.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as a firm without training leave: it also covers agreements coded before the field existed, employees under awards or individual contracts, and firms with no federal enterprise agreement at all. DEWR notes that "The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database."
rationale: The DEWR collection framework is the coding manual behind the WAD condition fields, and its entry 200 carries the exact wording the BLADE data item list reproduces.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides for leave (whether paid or unpaid) to attend training.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's one-line coding rule with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never warned that a blank is not an N.

value_domain: Dollar amount on the R&D tax incentive registration application
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The part of a levy paid to a research service provider that the provider reported back as spent on supporting R&D activities. It is question 32.6 of the registration application, a flow for the income period being registered, and it appears only where the company answered that it had "Expenditure paid via a levy to a Research Service Provider". The core-activity counterpart is reported separately, and the two together should reconcile to the levy used for providing R&D services.
value_definition: A dollar amount typed into a numeric field, one row per levy-collecting research service provider, since the form lets an applicant add more than one provider.
limitation: Registration is a claim made to AusIndustry before the ATO assesses anything, so this is not a deduction and not an audited amount; the split between core and supporting activities also comes from the levy-collecting body rather than the company. The RDTI module covers 2013-14 to 2020-21, so a zero in other years is an absence of data rather than an absence of levy spending.
rationale: The application guidance defines the levy sub-questions and states who supplies the core and supporting split, which is exactly what this column holds.
evidence_quote: the apportionment of the levies between core and supporting R&D activities as reported to the company by the levy-collecting research service provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Total levy allocated to supporting R&D activities' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the number is a registration claim nor who worked out the split.

value_domain: Dollar amount on the R&D tax incentive registration application
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: The portion of the levy the company paid to a levy-collecting research service provider that went to providing R&D services, question 32.4. The form derives it rather than asking for it: "The levy used for providing R&D services is automatically calculated from the data entered for the total levy paid and the proportion used for providing R&D services." It is therefore the control total that the core-activity and supporting-activity allocations should add up to, not a third independent amount.
value_definition: A dollar amount, calculated from the total levy paid at question 32.2 and the percentage at question 32.3, held one row per levy-collecting research service provider.
limitation: It is smaller than the levy the firm actually paid, because the total levy is a separate field and only the R&D-service share reaches this column, so it understates the cost of belonging to the levy body. Being a derived figure it also inherits any error in the reported proportion, and the guidance tells applicants to go back to the levy body when they are unsure.
rationale: The application guidance names this field, says how it is calculated and states the reconciliation with the core and supporting allocations.
evidence_quote: The levy used for providing R&D services is automatically calculated from the data entered for the total levy paid and the proportion used for providing R&D services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Levy used for providing R&D services' with the generic sentence twice over, so it never distinguished this derived total from the total levy paid or from the two allocations under it.

value_domain: Date attached to an IP application link
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID data dictionary, application-links table
variable_description: The date attached to a link between two intellectual property applications, and which event it dates depends on the link. IP Australia defines it as "The date associated with this linkage. For international rights converting to or entering the Australian IP system, this is the date on which this occurred. For claims of priority, divisional or additional associations, this is usually the application date of the linked_application_number." For a firm-level reader it dates the moment a filing family reached or reorganised inside the Australian system, not the moment the right was granted.
value_definition: A calendar date, carried in BLADE as DD/MM/YYYY, on the links table rather than on the application itself. One application can have several links and therefore several link dates.
limitation: It cannot be used as an invention date or a grant date, and because it often repeats the application date of the other side of the link it can fall years before the Australian filing it sits against. Counting link dates also over-counts activity, since a single patent family generates many link rows.
rationale: The IP RAPID data dictionary defines the application-links table that this BLADE table reproduces, and gives the column its own definition including the two cases it covers.
evidence_quote: The date associated with this linkage. For international rights converting to or entering the Australian IP system, this is the date on which this occurred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's first sentence only, with the generic no-value-list sentence used twice, so it never said which event the date marks or that it is a link attribute rather than an application attribute.

value_domain: IP Australia application link type code
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID data dictionary, table 5 link type definitions
variable_description: What kind of relationship this row records between two IP applications, which is what turns a list of pairs into a filing strategy. The codes are defined separately for each right type, so a patent row can be a conversion (complete_from_a_provisional), a family link (divisional_parent, additional_parent), a priority claim (convention, convention_child) or an association, while a design row uses a shorter list. Read with ip_right_type it tells you whether a firm was broadening a filing, converting one form of protection into another, or claiming an overseas priority date.
value_definition: A lower-case string from a categorical list. IP Australia sets out the permitted values by right type in table 5 of the data dictionary; the BLADE data item list points at the same list as its appendix 19.
limitation: The code names the legal relationship, not its outcome, so a divisional or a conversion recorded here may still have lapsed or been refused. Link types are also right-specific, so counts cannot be pooled across patents, designs, trade marks and plant breeder's rights without deciding which relationships are equivalent.
rationale: The data dictionary defines the column and then enumerates every permitted value against its right type, which is the code list the BLADE metadata refers to but does not carry.
evidence_quote: The type of link represented in the record. Table 5 contains the definitions of each of the link types for each of the IP rights.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's one-line description and pointed at an appendix the registry does not hold, with the generic sentence printed twice, so no value list or interpretation was available on the page.

value_domain: ISO 3166 two-letter country code, with WIPO office codes
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID data dictionary, application-links table
variable_description: Where the application on the other side of the link was filed, which is how you tell a domestic family link from an incoming foreign priority claim. IP Australia defines the field as "Two letter ISO country code. International right filings may also use WIPO two-digit office codes." The value au matters operationally: the dictionary notes that where the country is au the linked application number can in most cases be joined back to the application table, and where it is not, the linked application sits outside IP Australia's own data.
value_definition: A two-character code, lower case in the data. Mostly ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, with WIPO office codes such as those for regional and international offices appearing for international filings.
limitation: It is the country of the linked filing office, not the country of the applicant or of the invention, so an Australian firm's first filing overseas shows a foreign code without telling you anything about where the firm operates. Non-au codes also mark rows whose other side cannot be resolved to an application record in BLADE.
rationale: The data dictionary defines the column and, in the neighbouring row for linked_application_number, explains the join consequence of the au value.
evidence_quote: Two letter ISO country code. International right filings may also use WIPO two-digit office codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the single sentence 'Two letter ISO country code.' as the description with the generic sentence twice below it, so it never said whose country this is or why au behaves differently.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation (Business Locations module)
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this historic business location row, written in the ABS internal in-number form such as in166_v1. It describes the vintage of the record, not the business or the place, and it is the column to check first when two extracts of Business Locations disagree. Business Locations runs in BLADE from 2001-02 to the latest available year, so several versions can sit behind one long panel.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, where the in-number identifies the integration project and the suffix its version.
limitation: It is not a date and does not order cleanly in time, so it cannot be used to work out when a business was at a location; the location dates are separate columns. It is also project-specific, so a version string here means nothing next to the version columns on other BLADE modules.
rationale: The ABS page confirms Business Locations is a standard BLADE module and gives its coverage; the version string itself is documented only as an internal ABS reference in the data item list, so its reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: Business Locations: 2001-02 to latest available
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never told a reader the column is about extract vintage rather than about the business.

value_domain: Weeks of long service leave accrued per year
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How fast long service leave builds up under the agreement, expressed as weeks accrued per year of service. DEWR's field 8, "Accrual ___ weeks per year", records the rate written into the agreement and adds that "This is the rate of accrual in the first ten or fifteen years and ignores subsequent rates of accrual." A firm with 13 weeks after ten years is coded 1.3, so the column is comparable across agreements with different qualifying periods.
value_definition: A decimal number of weeks per year, typically between 1 and 2. The value 111111111 is a sentinel meaning the agreement varies the rate or the quantity is unknown.
limitation: Averaging the column without dropping 111111111 destroys the mean, because that value is a code and not a rate. The rate also covers only the first ten or fifteen years, so it understates entitlements at employers whose agreements accrue faster for long-serving staff, and it says nothing about how much leave was actually taken or paid out.
rationale: The DEWR framework defines the accrual field, the coding convention and the explicit exclusion of later accrual rates, which together explain both the units and the sentinel.
evidence_quote: This is the rate of accrual in the first ten or fifteen years and ignores subsequent rates of accrual.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's coding note as the description and printed the generic sentence twice, so the 111111111 sentinel was listed as a valid response with no warning about what it does to an average.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag, Y where present
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets employees take long service leave on flexible terms rather than as a fixed block. DEWR's field 7 defines it as "Access to taking LSL is flexible, i.e. may be taken at a time negotiated between employer and employee. It may also cover LSL which can be taken at 1/2 pay for an extended period or for half the period at double pay." It is about timing and pay conversion, not about how much leave accrues, which longserviceleaveaccrualrate carries separately.
value_definition: A single character, Y where the clause was found in the agreement, blank otherwise. It is a presence flag over agreements DEWR has coded for conditions, which is those approved from 1 January 1997.
limitation: Half pay for double the period and negotiated timing are coded into the same Y, so the flag cannot separate a genuine cash-flow concession from an ordinary scheduling clause. Cashing out long service leave is a different field again, so a Y here does not imply an employee could convert leave to money.
rationale: The DEWR framework entry is the coding rule the BLADE data item list reproduces word for word, and it names the two distinct arrangements the single flag covers.
evidence_quote: Access to taking LSL is flexible, i.e. may be taken at a time negotiated between employer and employee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated DEWR's coding rule with the generic sentence printed as both definition and limitation, so it never separated this flag from the accrual and cashing-out fields beside it.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at part M of the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part M
variable_description: Whether the company had an employee share scheme running at any point in the income year, answered yes or no at label N of the CGT schedule. The schedule asks it as "Did you have an employee share scheme in place at any time during the year? - to be completed by companies only", so trusts and funds lodging the same schedule leave it blank. The OF prefix on the BLADE label marks this as the old-form wording; the item is not on the current CGT schedule, which no longer asks the question.
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, taken from a yes and no tick box on the paper schedule. Anything else is an invalid or absent response.
limitation: It is a yes or no about the existence of a scheme, so it carries no headcount, no discount value and no indication that the scheme produced a capital gain. Because the question left the schedule, a run of blanks in later years is a form change and not a collapse in employee share schemes, and only entities that had to lodge a CGT schedule at all appear.
rationale: The form itself carries the question, the label letter and the companies-only restriction, and the current schedule instructions no longer contain the item, which fixes both the wording and the end of the series.
evidence_quote: Part M Did you have an employee share scheme in place at any time during the year? - to be completed by companies only
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with its OF prefix unexplained and the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the question is companies-only or that it disappeared from the form.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag, Y where present
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the agreement contains a make-up time clause, letting employees take time off and work the hours back later. DEWR codes it as field 89: "The agreement allows employees to take time off from work and at a later date make up the hours lost." It sits in the hours-of-work group beside mgtmayalterhoursafterconsulting, and the two point in opposite directions, one giving flexibility to the employee and the other to management.
value_definition: A single character, Y where the clause was found, blank otherwise. Coded for federal enterprise agreements from the conditions series that begins with agreements approved on 1 January 1997.
limitation: The flag does not say whether the hours are made up at ordinary rates or whether approval is at the employer's discretion, so it cannot measure how much flexibility the clause delivers. It also cannot be netted against other flexibility clauses to give a firm-level index, because the fields overlap in what they cover.
rationale: The DEWR framework carries the field number and the exact coding rule that the BLADE data item list reproduces.
evidence_quote: The agreement allows employees to take time off from work and at a later date make up the hours lost.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated DEWR's coding rule as the description with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never said the flag describes a document rather than observed practice.

value_domain: Binary flag on the ABN to business unit mapping
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, statistical unit and two-population model
variable_description: Whether this ABN is one of several the ABS maps onto a single Type of Activity Unit, marking it as part of a profiled, complex business. The ABS states that "The relationship between TAUs and their associated legal entities (ABNs) may be one-to-one, many-to-one, or one-to-many", and this flag isolates the many-to-one case. When it is set, tax data reported at ABN level is only a fragment of the activity the ABS attributes to the business.
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing on the ID to BN key table. It describes the mapping, not the business, so it can change when the ABS re-profiles a group.
limitation: It does not identify the other ABNs in the group, so a 1 is a warning rather than a means of aggregation. Summing ABN-level BAS or income tax amounts across a flagged group without going through the TAU will double count some activity and miss the rest, and the flag says nothing about the corporate ownership structure behind the grouping.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the profiled population, the TAU and the three permitted ABN to TAU relationships, which is exactly what the pair of flags on this table separates.
evidence_quote: The relationship between TAUs and their associated legal entities (ABNs) may be one-to-one, many-to-one, or one-to-many.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Many ABNs to one Type of Activity Unit (TAU)' with the generic sentence printed twice, so a reader had no definition of a TAU and no warning about aggregating tax data across the group.

value_domain: Method by which an ABN was matched to a Type of Activity Unit
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, and ANZSIC 2006 numbering system and titles
variable_description: How confidently an ABN was tied to a Type of Activity Unit, graded from an exact match down to a match made only on broad industry. The codes step through the ANZSIC 2006 hierarchy - Class is a four-digit match, Group three digits, SubDiv two digits and Div an industry division - with One-TAU-BG used where the business group holds only one TAU, BG Match where the link rests on the enterprise group alone, and NPP where the ABN belongs to the non-profiled population and has no TAU. The coarser the code, the more the industry and location attached to the ABN are borrowed rather than observed.
value_definition: A short string from a fixed list. The ANZSIC-based codes refer to the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification 2006, whose four-level structure of division, subdivision, group and class gives the codes their ordering.
limitation: NPP is not a failed match: the ABS states that for the non-profiled population "one ABN equates to one business", so those ABNs have no TAU to match to and should not be treated as missing. Nor is the code a quality score that can be compared over time, because re-profiling moves businesses between the two populations and changes the match method for reasons that have nothing to do with the firm.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the two-population model and the TAU, and the ANZSIC page defines the four-level code structure the match levels step through; together they explain every code in the list.
evidence_quote: For the non-profiled population, one ABN equates to one business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's code list with the generic sentence used as both definition and limitation, so it never said the codes are ordered by ANZSIC level or that NPP means no TAU exists.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation (Microdata on Australian Exporters module)
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this row of the Microdata on Australian Exporters panel. It is a housekeeping column about the extract, not about the exporter, and it is what distinguishes two otherwise identical panel rows delivered from different integration projects. MAX is a requestable BLADE module covering 2010-11 to 2024-25, so a long MAX panel can carry more than one version.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string identifying the ABS integration project and its version number.
limitation: It cannot be used as a time variable and does not indicate which version is more complete, so filtering on it silently drops exporters rather than fixing duplicates. It is also not comparable with the version columns on Business Locations or other modules, which are numbered by their own projects.
rationale: The ABS page confirms MAX is a BLADE module and fixes its coverage; the version string is documented only as an internal ABS reference, so its reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: Microdata on Australian Exporters (MAX): 2010-11 to 2024-25
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never told a reader the column identifies an extract rather than an attribute of the exporter.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Mesh Block code, eleven digits
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block that locates the farm business on the Farm Level Analytical Dataset control record. The ABS describes mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions" of the ASGS, so this one code aggregates up to SA1, SA2, LGA and state without a separate lookup. Being on the FLAD control table, it fixes the farm to which the agricultural and financial items on the surrounding tables belong.
value_definition: An eleven-digit numeric maincode from Edition 3 of the ASGS, which took effect in July 2021 and contains 368,286 mesh blocks covering Australia without gaps or overlaps.
limitation: A farm is not a point: the code locates the holding's recorded address, so a property spanning several mesh blocks, or several properties run as one business, still resolve to a single code, and the code cannot be used to place production on the ground. Edition 3 also includes 114 non-spatial special purpose codes, which are not places and have to be excluded before mapping.
rationale: The ABS page defines mesh blocks, gives the Edition 3 count and flags the non-spatial codes, which covers the classification, its edition and the trap in it; FLAD is confirmed as a BLADE module covering 2000-01 to 2019-20.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Maincode of Meshblock' with the generic sentence used twice, so it named neither the geography standard nor its edition, and gave no warning about non-spatial codes.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Mesh Block code, eleven digits
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block containing a business location on the historic Business Locations table, which is the finest geography BLADE holds for where a firm operates. Because Business Locations carries one row per location per period, a multi-site firm has several mesh block codes and no single one stands for the business. The ABS builds Local Government Areas, postal areas, suburbs and electoral divisions by aggregating mesh blocks, so this column is the hook for approximating any of those.
value_definition: An eleven-digit numeric code from Edition 3 of the ASGS, in force from July 2021, assigned on land use as well as population so that residential, commercial and industrial areas are kept apart.
limitation: A location is not employment and not output, so counting businesses by mesh block measures presence rather than activity, and a registered office in a tower can sit in the same mesh block as the firms it fronts for. Codes are also edition-specific: ASGS 2021 mesh blocks are not the 2016 ones renumbered, so a series that spans the change needs a concordance rather than a join.
rationale: The ABS page defines the mesh block, its edition and its role as the building block for non-ABS geographies, which is the whole content of this column.
evidence_quote: The Non ABS structures that will be approximated from Mesh Blocks include Local Government Areas, Postal Areas, Suburbs and Localities (formerly State Suburbs), Commonwealth Electoral Divisions, State Electoral Divisions, Australian Drainage Divisions and Destination Zones.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Mesh Block code' and pointed at ASGS 2021 without explaining what a mesh block is, with the generic sentence printed as both definition and limitation.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag, Y where present
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets management change employees' hours, but only after consulting them. DEWR codes it as field 88: "The agreement lets management change employee hours (shift or non-shift) but only after consultation." It is an employer-side flexibility clause, and the consultation qualifier is part of the definition rather than an aside, so agreements allowing unilateral change are a different field.
value_definition: A single character, Y where the clause was found in the agreement text, blank otherwise.
limitation: It does not record what consultation has to involve or whether the employee can refuse, so it cannot be graded against a clause that requires agreement rather than consultation. Nor does it show that hours were ever changed, since the whole WAD conditions series describes agreement text and not workplace practice.
rationale: The DEWR framework carries the field and the exact coding rule reproduced in the BLADE data item list, including the consultation qualifier.
evidence_quote: The agreement lets management change employee hours (shift or non-shift) but only after consultation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated DEWR's coding rule with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never distinguished consultation from agreement or warned that the flag is a document attribute.

value_domain: Binary indicator that a dollar value is attached to a market event row
value_source: Austrade, Programs, services and policies
variable_description: Whether this row of the Austrade markets table carries a dollar amount in mktdollaramount, rather than recording an involvement with no money attached. Many Austrade engagements are advisory - introductions, market research, coaching through the Landing Pads programme - and produce a market record with no financial value, which is what a 0 marks. It is a structural flag about the row, so it should be read before summing dollar amounts across event types.
value_definition: A numeric binary: 0 for no dollar value, 1 for a dollar value present, one value per market and event row.
limitation: A 0 does not separate an engagement that genuinely involved no money from one whose amount Austrade did not capture, so it cannot be used to prove a firm received no financial support. It also says nothing about the size or the direction of any amount that is present.
rationale: The Austrade page establishes that its exporter programmes include advisory services with no grant attached, which is the case the flag distinguishes; no published page defines the flag itself.
evidence_quote: The Landing Pads program helps tech scaleups to expand in new markets. They include offshore residencies, coaching, in-market connections and introductions to partners and venture capital.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Whether there is any dollar value associated with event type' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said what a 0 can and cannot be taken to mean.

value_domain: Austrade market involvement category
value_source: Austrade, Programs, services and policies
variable_description: What the business's involvement in a given overseas market consisted of, on the Austrade markets table. The list mixes two different things: outcome categories such as Export sales, Winning a Contract or Tender and Foreign direct investment with export outcomes, and service categories such as csmarketresearch, csintroductions and landingpad that name the assistance Austrade gave. Austrade's Landing Pads, for instance, provide "offshore residencies, coaching, in-market connections and introductions to partners and venture capital", so a landingpad row records support delivered rather than trade achieved.
value_definition: A character value from a fixed list of roughly twenty categories, some in title case and some in a lower-case system form prefixed cs for client services.
limitation: Because outcomes and services share one column, counting rows per firm overstates distinct engagements and mixes what a firm did with what Austrade did for it. The categories are also not exclusive over time, so a firm appearing under Interested in one year and Export sales in another has not necessarily converted one into the other.
rationale: The Austrade page names the programmes behind several of the codes, including the Landing Pads and the Go Global Toolkit, which is what the service-side categories refer to.
evidence_quote: The Landing Pads program helps tech scaleups to expand in new markets. They include offshore residencies, coaching, in-market connections and introductions to partners and venture capital.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the codes with no explanation and printed the generic sentence twice, so it never warned that outcomes and services are pooled in one column.

value_domain: Dollar value attached to an Austrade market event
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants
variable_description: The dollar amount Austrade attaches to a market and event row, which can be a grant paid out or a trade outcome the firm reported. Which it is depends on mktevent: an EMDG row is public money going out under a programme that "provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies", while a Trade Outcome row is revenue the firm claims to have won. The custodian warns that the amounts are meant to be positive and that any negative value should be treated as positive.
value_definition: A numeric dollar amount, one per market and event row, present only where mktamountflag is 1.
limitation: It is not export revenue and cannot be summed as if it were: adding a grant to a reported export sale on the same firm mixes an input with an outcome, and the same sale can be reported against more than one market. The sign convention also means the raw data cannot be used to detect reversals or adjustments.
rationale: The Austrade page defines the EMDG programme that supplies one of the event types carrying an amount; the mixed nature of the column follows from the event list rather than from a published definition of the field.
evidence_quote: The EMDG program provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies to: market and promote their goods and services globally undertake export training.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's note about negative values with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the amounts are of different kinds depending on the event type.

value_domain: Austrade programme or event type
value_source: Austrade, Export Market Development Grants
variable_description: Which Austrade programme or event stream this market row belongs to, taking one of six values. They are Client Services, EMDG, Excelerate, Go Global Toolkit, Tailored Services and Trade Outcome, and only EMDG is a grant: Austrade says the programme "provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies to: market and promote their goods and services globally undertake export training", and the rest of the values record advisory or informational contact. Trade Outcome is different again, being a result reported back rather than a service delivered.
value_definition: A character value from a fixed list of six programme names. It is the field that determines how mktdollaramount should be read on the same row.
limitation: It records that a firm engaged with a stream, not how much of it, so a single Client Services contact and a multi-year grant look the same at this level. Programme names also change over time as Austrade restructures its offerings, so an event type absent in early years may be a renamed stream rather than a new one.
rationale: The Austrade grants page defines EMDG, the only value in the list that carries public money, which is the distinction a reader needs to interpret the accompanying dollar amounts.
evidence_quote: The EMDG program provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies to: market and promote their goods and services globally undertake export training.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed six programme names with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said which of them involve money or how the value governs the amount column.

value_domain: Overseas market nominated by the business
value_source: Austrade, Programs, services and policies
variable_description: The overseas market the business nominated for this Austrade programme or event, which is why the markets table has more than one row per firm per year. It is a target of export effort, not a destination of goods, so a firm can select a market it never ships to; the same firm selecting several markets produces several rows, each with its own event and amount. Austrade organises much of its assistance geographically, through offshore posts and regional programmes such as the South Asia Business Exchange, which is the structure the market list follows.
value_definition: A character value from the market list the BLADE data item list carries as appendix 21. Entries are markets in Austrade's operational sense, mostly countries, with some regional groupings.
limitation: It cannot be reconciled with merchandise trade country codes: a market here is where Austrade support was directed, and it is neither the country of the buyer nor the port of discharge on an export declaration. Nor is it exhaustive, since only firms that used an Austrade programme appear at all.
rationale: The Austrade page shows the geographic organisation of its programmes, which is the structure the market list reflects; the code list itself sits in an appendix the registry does not hold.
evidence_quote: The South Asia Business Exchange (SABX) helps connect Australian businesses to South Asia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'The market selected by entity' and pointed at an appendix, with the generic sentence used twice, so it never distinguished a nominated market from a trade destination.

value_domain: Three-letter calendar month of the BAS reference period
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, Business activity statement
variable_description: The month the Business Activity Statement row refers to, not the month the statement was lodged or processed. It matters because remitters are not on a common cycle: the ABS notes that "Business Activity Statements (BAS) are reports that businesses lodge with the ATO on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis", so this month labels a period whose length varies by firm. It appears across thirteen BAS tables, giving each of them the same within-year position marker.
value_definition: Three characters, initial capital, in English month abbreviation form: Jan through Dec. It is a period label, not a date, and carries no year of its own.
limitation: For a quarterly or annual remitter the row cannot be read as one month's trading, so aggregating a mixed population by this column produces spikes at quarter ends rather than a monthly series. Because it holds no year, it must be combined with the financial year on the same table before any row can be placed in time.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the BAS and states the three lodgement frequencies, which is what makes a single month label mean different spans of activity for different firms.
evidence_quote: Business Activity Statements (BAS) are reports that businesses lodge with the ATO on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Month data is in reference to' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never warned that the reporting cycle varies or that the field carries no year.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement condition flag, Y where present
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets the employer move employees between roles or locations. DEWR codes it as field 201, "Multi-skilling/ flexible deployment of labour": "Employees can be moved between roles and/or locations to suit the needs of the business, or to develop their own skill sets", so business need and skill development sit in one flag. The custodian records that it should not be coded for agreements made in 2010, so that year is a documented hole rather than a year without such clauses.
value_definition: A single character, Y where the clause was found, blank otherwise, over federal enterprise agreements coded for conditions.
limitation: The 2010 gap means a year-on-year series through 2010 will show a false dip, and the flag cannot be repaired from the neighbouring skill-based wage movement field, which codes something else. It also cannot say whether redeployment ever happened or whether it was used for training rather than for cover.
rationale: The DEWR framework gives the field number and the coding rule the BLADE data item list reproduces; the 2010 exclusion comes from the custodian's own valid-response note.
evidence_quote: Employees can be moved between roles and/or locations to suit the needs of the business, or to develop their own skill sets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's coding rule and the 2010 note as a valid response, with the generic sentence twice below it, so nothing explained what the 2010 exclusion does to a time series.

value_domain: Capital gains on collectables, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains on collectables held as non-active assets, worked out under the indexation method, at label J of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO defines a collectable as "an artwork, an item of jewellery, an antique, a coin, a medallion, a rare folio, a rare manuscript, a rare book, a postage stamp or a first day cover that is used or kept mainly for personal use or enjoyment", so a business row here is unusual and typically a trust or a private company holding personal-use assets. The BLADE label carries both wordings because the schedule changed: OF splits collectables gains by method, while NF simply reads "Capital gains - Collectables", so a series spanning the change is not continuous.
value_definition: A dollar amount before any capital losses, the CGT discount or the small business concessions are applied. The indexation method uplifts the cost base by a factor based on the consumer price index up to September 1999.
limitation: Losses on collectables are quarantined and can only be applied against collectable gains, so this column cannot be netted against the real estate or shares columns beside it. A zero is also uninformative about the indexation method itself, since the ATO restricts it to assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999 and that population shrinks every year.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines both the collectables category and the indexation method, and the 2012 schedule fixes label J as the non-active collectables indexation cell.
evidence_quote: A collectable is an artwork, an item of jewellery, an antique, a coin, a medallion, a rare folio, a rare manuscript, a rare book, a postage stamp or a first day cover that is used or kept mainly for personal use or enjoyment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the paired OF and NF schedule labels with no explanation of the prefixes and the generic sentence used as both definition and limitation, so it never said the two labels are different quantities.

value_domain: Capital gains on forestry MIS interests, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests, non-active, under the discount method, at label Z of the old CGT schedule. Companies rarely have an amount here: the ATO states that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies", so a non-zero value normally signals a trust or a fund lodging the schedule. The OF prefix on the BLADE label marks the old-form wording; the current schedule no longer gives forestry interests their own row.
value_definition: A dollar amount before losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering interests in a forestry managed investment scheme disposed of or dealt with in the year.
limitation: It is not forestry income: thinning receipts and harvest proceeds taxed as ordinary income sit elsewhere on the return, so this column captures only the capital-account side of a forestry interest. Because the row disappeared from the schedule, a firm's forestry gains in later years fall into the other CGT assets rows and cannot be separated out.
rationale: The current schedule instructions state the company restriction on the discount method, and the 2012 form fixes label Z as the non-active forestry MIS discount cell.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form schedule label with the OF prefix unexplained and the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the discount method is largely unavailable to companies.

value_domain: Capital gains on forestry MIS interests, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests, non-active, under the indexation method, at label Y of the old CGT schedule. The interest is a capital asset for a subsequent participant who does not trade in securities: the ATO says such a participant includes acquisition costs "in the cost base or reduced cost base of your forestry interest for CGT purposes when the interest is subsequently disposed of prior to harvest or when the harvest proceeds are received". The OF prefix marks the old-form wording, and the current schedule has no forestry row at all.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and concessions, with the cost base uplifted by the indexation factor frozen at September 1999.
limitation: Almost nothing can qualify: indexation requires an asset acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999, and most forestry MIS interests postdate that, so a zero here says nothing about a firm's forestry holdings. Amounts received for thinning are excluded from the CGT treatment entirely and are assessable income instead, so this column understates money taken out of a forestry interest.
rationale: The ATO guide explains how a forestry interest enters the cost base and which receipts are excluded from CGT treatment; the 2012 schedule fixes label Y as the non-active forestry indexation cell.
evidence_quote: Amounts you receive for thinning are excluded from the CGT treatment of your forestry interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained what a forestry interest is on capital account or which receipts fall outside it.

value_domain: Capital gains on forestry MIS interests, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains on forestry managed investment scheme interests, non-active, under the other method, at label A of the forestry row. The other method is the residual: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds", and it is compulsory for anything bought and sold inside twelve months. For companies it is the usual column of the three, because indexation is confined to pre-1999 assets and the discount is closed to them.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions.
limitation: The label letter A is reused elsewhere on the form, so this column cannot be identified by its letter alone; it is the forestry row of part A that fixes it. Being the residual method, a large amount here also tells you nothing about holding period beyond the fact that indexation and the discount were unavailable or not chosen.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method, and the 2012 form shows the forestry row carrying labels Y, Z and A across the three method columns.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never explained the other method or warned that the label letter repeats across the form.

value_domain: Capital gains on hedging financial arrangements, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: Capital gains from hedging financial arrangements treated on capital account, at the discount label F of the hedging row on the old CGT schedule. The row exists only because of the taxation of financial arrangements rules: with a valid hedging tax-timing election in place, "gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged". The hedging row has no indexation cell at all, so it is split across two columns rather than three.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and the discount, reported only by entities within the TOFA rules that have made a hedging tax-timing method election.
limitation: It is not a measure of a firm's hedging: an entity that hedges heavily but has made no hedging election, or whose hedges relate to revenue rather than capital items, reports nothing here. The amount also mirrors the tax treatment of the hedged asset rather than the economics of the hedge itself.
rationale: The ATO page explains why hedging gains reach the CGT schedule at all and names the election that gates the row, and the 2012 form shows the hedging row with only discount and other columns.
evidence_quote: gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row depends on a TOFA hedging election or that it has no indexation cell.

value_domain: Capital gains on hedging financial arrangements, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, hedging financial arrangements, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains from hedging financial arrangements worked out under the other method, at label H of the hedging row on the old CGT schedule. For a company this is normally the only hedging cell with an amount in it, since the discount is closed to companies and the row carries no indexation cell. The ATO directs entities with a hedging tax-timing election to "specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule", which is what this column holds.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to proceeds less cost base on the hedging arrangement, before capital losses are applied.
limitation: Losses on hedging arrangements are reported in a separate part of the schedule, so this column is a gross gain and cannot be read as the net result of a hedging programme. It also shares the label letter H with the other CGT assets discount cell, so the row, not the letter, identifies it.
rationale: The ATO page states that hedging gains and losses go on the CGT schedule under the tax-timing election, and the 2012 form places label H in the hedging row's other-gains column.
evidence_quote: If this applies to you, specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2016 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained why this is the only hedging cell most companies use.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets that fall outside the named categories, worked out under the discount method, at label H of part A of the old CGT schedule. This is the catch-all row, so it absorbs goodwill, intangibles, plant used privately and any CGT event that is not a disposal of shares, real estate, collectables or a forestry interest. A company will almost always show zero, because the ATO states that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies".
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering every non-active asset class not itemised elsewhere in part A.
limitation: Being a residual, it cannot be decomposed: a large amount says a gain was made on something outside the named categories but not on what. It is also not evidence of a twelve-month holding period for a company, since the few company amounts that do appear are life insurance cases rather than ordinary trading entities.
rationale: The current schedule instructions define the discount method and its company restriction, and the 2012 form fixes label H as the non-active other-assets discount cell.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form schedule label with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the row is a residual category or that companies rarely use the discount method.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets outside the named categories, worked out under the indexation method, at label G of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO describes the category as covering "the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule", which for a business usually means goodwill, intangibles or a CGT event that is not an asset disposal. Indexation restricts it further: the method is only available where the asset was acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and concessions, with the cost base increased by an indexation factor based on consumer price index movements up to September 1999.
limitation: The column shrinks mechanically over time as pre-1999 assets are sold out of the population, so a downward trend is an ageing effect and not a change in business behaviour. It also cannot be compared with the discount column on the same row, because an entity that could use either had to choose one and the schedule does not record the choice.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines both the other CGT assets category and the indexation method, including the acquisition cut-off that governs eligibility.
evidence_quote: The indexation method is one of the ways to calculate your capital gain if you acquired a CGT asset before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so nothing said what the residual category holds or why the column empties out over time.

value_domain: Capital gains on other CGT assets, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on non-active assets outside the named categories, worked out under the other method, at label I of part A of the old CGT schedule. For most companies this is the single most populated cell of the whole part A grid, because the residual asset category and the residual method are the two defaults. The ATO requires the method for short holdings: "You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months".
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: Because both the row and the column are defaults, a large amount here is the least informative number in part A: it identifies neither the asset nor the holding period. Reading it as short-term trading gains would be wrong, since assets held for years also land here whenever indexation and the discount do not apply.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method and the other CGT assets category, which are the two residuals that intersect in this cell.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months (that is, when the indexation and discount methods don't apply).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never warned that this cell is where everything unclassified accumulates.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule 2025 instructions
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the discount method, at label E of part A of the old CGT schedule. It is the property equivalent of the shares discount cell, and it is closed to ordinary companies: the ATO says "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies". Non-active is a concession status, not a statement about use, because the ATO directs that "If the asset doesn't qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets".
value_definition: A dollar amount before capital losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering land and buildings disposed of in the year.
limitation: A trust or fund with an amount here is not necessarily a property business: an incidental sale of premises produces the same entry as a portfolio disposal, and the schedule holds no count of properties. The non-active label also means a genuine business premises can appear here whenever the small business concessions were not available.
rationale: The current schedule instructions state both the company restriction on the discount method and the rule that pushes non-qualifying assets into the non-active rows.
evidence_quote: If the asset doesn't qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained what non-active means or that companies cannot use the discount method.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the indexation method, at label D of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO defines the category narrowly as location-based: "Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia", so foreign property falls into the other CGT assets rows instead. Indexation makes this the long-held property cell, since the method needs an acquisition before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and concessions, with the cost base uplifted by an indexation factor frozen at the September 1999 consumer price index.
limitation: Overseas real estate is excluded from the row, so this column understates a firm's property gains whenever it holds assets offshore. Indexation was also frozen rather than abolished, so the uplift shrinks in real terms every year an old property is held and the gain reported here grows for reasons unrelated to the market.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines real estate situated in Australia and the indexation method, and the 2012 form fixes label D as the non-active real estate indexation cell.
evidence_quote: Real estate situated in Australia is any real property, including land and buildings, that is in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row excludes overseas property or what indexation does to the cost base.

value_domain: Capital gains on real estate, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions, and Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012)
variable_description: Capital gains on real estate held as a non-active asset, worked out under the other method, at label F of part A of the old CGT schedule. This is where a company's property gains normally sit, since indexation is confined to pre-1999 acquisitions and the discount is closed to companies. The gain is simply proceeds less cost base, with no holding-period adjustment of any kind.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions.
limitation: Sharing the label letter F with the hedging discount cell, it can only be identified by its row, which matters when reading the raw schedule rather than the BLADE column name. The amount is also gross: development costs already deducted elsewhere and any prior-year losses are not netted here, so it is not the profit on the sale.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method, and the 2012 form shows label F appearing twice in part A, in the real estate other-gains cell and in the hedging discount cell.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so nothing said this is the usual cell for company property gains or that the label letter repeats.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts held as non-active assets, worked out under the discount method, at label B of part A of the old CGT schedule. The ATO's rule for the method is that "the CGT event happened after 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999" and "you acquired the asset at least 12 months before the CGT event", so an amount here marks a holding of at least a year. The discount itself is not applied at this point: current year and prior year losses come off first.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses and before the discount percentage is applied, covering shares and units disposed of in the year.
limitation: The column is not a company portfolio measure, because ordinary companies cannot use the discount method at all and the amounts that do appear come mostly from trusts and funds lodging the same schedule. It also cannot be netted against the losses parts of the schedule to give a net gain, since the sequence of loss application is set out separately.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the discount method, its twelve-month test and the order in which losses and the discount are applied.
evidence_quote: the CGT event happened after 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999 you acquired the asset at least 12 months before the CGT event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the discount is applied after losses or who can use the method.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts, non-active, under the indexation method, at label A of part A of the old CGT schedule. It is the first cell of the schedule's method grid and covers the oldest holdings: the ATO explains that the method "allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999)". Amounts here therefore come from parcels acquired before that date and still held when the CGT event happened.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with the cost base uplifted by the frozen indexation factor.
limitation: A zero does not mean no share gains: the same disposals appear in the discount or other cells whenever indexation was unavailable or the entity chose a different method, and the schedule never records which method was rejected. Label A is also reused in the forestry row of the same part, so the column name rather than the letter identifies the cell.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the indexation method and its cut-off date, and the 2012 form fixes label A as the non-active shares and units indexation cell.
evidence_quote: This method allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said what indexation does or that a zero can hide a gain reported by another method.

value_domain: Capital gains on shares and units, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, appendix 4 definitions
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units in unit trusts held as non-active assets, worked out under the other method, at label C of part A of the old CGT schedule. For a company this is the working column for equity disposals, because the discount is closed to it and indexation reaches only pre-1999 parcels. The ATO makes the method compulsory for short holdings: "You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months".
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to capital proceeds less cost base on shares and units, gross of capital losses and concessions.
limitation: It cannot be read as short-term trading, because a company holding shares for a decade also reports here once indexation and the discount are out of reach. Gains distributed from a trust are grossed up and reported in a separate row of the modern schedule, so this cell is not a complete picture of a firm's equity gains.
rationale: The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method and states when it is compulsory, and the 2012 form fixes label C as the non-active shares and units other-gains cell.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months (that is, when the indexation and discount methods don't apply).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never explained that the other method is a residual rather than a marker of short holdings.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at part N of the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part N
variable_description: Whether Division 149 applied to the company, so that assets bought before 20 September 1985 lost their pre-CGT status. It applies when the majority underlying ownership of those assets changed, and the schedule puts it as "Same majority underlying ownership and pre-CGT assets - Division 149 - to be completed by companies only" at label O. It matters because the ATO treats pre-CGT assets as "generally exempt from CGT", so a yes marks the year an old asset base came into the CGT net.
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, from a yes and no tick box; anything else is an invalid or absent response. Companies only, and only those lodging a CGT schedule.
limitation: The flag does not value the assets that lost their pre-CGT status, so it identifies the event without measuring it, and nothing on the schedule links it to the gains reported in part A. Earlier forms worded the same question as a change in majority underlying ownership, so wording rather than meaning shifts across the series.
rationale: The form carries the part title, the division reference, the label letter and the companies-only restriction, and the ATO definitions appendix supplies the pre-CGT asset concept the question turns on.
evidence_quote: Part N Same majority underlying ownership and pre-CGT assets - Division 149 - to be completed by companies only
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with its OF prefix unexplained and the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said what Division 149 does or why a company would answer yes.

value_domain: ABS integration version identifier
value_source: ABS, BLADE Data and Legislation
variable_description: Which ABS integration run produced this row of the National Family Violence Funded Agencies data. The dataset is not part of standard or requestable BLADE: the ABS notes that as an accredited data service provider it integrates additional sources "for approved projects and subject to agreement from data custodians", which is how a service-delivery collection like this reaches a business asset. The version string is therefore also the marker of which approved project the row belongs to.
value_definition: An eight-character alphanumeric string of the form inNNN_vN, for example in293_v1, identifying the ABS integration project and its version.
limitation: It is not a date and not an attribute of the funded agency, so it cannot order records in time or distinguish one agency from another. Because the underlying collection is project-specific rather than an enduring BLADE module, the version cannot be matched against the version columns on the standard modules.
rationale: The ABS page explains the project-based route by which non-standard collections are integrated into BLADE, which is the status of this dataset; the version string itself is documented only as an internal ABS reference.
evidence_quote: As the ABS is an Accredited Data Service Provider , additional data sources can be integrated to BLADE for approved projects and subject to agreement from data custodians.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the column marks an extract vintage from a project-specific integration.

value_domain: Nickel content of an ore shipment, per cent
value_source: ABS, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC)
variable_description: The assayed nickel content of an exported ore or concentrate shipment, as a percentage of the shipment. Nickel is usually shipped as a low-grade concentrate or matte and priced on contained metal, so the grade recorded here is what converts a tonnage into the quantity the buyer pays for. It qualifies a single export line of a single consignment, not the exporter's output for the year.
value_definition: A number expressed as a percentage, held against an export transaction classified by the AHECC, the eight-digit Australian extension of the Harmonized System maintained with the Department of Home Affairs.
limitation: It cannot be compared with the lead percentage on the same shipment as if the two were shares of one whole, since each metal is assayed against the total mass and other elements make up the rest. A missing value is also not a zero grade: it marks a line that is not an ore or concentrate, which for a nickel producer includes refined and intermediate products.
rationale: The AHECC page establishes the classification governing Australian export lines, including the ore and concentrate classes this grade qualifies; no fetchable page defines the metal-percentage field itself.
evidence_quote: The AHECC is used in the preparation of export documentation and in the compilation of Australian export statistics
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Percentage of nickel in shipment of ore' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the figure is a per-consignment grade rather than a firm-level composition.

value_domain: Nominal term of an enterprise agreement, in years
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Nominal expiry date
variable_description: How long the enterprise agreement runs on paper, measured in years from commencement to its nominal expiry date. The nominal term is capped: the Commission notes it "will not be more than 4 years from the date the Commission approves the agreement". A negative value is not an error but a timing artefact, arising when the Commission approved the agreement after the expiry date the parties had written into it.
value_definition: A numeric duration in years, normally between 0 and 4, and negative where approval postdates the nominal expiry date.
limitation: It is not the period the agreement actually governed the workplace: the Commission states that "Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated", so an expired agreement can still set pay years later. Treating this as coverage duration therefore understates how long an employer's terms stayed in force.
rationale: The Commission page defines the nominal expiry date, the statutory four-year cap and the fact that agreements keep operating past it, which is what separates nominal duration from effective duration.
evidence_quote: Agreements continue to operate after their nominal expiry dates until they are replaced or terminated by the Commission.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's note about negative values with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said the term is nominal and that agreements outlive it.

value_domain: Binary flag for New South Wales coverage of an agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the enterprise agreement operates in New South Wales, one of a set of per-jurisdiction flags DEWR records as "State or Territories covered". The flags are not mutually exclusive, so a national employer's agreement carries a 1 in several of them at once and the set cannot be collapsed into a single state variable. It describes the reach of the agreement, not where the employer's ABN is registered.

value_domain: Head count of Australia-based staff from a company web profile

value_domain: Days of paid personal or sick leave per year under the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How many days of paid sick leave the agreement provides, as a number rather than a yes flag. DEWR codes it as field 34, "Days ____ sick leave": "The agreement provides for paid leave available for employees when they are sick or injured. The number of days of paid leave is recorded." It is one of the few WAD condition fields carrying a quantity rather than a yes flag, which makes it usable as a measure of entitlement generosity. Two sentinels sit in the same column, so it has to be filtered before it is averaged.
