The number is also an entitlement written into an agreement, not leave taken, and it excludes the separate carer's leave and casual personal leave provisions coded in neighbouring fields.
rationale: The DEWR framework defines the field, and the neighbouring entries for unlimited sick leave and carer's leave show what this count does and does not include.
evidence_quote: The agreement provides for paid leave available for employees when they are sick or injured. The number of days of paid leave is recorded.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's coding rule and listed both sentinels as valid responses, with the generic sentence twice below, so nothing warned what they do to a mean.

value_domain: Full-time equivalent R&D staff on an R&D tax incentive registration
value_source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, R&D Tax Incentive online application questions and guidance
variable_description: How much employee labour went into the R&D activities in this registration, measured in person years rather than head count. The application defines question 39 as "the full-time equivalent (FTE) number of people engaged by the company to perform research and development (R&D) activities during the income year covered by this application", with part-time staff counted as a fraction, so someone working half a full-time load is 0.5. For a consolidated group the figure is reported across all relevant subsidiaries, which is why the BLADE label says it spans all companies in the application.
value_definition: A numeric full-time equivalent count, which can be fractional, covering employees including working directors, partners and proprietors.
limitation: Independent contractors are counted in a separate question, so this figure understates the people who worked on the R&D wherever a firm outsourced. Because it is reported across a consolidated group but attaches to the registering ABN, R&D staffing intensity computed against that ABN's own payroll can exceed one, and the application guidance accepts best reasonable estimates rather than payroll extracts.
rationale: The application guidance defines the field, its FTE basis, the consolidated group treatment and the separate contractor question, which together give both the unit and the main confusion.
evidence_quote: This is the full-time equivalent (FTE) number of people engaged by the company to perform research and development (R&D) activities during the income year covered by this application.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about employees across all companies with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the unit is full-time equivalent person years or that contractors are excluded.

value_domain: Count of employers covered by an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: How many employers are party to the agreement, which separates a single-enterprise agreement from a multi-enterprise or greenfields one. Most federal agreements cover one employer, so a value above one marks the minority that bargain collectively across firms, and the same agreement record then attaches to several businesses in BLADE. DEWR records agreement type alongside it, so the two together identify what kind of bargaining produced the terms.
value_definition: A whole number of employers, counted at the agreement rather than at the workplace, so a single employer with many sites counts once.

rationale: The DEWR page lists the general details recorded for each agreement, including agreement type and the number of employees covered, which places this count at the agreement level; the field's own coding note comes from the data item list.

supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indicates the number of employers covered by an agreement' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said an employer is a bargaining party rather than an ABN.

value_domain: Count of wage increases scheduled in an enterprise agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database 2021 data collection framework
variable_description: How many separate wage increases the agreement schedules over its term, which is the count behind the quantum and timing series DEWR maintains. The framework records "Quantum and timing of any wage increases" for each agreement, so this column is the number of those events rather than their size; dividing the total increase by it gives the average step. A count of zero belongs with the agreements DEWR flags as containing no wage rates or no quantifiable increase.
value_definition: A whole number of scheduled increases over the life of the agreement, held with separate fields recording the reason where an increase cannot be quantified.
limitation: More increases do not mean higher pay: an agreement with four small annual steps and one with a single large rise can deliver the same wage outcome, so the count has to be read with the quantum fields. It also does not distinguish increases that were expressed as percentages from those linked to Minimum Wage Panel decisions or to the consumer price index, which DEWR records separately.
rationale: The DEWR framework sets out the wage increases group of fields, including the non-quantifiable and no-wage-rates cases that explain zero values here.
evidence_quote: Wage increases Quantum and timing of any wage increases
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'The number of wage increases that apply to the agreement' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the count is silent on size or how zeros arise.

value_domain: Total cost base reduction from debt forgiveness (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
variable_description: The total amount by which the company cut the cost bases of its CGT assets after a commercial debt was forgiven, at label Q of part O. The form heads the part "Cost base adjustments resulting from debt forgiveness - Division 139 - to be completed by companies only" and pairs this amount with the yes or no at label P, "Interest in creditor". A reduced cost base means a larger capital gain whenever the affected assets are later sold, so the figure is a forward-looking tax consequence rather than a gain in the year.
value_definition: A dollar amount, reported once for the year rather than per asset, on a part of the schedule completed only by companies.
limitation: It does not say which assets were written down or by how much each, so the future gains it creates cannot be traced to anything in the data. Part O left the CGT schedule after 2004, so an empty column in later years reflects the form and not a stop to commercial debt forgiveness, and the ATO's own guidance describes the current rules under Division 245 rather than the division named on the form.
rationale: The 2004 schedule carries the part title, the division reference, both label letters and the companies-only restriction, and the 2005 schedule shows the part gone, which fixes the end of the series.
evidence_quote: Part O Cost base adjustments resulting from debt forgiveness-Division 139-to be completed by companies only
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the part is companies-only, that it was dropped after 2004, or what a cost base reduction does to later gains.

value_domain: Total cost base adjustment from debt forgiveness (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2004 (NAT 3423-6.2004), part O
variable_description: The total cost base adjustment the company made on the debtor side of a commercial debt forgiveness, at label S of part O of the old CGT schedule. It is the companion to the reduction at label Q: the form pairs label S with the yes or no at label R, "Interest in debtor", where label Q is paired with an interest in the creditor. The two amounts therefore describe the same transaction from opposite ends of the relationship and should not be added together as if they were one exposure.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the year, reported by companies only, on the same part of the schedule as the creditor-side reduction.
limitation: Confusing it with the label Q amount reverses the direction of the transaction, since one side holds an interest in the creditor and the other an interest in the debtor. The ATO also applies a forgiven amount in a fixed order - revenue losses, then capital losses, then deductible expenditure, then cost bases - so this figure is only the residue that reached cost bases and understates the size of the forgiveness.
rationale: The 2004 schedule shows part O's two label pairs and their headings, and the ATO's commercial debt forgiveness appendix gives the order in which a net forgiven amount is applied.
evidence_quote: Interest in debtor R yes no Print X in the appropriate box Total cost base adjustment S
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old-form label with the generic sentence used twice, so it never distinguished the debtor side from the creditor side or said where cost bases sit in the order of application.

value_domain: Non-capital purchases reported at G11 of the business activity statement (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 3 purchases
variable_description: The business's non-capital purchases for the BAS period, label G11, which is the closest thing BLADE has to a high-frequency measure of operating inputs. The ATO tells businesses to report at G11 "all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10 ), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale", so it covers trading stock, running expenses and equipment leases. The split from capital purchases at G10 is partly conventional: firms expecting turnover under $1 million may put capital items of $1,000 or less at G11.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one BAS period, reported GST-inclusive unless the business uses the accounts method and has chosen to show amounts as GST-exclusive.
limitation: It is not an expense measure from the accounts: it is purchases in the period on the firm's chosen GST accounting basis, so a cash-basis remitter's G11 moves with payment timing rather than with activity. The $1,000 threshold also lets genuinely capital spending sit in G11, so the G10 and G11 split cannot be used as a clean investment and operating expenditure divide.
rationale: The ATO page defines what belongs at G11, lists the inclusions and states the $1,000 rule that blurs the boundary with capital purchases.
evidence_quote: At G11, you need to report all of your business purchases relevant to the reporting period (other than those reported at G10 ), such as most business purchases, including services and stock bought for resale
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Non-capital purchases' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never named the BAS label, the GST basis or the threshold that lets capital items in.

value_domain: Binary flag on the ABN to business unit mapping
value_source: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses methodology, statistical unit and two-population model
variable_description: Whether this ABN is split by the ABS across more than one Type of Activity Unit, which happens when one legal entity runs distinct kinds of production. The ABS builds TAUs so that each "consists of one or more business entities, sub entities or branches of a business that can be grouped according to production activity", and classifies each by the industry of its main activity. When the flag is set, the ABN carries one tax record but several industry classifications, so an industry analysis using ABN-level ANZSIC will attribute all of the firm's activity to whichever unit won the label.
value_definition: A numeric flag: 1 for yes, 0 for no, and a full stop for missing. It is the mirror image of many_abn_to_one_tau, and both can be 0 for a simple one-to-one mapping.
limitation: It does not say how the ABN's reported income, purchases or wages divide between the units, and the ABS does not publish that apportionment in BLADE, so a flagged ABN cannot be split for analysis. It also does not mark a change: an ABN can gain or lose units as the ABS re-profiles the business, without anything happening to the business itself.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the TAU as a production-activity grouping classified by main activity, which is what makes a one-to-many mapping possible and what it costs an analyst.
evidence_quote: A Type of Activity Unit (TAU) consists of one or more business entities, sub entities or branches of a business that can be grouped according to production activity, and can report a minimum set of data items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'One ABN to many Type of Activity Units (TAUs)' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never explained what splitting an ABN does to industry coding.

value_domain: Count of options or rights issued in a scrip-for-scrip rollover
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2012 (NAT 3423-6.2012), part L
variable_description: How many options or rights the acquiring entity issued as consideration in a scrip-for-scrip rollover, at label I of part L of the CGT schedule. Part L is headed "Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity - to be completed by companies and trusts only", so a value here identifies the firm as the acquirer in a takeover or merger, not the target. The ATO explains that such a rollover "allows you to defer your CGT obligation until a later CGT event happens to your shares or units", which is why the count of paper issued is collected alongside the number of original entities and the cost base of the interests acquired.
value_definition: A count, up to eleven digits, of options, rights and similar instruments issued. It sits beside a separate count of shares and units issued in the same part.
limitation: It is a number of instruments and not a value, so it cannot be compared across deals without a price, and a large count can represent a small consideration. Nor does it identify the target: the schedule collects the original entity's tax file number in a neighbouring label, which is not carried through to a usable business identifier.
rationale: The 2012 schedule shows part L, its companies-and-trusts restriction and the label I count, and the ATO definitions appendix explains what a scrip-for-scrip rollover does.
evidence_quote: Part L Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity - to be completed by companies and trusts only
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of options/rights etc issued' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the row marks an acquirer in a scrip-for-scrip rollover.

value_domain: Other GST-free sales reported at G3 of the business activity statement (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Complete your BAS, step 1 sales
variable_description: GST-free sales other than exports, label G3 on the business activity statement. It is where basic food, most health and education services, childcare, water and sales of going concerns are reported. The ATO instructs that "All amounts reported at G3 should also have been reported at G1", so it is a carve-out of total sales rather than an addition to them. The label is a strong industry signal: a food retailer, a medical practice or a childcare centre will show a large G3 where a manufacturer shows nothing.

limitation: A large G3 does not mean a firm paid no GST: it still claims credits on its purchases, and it can have taxable sales at the same time. Food retailers may also use simplified accounting methods to estimate the GST-free share, so G3 for those businesses is an approved estimate rather than a transaction total, and a sale of a going concern can put an unusually large one-off amount in an otherwise small firm's G3.
rationale: The ATO page lists what belongs at G3, states its relationship to G1 and notes the simplified accounting methods available to food retailers.
evidence_quote: At G3 report your other GST-free sales as listed below. All amounts reported at G3 should also have been reported at G1 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Other GST-free sales' with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the amount is a subset of total sales or that exports go elsewhere.

value_domain: Dealroom binary tag for businesses outside its technology taxonomy
value_source: Dealroom, sector taxonomy guide
variable_description: Whether Dealroom tags the business as sitting outside technology, held constant across every observation of the ABN. supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence about a binary time-invariant tag with the generic sentence used twice, so it never said the classification is a vendor's and cannot be mapped to ANZSIC.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Flags a federal enterprise agreement that caps how much overtime an employee can be required or allowed to work. It is a coded reading of the agreement's clauses by DEWR staff, not a measure of overtime actually worked, and the unit is the registered agreement rather than the business. DEWR holds "conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997", but the valid-response note confines this particular flag to agreements coded between 2002 and 2009.

Coding stops after 2009, so a business whose current agreement was approved in 2015 looks identical to one whose agreement says nothing about overtime limits, and DEWR warns that "not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database". A capped-overtime clause also says nothing about how binding the cap is in practice.
rationale: DEWR publishes what the Workplace Agreements Database is, which agreements are in scope, that about 200 items are coded per agreement, and that the set of conditions coded is reviewed annually, which is what explains a flag that exists only for part of the series.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried DEWR's one-line clause wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the flag is coded only for 2002 to 2009 agreements or that it describes a clause rather than hours worked.

value_domain: Enterprise agreement clause indicator (Y = yes)
value_source: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Flags an agreement that folds overtime pay into an annualised or loaded salary instead of paying it as a separate penalty. It marks a pay-structure choice in the agreement text, so a business with this clause can have staff working overtime with no overtime line in the payroll. DEWR codes "around 200 data items" for each agreement, of which this is one, and the record covers the agreement rather than any one employee under it.

rationale: The DEWR page defines the database, its coverage of conditions since 1997 and the volume of coded items per agreement, which places this clause flag in its collection and fixes the unit of record.

supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's clause wording and used the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the flag is an agreement-level clause code with no loading amount behind it.

value_domain: Count of chemistry-area patents in the event stream
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many chemistry-area patents the business had lodged with IP Australia during the financial year. Chemistry is one of five coarse classification areas IPLoRD uses for patents and covers "Chemistry (11 classification areas)", running from organic fine chemistry and biotechnology through to chemical engineering and environmental technology. Filing is the entry point of the patent lifecycle, so the column records that the firm sought protection in a chemistry field, not that it obtained any.
value_definition: A non-negative integer counting patents in the chemistry coarse classification area for one financial year, built from the IPLoRD naming rule of right type, coarse area, event stream and activity metric.
limitation: A patent classified in more than one coarse area is counted in each of them, so the chemistry, instruments, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and other counts on the same row do not add to the firm's patent total. Joint applications are also counted in full for every applicant, which is what the weighted count column corrects.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the activity metrics, the four event streams and the coarse classification areas, and gives the naming convention that produces this column name from right type, chemistry, event stream and metric.
evidence_quote: Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's one-line label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said what the chemistry grouping is, which classification stands behind it, or how this metric differs from the other three on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 48 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The partnership's aggregated turnover in dollars, reported only by the very largest partnerships. The ATO asks for it at label V only where the answer to "Did you have aggregated turnover of $1 billion or more, or are you a significant global entity?" is yes, and then says: "Show at label V Aggregated turnover your actual aggregated turnover, round the amount to the nearest $100 million". Aggregated turnover is the partnership's own annual turnover plus that of its connected entities and affiliates, so it is a group measure carried on an entity return.
value_definition: A dollar figure for the income year, rounded to the nearest $100 million, so the smallest non-zero value possible is $100 million. The banded column at label U carries the same concept for smaller partnerships.
limitation: It is not a turnover variable for the population: almost every partnership leaves it blank, and a blank means the billion-dollar test was not met rather than that turnover was nil. The rounding also destroys any year-on-year movement below $100 million.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions set out item 48, the trigger question for label V and the rounding rule, which is exactly what the data item list label leaves unsaid.
evidence_quote: Yes – Show at label V Aggregated turnover your actual aggregated turnover, round the amount to the nearest $100 million.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label 'Aggregated Turnover' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the field is reported only above $1 billion or that the amount is rounded to $100 million.

value_domain: Aggregated turnover band code (categories A to P)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The band the partnership's aggregated turnover falls in, from under $7.5 million up to $1 billion or over. The ATO requires label U only where the partnership or a partner "will, or a partner in the partnership may reasonably expect to, rely on the partnership's aggregated turnover" for the instant asset write-off, the small business CGT concessions or the small business restructure roll-over, so it is completed by concession claimants rather than by everyone. Aggregated turnover adds the turnover of connected entities and affiliates to the partnership's own.
value_definition: A sixteen-way band code. The BLADE numeric codes 5 to 80 map onto the ATO's categories A to P, where A is "$0 to less than $7.5 million" and P is "$1 billion or over".
limitation: A missing band does not mean a small partnership; it usually means no concession was being claimed. The band is also a best estimate the ATO does not police - "We won't penalise you for specifying an incorrect category where you make your best attempt" - and it may be built from either the current or the previous year's turnover, so two partnerships in the same band can be a year apart.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions publish item 48 label U, the exact band table that the data item list codes reproduce, and the eligibility trigger that determines who completes it.
evidence_quote: You must complete item 48 – label U if the partnership will, or a partner in the partnership may reasonably expect to, rely on the partnership's aggregated turnover for eligibility for any of the following:
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the sixteen codes with no statement of who has to complete the item, and repeated the generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Personal services income results test indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Whether the partnership claims it passed the personal services income results test for at least one individual whose income it reports. The test asks whether the individual is paid to produce a result, supplies their own tools and bears the cost of fixing defects, and passing it takes the partnership outside the personal services income rules. The ATO makes clear it is a claim, not a ruling: "You can self-assess whether you satisfy the results test irrespective of how much income comes from one source."
value_definition: A one-character indicator, Y or N, with anything else treated as an invalid or missing response. The item is asked once for the whole return, not once per individual.
limitation: A yes is untested unless the ATO audits it, so it records a position taken rather than a legal fact. Because the question covers any individual, it also cannot say how many of the partnership's service providers passed, and a no does not mean the personal services income rules applied, since the unrelated clients, employment and business premises tests or a Commissioner's determination may still have saved it.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define the results test, its three conditions, the label it is reported at and its self-assessed character.
evidence_quote: You can self-assess whether you satisfy the results test irrespective of how much income comes from one source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the question text from the form and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the test is or that the answer is self-assessed.

value_domain: ATO business industry code (5 digits, modified ANZSIC)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The industry the partnership nominated for its main business activity, as a five-digit ATO business industry code. The ATO explains that "The industry coding regime we use is a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)" produced by the ABS and Statistics New Zealand, so the codes look like ANZSIC classes but are not identical to them. The code is self-selected by the lodger from the business industry code tool.
value_definition: A five-digit character code, for example 01600 for dairy cattle farming, covering one main activity per return.
limitation: It records one nominated main activity, so a partnership operating across several industries is invisible beyond its largest, and the ATO itself warns an incorrect code can cause "incorrect targeting of audits". It is also not the ABS industry variable in BLADE, which comes from the Business Register, so the two can disagree for the same business in the same year.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions state which classification the industry code is derived from, its length and how the lodger picks it, which is what a reader needs before joining it to ANZSIC-coded data.
evidence_quote: The industry coding regime we use is a modified version of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) External Link the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) and Statistics New Zealand produce together.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'ANZSIC code' and pointed at a code list without saying the ATO code is a modified ANZSIC, self-selected, and limited to the main activity.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 49 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The assessable half of the balancing adjustment when the partnership disposes of intangible depreciating assets such as patents or in-house software. The ATO explains that when a partnership "ceases to hold or to use a depreciating asset, a balancing adjustment event may occur" and it must then "calculate a balancing adjustment amount to include in its assessable income or to claim as a deduction"; this column carries the income side only. The deductible side sits in the neighbouring label, and the termination value labels carry the disposal proceeds.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported at item 49 label F of the partnership return, covering intangible depreciating assets only.
limitation: It is not a profit on sale. The ATO warns that a profit shown in the accounts "will differ from the balancing adjustment amount taken into account for taxation purposes", because the adjustment measures proceeds against the tax written-down value and is scaled back for non-taxable use, so this column cannot be used as a gain on disposal of intellectual property.
rationale: Appendix 6 of the partnership instructions defines balancing adjustment events and amounts, states where the assessable and deductible sides go, and separates them from the accounting profit on sale.
evidence_quote: If the partnership ceases to hold or to use a depreciating asset, a balancing adjustment event may occur.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said this is one side of a tax adjustment rather than a sale price or an accounting gain.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 5 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Assessable government grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies received in the partnership's primary production business, reported at item 5 label E. The ATO's test is the use of the money, not its source: "Generally, government grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income in the hands of the recipient if they are received in, or for, the carrying on of a business." The identically defined non-primary-production column sits beside it, and the split follows the partnership's primary production activity rather than the type of grant.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering the primary production side of assessable government industry assistance, including fuel tax credits and producer rebates where a code letter D is also present.
limitation: It is not a measure of government support to farm businesses. Tax-free grants, and payments that are non-assessable non-exempt income, never appear, so a partnership that received large disaster or drought support can show nil; amounts relating to starting or ceasing a business may also be excluded.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define what belongs at the assessable government industry payments labels, list examples and set out what must be left out.
evidence_quote: Generally, government grants, rebates, bounties and subsidies are assessable income in the hands of the recipient if they are received in, or for, the carrying on of a business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that only assessable payments are in scope or what the PP split means.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 5 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Assessable government industry payments on the non-primary-production side of the partnership's business, reported at item 5 label F. The boundary with ordinary trading income matters here: the ATO directs that "Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments", so payments for services rendered to government are not government industry assistance. Fuel tax credits, wine producer rebates and the product stewardship (oil) benefit belong here and are marked by a code letter.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering non-primary-production assessable government assistance, reported gross and separately from the primary production label.
limitation: It will not measure a firm's public funding. Program payments that the law makes tax free sit outside the item altogether, and fee-for-service receipts from government, of which Medicare billing is the clearest case, are reported as ordinary business income instead, so two similarly subsidised firms can differ here for reasons of tax character alone.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions give the label, list the qualifying payment types and draw the explicit line between industry assistance and payments for services.
evidence_quote: Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated form label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the distinction between industry assistance and government fee income was nowhere on the page.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income, older return label
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Foreign income attributed to the partnership from controlled foreign entities in the old broad-exemption listed countries. Income attributed from a transferor trust in one of those countries is reported here too, and attribution is a tax construct rather than a receipt: the ATO defines it as "the income attributed to the taxpayer from controlled foreign entities, calculated in accordance with Division 7 of Part X of the ITAA 1936", and it is grossed up for foreign tax paid. The broad-exemption wording belongs to the pre-2005 form, which later returns replaced with a single listed country label.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported gross, on the version of item 22 that split listed countries into broad-exemption and limited-exemption classes.
limitation: A series built on this column stops rather than falls to zero: once the form dropped the broad-exemption wording, the same economic income appears under the plain listed country label instead, so a break in the column is a form change and not a change in offshore activity.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions define attributed foreign income and show the country-class split at item 22; the broad-exemption naming is read from the older label wording rather than from that page.
evidence_quote: Attributed foreign income is the income attributed to the taxpayer from controlled foreign entities, calculated in accordance with Division 7 of Part X of the ITAA1936, and includes an amount grossed-up under section 392 of the ITAA 1936, as appropriate, to the extent of any foreign taxes paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that attributed income is not a distribution or that this country class only exists on older forms.

value_domain: Foreign interest indicator on item 22 (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Whether the partnership held a direct or indirect interest in a foreign trust, a controlled foreign company or a transferor trust at any time in the year. It is the gateway question at item 22 that decides whether the partnership must lodge the accompanying international schedule, and the ATO ties it to statute: "Direct or indirect interests in a controlled foreign company or a foreign trust are taken to have the same meaning as set out in Division 3 of Part X of the ITAA 1936." The dollar columns on the same row carry the income, if any, that the interest produced.
value_definition: A one-character indicator, Y or N, with anything else invalid or missing; it covers the whole income year rather than a point in time.
limitation: A yes says nothing about scale or income. A partnership can hold a small interest, or a transferor trust interest created by a past transfer of property, and report nil attributed income, so the flag identifies exposure to the attribution rules rather than offshore earnings.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions publish this question, define the interests it covers by reference to the ITAA 1936 and describe the schedule it triggers.
evidence_quote: Direct or indirect interests in a controlled foreign company or a foreign trust are taken to have the same meaning as set out in Division 3 of Part X of the ITAA 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the flag is a schedule trigger that can sit above nil attributed income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net attributed FIF and FLP income
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Income attributed to the partnership from foreign investment funds and foreign life assurance policies. The ATO's instruction is precise about the measure: "Show at Y the amount of net attributed foreign income from foreign investment funds (FIFs) and foreign life assurance policies (FLPs)", which makes this the only attributed foreign income column on the return reported net rather than gross. The country columns beside it carry attribution under the controlled foreign company rules instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of the deductions allowed under the foreign investment fund measures, reported at label Y of the older item 22.
limitation: The column dies by legislation, not by behaviour: the foreign investment fund rules were repealed with effect from the 2010-11 income year, so nil values in later years mean the question no longer exists and cannot be read as firms withdrawing from offshore funds.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions define the FIF and FLP labels and state that the amount is net attributed income; the repeal date is general tax knowledge rather than a claim from that page.
evidence_quote: Show at Y the amount of net attributed foreign income from foreign investment funds (FIFs) and foreign life assurance policies (FLPs).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is net, nor that the underlying rules were repealed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income, older return label
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Foreign income attributed to the partnership from controlled foreign entities in the old limited-exemption listed countries. That class sat between the fully listed countries and the unlisted ones. On later forms the same class was relabelled the section 404 country column, which the ATO describes as covering "attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in section 404 countries". The distinction mattered because only designated concession income was attributed from these countries, so amounts here are typically small next to the unlisted country column.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported gross, on the version of item 22 that separated limited-exemption listed countries from broad-exemption listed and unlisted countries.
limitation: It cannot be added to a section 404 country series to make a continuous measure without saying so, because the two labels describe the same class under different names and the countries in the class were themselves changed by regulation over the period.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions document the three-way country split at item 22, including the section 404 class that succeeded the limited-exemption wording; the mapping between the two labels is inferred.
evidence_quote: Show at U the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in section 404 countries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished this country class from the broad-exemption and unlisted columns on the same return.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign income from unlisted countries
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Foreign income attributed to the partnership from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries, meaning everywhere outside the listed schedule. The ATO instruction is direct: "Show at X the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries", and income attributed from a transferor trust that does not belong in the listed columns is also reported here. Of the country columns this is the one that survived the form changes, so it is the most comparable of them across years.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported gross of foreign tax, at label X of item 22.
limitation: Because unlisted is defined as a residual, a rise here can follow a country leaving the listed schedule rather than any change in where the partnership invests, and the column carries no country detail to check that against.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions define the unlisted country label, its residual construction against the listed schedule, and the transferor trust income that also falls into it.
evidence_quote: Show at X the amount of attributed foreign income from controlled foreign entities in unlisted countries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said unlisted is a residual class defined by regulation.

value_domain: Foreign investment fund interest indicator on item 22 (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010
variable_description: Whether the partnership held an interest in a foreign investment fund or a foreign life assurance policy during the year. It is the companion gateway question to the controlled foreign entity indicator and, like it, decides whether the international schedule had to be attached; the ATO anchors it in statute, saying "Interest in a FIF or FLP has the same meaning as set out in section 483 of the ITAA 1936." The dollar column for FIF and FLP income sits on the same item.
value_definition: A one-character indicator, Y or N, with anything else invalid or missing, covering the income year as a whole.
limitation: It is only available while the foreign investment fund rules were in force, so it cannot be used to track offshore fund holdings past 2009-10, and even within that period a yes says nothing about the value of the interest or whether any income was attributed from it.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions publish the question, define the interest by reference to the ITAA 1936 and explain the schedule it triggers.
evidence_quote: Interest in a FIF or FLP has the same meaning as set out in section 483 of the ITAA 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the abbreviated label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said this is an interest flag rather than an income amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Australian franking credits at item 23
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Australian franking credits attached to dividends the partnership received from a New Zealand franking company, directly or through another partnership or trust. Under trans-Tasman imputation a New Zealand company can maintain an Australian franking account, and the ATO instructs partnerships to "Show at label D the amount of Australian franking credits that are included in the net income of the partnership because of franked dividends received from a New Zealand franking company". The dividend itself is reported as foreign source income at the same item, not as an Australian dividend.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, expressed in Australian dollars, at item 23 label D.
limitation: It is not the partners' entitlement. The ATO warns that "The amount shown at label D isn't necessarily the total amount that each partner can claim", since the holding period and related payments rules apply partner by partner, and New Zealand imputation credits are excluded entirely because Australian residents cannot use them.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define the label, explain the trans-Tasman imputation treatment and state what is excluded from it.
evidence_quote: Show at label D the amount of Australian franking credits that are included in the net income of the partnership because of franked dividends received from a New Zealand franking company directly, or indirectly through another partnership or trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained trans-Tasman imputation or why New Zealand credits are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net Australian income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The partnership's Australian income for the year less its Australian deductions, the closest thing on the return to a bottom line. The ATO defines it as "the net income or loss relating to Australian income, that is, total Australian income minus total deductions", and a loss is marked by an L indicator beside the amount rather than by a negative sign. Foreign income and attributed foreign income are added afterwards at items 22 to 24, so this figure is deliberately domestic.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, unsigned on the form, with a separate loss indicator carrying the sign.
limitation: It is not taxable income of anyone. A partnership pays no tax; the amount is divided among partners in the statement of distribution and taxed in their hands, so aggregating this column across partnerships and adding it to company taxable income double counts income that flows to corporate partners.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions state the arithmetic behind item 20, the treatment of the loss indicator and the exclusion of foreign income.
evidence_quote: Show at label $ the net income or loss relating to Australian income, that is, total Australian income minus total deductions from item 19.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the form's own bracketed arithmetic and printed the generic sentence twice, so it never said the amount is untaxed at the partnership or that foreign income sits outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductions against Australian investment income
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: What the partnership deducted against its Australian interest and dividend income, reported at item 16. The ATO scopes it tightly - "Show at label P the expenses the partnership incurs in earning interest and dividends" - so business expenses belong at item 5 and rental expenses at item 9. Decline in value on assets used to earn that investment income is also included here unless the assets sit in a low-value pool.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 16 label P, reported after any statutory reduction rather than as expenses incurred.
limitation: It is the allowable figure, not the incurred one: the thin capitalisation and debt deduction creation rules can disallow part of the interest cost before it reaches this label, so a partnership with heavy borrowing may show a smaller deduction than its accounts do, for reasons the column cannot reveal.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define what belongs at label P, what is pushed to other items, and the rules that reduce the amount before it is reported.
evidence_quote: Show at label P the expenses the partnership incurs in earning interest and dividends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is net of thin capitalisation disallowance or how it differs from business expenses.

value_domain: Dollar amount of bad debts expense at item 5
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The bad debts the partnership wrote off as a business expense during the income year. The ATO asks for the accounting figure - "Show at label F the bad debts expense incurred for the income year" - so it is the expense as booked, before the tax tests are applied, and recoveries of amounts previously written off are reported separately as other business income. Deductibility is conditional, since the ATO states you cannot claim under subsection 25-35(1) of the ITAA 1997 unless the debt was previously included in assessable income or is a money-lending debt.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 5 label F, gross of any later recovery.
limitation: Writing a debt off is not the same as deducting it: amounts here can be added back at the expense reconciliation label when the statutory conditions are not met, and because recoveries are booked as income elsewhere the column cannot give a firm's net loss on debtors for the year.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions give the label, state what the expense covers, where recoveries go and which statutory test governs deductibility.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the bad debts expense incurred for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two-word label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never separated the accounting write-off from the deduction, or said where recoveries appear.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2021
variable_description: How many depreciating assets the partnership kept out of the backing business investment concession. The ATO asks for the count of opted-out assets: "Show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation for." The concession gave an extra 50 per cent deduction in the first year for eligible assets first used or installed from 12 March 2020 to 30 June 2021, and opting out is an asset-by-asset choice that cannot be revoked. The companion column carries the value of the same assets.
value_definition: An integer count of assets, held as a five-digit character field, for one income year.
limitation: It counts only the assets a partnership declined the concession on, never the eligible population, so it cannot be used as a denominator or as a measure of investment. The measure itself ran for two income years either side of 30 June 2021, so the column is structurally empty elsewhere.
rationale: The 2021 partnership instructions publish the backing business investment labels, the eligibility window and the irrevocable, asset-by-asset nature of the opt-out choice.
evidence_quote: Show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation for.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the count covers only opted-out assets in a two-year window.

value_domain: Dollar value of assets opted out of backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2021
variable_description: The cost of the assets the partnership kept out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation, reported at label X. The ATO asks for asset cost here - "Show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation" - which is a different quantity from the temporary full expensing opt-out value on the same page, where the amount asked for is the deduction forgone. Reading the two columns as the same thing overstates or understates whichever is being compared.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year, measured as asset cost rather than as a deduction, at item 49 label X.
limitation: It cannot be added to the temporary full expensing opt-out value to make a total, because the two labels measure different things, and neither tells you what the partnership claimed instead under the ordinary capital allowance rules.
rationale: The 2021 partnership instructions define both opt-out value labels in adjacent paragraphs, which is what establishes that one is asset cost and the other a forgone deduction.
evidence_quote: Show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment – accelerated depreciation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and printed the generic sentence twice, so it never distinguished this value from the temporary full expensing opt-out value.

value_domain: Dollar amount of temporary full expensing deductions
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2021
variable_description: The total deduction the partnership claimed under temporary full expensing. That COVID-era measure let the whole cost of an eligible depreciating asset be written off in the year it was first used. It is a timing measure: the deduction that would otherwise have been spread over the asset's effective life is pulled into a single year, so a spike here is not a change in investment returns. The count of assets claimed for and the opt-out labels sit beside it on item 49.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one income year at item 49 label S, covering assets and improvements written off in full rather than depreciated.
limitation: A zero does not mean the partnership chose ordinary depreciation. The ATO states that small businesses using the simplified depreciation rules "must apply temporary full expensing" and "can't opt out" for those assets, so the column mixes voluntary claims with compulsory ones and cannot measure take-up of a choice.
rationale: The 2021 partnership instructions list label S among the new capital allowances labels and set out who must apply temporary full expensing and who may opt out.
evidence_quote: Small businesses using the simplified depreciation rules must apply temporary full expensing. You can't opt out of temporary full expensing for assets that the simplified depreciation rules apply to.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the deduction is a timing effect or that some businesses had no choice about it.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 32 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 (NAT 0659)
variable_description: The part of the partnership's primary production business income that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, reported at item 32 label A. Non-concessional MIT income is income from stapled and similar structures that the 2019 rules deny the concessional managed investment trust withholding rate, so it is a tax character rather than a line of business. The form notes that "Amounts shown at A and B must also be included at 5G PP - Other business income", which places it inside item 5 rather than beside it.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 32 label A, covering the primary production side of business income only.
limitation: Adding it to total business income double counts, because the same dollars are already reported at item 5. It is also a partnership-level split with no counterparty detail, so it will not identify which stapled structure the income came through.
rationale: The partnership tax return form sets out item 32, its four business income labels and the notes tying each pair back to the item 5 income labels.
evidence_quote: Note: Amounts shown at A and B must also be included at 5G PP – Other business income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is a memorandum split of income already counted at item 5.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 32 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 (NAT 0659)
variable_description: Primary production business income that the stapled structure rules reach but exclude, so it keeps its concessional treatment. It is the counterpart to the non-concessional label on the same item, and the pair together cover the income the rules touch: the form reports them at labels A and B and notes that both "must also be included at 5G PP - Other business income". Income the rules never reach is not reported at item 32 at all.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 32 label B, restricted to primary production business income.
limitation: A nil value is ambiguous: it can mean the partnership had no stapled structure income, or that all of it was non-concessional, and the column does not record which exclusion, such as the transitional or economic infrastructure exclusions, was relied on.
rationale: The partnership tax return form prints the excluded-from-NCMI labels alongside the NCMI labels and ties both to the item 5 business income labels.
evidence_quote: Note: Amounts shown at A and B must also be included at 5G PP – Other business income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing explained what excluded from NCMI means or why the amount is also inside item 5.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 32 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 (NAT 0659)
variable_description: The part of the partnership's non-primary-production business income that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, reported at item 32 label C. This is the general-business counterpart of the primary production label, and it is where stapled structure income of trading, property and infrastructure partnerships appears. The form directs that "Amounts shown at C and D must also be included at 5H Non-PP - Other business income".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 32 label C, covering non-primary-production business income only.
limitation: It cannot be summed with the primary production NCMI label to get an entity total without first checking the partnerships and trusts NCMI labels on the same item, which carry the same character of income received indirectly and are reported separately.
rationale: The partnership tax return form separates business income NCMI from partnerships and trusts NCMI and gives the item 5 label each pair must also appear at.
evidence_quote: Note: Amounts shown at C and D must also be included at 5H Non-PP – Other business income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said there are four NCMI blocks on the item and how this one differs.

value_domain: Dollar amount at item 32 of the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 (NAT 0659)
variable_description: Non-primary-production business income that the stapled structure rules reach but exclude, reported at item 32 label D. It retains concessional managed investment trust treatment and is the largest of the four business income NCMI labels in practice, because most excluded income arises in trading and infrastructure activity rather than in primary production. Like its three neighbours it duplicates amounts already shown at item 5.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 32 label D, restricted to non-primary-production business income.
limitation: The exclusion it records is a statutory carve-out, not a judgement about the economics of the arrangement, so a reader cannot infer from a large value here that the structure was ordinary commercial trading rather than stapled.
rationale: The partnership tax return form prints label D beside the non-concessional label C for non-primary production business income and gives the item 5 tie-back note for both.
evidence_quote: Note: Amounts shown at C and D must also be included at 5H Non-PP – Other business income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the abbreviated label with the generic sentence printed twice, so the split between excluded and non-concessional income was never explained.

value_domain: Personal services income business premises test indicator (Y/N)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Whether the partnership claims it satisfied the business premises test for personal services income. The ATO sets a demanding standard: the premises must be maintained "at all times" during the year, used mainly to earn the personal services income, used exclusively, and physically separate from the private residence of the individual and their associates. Passing it is one of three fallback routes to personal services business status once the results test has failed.
value_definition: A one-character indicator, Y or N, with anything else invalid or missing, asked once for the return rather than for each individual.
limitation: A blank is not a failure. The question is only reached where the results test was not satisfied, no Commissioner's determination is held, and the 80 per cent rule does not shut the tests off, so most partnerships never answer it and the population that does is selected.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions set out the conditions of the business premises test and the sequence of questions that governs when the label is completed.
evidence_quote: You met the business premises test if, at all times during 2024–25, you maintain and use business premises:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the three-word label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the test requires or that the question is only reached in some cases.

value_domain: ATO client market segment code
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE) overview
variable_description: The ATO's own market segment for the business lodging the return: government, large, small to medium, individual and non-business, micro, or not for profit. It is an administrative classification the ATO attaches to a client for service and compliance purposes, not a field anyone completes on the return, and it is driven mainly by entity type and size. It sits beside the industry code and the aggregated turnover band as the third size-and-type descriptor on the record.
value_definition: A three-letter code with six categories, GOV, LGE, SME, INB, MIC and NFP, and everything else treated as an invalid or missing response.
limitation: The thresholds behind the segments are ATO operational settings that have been revised over the years, so a business can move between segments without changing size, and a segment change cannot be read as growth. It is also not the ABS employment or turnover size class used elsewhere in BLADE.
rationale: No fetchable ATO page publishing the market segment definitions was found, so the reading is assembled from the code labels in the data item list and general knowledge of ATO client segmentation; the ABS BLADE page is cited because it establishes that the Business Income Tax module is ATO-sourced.
evidence_quote: Australian Taxation Office: Business Activity Statements (BAS), Business Income Tax (BIT) filings
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed the six codes with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the segment is assigned by the ATO rather than reported by the business.

value_domain: Significant global entity indicator code
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Whether the partnership was a significant global entity for the income year. The status turns on the size of the global group rather than of the Australian business. The ATO instructs the lodger to "Print X at label G1 if the partnership was a significant global entity (SGE) for the income year", and an entity qualifies if it is, or belongs to a group headed by, "a global parent entity with an annual global income of A$1 billion or more". Being an SGE brings country-by-country reporting, general purpose financial statement and higher penalty obligations.
value_definition: A single code where 5 means significant global entity and everything else is an invalid or missing response, so the column works as a one-sided flag rather than a yes-no pair.
limitation: It is not a size measure for the Australian entity: a small partnership inside a large multinational group is flagged, while a substantial standalone Australian partnership is not. The population also widens over time, because from 1 July 2019 the definition was extended past listed groups to groups headed by private companies, trusts and partnerships.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions give the label, the statutory tests for SGE status and the notional listed company group extension, which is what the bare data item list code lacks.
evidence_quote: Print X at label G1 if the partnership was a significant global entity (SGE) for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the single code and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the test is about global group income rather than Australian scale.

value_domain: Dollar value of trading stock on hand at year end
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The value of the partnership's trading stock on hand at the end of the income year, reported at item 41. It is a stock at a point in time rather than a flow, and it feeds the cost of sales figure at item 5 through the opening-plus-purchases-less-closing arithmetic. Small business entities can take a shortcut: they need to account for the change in value only where opening stock and a reasonable estimate of closing stock "varies by more than $5,000".
value_definition: A dollar amount at one date, the last day of the income year, accompanied by a code letter recording the valuation method used.
limitation: A flat series is not evidence of stable inventory. Where the small business shortcut applies, closing stock is simply set equal to opening stock, so the figure can repeat unchanged for years while the actual stock on hand moves, and stock valued below cost for obsolescence is not identifiable here.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions give item 41, the $5,000 rule for small business entities and the valuation code that accompanies the amount.
evidence_quote: Small business entities only need to account for changes in the value of trading stock if the value of stock on hand at the start of the income year and a reasonable estimate of the value of stock on hand at the end of the income year varies by more than $5,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two-word label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never mentioned the simplified trading stock shortcut that can freeze the value.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation method code (cost, market selling value, replacement value)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Which method the partnership used to value its closing stock: cost, market selling value or replacement value. The ATO lets a taxpayer choose among the three for each item of stock each year and records the choice in a code box beside the amount, instructing the lodger to "Print in the CODE box at label D the code letter from Table that matches the code the partnership uses to value closing stock". The method chosen changes the reported stock value, and therefore cost of sales, without any change in the goods themselves.
value_definition: A three-way code. The BLADE codes 5, 10 and 15 correspond to the ATO's C for cost, M for market selling value and R for replacement value; anything else is an invalid or missing response.
limitation: It does not record a valuation below the lowest of the three, which a partnership may elect for obsolete stock and which is instead flagged by the separate trading stock election question. The code also applies to the return as a whole even though the choice is legally available item by item.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions publish the code table at item 41 and the rule for which year's method the code refers to.
evidence_quote: Print in the CODE box at label D the code letter from Table that matches the code the partnership uses to value closing stock in the previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry listed three numeric codes with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never said that changing method moves the reported stock value on its own.

value_domain: Dollar amount of cost of sales at item 5
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: What the partnership's goods cost it, reported as the cost of sales expense at item 5 label E. It is an accounting figure taken from the profit and loss statement before the tax reconciliation at the same item, except for small business entities, who "should use tax values for their closing stock in calculating label E Cost of sales". Wages of staff engaged in production are inside it, which is why the salary and wage item elsewhere on the return overlaps with it.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 5 label E, reported on an accounting basis and excluding GST where the partnership is registered.
limitation: Expense labels on this return cannot simply be added: the ATO states that the total salary and wage expenses item "include any salary and wage component shown at item 5 - label E Cost of sales", so a sum across labels counts the same wages twice.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define the cost of sales label, the treatment for small business entities using simplified trading stock rules and the overlap with the salary and wage item.
evidence_quote: These expenses include any salary and wage component shown at item 5 – label E Cost of sales
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the three-word label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that the expense labels overlap.

value_domain: Dollar amount of capital works deductions
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The deduction the partnership claimed for the construction cost of buildings and structural improvements, under the Division 43 capital works rules. The ATO explains that "Division 43 of the ITAA 1997 provides for a system of deducting capital expenditure incurred in the construction of capital works used to produce assessable income", covering buildings, extensions, fit-outs, and structural improvements such as bridges, retaining walls and sealed roads. On the partnership return the label sits inside the rent item, so it is the rental property figure rather than a deduction for the partnership's own trading premises.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, calculated as a fixed annual percentage of actual construction cost rather than of the building's market value.
limitation: It will not track property values or capital spending in the year: the deduction runs off historical construction cost, often incurred by a previous owner and estimated by a quantity surveyor, and continues at the same rate whether the building appreciates or falls in value.
rationale: Appendix 5 of the 2025 partnership instructions defines capital works deductions, what construction expenditure qualifies and how the amount must be based on actual costs.
evidence_quote: Division 43 of the ITAA 1997 provides for a system of deducting capital expenditure incurred in the construction of capital works used to produce assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the three-word label with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said the deduction runs off historical construction cost or that it is reported in the rent item.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign resident withholding credit
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: Tax withheld in Australia from payments to the partnership under the foreign resident withholding rules, claimed as a credit at item 6. The ATO restricts the item sharply: "Only foreign residents complete this item", and the corresponding gross payments must be shown as business income at item 5 label B. The credit flows through to partners rather than being refunded to the partnership.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 6 label U, covering amounts withheld and remitted in Australia.
limitation: It is not the partnership's total withholding credit. Shares of foreign resident withholding credits received through other partnerships and trusts are reported at item 8 instead, and foreign resident capital gains withholding is excluded altogether, so a firm's exposure to withholding cannot be read off this column alone.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions define who completes the label, what it covers, the income label it must match and the two categories deliberately kept out of it.
evidence_quote: Only foreign residents complete this item.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the item is completed only by foreign residents or where the indirect credits go.

value_domain: Dollar amount of TFN withholding credit received indirectly
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The partnership's share of tax file number amounts withheld from investment income received through other partnerships and trusts. It is reported at item 8, and covers interest, dividends and unit trust distributions. TFN withholding is applied by investment bodies at the top marginal rate when an investor has not quoted a tax file number, so a non-zero amount here signals a missing TFN somewhere upstream rather than a tax liability of the partnership. Amounts withheld directly from the partnership's own interest and dividends are reported at items 11 and 12 instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year at item 8, being a share of credits withheld by third parties rather than an amount the partnership itself withheld or paid.
limitation: It cannot be used to identify which investment or which upstream entity failed to quote a tax file number, and it is not additive with the direct TFN withholding columns at the interest and dividend items, which cover the same mechanism at a different point in the chain.
rationale: The 2025 partnership instructions list the credit types that come through the partnerships and trusts item, including the share of TFN amounts withheld, and separate them from the directly withheld amounts.
evidence_quote: Share of credit for TFN amounts withheld from interest, dividends and unit trust distributions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long form label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is an indirect share or what triggers TFN withholding.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Trade creditors on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: What the partnership still owed its suppliers on the last day of the income year. The ATO instruction for item 43 reads: "Show at label H the total amounts owed by the partnership at year end for goods and services received during the income year, that is, current trade creditors." It is a balance sheet stock read on one day, and the ATO directs the same money to be counted again inside All current liabilities, so this column and p_currliab must never be added together.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label H of item 43 in the business and professional items section of the partnership return, taken from the partnership's own accounts.
limitation: A year-end balance is not a year's purchasing. A firm that buys heavily but settles within a week shows almost nothing here, and a firm that stretches its suppliers shows a large number on the same trading volume, so the column measures payment behaviour and timing at least as much as scale.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces item 43 of the partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction for that item defines what the label holds and how it relates to All current liabilities.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the total amounts owed by the partnership at year end for goods and services received during the income year, that is, current trade creditors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word return label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said this is a year-end stock nested inside current liabilities.

value_domain: Dollar amount of TFN withholding credit from a closely held trust, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Tax that a closely held trust withheld from its distributions to this partnership because no tax file number was given, claimed back as a credit. The ATO instruction for item 8 label O reads: "Show at label O the amounts withheld from payments where a TFN has not been provided to the trustee of a closely held trust." The credit does not stop at the partnership: it is passed out to the partners in proportion to their interests, so the same money reappears in the statement of distribution.
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 8 label O of the partnership return. Non-negative, and populated only for a partnership that was a beneficiary of a closely held trust which withheld from a payment or distribution.
limitation: A figure here records a missing tax file number somewhere in the chain above the firm, not a tax liability of the firm itself, and the withholding was performed by a trustee the partnership does not control. It is a credit rather than income, so adding it to the distribution amounts on the same row double counts.
rationale: The DIL label is the wording of item 8 label O on the partnership return, and the ATO instruction for that label defines the credit and says who may ultimately claim it.
evidence_quote: Show at label O the amounts withheld from payments where a TFN has not been provided to the trustee of a closely held trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long return label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is a credit that flows through to the partners rather than a receipt of the partnership.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at All current assets on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Key financial information items 33 to 36
variable_description: Everything the partnership held at year end that it expected to turn into cash within the year.
