The ATO instruction is broad: "Show at label F all current assets of the partnership, including cash on hand, short-term bills receivable, inventories and trade debtors as shown at item 42 Trade debtors." It is a book figure lifted from the partnership's accounts rather than a tax-law amount, and it contains the trade debtors reported separately at p_debtors.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label F of item 33, one of the four key financial information items that carry the partnership's balance sheet totals.
limitation: It is not a liquidity measure on its own, because the matching claim on those assets sits in a different column and the mix inside the total is invisible: cash and slow-moving stock are added together here. Partnerships that keep no formal balance sheet can leave the key financial information items empty, so a blank is not evidence of a firm with no assets.
rationale: The DIL label is item 33 of the partnership return and the ATO instruction lists what the label must contain and which other item it overlaps.
evidence_quote: Show at label F all current assets of the partnership, including cash on hand, short-term bills receivable, inventories and trade debtors as shown at item 42 Trade debtors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Current assets' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is an accounting total that already includes trade debtors.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at All current liabilities on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Key financial information items 33 to 36
variable_description: What the partnership owed at year end and expected to settle within the year. The ATO instruction for item 35 reads: "Show at label I the total obligations payable by the partnership in 2022-23; include the amount shown at item 43 Trade creditors." Trade creditors are therefore a component of this total, not an addition to it, and the figure is a stock on the balance sheet date rather than anything the partnership paid over the year.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label I of item 35, sitting alongside All current assets, Total assets and Total liabilities in the key financial information block.
limitation: The column cannot show what the money is owed for. Bank overdrafts, unpaid tax, supplier balances and employee entitlements all land in the one number, so a rising figure could mean growth, distress or a shift in financing, and only the split against current assets and total liabilities distinguishes them. Partnerships without accounts leave it blank.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 35 of the partnership return and the ATO instruction states both what belongs in it and that it subsumes the separately reported trade creditors item.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the total obligations payable by the partnership in 2022-23; include the amount shown at item 43 Trade creditors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Current liabilities' with the generic sentence printed twice, so it never distinguished a balance sheet stock from a flow or flagged the overlap with trade creditors.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductible balancing adjustment on intangible depreciating assets, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: The deduction the partnership took because it disposed of a patent, a copyright or in-house software for less than the value still on its books. The ATO instruction reads: "At label G, show the total deductible amount you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred in 2021-22 (this type of deduction may arise if, for example, you disposed of a depreciating asset for less than its adjustable value)." Its mirror image, the assessable balancing adjustment at the neighbouring label, records disposals above adjustable value.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label G in the capital allowances block of the partnership's business and professional items, covering intangible depreciating assets only.
limitation: This is a write-down on exit, not a measure of how much intellectual property the partnership sold or how much it was worth: an asset sold at a good price produces nothing here and shows up in the assessable balancing adjustment instead. Assets costing under $1,000 that were put in a low-value pool are excluded by instruction, so small software disposals never appear.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the partnership return label for deductible balancing adjustments on intangible depreciating assets and the ATO instruction for that label defines when the amount arises and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: At label G, show the total deductible amount you have from balancing adjustment events on the disposal of intangible depreciating assets that occurred in 2021-22 (this type of deduction may arise if, for example, you disposed of a depreciating asset for less than its adjustable value).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long return label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that a balancing adjustment is a disposal calculation or that the deductible and assessable versions are opposite outcomes.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the small business skills and training bonus deduction, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Small business skills and training boost
variable_description: The extra 20 per cent deduction the partnership claimed for sending its employees on external training courses. The ATO describes the measure as allowing "an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers", available to businesses with aggregated annual turnover under $50 million for spending between 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2024. Dividing the amount by 0.2 recovers the eligible training spend, which is not itself reported.
value_definition: A whole-dollar bonus deduction amount, equal to 20 per cent of eligible external training expenditure, reported only for income years touching the 29 March 2022 to 30 June 2024 window.
limitation: It is not a training budget. The training must be charged by a registered external provider and delivered to employees, so in-house training, coaching by an associate, and anything supplied to partners or contractors is invisible here even where the firm paid for it. The column is structurally zero outside the measure's short life, so a time series across it measures the policy, not the firm.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business skills and training boost, and the ATO's page for that measure gives the rate, the turnover threshold, the eligibility rules and the dates that bound the column.
evidence_quote: Small businesses with an aggregated annual turnover of less than $50 million will be allowed an additional 20% tax deduction for external training courses delivered to employees by registered training providers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the measure's name as its description with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a 20 per cent bonus on top of an ordinary deduction or that it exists for two income years only.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the small business technology investment bonus deduction, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Small business technology investment boost
variable_description: The extra 20 per cent deduction the partnership claimed for digitising its operations. The ATO allows businesses under $50 million turnover "an additional 20% tax deduction to support their digital operations and digitise their operations", for spending between 29 March 2022 and 30 June 2023, "capped at $100,000 of expenditure per income year". Eligible spending runs from hardware and cloud subscriptions to web design and cyber security, so this is the closest thing in the tax data to a firm's digital adoption spend.
value_definition: A whole-dollar bonus deduction, 20 per cent of eligible digital expenditure, capped at $20,000 a year and $40,000 across the measure. It has values only for income years overlapping 29 March 2022 to 30 June 2023.
limitation: The cap truncates it exactly where the interesting variation is: any firm spending more than $100,000 on digital in a year reports the same capped amount as one spending $100,000, so the column cannot rank heavy digital investors. A zero also cannot separate a firm that bought no technology from one that simply did not claim the bonus.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business technology investment boost, and the ATO's page for that measure sets out the rate, the expenditure cap, the eligible categories and the dates.
evidence_quote: An annual cap applies so that expenditure up to $100,000 is eligible for the bonus deduction, with the bonus deduction capped at $20,000 per year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the measure's name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned about the annual cap that flattens the top of the distribution or the narrow eligibility window.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Trade debtors on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: What the partnership's customers still owed it at the end of the income year. The ATO instruction for item 42 reads: "Show at label E the total amounts owing to the partnership at year end for goods and services provided during the income year, that is, current trade debtors." The same money is required to be counted again inside All current assets, so p_debtors is a component of p_currasst rather than something to add to it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at label E of item 42 in the partnership's business and professional items, taken from the partnership's accounts.
limitation: Read against turnover it looks like a collection period, but it cannot be one: the balance is struck on 30 June, so a business with seasonal sales or a large June invoice shows a debtor balance that has nothing to do with how slowly it is paid. Nothing distinguishes a current receivable from one that is long overdue and unlikely to be recovered.
rationale: The DIL label is item 42 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines both the amount and its relationship to the current assets total.
evidence_quote: Show at label E the total amounts owing to the partnership at year end for goods and services provided during the income year, that is, current trade debtors.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Trade debtors' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is a single-day balance already inside current assets.

value_domain: Dollar amount of depreciation expenses on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The depreciation the partnership charged in its profit and loss account for the year. The ATO instruction is explicit that this is an accounting figure: "Show at label K the book depreciation expenses for depreciating assets other than for those assets allocated in a prior year to a general small business pool." It is not the tax deduction for decline in value, which is reconciled to this number through Expense reconciliation adjustments at p_exprcadj.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at label K of item 5, in the primary production, non-primary production or totals column. For a small business entity using simplified depreciation it instead carries the pooled and immediate tax deductions, including temporary full expensing.
limitation: The same label means two different things depending on which depreciation regime the partnership uses, so book depreciation for one firm sits beside a full tax write-off for another and the two are not comparable. Because temporary full expensing is claimed here, the 2021 to 2023 years show large one-off amounts that reflect the timing of a deduction rather than any change in the capital a firm consumed.
rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label K on the partnership return, and the ATO instruction states that the label is book depreciation for general taxpayers but tax depreciation for small business entities using the simplified rules.
evidence_quote: The accounting or book depreciation may differ from the deduction for the decline in value of depreciating assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label 'Depreciation expenses' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that the number is book depreciation for some lodgers and a tax deduction for others.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the franked portion of dividends received, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: The part of the dividends the partnership received directly from Australian companies that carried franking credits. The ATO instruction for item 12 reads: "Show at label L the franked amount of franked dividends received before any TFN amounts were withheld." It is a gross figure struck before withholding, and it pairs with the unfranked amount at p_dufrkamt and the franking credit at p_dimpcred to describe one dividend three ways.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 12 label L, covering dividends received directly from a paying company. Distributions received through another partnership or trust are excluded and belong at item 8.
limitation: A franked amount is a share of company profit that has already borne tax, not a measure of investment return, and it says nothing about the size of the holding that produced it. Where a distribution statement did not split the dividend, the ATO directs the whole dividend to be shown here, so this label absorbs unfranked money in exactly the cases where the split is unknown.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 12 label L of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the amount, its timing relative to withholding and the treatment of unsplit distributions.
evidence_quote: Show at label L the franked amount of franked dividends received before any TFN amounts were withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the return label 'Dividends - franked amount' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished direct dividends from distributions received through a trust or partnership.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franking credits received directly, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: The company tax already paid on the dividends the partnership received directly, attached to those dividends as a credit. The ATO instruction for item 12 reads: "Show at label M the amount of franking credits received directly from a paying company." The DIL's word 'imputation credit' is the older name for the same thing; the current return calls it a franking credit, and credits arriving indirectly through another partnership or trust are excluded and sit at p_fcr_wheld_amt instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 12 label M. It is both assessable income of the partnership and the offset that flows to the partners, so it is counted in the gross-up as well as in the credit.
limitation: A partnership cannot use a franking credit itself, so this is not tax the firm recovers; the offset is claimed by the partners in their own returns and can be lost entirely if the holding period rule or the related payments rule is failed. Credits attached to New Zealand franking company dividends are excluded by instruction, so the column understates imputation for firms with trans-Tasman holdings.
rationale: The DIL label is item 12 label M of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the credit, names what is excluded and identifies where indirect credits go instead.
evidence_quote: Show at label M the amount of franking credits received directly from a paying company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the old label 'Dividends - imputation credit' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the old wording to the current franking credit label or said the offset is used by the partners.

value_domain: Dollar amount of TFN withholding on dividends, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: Tax withheld from the partnership's dividends because it had not quoted a tax file number to the paying company. The ATO instruction for item 12 reads: "Show at label N the total of TFN amounts withheld from dividends received, minus any refund of TFN amounts withheld." It is a net figure, reduced by any refund of earlier withholding, and it sits beside the franked, unfranked and franking credit labels that describe the dividends themselves.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 12 label N. Withholding runs at the top marginal rate plus levy where a TFN is not quoted, so a non-zero value implies a large proportion of the related dividend.
limitation: A value here marks an administrative gap rather than a business fact, and it cannot be read as a tax cost, since the credit is claimed by the partners. Because the amount is net of refunds, a partnership that quoted its TFN part-way through the year and recovered the withholding can report a small figure that understates what was actually taken.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces item 12 label N on the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the amount and states that refunds are netted off.
evidence_quote: Show at label N the total of TFN amounts withheld from dividends received, minus any refund of TFN amounts withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'TFN amounts withheld from dividends' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is net of refunds or that the credit passes to the partners.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net non-primary production distributions received, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: What the partnership netted from its interests in other partnerships and trusts, outside farming. The ATO defines the total as "the net result of adding the partnership distributions of non-primary production income and the partnership's share of non-primary production income included in the trust's net income (for tax purposes), minus deductions related to that income, plus the net amount of the franked distributions from trusts, minus the deductions relating to the franked distributions from trusts". It can be negative, in which case the return prints an L beside it, and a sign is not carried in the dollar figure itself.
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 8 of the partnership return, built from labels B, R, T, F and G. Its primary production twin is p_dstbn_pp_net_amt, and the two are quarantined from each other because primary producers get separate treatment.
limitation: It is income the partnership received from elsewhere, not income it earned by trading, so treating it as revenue attributes another entity's activity to this firm. A loss shown here is marked by a code letter on the paper return, so a data extract that drops the loss indicator turns a negative into a positive of the same size.
rationale: The DIL label matches the Net non-primary production amount box at item 8 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction states exactly which labels are added and subtracted to reach it.
evidence_quote: Show at this entry the net result of adding the partnership distributions of non-primary production income and the partnership's share of non-primary production income included in the trust's net income (for tax purposes), minus deductions related to that income, plus the net amount of the franked distributions from trusts, minus the deductions relating to the franked distributions from trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the abbreviated label 'Net distribution amount - NPP' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which components it nets or that it can be a loss.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net primary production distributions received, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: What the partnership netted from farming interests held through other partnerships and trusts. The ATO defines it as "the net result of adding partnership distributions of primary production income and the partnership's share of primary production income that has been included in the net income (for tax purposes) of a trust minus allowable deductions related to that income". A firm with a value here is a participant in a farming structure it does not itself operate, which is why the primary production column is kept apart from the non-primary production one.
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 8 built from labels A, Z and S. The separate primary production stream exists because farm income attracts averaging and farm management deposit rules at the partner level.
limitation: The column identifies farm income received, not farming done: a partnership can report a large amount here while owning no land, running no stock and employing nobody in agriculture. It is also not a farm profit, since the trust or partnership above it has already taken out its own costs.
rationale: The DIL label matches the Net primary production amount box at item 8, and the ATO instruction sets out the components that are added and the deductions taken off.
evidence_quote: Show at this entry the net result of adding partnership distributions of primary production income and the partnership's share of primary production income that has been included in the net income (for tax purposes) of a trust minus allowable deductions related to that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net distribution - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the primary production split or that the money comes from another entity.

value_domain: Dollar amount of deductions against franked distributions from trusts, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: The partnership's own costs of earning the franked distributions it received through trusts. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label G the partnership's deductions for its own expenses incurred in deriving its share of the franked distributions from trusts at label F." The label F referred to in the BLADE wording is p_frkdntrst on the same row, so the two columns are a matched income and expense pair and neither is meaningful alone.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at item 8 label G of the partnership return, restricted to expenses attributable to the franked distributions reported at label F.
limitation: Only the partnership's own expenses belong here; costs the trust incurred before distributing are already netted off upstream and can never be recovered from this column. Borrowing costs shown here may be cut back under the thin capitalisation rules, so the figure is what survived those rules rather than what the partnership spent.
rationale: The DIL label quotes the partnership return's own cross-reference to label F, and the ATO instruction for label G defines the deduction and its restriction.
evidence_quote: Show at label G the partnership's deductions for its own expenses incurred in deriving its share of the franked distributions from trusts at label F.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the return label, including its bare reference to 'label F', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know which column label F is.

value_domain: Dollar amount of project pool deduction on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: The deduction the partnership took for capital spending on a project, written off over the project's life rather than against any one asset. The ATO instruction is short: "Show at label J the partnership's deductions for project pools." A project pool holds capital costs that are directly connected with a project but do not form the cost of a depreciating asset, such as site preparation or feasibility work, which is why the amount sits in capital allowances rather than in ordinary expenses.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at label J in the capital allowances block of the partnership's business and professional items, and one of the expense subtractions that also feeds the reconciliation at p_exprcadj.
limitation: The amount is one year's slice of a pool, so it tells you a project exists but not what it cost, when it started or whether it succeeded. It also cannot be added to depreciation without double counting the reconciliation, because project pool deductions are among the items reconciled at Expense reconciliation adjustments.
rationale: The DIL label is the partnership return's label J in the capital allowances block, and the ATO instruction for that label and for the reconciliation item together place the deduction.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the partnership's deductions for project pools.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Deduction for project pool' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a project pool holds or that the deduction is an annual instalment.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the unfranked portion of dividends received, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: The part of the partnership's directly received dividends that carried no franking credit. The ATO instruction for item 12 reads: "Show at label K the gross amount of unfranked dividends, and the unfranked amount of partially franked dividends, received before any TFN amounts were withheld." A partially franked dividend is therefore split across this column and p_dfrkdamt, and the ATO also directs certain Division 7A deemed dividends here.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 12 label K, gross of any tax file number withholding, covering dividends received directly rather than through a partnership or trust.
limitation: An unfranked dividend is not evidence that the paying company avoided tax: it can equally mean profits taxed overseas, capital returns or a company with no franking account balance. Because the same label carries amounts treated as dividends under Division 7A, a figure here can also reflect a loan or forgiven debt rather than a distribution of profits.
rationale: The DIL label is item 12 label K of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the amount, the treatment of partly franked dividends and the deemed dividends that also land here.
evidence_quote: Show at label K the gross amount of unfranked dividends, and the unfranked amount of partially franked dividends, received before any TFN amounts were withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dividends - unfranked amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column splits partly franked dividends or absorbs deemed dividends.

value_domain: Coded choice to opt out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2021 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: Whether the partnership chose not to use the accelerated depreciation offered under backing business investment, for some of its eligible assets or for all of them. The ATO instruction reads: "Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets." The choice is made asset by asset and cannot be reversed: "Once a choice is made it can't be revoked." Backing business investment applied to new assets first used between 12 March 2020 and 30 June 2021, so the column is alive for two income years only.
value_definition: A coded flag with 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets and 15 for no; anything else is an invalid or absent response. The letters A and B on the paper return map to 5 and 10.
limitation: Opting out is not the same as not claiming. A firm that bought no new assets, or that used temporary full expensing or the instant asset write-off instead, never reaches this question, so a code of 15 or a blank covers both a deliberate no and a firm the measure never touched.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the 2021 partnership return question at label V, and the ATO instruction for that label gives the two response letters, the irrevocability of the choice and the years the measure ran.
evidence_quote: Show A at V if you are opting out for some of your eligible assets and show B if you are opting out for all of your eligible assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text and its code list but printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the choice is per asset, irreversible, or confined to 2019-20 and 2020-21.

value_domain: Count of assets claimed under temporary full expensing, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: How many separate assets the partnership wrote off in full under temporary full expensing this year. The ATO label guide says to "Show the total number of assets for which you are claiming temporary full expensing", at label 49T on the partnership return. It is a count that sits beside the dollar deduction, so the two together give an average cost per asset written off, which no other column in the return provides.
value_definition: A five-digit character count of assets at the partnership return's temporary full expensing label, reported for income years from 2020-21 to 2022-23.
limitation: The number is a best effort rather than a verified count: the ATO states that "You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect number of assets where you have made your best attempt to determine the number of assets you are claiming for." A firm that groups a fitout as one asset and a firm that lists every component report very different counts for the same spend.
rationale: The ATO label guide maps this exact wording to the partnership return label and states both what the count covers and the tolerance applied to it.
evidence_quote: You will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect number of assets where you have made your best attempt to determine the number of assets you are claiming for.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the count is self-assessed and tolerant of error, or that it pairs with the deduction amount.

value_domain: Coded choice to opt out of temporary full expensing
value_source: ATO, Temporary full expensing tax return label guide
variable_description: Whether the partnership chose not to write off some or all of its eligible assets immediately under temporary full expensing. The ATO label guide directs the lodger to write "A if you are opting out for some of your assets" or "B if you are opting out for all of your assets", at label 49P on the partnership return. Opting out is a real economic choice, because it moves a deduction from this year into later years and can preserve a loss position or a distribution to partners.
value_definition: A coded flag with 5 for some eligible assets, 10 for all eligible assets and 15 for no; anything else is an invalid or absent response. It mirrors the letters A and B used on the paper return.
limitation: The question is closed to small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules, who cannot opt out at all and are told to leave the label blank. A blank therefore mixes those firms with firms that had no eligible assets and firms that simply took the full deduction, and this column cannot separate the three.
rationale: The ATO label guide gives the response letters for this question and, in the tables covering small business entities, states that firms using simplified depreciation cannot opt out and must leave it blank.
evidence_quote: You cannot opt out of temporary full expensing for assets that the simplified depreciation rules apply to. Leave this blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question text and its codes with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a whole class of small businesses is barred from answering.

value_domain: Personal services business employment test indicator (Y or N)
value_source: ATO, Personal services income, Employment test
variable_description: Whether the firm claims it passed the employment test, one of four tests that let personal services income be treated as a personal services business. The ATO sets the bar as employing or contracting others, plus one of two conditions: "at least 20% of the principal work is performed by others" or "one or more apprentices are employed for at least 6 months of the income year". Passing means the personal services income rules do not apply, so income is not attributed back to the individual who earned it.
value_definition: A single character flag, Y for yes and N for no, with anything else an invalid or absent response. It sits in the personal services income block alongside the results, unrelated clients and business premises tests.
limitation: This is a self-assessment, not a determination: the ATO allows a taxpayer to self-assess against the employment test without applying for a ruling, so a Y is the firm's own claim and can be overturned on review. Where a partnership or company has more than one individual generating personal services income the test is applied to each of them separately, so one flag cannot describe the whole entity.
rationale: The ATO's personal services income guidance defines the employment test, its two alternative conditions, the 80 per cent rule that must also be met, and its application to partnerships, which is what a Y or N on this column asserts.
evidence_quote: If you operate through a company, partnership or trust and you have more than one individual generating PSI, you will need to work out whether you pass the employment test for each individual.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Employment test' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which test it is, what passing requires, or that the answer is self-assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of expense reconciliation adjustments, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss item 5
variable_description: The single line that bridges the partnership's accounting expenses and its tax deductions. It nets add backs, such as non-deductible entertainment, penalties and fines and prepayments not yet deductible, against subtractions, such as the tax decline in value of depreciating assets, project pool deductions and section 40-880 deductions. The ATO notes the result may be negative: "If the expense subtractions exceed the expense add backs, the total is a negative amount."
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed amount at item 5 label B of the partnership return, with a loss indicator printed beside it on the paper form when the net figure is negative.
limitation: The column is a residual, so a large value can come from timing, from permanent differences, or from a single depreciation regime change, and no part of the return decomposes it. Because the loss position is carried by a code letter rather than by the number, an extract that drops the indicator silently converts negative reconciliations into positive ones.
rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label B of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction lists the add backs and subtractions that make it up and states that the net figure can be negative.
evidence_quote: If the expense subtractions exceed the expense add backs, the total is a negative amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Expense Reconciliation Adjustments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is signed or that it is the accounting-to-tax bridge.

value_domain: Dollar amount of contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What the partnership paid for labour it bought in rather than employed. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages", and the examples run from consultants and sub-contractors to commissions, agency fees and management fees. The DIL label records a form change: the item used to be called External labour costs, so a long series has one wording before the change and another after it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at item 5 label C, reported in the primary production, non-primary production or totals column. It sits beside Total salary and wage expenses, which carries employed labour.
limitation: It is not the whole of a firm's outsourced labour: the ATO directs external labour recorded in the cost of sales account to stay there, and sends accounting and legal fees to All other expenses, so labour-heavy firms that book contractors into cost of sales show little here. Renaming the item also means the label change, rather than any change in behaviour, can shift what lodgers put in it.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 5 label C on the partnership return, including the note about the previous label, and the ATO instruction defines the expense and names what is directed elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Show at label C the expenditure incurred for labour and services provided under contract other than those in the nature of salaries and wages.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the return label, including the parenthetical about the previous name, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that cost-of-sales labour is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of fringe benefit employee contributions, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: What employees paid the partnership towards fringe benefits they received, such as a contribution towards a car. The ATO instruction for item 46 reads: "Show at label T all the payments the partnership has received from recipients of fringe benefits", and adds that "Employee contributions form part of the employer's or associate's assessable income in situations where employees make payments for fringe benefits they have received." A non-zero value therefore marks a firm that both provides fringe benefits and recovers part of their cost.
value_definition: A whole-dollar income amount at label T of item 46 in the partnership's business and professional items, assessable to the partnership.
limitation: It measures recovery, not provision. A firm that gives generous fringe benefits and charges nothing for them reports zero, exactly like a firm that gives none, so this column cannot be used to identify which businesses provide fringe benefits. The value of the benefits themselves is reported in the separate fringe benefits tax system, not here.
rationale: The DIL label is item 46 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the receipts and states their assessable character.
evidence_quote: Show at label T all the payments the partnership has received from recipients of fringe benefits.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Fringe benefit employee contributions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is income to the firm rather than a cost, or that zero does not mean no benefits.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franking credits received indirectly, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Franking credits that reached the partnership through another partnership or trust rather than straight from the paying company. The ATO instruction for item 8 reads: "Show at label D the partnership's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received through another partnership or trust", and directs credits received directly to item 12 instead, which is p_dimpcred. The split matters because it separates a firm that holds shares from a firm that holds an interest in an entity that holds shares.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 8 label D of the partnership return, part of the share of credits block that also carries ABN withholding, TFN withholding and foreign resident withholding credits.
limitation: A credit shown here is not necessarily usable. The ATO excludes credits where the holding period rule or the related payments rule fails, or where dividend washing applies, but only credits the lodger already knew were excluded are kept out, so the column records a claim rather than a settled entitlement. The credit is ultimately used by the partners, not by the partnership.
rationale: The DIL label is item 8 label D of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the credit, contrasts it with the direct credit at item 12 and lists the integrity rules that exclude amounts.
evidence_quote: Show at label D the partnership's share of any franking credits from a franking entity received through another partnership or trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Share of franking credits from franked distributions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished indirect credits from the direct credits at item 12.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign resident withholding credit, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Tax withheld in Australia under the foreign resident withholding measure and claimed by the partnership as a credit. The regime is narrow: it "applies to foreign residents who engage in certain regulated categories of activities in Australia, such as foreign residents involved in sport, entertainment, and building and construction". The 'share of' wording points to item 8 label U, the partnership's share of credits flowing from other partnerships and trusts, rather than item 6 label U, where withholding from the partnership's own payments is claimed.
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit amount on the partnership return, reported in whole dollars alongside the gross payments it relates to. Foreign resident capital gains withholding is excluded by instruction.
limitation: The column identifies a withholding obligation, not the firm's residence or its foreign ownership, and it exists only for the handful of regulated activity classes prescribed in the Taxation Administration Regulations. The numeric infix in the column name is a form-label sequence marker that the data item list does not explain, so it should not be read as pinning the amount to a particular return item.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the partnership return defines foreign resident withholding, sets out both the direct claim at item 6 and the share of credits at item 8, and states what is excluded, which together fix the meaning of a 'share of credit' column.
evidence_quote: Show at label U the partnership's share of any foreign resident withholding credits received from other partnerships and trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which activities the regime covers or that capital gains withholding is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount of franked distributions from trusts, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 6 to 9
variable_description: Franked dividends that reached the partnership through a trust, reported grossed up by the franking credit attached to them. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label F the partnership's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions) plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution." The deductions against this income sit at p_dtnfdtrst, and the credit itself is also counted at p_fcr_wheld_amt.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 8 label F, inclusive of the franking credit gross-up, and therefore larger than the cash the partnership actually received.
limitation: Because the figure is grossed up, treating it as cash income overstates receipts by the amount of the franking credit, and adding it to p_fcr_wheld_amt counts that credit twice. Distributions traceable to a New Zealand franking company are excluded by instruction and reported as foreign income, so a trans-Tasman group's franked income is split across two parts of the return.
rationale: The DIL label matches item 8 label F on the partnership return, and the ATO instruction states that the amount includes the franking credit gross-up and what is excluded.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the partnership's share of the franked distribution (described as franked dividends, franked distributions or attributable franked distributions) plus its share of the franking credit attached to the franked distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Franked distributions from trusts' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount is grossed up and overlaps the franking credit column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of first year backing business investment accelerated depreciation, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2021 instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 52
variable_description: The accelerated depreciation the partnership claimed in the first year it held a new asset under backing business investment. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21", and defines the amount as 50 per cent of the asset's cost plus the ordinary decline in value calculated on the remaining half. A separate label carries the subsequent year claims for the same assets, so this column isolates new investment.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at label M in the capital allowances block of the 2020-21 partnership return, restricted to assets first used or installed ready for use in that year.
limitation: The measure ran only for assets first held from 12 March 2020 and first used by 30 June 2021 by businesses under $500 million turnover, and it cannot be used on an asset that took temporary full expensing or the instant asset write-off. A zero is therefore usually a choice of a competing concession rather than an absence of investment, and a series across 2020-21 to 2021-22 breaks because the label ceases.
rationale: The DIL label reproduces the 2020-21 partnership return label M, and the ATO instruction for that label gives the calculation, the eligible assets and the year covered.
evidence_quote: Show at M the total amount claimed using Backing business investment for assets first used or installed ready for use in 2020-21.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is a first-year-only claim or that it is mutually exclusive with temporary full expensing.

value_domain: Dollar amount of forestry managed investment scheme deduction, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Deductions items 16 to 20
variable_description: What the partnership deducted for payments into a forestry managed investment scheme. The ATO allows the deduction at item 17 where the partnership holds a forestry interest, paid a forestry manager under a formal agreement and was told the scheme met the 70 per cent direct forestry expenditure rule in Division 394 of the ITAA 1997. Timing is cash based: "The deduction is claimed in the income year in which the payment is made." Its income counterpart is p_frstry_mis_incm_amt.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction at item 17 of the partnership return, covering both initial and ongoing payments for an initial participant in a scheme.
limitation: The deduction is conditional after the fact: it is denied if the partnership disposes of its forestry interest within four years of the end of the year of first payment, unless the disposal was outside its control, so a claim in the data can later be reversed. A payment here buys an interest in trees managed by someone else and is not evidence that the partnership carries on forestry.
rationale: The DIL label is item 17 of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction gives the eligibility conditions, the timing rule and the four-year clawback.
evidence_quote: The deduction is claimed in the income year in which the payment is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Forestry managed investment scheme deduction' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the deduction can be clawed back or that it is cash-timed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of forestry managed investment scheme income, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Income excluding foreign income items 10 to 15
variable_description: What the partnership received back from a forestry managed investment scheme, at item 10 of the return. It gathers thinning proceeds, harvest and sale receipts, and, where a capital gains tax event ended or reduced a forestry interest, the market value of the interest rather than the cash received. The DIL calls it income, but part of it is a deemed amount: a partnership that sold its interest reports the market value at the time of the event.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount at item 10 label Q, combining actual receipts with market-value amounts brought to account on a capital gains tax event affecting a forestry interest.
limitation: It is lumpy and event-driven, so a large value marks a harvest or a sale rather than a year of trading, and it can appear in a year in which no money changed hands. Because initial and subsequent participants are treated differently, two partnerships with the same interest can report very different amounts on the same event.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 10 of the partnership return sets out exactly which receipts and deemed amounts go to label Q and how the treatment differs for initial and subsequent participants.
evidence_quote: Include the market value of the forestry interest at the time of the CGT event at label Q
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Forestry managed investment scheme income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount can be a deemed market value rather than a receipt.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign tax paid on net foreign source income, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: Foreign tax the partnership itself paid on its foreign source income, which the partners may later claim as an offset. The current return calls the same figure a foreign income tax offset and instructs the lodger to "Show at label Z the amount of any foreign income tax paid by the partnership on foreign source income"; the data item list's phrase 'foreign tax credits' is the earlier form wording for the same idea. The offset is not used by the partnership, since the partnership is not taxed on its own income.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of foreign income tax paid, converted to Australian dollars, reported beside the gross and net foreign source income labels at item 23.
limitation: The amount is paid tax, not offset obtained: each partner's claim is apportioned by their share of net income and is capped by the foreign income tax offset limit, so the sum of offsets actually allowed can be well below this figure. The change of label from foreign tax credits to foreign income tax offset means a long series crosses a wording change and should not be assumed continuous.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 23 of the partnership return defines the foreign tax amount reported at label Z, states that it is the partners who claim the offset, and shows the current label wording against which the older 'foreign tax credits' phrasing can be read.
evidence_quote: Show at label Z the amount of any foreign income tax paid by the partnership on foreign source income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'General net foreign source income - foreign tax credits' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the old credit wording to the current offset label or said the partners claim the relief.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net foreign source income, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: What the partnership earned offshore, after the deductions allowed against that income. The ATO instruction for item 23 reads: "Show at label V the net income derived from foreign sources", being the gross foreign income at label B less allowable deductions, and it can be negative. The data item list's word 'general' has no counterpart on the current form, which carries a single net foreign source income label, so treat it as the residual foreign income class from an earlier version of the return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar net amount at item 23 label V, in Australian dollars, with a loss indicator on the paper return where the amount is negative. Attributed foreign income at item 22 and capital gains are excluded.
limitation: It is not a measure of a firm's international operations: interest and borrowing costs against foreign income that do not belong to an overseas permanent establishment are directed to Other deductions instead, so the net figure is struck after only some of the related costs. Capital gains never appear, because a partnership does not own assets for capital gains tax purposes.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 23 defines the net foreign source income label, the deductions that are and are not applied against it, and the exclusions, which is what this column reports.
evidence_quote: The amount at label V is the gross amount shown at label B, minus any deductions allowable to the partnership against that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'General net foreign source income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is net, can be a loss, or excludes capital gains and attributed foreign income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: Non-farm business income the partnership received after its payer withheld tax because no Australian business number had been quoted. The ATO instruction for item 5 reads: "Show at label C and D, as appropriate, gross income received by the partnership that was subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted. This includes amounts of tax withheld." The amount is gross, so it is larger than the cash received, and the withholding itself is claimed at item 6.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount in the non-primary production column of item 5, matched by a Non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule that must be attached to the return.
limitation: A value here is an administrative artefact of a missing ABN, not a category of business activity, so it should not be treated as a distinct revenue stream and it will move between this column and ordinary business income when the ABN situation is fixed. It also cannot be netted for the tax withheld, since that credit is reported separately.
rationale: The DIL label is the non-primary production side of item 5's gross payments where ABN not quoted, and the ATO instruction defines what the amount contains and where the matching credit goes.
evidence_quote: Show at label C and D, as appropriate, gross income received by the partnership that was subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted. This includes amounts of tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is gross of withholding or why a firm has such payments at all.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The farming half of the same item: primary production income received with tax withheld because no Australian business number was quoted. Item 5 of the partnership return splits income and expenses into "primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from primary production" and a non-primary production column, so this column and p_gpabnnpp are the two halves of one label and add to the totals column. Primary production is separated because farm income attracts averaging and farm management deposit treatment at the partner level.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount in the primary production column of item 5, inclusive of the tax withheld, with the credit claimed at item 6 label T.
limitation: Most partnerships have nothing here, and a zero says nothing about whether the firm farms, only that any no-ABN withholding it suffered was not primary production income. Because the split into primary and non-primary production is the lodger's own classification, a mixed farming and processing business can allocate the same receipt either way.
rationale: The DIL label is the primary production side of item 5's gross payments where ABN not quoted, and the ATO instruction defines the three-column structure that gives the PP and NPP suffixes their meaning.
evidence_quote: primary production, showing relevant amounts of income and expenses from primary production
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross Payment ABN not quoted - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the PP suffix or why the return keeps farm income in its own column.

value_domain: Dollar amount of expenses against foreign resident withholding income, partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The costs the partnership incurred in earning the payments that were subject to foreign resident withholding. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label P all expenses directly relating to gaining the income shown at item 5 - label B Gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding. These amounts should not be shown at any other expenses label in item 5." It is a ring-fenced expense line, so the same costs are excluded from the ordinary expense labels on the same row.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense at item 5 label P of the partnership return, reported only where the partnership had gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding.
limitation: Because the instruction excludes these costs from every other expense label, summing the item 5 expense labels without this one understates the firm's total costs for the year. Expenses incurred in earning income that is not assessable in Australia are excluded, so the figure is not the full cost of the activity that generated the withheld payments.
rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label P of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines the expense, ties it to the label B income and states that it must not appear elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Show at label P all expenses directly relating to gaining the income shown at item 5 - label B Gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding. These amounts should not be shown at any other expenses label in item 5.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Foreign resident withholding expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the costs are quarantined out of the other expense labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding, non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: Payments to the partnership that were subject to the foreign resident withholding measure, reported gross of the tax withheld. The ATO instruction reads: "Show at label B gross payments to the partnership that were regulated foreign resident income. Gross payments includes amounts withheld." This is the column where the whole item lives, because foreign resident withholding income is shown "only at label B in the 'Non-primary production' column and the 'Totals' column".
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount at item 5 label B, supported by a Non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule. Regulated foreign resident income is defined by the Taxation Administration Regulations 2017 and its predecessor.
limitation: The column is narrow by design and marks a foreign resident partnership operating in prescribed activities such as sport, entertainment or construction, so it cannot be read as a general measure of foreign-owned or export-facing business. Payments varied to nil under a tax treaty are excluded, so a foreign resident firm covered by a treaty shows nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label is item 5 label B of the partnership return, and the ATO instruction defines regulated foreign resident income, the gross basis and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: Show at label B gross payments to the partnership that were regulated foreign resident income. Gross payments includes amounts withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross payments subject to FRW - NPP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which activities are regulated or that treaty-exempt payments are left out.

value_domain: Dollar amount of gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding, primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2022 instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The primary production column of the foreign resident withholding item, which the ATO says should always be empty. The instruction is direct: "You will not have any primary production amounts at this item", because income subject to foreign resident withholding is shown "only at label B in the 'Non-primary production' column and the 'Totals' column". The column exists to complete the return's three-column grid rather than to carry farm data.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount in the primary production column of item 5 label B. By the return's own design the domain is effectively a single value of zero or blank.
limitation: Any non-zero value is a reporting error rather than a fact about the firm, so this column must not be used to identify foreign resident farming businesses, and its distribution carries no information. Analysts totalling the foreign resident withholding income should use the non-primary production column and ignore this one.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 states both that foreign resident withholding income appears only in the non-primary production and totals columns and that there will be no primary production amounts at the item.
evidence_quote: You will not have any primary production amounts at this item.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Gross payments subject to FRW - PP' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the ATO expects the column to be empty.

value_domain: De-identified predecessor farm business identifier in the Farm Level Analytical Dataset
value_source: ABARES, Agricultural Data Integration Project
variable_description: The identifier a farm business carried before the one in fd_id on the same row, which is what lets a farm be followed across a change of unit. ABARES describes FLAD as combining "farm-level micro-data from all ABS Agricultural surveys and census' undertaken between 2000-01 and 2017-18", so units are re-formed as collections change and this column is the link back to the earlier record. It sits on the FLAD control table beside fd_id, the de-identified ABN and the time series identifier, the four keys that hold a farm's history together.
value_definition: A ten-digit alphanumeric identifier of the same shape as fd_id, opaque by construction and pointing to a farm business unit in an earlier FLAD build or collection.
limitation: It records a link, not a reason for the link, so a change of identifier could be a merger, a split, a change in the ABS unit model or a correction, and this column cannot say which. Where a farm has no predecessor, or where the antecedent could not be established, the field is empty, so a blank cannot be read as evidence that the business is new.
rationale: The ABARES page describes the Farm Level Analytical Dataset, its coverage across successive ABS agricultural collections and its integration into BLADE, which is what makes a previous-unit link necessary and interpretable.
evidence_quote: farm-level micro-data from all ABS Agricultural surveys and census' undertaken between 2000-01 and 2017-18
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'De-identified previous Ag unit' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is an antecedent link to fd_id or why a farm's unit identifier changes.

value_domain: Count of electrical engineering patent applications filed in the financial year (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many patent applications the business filed during the financial year in the electrical engineering group of technologies. IP Australia defines the filed event stream as "rights filed during the financial year" and electrical engineering as a coarse classification area made of "8 classification areas", which include computer technology, digital communication, telecommunications and semiconductors. It counts filings, not inventions or grants, and a filing enters this column in the year it was lodged regardless of what happens to it later.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of patent applications, classified through IP Australia's simplification of the WIPO technology-to-IPC concordance, which assigns a patent to one or more of 35 technology areas.
limitation: A patent can sit in more than one coarse area at once, so this count and its chemistry, instruments, mechanical engineering and other siblings overlap and will sum to more than p_filed_count. Every applicant on a joint filing gets a full unit here, so summing across firms overstates the number of applications; the weighted count exists for that reason.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the count metric, the filed event stream and the electrical engineering coarse classification area, and gives the naming convention that assembles them into this exact column.
evidence_quote: Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated IP Australia's field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the coarse areas overlap or that joint filings are counted in full for each applicant.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted count of electrical engineering patent filings (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's share of the electrical engineering patent applications filed in the year, splitting each joint application between its applicants. IP Australia explains that "when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score", so the weighted counts add correctly across firms while the unweighted counts do not. A firm that never collaborates has identical values in this column and p_elec_eng_filed_count.
value_definition: A non-negative fractional count in units of applications, formed from 1/n shares. Values are rarely whole numbers for firms that co-file, and the sum across all applicants reproduces the true number of filings.
limitation: An equal split is an assumption, not an observation: a firm contributing most of the invention gets the same half as a nominal co-applicant on a two-party filing. Comparing this column with the unweighted count as though the gap measured collaboration also conflates the number of partners with the number of collaborative filings.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count metric and its 1/n construction, and the naming convention places it in the filed event stream within the electrical engineering coarse area.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the field wording about an application fraction with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the fraction is or why the weighted series exists.

value_domain: Most frequent electrical engineering technology area among filings (IPLoRD class code)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Which of the eight electrical engineering technology areas the business filed in most often during the year. IP Australia says modal variables "record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year" and are "useful for getting a high-level understanding of an applicant's IP filing's economic area". The eight areas run from electrical machinery and audio-visual technology through telecommunications, digital communication, computer technology, IT methods for management and semiconductors.
value_definition: A character code for one technology area drawn from IP Australia's simplification of the WIPO technology-to-IPC concordance; the BLADE data item list carries the code labels in its appendix. Blank where the firm filed no electrical engineering patents that year.
limitation: A mode discards the distribution behind it, so a firm with nine filings in computer technology and one in semiconductors is indistinguishable from a firm with one filing in computer technology alone. It also cannot be compared across firms as a measure of specialisation, because the class scope column, not this one, says how spread the activity was.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the modal class metric and lists the eight electrical engineering classification areas that this column selects among.
evidence_quote: Modal value variables record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording and pointed at an appendix, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a mode conceals or how many areas it selects among.

value_domain: Count of distinct electrical engineering technology areas filed in (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many different electrical engineering technology areas the business filed patents in during the year, a breadth measure rather than a volume one. IP Australia describes scope variables as indicating "the breadth of an applicant's activity" and defines them as "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year". Because electrical engineering holds eight areas, this column runs from zero to eight and cannot exceed the filing count.
value_definition: A non-negative integer, bounded above by the eight electrical engineering classification areas in IP Australia's simplified patent classification. Its all-patent counterpart, p_filed_class_scope, is bounded by 35.
limitation: Breadth is not diversification of business activity: a single patent classified into four areas produces a scope of four while a firm with forty patents in one area produces one. Because a patent may carry several classifications, scope can rise without the firm filing in any genuinely new field.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the class scope metric, states the number of electrical engineering classification areas, and notes that patents commonly carry multiple classifications.
evidence_quote: Scope variables are intended to indicate the breadth of an applicant's activity across multiple event streams in a given financial year and are used as a term to describe the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing gave the upper bound of eight or warned that multi-classified patents inflate scope.

value_domain: Count of electrical engineering patents granted in the financial year (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many of the business's electrical engineering patent applications were granted during the financial year. IP Australia defines the granted event stream simply as "rights granted during the financial year", so the year on the row is the year of IP Australia's decision, not the year the application was lodged. Grants are the flow that adds to the enforceable stockpile measured at p_elec_eng_le_count.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of granted applications in the electrical engineering coarse area, which is one of five coarse areas defined over the 35 technology areas of the simplified patent classification.
limitation: Australian patent examination takes years, so a grant counted here answers to a filing decision made well before the row's financial year, and pairing grants with the same year's research spending misdates the relationship. Grant counts are also censored at the end of the dataset: applications still pending when IPLoRD was built appear as filings that were never granted.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the granted event stream and the count metric, and explains how grants feed the enforceable stockpile.
evidence_quote: Granted - rights granted during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the year is the decision year or that late filings are censored.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted count of electrical engineering patents granted (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's fractional share of the electrical engineering patents granted in the year, with each jointly held grant split between its applicants. IP Australia says the weighted metric exists so that "accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type", which is what makes this the right column for adding grants across firms. Its unweighted twin, p_elec_eng_granted_count, gives every co-applicant a whole grant.
value_definition: A non-negative fractional count of grants formed from 1/n applicant shares, in the electrical engineering coarse area of the simplified patent classification.
limitation: The split is by number of applicants recorded on the right, so a firm that funded the work and a university named alongside it receive the same half share, and the column cannot be read as economic ownership. It also says nothing about the value or breadth of the rights granted, only about how many were shared.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count and its purpose of preserving aggregate totals, and the naming convention places it in the granted stream within electrical engineering.
evidence_quote: The inclusion of weighted count variables allows for accurate numbers of applications to be preserved in aggregate for each IP right type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the field wording about an application fraction with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why the weighted grant series exists or what its shares mean.

value_domain: Most frequent electrical engineering technology area among grants (IPLoRD class code)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Which electrical engineering technology area accounted for most of the business's patent grants in the year. It differs from the filing mode on the same row because grants arrive years after filings, so a firm's granted mode describes what it was working on some time ago while its filed mode describes what it is working on now. IP Australia's technology areas come from its extension of the WIPO concordance: "Table 2 of that document describes how to use IPC marks to assign a patent to one or more of 35 possible technology areas."
value_definition: A character code for one of the eight electrical engineering technology areas, selected as the most frequent among the year's granted applications. Blank where nothing was granted in the area that year.
limitation: A mode over a small number of grants is unstable: most firms have one or two grants in a year, so the value can swing between areas without any change in what the firm does. The code also describes the technology of the right, not the industry of the firm, so it should not be substituted for an ANZSIC class.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal class variables, the granted event stream, and the WIPO-derived 35-area classification the codes come from.
evidence_quote: Table 2 of that document describes how to use IPC marks to assign a patent to one or more of 35 possible technology areas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the granted mode from the filed mode or warned how thin the underlying counts are.

value_domain: Count of distinct electrical engineering technology areas granted in (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: In how many different electrical engineering technology areas the business had patents granted during the year.
