IP Australia uses this exact column as its worked example of the naming convention: "if we are interested to know how many of the eight possible electrical engineering classification areas a firm has had patents granted in a given financial year, we would look for p_electrical_engineering_granted_class_scope". The BLADE column is that variable with the coarse area abbreviated.
value_definition: An integer from zero to eight, counting distinct electrical engineering classification areas among the year's grants rather than the grants themselves.
limitation: Granting scope is capped by what was filed several years earlier, so a firm that recently broadened its research shows a narrow granted scope for years afterwards; the filed scope on the same row moves first. A value of zero is also produced both by a firm with no grants and by a firm whose grants all fell outside electrical engineering.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary names this variable directly when explaining scope variables and the coarse classification naming convention.
evidence_quote: For example, if we are interested to know how many of the eight possible electrical engineering classification areas a firm has had patents granted in a given financial year, we would look for p_electrical_engineering_granted_class_scope.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing gave the bound of eight or explained the lag behind the filed scope.

value_domain: Stock of legally enforceable electrical engineering patents at year end (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many electrical engineering patents the business could actually enforce at the end of the financial year, a stock rather than a flow. IP Australia defines the stream as the "Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year" and gives its arithmetic: "Each year's enforceable stockpile will be the previous year's enforceable stockpile plus rights granted in that financial year and rights retired in that financial year. Filings do not affect the stockpile." This is the column to use for a firm's patent holdings; the filed and granted counts are events, not holdings.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of enforceable rights held at 30 June, in the electrical engineering coarse area. IP Australia carries the term 'gained enforceable status' over from IPGOD, which is what the 'le' in the BLADE column name abbreviates.
limitation: A stock of enforceable rights is not a stock of useful ones: a patent kept alive by renewal fees counts the same as one generating revenue, and nothing here says whether it is worked, licensed or defensive. Because retirement is driven by fee decisions, the stockpile falls when a firm stops paying rather than when the technology stops mattering.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the enforceable stockpile, its year-to-year arithmetic, and the IPGOD terminology behind 'gained enforceable status'.
evidence_quote: Each year's enforceable stockpile will be the previous year's enforceable stockpile plus rights granted in that financial year and rights retired in that financial year. Filings do not affect the stockpile.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the field wording about legally enforceable patents with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is a stock, how it evolves, or that filings never move it.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted stock of legally enforceable electrical engineering patents (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's fractional share of the electrical engineering patents it could enforce at year end, splitting co-owned rights between their holders. It applies the 1/n weighting to a stock rather than to a flow, so it is the right column for asking what proportion of Australia's enforceable electrical engineering patents a firm holds. IP Australia's enforceable stream is the "Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year".
value_definition: A non-negative fractional count of enforceable rights, formed from 1/n shares across the applicants recorded on each right, in the electrical engineering coarse area.
limitation: The weighting follows the applicants recorded at filing, so later assignments, licences and corporate restructures are not reflected and a right may be shared with a party that no longer exists. Comparing this fractional stock against the unweighted stock as a co-ownership rate also breaks down for firms whose rights are individually large.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines both the weighted count metric and the enforceable stockpile stream that this column combines.
evidence_quote: Enforceable - Stockpile of granted, non-retired rights at the end of each financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the field wording about owned and enforceable application fractions with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the fraction is an applicant share of a year-end stock.

value_domain: Most frequent electrical engineering technology area in the enforceable stock (IPLoRD class code)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The electrical engineering technology area that dominates the business's enforceable patent holdings at the end of the year. Because it is taken over a stock rather than a year's events, it moves slowly and is the most stable of the four modal columns on the row. IP Australia intends modal variables for "getting a high-level understanding of an applicant's IP filing's economic area and the main focuses of the company's activity".
value_definition: A character code for one of the eight electrical engineering technology areas, chosen as the most common among rights that were granted and not retired at 30 June.
limitation: The stock mode reflects accumulated history, so a firm that changed direction years ago still reports its old area until the earlier patents are retired, and reading it as current focus is wrong. Comparing it with the filed mode on the same row shows a change in direction only once the older rights lapse.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the modal metric, states its intended use, and defines the enforceable stockpile that this mode is taken over.
evidence_quote: They are useful for getting a high-level understanding of an applicant's IP filing's economic area and the main focuses of the company's activity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a mode over a stock is backward looking.

value_domain: Count of distinct electrical engineering technology areas in the enforceable stock (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Across how many electrical engineering technology areas the business's enforceable patent holdings are spread. The custodian's wording for this column describes areas the rights holder "has applications in", which in IPLoRD's scheme means areas represented in the enforceable stockpile at year end rather than areas filed in that year. It is the breadth partner to p_elec_eng_le_count, which gives the depth.
value_definition: An integer from zero to eight, counting distinct electrical engineering classification areas represented among rights that were granted and not retired at the end of the financial year.
limitation: Scope over a stock saturates: a long-lived firm accumulates coverage of most areas and sits at or near eight for years, so the column stops discriminating between firms once they are large. It also cannot show concentration, because one patent in an area counts the same as fifty.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables as counting classification areas of activity and defines the enforceable stream as a year-end stockpile, which together fix what this column counts.
evidence_quote: Scope variables are intended to indicate the breadth of an applicant's activity across multiple event streams in a given financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording about areas the rights holder has applications in, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the count is taken over the enforceable stock or that it saturates.

value_domain: Count of electrical engineering patents retired in the financial year (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: How many electrical engineering patent applications or rights the business let go during the financial year. IP Australia defines the stream as "Retired - rights retired during the financial year", and retirements are the outflow that reduces the enforceable stockpile at p_elec_eng_le_count. It is the closest signal in the intellectual property data to a firm withdrawing from a technology.
value_definition: A non-negative integer count of retirement events in the electrical engineering coarse area during the financial year.
limitation: Retirement gathers several very different endings into one number: a patent that reached the end of its twenty-year term, one abandoned by not paying a renewal fee, and an application withdrawn or refused all count the same. A rise here is therefore not evidence of retreat, since an ageing portfolio retires rights on schedule.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the retired event stream and the count metric and places retirements in the stockpile arithmetic.
evidence_quote: Retired - rights retired during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that expiry, lapse and withdrawal are pooled into a single count.

value_domain: Applicant-weighted count of electrical engineering patents retired (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: The business's fractional share of the electrical engineering rights retired in the year, splitting jointly held retirements between their applicants. Using the weighted rather than the unweighted retirement count matters when netting flows against the stockpile, because both must be measured on the same basis. IP Australia's weighting rule is the same throughout IPLoRD: an application filed by n applicants counts 1/n towards each.
value_definition: A non-negative fractional count of retirement events, formed from 1/n applicant shares, in the electrical engineering coarse area.
limitation: A retirement decision on a co-owned right is usually made by one party, so attributing an equal share of it to every applicant misstates who withdrew. The fraction also cannot distinguish a deliberate abandonment from a right that simply reached the end of its term, which is the same weakness as the unweighted count.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the weighted count metric and the retired event stream, and the naming convention combines them with the electrical engineering coarse area to give this column.
evidence_quote: when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording about application fractions allowed to retire, with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the weighting follows applicants rather than the party that decided to let the right go.

value_domain: Most frequent electrical engineering technology area among retirements (IPLoRD class code)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Which electrical engineering technology area the business retired most rights in during the year. IP Australia gives the parallel construction for another right type: "the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class", and this column is the patent equivalent within the electrical engineering group. Compared with the filed mode on the same row, it shows what a firm is leaving behind against what it is moving into.
value_definition: A character code for one of the eight electrical engineering technology areas, the most common among the year's retirements. Blank in a year with no electrical engineering retirements.
limitation: Most firms retire very few rights in a year, so the mode is frequently decided by a single event and should not be read as a strategic exit. Because retirements follow the age profile of the portfolio, the area shown is often simply whatever the firm was patenting twenty years earlier.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal class variables and names the retired-stream modal variable for trade marks as its worked example of the naming pattern this column follows.
evidence_quote: Similarly, the modal classification (activity_metric) of trade marks retired (event stream) is recorded as the variable tm_retired_modal_class.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the field wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the mode usually rests on one or two events.

value_domain: Count of distinct electrical engineering technology areas retired from (IPLoRD)
value_source: IP Australia, IPLoRD Data Dictionary 2021
variable_description: Across how many electrical engineering technology areas the business let rights lapse in the year. It is the breadth of withdrawal, so a value near eight with a low retired count marks a firm shedding one right in each of many areas, while a value of one with a high count marks a firm exiting a single technology. IP Australia defines scope as "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year".
value_definition: An integer from zero to eight, counting distinct electrical engineering classification areas represented among the year's retirements.
limitation: Retiring a right in an area does not mean leaving it, because the firm may hold others in the same area that remain enforceable; only the enforceable scope on the same row can say whether coverage was actually lost. Zero is also the usual value, since most firms retire nothing in a given year.

value_domain: ATO trust type code, partnership return item 8 non-primary production
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Which kind of trust the partnership's non-primary-production trust distribution mainly came from. The ATO instructs that at the label for the share of net income from trusts "print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made", and "If this amount is from more than one type of trust, print the code that represents the trust with the greatest amount of distribution." It qualifies the dollar amount reported for the non-primary-production share of trust income on the same row, and it is only printed when that amount is not a loss.
value_definition: A single ATO trust code carried in BLADE as a numeric mapping: 5 D deceased estate, 10 F fixed trust, 15 H hybrid, 20 I discretionary trust with investment income, 25 M cash management unit trust, 30 P listed public unit trust, 35 Q unlisted public unit trust, 40 S discretionary trust with service or management income, 45 T discretionary trust with trading income, 50 U fixed unit trust, 55 C special disability trust and 60 E testamentary trust, with everything else invalid or no response.
limitation: One code stands for a whole year of distributions, so a partnership that received income from a discretionary trust and a public unit trust shows only the larger of the two and the mix is lost. No code is printed at all when the amount is a loss, so a blank is not evidence that no trust distribution was received.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-primary-production distribution from trusts action code, which is the trust code box beside label R of item 8 on the ATO partnership tax return. The ATO instructions publish both the rule for choosing the code and the code table itself.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at the right of label R print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the code describes the source trust, that only the largest source is recorded, or that a loss suppresses it.

It is the primary-production twin of the non-primary-production trust code on the same return, sitting beside the partnership's share of primary production income included in a trust's net income. The ATO directs the lodger to "print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made", so this column tells a reader whether farm and forestry income reached the partnership through a deceased estate, a discretionary trust or a unit trust.
value_definition: The same ATO trust code list as the non-primary-production column, carried in BLADE as a numeric mapping from 5 through 60 onto the letters D, F, H, I, M, P, Q, S, T, U, C and E, with everything else invalid or no response. Primary production here has the ATO's meaning for the return, not an ANZSIC industry test.
limitation: It classifies the trust, not the farming activity, so it cannot be used to identify agricultural businesses; a discretionary trust code says nothing about what the trust does. It is also only present where a primary production trust distribution was reported and was not a loss, which makes it a small and selected subset of partnerships.
rationale: The DIL label names the primary production distribution from trusts action code, the trust code box at label Z of item 8 on the partnership return, for which the ATO publishes the selection rule and the code table.
evidence_quote: If this amount is not a loss, in the box at label Z print the code from Table: Trust codes that best describes the type of trust from which the distribution is made.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish the primary production code from its non-primary-production twin.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, gross interest
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Interest the partnership received or was credited during the year, before any expense is set against it. The ATO defines the label as "the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities, and interest paid by us". It is a whole-year flow and it is gross, so the firm's interest expense sits separately at the total interest expenses label.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, not negative, self-assessed by the lodger. It includes amounts accrued rather than paid on discounted and deferred interest securities.
limitation: It is not the partnership's whole interest income. Interest received through a cash management trust or other trust investment product is reported with trust distributions at item 8 instead, and interest from an account held jointly outside a business partnership belongs on the partners' own returns, so a low figure can mean interest was reported elsewhere.
rationale: The DIL label matches the gross interest item of the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction for that label lists exactly what belongs in it and what is reported elsewhere.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the interest from banks and credit unions, building societies, debentures, notes and deposits, income accrued on discounted or deferred interest securities, government securities, and interest paid by us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Gross interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the figure is gross, whole-year and self-assessed, nor which interest is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, gross rent
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Rental income the partnership earned from property held in the business, before any rental deduction. The ATO says "Show at label F the gross amount of rental income. This item can't be a loss." and counts booking and letting fees, retained bond money, insurance payouts for lost rent and tenant reimbursements of deductible expenses as part of it. Interest deductions, capital works deductions and other rental deductions on neighbouring labels are what turn it into net rent.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, never negative, excluding GST where the partnership is registered and GST is payable on the rent.
limitation: It only exists where the rent is business income of the partnership. Where the property is merely a joint investment the partners report their shares on their own returns, so a zero here does not mean the partners hold no property. Rent from foreign sources is reported with other assessable foreign source income instead.
rationale: The DIL label matches the gross rent label of item 9 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction for that label defines its content, its sign and its exclusions.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the gross amount of rental income. This item can't be a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the label 'Gross rent' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both slots, so it did not say the amount is gross, cannot be negative, or only appears for partnership business rent.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, personal services business determination
value_source: ATO, Personal services income: Self-assessing as a PSB
variable_description: Whether the partnership holds a Commissioner's determination that it is conducting a personal services business for at least one individual whose income it receives. A determination is granted by the ATO on application, and the ATO says "If you are unable to self-assess as a PSB for a particular income year, you may be able to apply for a PSB determination (PSBD) in some circumstances." That makes this column administratively different from the four self-assessment tests reported beside it, which the partnership asserts for itself.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and everything else an invalid or absent response. It sits beside the four self-assessment indicators on the same return, for the results test, the unrelated clients test, the employment test and the business premises test.
limitation: A yes does not say how many individuals are covered or that all the partnership's personal services income is protected: the ATO applies the tests to each individual separately, so one determination can cover one worker and not another. It also does not date the determination, so a yes cannot be read as coverage for the whole income year.
rationale: The DIL label is the personal services business determination question on the partnership return, and the ATO's PSI guidance defines what a determination is and how it relates to self-assessment against the four tests.
evidence_quote: If you are unable to self-assess as a PSB for a particular income year, you may be able to apply for a PSB determination (PSBD) in some circumstances.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the question with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish a determination granted by the ATO from the self-assessed tests recorded on the same return.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, personal services income present
value_source: ATO, Personal services income: Income that is PSI
variable_description: Whether any of the partnership's income is really the reward for one individual's personal effort. The ATO defines it as income "that is mainly a reward for your personal effort or skill", and where an individual earns it through a company, partnership or trust that entity is a personal services entity. This is the gate question on the return: a yes opens the personal services income labels and the four personal services business tests, and a no closes them.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and everything else an invalid or absent response. It gates the personal services income amount labels on the return, which stay blank unless the answer is yes.
limitation: A yes does not mean the personal services income rules bit. A partnership that answers yes can still be conducting a personal services business, in which case the attribution and deduction rules do not apply. The answer is also a self-assessment of the more-than-half test, so it records the lodger's judgement rather than an audited fact.
rationale: The DIL label is the personal services income gate question on the partnership return, and the ATO's own PSI page gives the definition of personal services income that the question turns on.
evidence_quote: Personal services income (PSI) is income that is received by you, or another entity connected with you, that is mainly a reward for your personal effort or skill
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never explained what personal services income is or that a yes does not imply the rules apply.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, total net income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Foreign income items 22 to 24
variable_description: The partnership's whole-of-year net income or loss for tax purposes, Australian and foreign together, before it is divided among the partners. It is the total box at the foot of the income side of the return: the ATO says "Show at item 24 the total of the amounts shown at items 20 to 23", which adds net Australian income or loss to attributed foreign income and other assessable foreign source income. The statement of distribution then splits this figure between the partners.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss. The item number moves between form years; it is item 24 on the 2024 partnership return.
limitation: It is not a tax base and not a profit. A partnership pays no income tax, so this amount is only a step towards each partner's assessment, and it excludes capital gains entirely because a partnership does not own assets for capital gains tax purposes. Prior-year Australian and foreign losses are also excluded, so it is not the amount that a partner can ultimately be taxed on.
rationale: The DIL label matches the total net income or loss box of the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction states exactly which items it totals.
evidence_quote: Show at item 24 the total of the amounts shown at items 20 to 23.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which components are summed, that capital gains are outside it, or that a partnership is not itself taxed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, income reconciliation adjustment
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss item 5
variable_description: The net amount by which the partnership's accounting income had to be changed to reach income for tax purposes. The ATO says "Show at label A the net income-related reconciliation adjustments", the net of add-backs for assessable amounts missing from the accounts and subtractions for accounting income that is not assessable, such as exempt income and the profit on the sale of a depreciating asset. It measures the gap between the books and the tax law, not any transaction the business made.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be negative, since the subtractions can exceed the add-backs. The expense-side equivalent is reported at the expense reconciliation adjustments label.
limitation: A net figure conceals its parts, so a large add-back offset by a large subtraction is reported as a small number and the two adjustments cannot be recovered. On the paper form a negative result is shown by printing L in a separate box rather than a minus sign, so whether the stored amount carries its sign has to be checked in the data before the column is used.
rationale: The DIL label matches the income reconciliation adjustments label of item 5 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction defines the label as a net amount and lists what makes it up.
evidence_quote: Show at label A the net income-related reconciliation adjustments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both slots, so it did not say the amount is a net of add-backs and subtractions or that it can be negative.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, cost of intangible depreciating assets first deducted
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The cost of intangible assets the partnership started depreciating this year, which is the closest thing on the return to a measure of new intangible investment. The ATO says "Show at label A the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time", and counts intellectual property such as patents, registered designs and copyright, acquired or developed in-house software, mining and prospecting rights, spectrum licences and certain telecommunications cable rights. The tangible equivalent is reported at the other depreciating assets label.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, being cost rather than the deduction claimed, and not reduced for expected non-taxable use. Intangibles costing under $1,000 that were put into a low-value pool are included at cost.
limitation: It is cost at first deduction, so it is neither the deduction claimed nor the stock of intangibles the business holds, and an asset appears once and never again. Expenditure on in-house software allocated to a software development pool is excluded, and an internally generated intangible that is not a depreciating asset never appears at all, so this understates intangible investment.
rationale: The DIL label matches the intangible depreciating assets first deducted label of the capital allowances item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO defines both the amount and the kinds of asset it covers.
evidence_quote: Show at label A the cost of all intangible depreciating assets for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is cost rather than deduction, nor which intangibles are inside and outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, interest paid to non-residents
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
variable_description: How much of the partnership's interest bill went to lenders outside Australia. The ATO says "Show at label D the amount of interest paid to non-residents", and reporting an amount here obliges the partnership to lodge an International dealings schedule. It is a subset of the total interest expenses label, not an addition to it, so the two must not be summed.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported at the overseas transactions item and also included in total interest expenses at item 5.
limitation: It identifies neither the lender nor the country, so it cannot support any analysis of where a firm borrows. A nil is also weak evidence of no foreign borrowing: the deduction is denied until any withholding tax is remitted, so unremitted interest drops out of the column while the debt remains.
rationale: The DIL label matches the interest expenses overseas label of the overseas transactions item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO defines the amount and its relationship to the item 5 total.
evidence_quote: Show at label D the amount of interest paid to non-residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the amount is a subset of total interest or that it triggers an International dealings schedule.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, total interest expenses
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What the partnership's borrowing cost it over the year, from Australian and overseas lenders together. The ATO defines the label as "the interest incurred on money borrowed within Australia and overseas that relates to producing Australian income and that is to acquire income-producing assets, to finance business operations or to meet current business expenses". It is the business's gearing cost as reported in the profit and loss statement, and the overseas share of it is reported separately at the overseas transactions item.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, incurred rather than paid, and reported as an expense within item 5 of the return.
limitation: It is not the firm's whole interest bill, because interest claimed against rental income is deliberately reported at the rent item instead; the two have to be added. It is also an accounting figure rather than an allowed deduction, since interest denied by the thin capitalisation rules is added back through the expense reconciliation adjustment rather than removed here.
rationale: The DIL label matches the total interest expenses label of item 5 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction defines its content and the rental interest carve-out.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the interest incurred on money borrowed within Australia and overseas that relates to producing Australian income and that is to acquire income-producing assets, to finance business operations or to meet current business expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that rental interest sits elsewhere or that denied interest stays in the figure.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, international related party dealings above the $2 million threshold
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
variable_description: Whether the partnership's dealings with international related parties passed the ATO's $2 million reporting threshold for the year. The question the label answers is "Was the aggregate amount of your transactions or dealings with international related parties (including the value of any property or service transferred, or the balance of any loans) greater than $2 million?", and a yes obliges the partnership to lodge an International dealings schedule. Dealings are aggregated gross, so a $600,000 purchase and a $700,000 sale count as $1.3 million rather than $100,000.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and everything else an invalid or absent response. The threshold behind it is an aggregate of $2 million across all international related party dealings, outstanding loan balances included.
limitation: It is a threshold flag, so a partnership with $1.9 million of related-party dealings is indistinguishable from one with none, and the column can never give a magnitude. It also names no country and no counterparty, and it captures loan balances alongside transactions, so a yes can be driven by a single standing intragroup loan rather than by trade.
rationale: The DIL label matches the overseas transactions question on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction states the threshold, the aggregation rule and the schedule the answer triggers.
evidence_quote: Was the aggregate amount of your transactions or dealings with international related parties (including the value of any property or service transferred, or the balance of any loans) greater than $2 million?
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Overseas transactions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not give the $2 million threshold or the gross aggregation rule that make the flag interpretable.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, interest deductions against rental income
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Interest the partnership deducted against its rental income, which is the financing cost of the property side of the business. The ATO says "Show at label G the total deductible amount of interest expense incurred in earning the rental income", and this amount is deliberately kept out of the total interest expenses label at item 5. With gross rent above it and capital works and other rental deductions beside it, it is one of the three subtractions that produce net rent.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, reported at the rent item and excluded from the item 5 total interest expenses label.
limitation: Reading either interest column alone understates how geared the business is, because the return splits interest between the rent item and item 5 and neither is a total. The figure is also net of any thin capitalisation denial, so it is what was claimed rather than what was incurred.
rationale: The DIL label matches the interest deductions label of item 9 on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO defines the amount and states that item 5 interest excludes it.
evidence_quote: Show at label G the total deductible amount of interest expense incurred in earning the rental income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say this is rental interest only and is excluded from the total interest expenses column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, lease expenses
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What the partnership spent leasing equipment and vehicles during the year. The ATO defines the label as "the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, such as motor vehicles, plant or other equipment", which makes it a measure of capital used but not owned. Property leasing is excluded and reported at the rent expenses label instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering both finance and operating leases on non-real-estate assets, reported as an expense within item 5.
limitation: It is not the cost of accessing capital goods generally, because hire-purchase and instalment-sale payments are excluded and treated under the depreciating asset rules. It is also not a deduction: capital expenditure to end a lease is reported here and then added back through the expense reconciliation adjustment, as are lease amounts denied by the thin capitalisation rules.
rationale: The DIL label matches the lease expenses label of item 5 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction defines what belongs in it and what is written back.
evidence_quote: Show at label G the expenditure incurred through both finance and operating leases on leasing assets, such as motor vehicles, plant or other equipment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed 'Lease expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate leases from rent and hire purchase or flag the reconciliation write-back.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, motor vehicle expenses
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: What it cost the partnership to run its vehicles over the year. The ATO says "Show at label L motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums." A code beside the amount records how a car claim was worked out, S for cents per kilometre and B for logbook, or N where the claim is for a motorcycle, a taxi, a one-tonne or nine-passenger vehicle, or where no partner is an individual.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year covering running costs only, reported as an expense within item 5 and accompanied by a claim-method code.
limitation: It is not the cost of the fleet. Leasing, interest and depreciation on the same vehicles are reported at three other labels, so a firm that leases its vehicles looks cheap here. Where the cents-per-kilometre method is used the figure is a statutory formula rather than money actually spent, and the method varies between businesses and between vehicles within a business.
rationale: The DIL label matches the motor vehicle expenses label of item 5 on the ATO partnership tax return, and the ATO instruction restricts it to running expenses and publishes the claim-method codes.
evidence_quote: Show at label L motor vehicle running expenses only. These expenses include fuel, repairs, registration fees and insurance premiums.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the amount excludes lease, interest and depreciation or that a cents-per-kilometre claim is a formula.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, income tests net rental property income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's whole-of-year net result from rental property, reported so that each partner can complete the income tests on their own return. The ATO says "Show at item 53 - label H the amount of the partnership's net income or loss from rental properties" and requires Australian rent, foreign rent and net rental income distributed from other partnerships all to be counted. It exists for eligibility testing, feeding study and training loan repayment income, super co-contributions and the Medicare levy surcharge.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss, reported at the income tests item and split between partners in the statement of distribution.
limitation: It is not the net rent reported at the rent item and the two will not agree, because this figure adds foreign rent and rental income received through other partnerships. It is also not a return on property: capital gains and capital losses on rental property are excluded, so a business that made its money on disposal shows nothing here.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net rental property income or loss label of the income tests item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO defines its scope and its purpose.
evidence_quote: Capital gains or losses made in regard to a rental property are not included in the partnership’s net rental property income or loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say this is an income-tests figure with a wider scope than the rent item's net rent.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership return, income tests net financial investment income or loss
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's net result from financial investments over the year, reported for the partners' income tests rather than for the partnership's own assessment. The ATO instructs that "If the partnership received income or claimed deductions during 2023-24, then work out the net income or loss from financial investments and show it at label G", counting shares, interests in managed investment schemes including forestry schemes, rights and options over them, and investment income distributed from other partnerships. Each partner's share is then carried into the statement of distribution.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year that can be a loss, reported at the income tests item alongside the net rental property income or loss figure.
limitation: It is not the partnership's investment return. Interest from everyday transaction accounts is excluded by rule, and so are capital gains and capital losses, which is where most of the return on shares actually lands. Its purpose is to stop a partner reducing income-tested entitlements through an investment loss, so a zero says the tests found nothing to report, not that the firm holds no investments.
rationale: The DIL label matches the net financial investment income or loss label of the income tests item on the ATO partnership tax return, where the ATO lists what is a financial investment and what is left out.
evidence_quote: Don't include any of the following when calculating the partnership's net financial investment income or loss: interest from everyday transactions accounts, capital gains, capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not name the excluded items that make the figure unusable as a measure of investment return.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule, cost base adjustment from loss transfers
value_source: ATO Legal Database, Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 section 170-225
variable_description: The total cost base adjustment the entity made to its interests in another company in the same wholly owned group after a loss was transferred within that group. The adjustment reaches shares held in, and debts owed by, the other company. Subdivision 170-C of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 is headed "Provisions applying to both transfers of tax losses and transfers of net capital losses within wholly-owned groups of companies", and section 170-225 deals with the increase side, "Transfer of net capital loss: direct and indirect interests in the gain company". The DIL prefix OF marks this as the old form's wording: the label was dropped when the schedule changed, so a series across the change is not continuous.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, a total across all affected interests rather than an amount per share or per debt, reported only on the old capital gains tax schedule.
limitation: It changes nothing about this year's tax. A cost base adjustment only alters the gain or loss on a future disposal, so a large number here has no counterpart in the year's taxable income. The column also names neither the group company involved nor the transfer that caused it, and because only the old schedule carried the label, a blank after the form change means the question was not asked.
rationale: The DIL label names Division 170-C cost base adjustments arising from loss transfers, and the ATO legal database publishes the Subdivision and the two sections that create the reduction and the increase. Which of the two directions the schedule's adjustment label carries is inferred from its pairing with the reduction label rather than from published schedule instructions.
evidence_quote: Transfer of net capital loss: direct and indirect interests in the gain company
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw schedule label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not explain what a Subdivision 170-C adjustment does, or that the OF prefix marks a label the new schedule dropped.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the capital gains tax schedule, cost base reduction from loss transfers
value_source: ATO Legal Database, Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 section 170-220
variable_description: The total reduction the entity made to the cost base and reduced cost base of shares in, or debts owed by, the group company that gave up a loss. Section 170-220, "Transfer of net capital loss: direct and indirect interests in the loss company", is the mechanism: a company that hands a loss to a group member is worth less afterwards, so interests in it are written down. This is the reduction side of the pair, the increase side being the adjustment label beside it, and the DIL prefix OF marks it as an old-form label.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, aggregated over every affected share and debt, reported only on the old capital gains tax schedule.
limitation: The reduction is not applied when it is reported. The Act requires it to be made immediately before a later capital gains tax event, so the year the amount appears in the schedule is not the year it affects a gain. The column also cannot separate reductions arising from transferred tax losses from those arising from transferred net capital losses, since one label covers both.
rationale: The DIL label names the Division 170-C cost base reduction resulting from loss transfers, and section 170-220 in the ATO legal database defines the reduction to interests in the loss company and states when it is made. The mapping of the schedule's reduction label to the loss-company side is inferred from the pairing with the adjustment label.
evidence_quote: Transfer of net capital loss: direct and indirect interests in the loss company
supersedes_rationale: The entry printed the schedule label alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what is written down, when the write-down applies, or that the label belongs to the superseded form.

value_domain: Boolean flag, party currently in the role at extract
value_source: IP Australia, Open IP data
variable_description: Whether the party named on this row was still filling its role on the IP right when the extract was cut, not at the end of the reference period on the row. IP Australia says "IP Refreshed Automated Product for Information and Data (IP RAPID) provides access to over 100 years of information on IP rights applications" and that "IP RAPID is updated weekly", so the flag is anchored to a moving extract date. The role itself is in the party role column, and the dates the role began and ended are in the effective-from and effective-to columns.
value_definition: A numeric boolean: 0 for no and 1 for yes. The companion flag on the same table records whether the party was the earliest one on record in that role.
limitation: It is not a longitudinal variable and must not be read as ownership at the date of the row. A patent sold in 2015 will show its current owner as current on every historical row, so questions about who held a right in a given year have to be answered from the effective-from and effective-to dates instead. Because the product refreshes weekly, the moment the flag refers to also differs between BLADE vintages.
rationale: The variable sits on the IPRAPID party table, and IP Australia's Open IP data page describes what IP RAPID is and how often it is refreshed, which is what fixes the meaning of an extract-time flag.
evidence_quote: IP RAPID is updated weekly.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about a Boolean flag with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never warned that the flag refers to extract time rather than to the row's own period.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The partnership's overall business profit or loss for the year, primary production and non-primary production combined. The ATO defines it as "total business income minus total expenses incurred in producing that income, adjusted by any reconciliation items", and it is reported at item 5 label S of the partnership return. It sits at the end of the trading account, after the accounting figures at labels C to N have been converted to tax figures by the income and expense reconciliation adjustments.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount and a flow over the income year. It can be negative; on the paper form a loss is marked with an L indicator beside the amount rather than a minus sign, so the sign may need reconstructing from a companion loss flag.
limitation: It is not the partnership's taxable income and not what the partners are taxed on. Distributions received from other partnerships and trusts, rent, interest, dividends and foreign income are all reported at separate items and sit outside this figure, so a firm with a small trading business and large investment income looks small here.
rationale: The BIT table carries c_, i_, p_ and t_ variants of the same tax labels for the company, individual, partnership and trust returns; the p_ prefix identifies the partnership return, where net income or loss from business is item 5 label S and the ATO instruction defines it directly.
evidence_quote: The net income or loss from business is total business income minus total expenses incurred in producing that income, adjusted by any reconciliation items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Net income or loss from business' as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is the post-reconciliation total or that investment income sits outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The non-primary-production half of the partnership's business result, kept apart from its farming, fishing and forestry income. The ATO directs the lodger to "Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production, R for non-primary production", so this column is label R. Read with p_netincpp it decomposes the total at label S, and the split exists because primary production income attracts averaging and farm management deposit treatment in the partners' own returns.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow over the income year, signed, with losses flagged rather than signed on the form. It is one of two columns of the item 5 trading account, not a standalone total.
limitation: The split is made on the activity, not on the entity, so it cannot be read as an industry classification of the firm. A mixed farm with a farm-gate shop divides its own income and expenses between the two columns on its own allocation, and nothing in the data records how that allocation was made.
rationale: The p_ prefix in the BIT table marks the partnership return, where the ATO instruction names labels Q and R as the primary and non-primary production halves of net income or loss from business.
evidence_quote: Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Net income or loss from business - NPP' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never explained what NPP means or why the return splits the result at all.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The farming, fishing and forestry share of the partnership's business result, reported at item 5 label Q. The ATO instruction is "Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production", and the amount is what flows through to each partner's share of primary production income. A non-zero figure here is the clearest sign in the tax data that the partnership carries on a primary production business.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow over the income year, signed, and one of the two columns whose sum is the item 5 label S total. The form marks a loss with an L indicator rather than a minus sign.
limitation: A positive primary production figure can sit alongside a non-primary-production loss that leaves the partnership in deficit overall, so this column alone does not say whether the business made money. The non-commercial loss rules can also quarantine a partner's share of a loss, so a negative value here is not a deduction anyone necessarily received.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the partnership return names label Q as the primary production net income or loss, which is the item the p_ prefixed BIT label refers to.
evidence_quote: Show the net income or loss from business at label: Q for primary production R for non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net income or loss from business - PP' with the generic sentence printed twice, so a reader could not tell PP from NPP or know which partners' concessions it drives.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Rent the partnership earned as part of its business, after the interest, capital works and other deductions claimed against it. The ATO sets the arithmetic out directly: "Calculate net rent by subtracting the deductions at labels G, X and H from label F Gross rent." It is the bottom line of item 9, and p_othrtldt is one of the three deductions taken off it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, which can be negative; the form flags a rental loss with an L indicator beside the figure.
limitation: It covers only rent that is partnership business income. Where a property is merely held jointly as an investment, the ATO sends the rent to each owner's individual return instead, so a partnership of passive landlords can show nothing here while collecting rent all year.
rationale: Item 9 of the partnership return is the rent item and the instruction gives both the calculation and the boundary between business rent and jointly held investment property.
evidence_quote: Calculate net rent by subtracting the deductions at labels G, X and H from label F Gross rent.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Net rent' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as definition and limitation, so it did not say which deductions were netted off or that passive rental income is excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: What the partnership spent to earn its non-primary-production distributions from other partnerships and trusts. The ATO instruction for item 8 label T is to show "the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to non-primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts", and it excludes expenses of earning franked distributions, which go to label G. Its own expenses are the point: costs the upstream trust incurred on its own account are not deductible here.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, sitting beside the two non-primary-production income labels B and R that it is netted against to give the net non-primary production amount.
limitation: It is not the cost of running the business. These are only the holding costs of interests in other entities, typically interest on money borrowed to buy in, and thin capitalisation or prepayment rules may already have cut the figure down before it is written on the form.
rationale: The partnership return's item 8 label T is defined by the ATO as the deductions relating to the non-primary-production distribution labels B and R, which is exactly what the DIL label describes.
evidence_quote: Show at label T the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to non-primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductions relating to distribution - NPP' and the generic sentence twice, leaving unclear whose expenses these are and which income labels they attach to.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Income this partnership received as a partner in another partnership, on the non-primary-production side. The ATO instruction for item 8 label B is to "Show at label B the amount of non-primary production income or loss distributions from other partnerships", including any share of foreign resident withholding credit attached. A non-zero value is direct evidence that the firm sits inside a tiered partnership structure rather than trading alone.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year that can be a loss, in which case the form marks it with an L indicator. Foreign source amounts are stripped out and reported at item 23 instead.
limitation: It does not identify the upstream partnership, so this column cannot be used to reconstruct a group structure on its own; the counterpart partnership has to be found through other means. It also excludes any capital gain, because a partnership holds no CGT assets and each partner reports their own gain.
rationale: Item 8 of the partnership return covers distributions received from other partnerships and trusts, with label B the non-primary-production partnership distribution named by the DIL label.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the amount of non-primary production income or loss distributions from other partnerships.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Distribution from partnerships - NPP' with the generic sentence printed twice, and never distinguished a distribution received from a distribution made.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partnership's share of a trust's non-primary-production net income, reported at item 8 label R. The ATO defines it as "the partnership's share of non-primary production income that was included in the net income (for tax purposes) of trusts", excluding capital gains, foreign income and franked distributions, which have their own labels. The amount is what the partnership became presently entitled to, whether or not the cash arrived.
value_definition: A whole-dollar entitlement for the income year, carrying a trust type code on the form alongside the amount. Where the amount is not a loss the lodger also prints a code identifying the kind of trust it came from.
limitation: It is a tax-law share of trust net income, not a cash distribution, so it can be positive in a year the partnership received nothing. It also strips out the franked distribution component, which is reported at label F, so it understates what a partnership with a share portfolio in a family trust actually got.
rationale: Label R of item 8 on the partnership return is the share of trust net income on the non-primary-production side, which the ATO instruction defines and bounds against the neighbouring labels.
evidence_quote: Show at label R the partnership's share of non-primary production income that was included in the net income (for tax purposes) of trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Distribution from trusts - NPP' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that present entitlement rather than cash drives the figure.

value_domain: Refundable tax offset entitlement in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The refundable tax offset the partnership claims for renting dwellings under the National Rental Affordability Scheme, at item 51 label F. The amount is not self-calculated: the ATO says "The amount of the entity's tax offset is the amount stated in the certificate issued by the Secretary of the Department of Social Services", and the offset is available only where such a certificate exists. A value here identifies the firm as an NRAS investor supplying dwellings below market rent.
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset entitlement for one NRAS year, which for the 2023-24 return runs from 1 May 2023 to 30 April 2024 rather than over the income year.
limitation: The scheme has been winding down since allocations ceased, so a fall to zero measures the end of a dwelling's ten-year incentive period rather than a change in the business. The column also does not say how many dwellings the certificate covers, so it cannot be turned into a count of affordable homes.
rationale: Item 51 of the partnership return is the NRAS tax offset, and the instruction states both that a Department of Social Services certificate is required and that the certificate sets the amount.
evidence_quote: The amount of the entity's tax offset is the amount stated in the certificate issued by the Secretary of the Department of Social Services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the label 'National rental affordability scheme tax offset entitlement' and the generic sentence twice, without saying that the figure is certified externally or that the NRAS year is offset from the income year.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The value of the partnership's inventory at the start of the year, at item 39 label C. The ATO defines it as "the total value of all trading stock on hand at the beginning of the income year or accounting period", valued for income tax purposes under section 70-40 of the ITAA 1997. Unlike most of the surrounding tax items it is a stock rather than a flow, and it is chained: "The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year."
value_definition: A whole-dollar valuation at a single point in time, on the tax basis rather than the accounting basis, and including motor vehicle floor plan stock and work in progress of manufactured goods.
limitation: A zero does not mean the business held nothing. A partnership that started operations during the year is told to leave this blank and report the stock through cost of sales instead, and small business entities using the simplified rules may carry opening value forward untouched, so year-on-year movement can be an accounting choice rather than real destocking.
rationale: Item 39 of the partnership return is opening stock, and the ATO instruction gives the definition, the valuation provision and the rule that links it to the previous year's closing value.
evidence_quote: Show at label C the total value of all trading stock on hand at the beginning of the income year or accounting period for which the partnership tax return is being prepared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Opening stock' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing flagged that this is a point-in-time valuation on a tax rather than accounting basis.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Foreign income - items 22 to 24
variable_description: All the assessable income the partnership earned offshore, before any deduction, at item 23 label B. The ATO asks for "the gross amount of assessable income derived from foreign sources, including amounts distributed from partnerships and other trusts as well as New Zealand franking company dividends and supplementary dividends", with foreign tax withheld at source added back in. It is the broadest single measure in the return of a partnership's exposure to offshore earnings.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross flow for the income year, stated before deductions; the net figure after allowable deductions is the separate label V.
limitation: Gross is the trap: a partnership with large offshore turnover and matching costs looks internationally exposed here while earning almost nothing. Attributed foreign income under item 22, foreign capital gains and income exempt under sections 23AI and 23AK are all excluded, so this is not the whole of the firm's foreign activity either.
rationale: Item 23 label B of the partnership return is gross other assessable foreign source income, and the instruction lists exactly what is in and out of the figure.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the gross amount of assessable income derived from foreign sources, including amounts distributed from partnerships and other trusts as well as New Zealand franking company dividends and supplementary dividends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Other Assessable Foreign source Gross Income' and the generic sentence twice, without distinguishing gross from net or naming what item 22 takes out.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 14 Other Australian income and 15 Total of items 5 to 14
variable_description: Australian income that fitted nowhere else on the partnership return, gathered at item 14 label O. The ATO lists what lands there: gains on the disposal of traditional securities, bonuses from life insurance companies and friendly societies, royalty income, add-backs of listed investment company capital gain deductions, and assessable foreign exchange gains not already shown at item 5. The DIL calls it a type of income but the recorded response is a dollar amount, so this column holds the amount at label O and not a category code.
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual income flow for the income year, which can be a loss; the current partnership return has no type-of-income code box beside it despite the DIL wording.
limitation: It is a mixed bag by construction, so a movement in it cannot be attributed to any one activity without other columns; a forex gain, a life insurance bonus and a royalty stream all read the same here. The DIL's trailing 'type of Income' has no counterpart on the 2024 partnership return, so do not expect a code list behind this column.
rationale: Item 14 of the partnership return is other Australian income and the ATO instruction enumerates its components; the DIL's numeric response type rules out the column being a code, but the source does not explain the label's trailing wording.
evidence_quote: Show at label O the assessable Australian source foreign exchange (forex) gains or deductible losses that you have not already included at any other label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Other Australian income - type of Income' and the generic sentence twice, which left a reader expecting a category code where the data holds dollars.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Ordinary trading revenue from the partnership's primary production business, at item 5 label G. The ATO describes labels G and H as "other business income such as revenue from the sale of goods, services rendered, disposal of depreciating assets, work in progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997, and royalties", with G the primary production column. For most farming partnerships this is the largest single income figure on the return, since the specialised labels above it capture only withholding and government payments.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system amount for the income year, GST exclusive where the partnership is registered, and able to be a loss, in which case the form marks it with an L.
limitation: It is an accounting figure, not a tax figure: adjustments for tax purposes are made further down at the reconciliation labels, so this does not equal assessable primary production income. Assessable government industry payments such as drought and disaster grants are reported separately at label E and are absent from here.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return splits business income into primary and non-primary production columns, with other business income at labels G and H respectively.
evidence_quote: Show at labels G and H, as appropriate, other business income such as revenue from the sale of goods, services rendered, disposal of depreciating assets, work in progress amounts assessable under section 15-50 of the ITAA 1997, and royalties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Other business income - PP' and the generic sentence twice, so it never said that this is the main sales line rather than a residual.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Ordinary trading revenue from everything the partnership does outside primary production, at item 5 label H. It takes the same content as the primary production column beside it, and the ATO singles out one case worth knowing: "Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments." For a professional or retail partnership this is effectively turnover.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system amount for the income year, GST exclusive where the partnership is registered for GST, and signed with an L indicator when it is a loss.
limitation: It is not turnover as the ABS would define it, because the withholding, foreign resident and government payment labels above it hold income that never reaches this line. Nor is it a tax figure, since the income reconciliation adjustment at label A can move large amounts in or out afterwards.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines labels G and H as the other business income columns for primary and non-primary production, and gives the medical practice example that pins label H.
evidence_quote: Medical practices should show their Medicare payments at label H Other business income, not at label F Assessable government industry payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other business income - NPP' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing indicated that this line is close to turnover for a non-farming partnership.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The cost of tangible assets the partnership began depreciating this year, at item 49 label B. The ATO asks for "the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time", so the column measures new capital going into the business rather than the deduction taken. It is the tangible counterpart of label A, which holds patents, in-house software and other intangibles.
value_definition: A whole-dollar cost, not reduced for any estimated non-taxable use, and including assets under $1,000 that were allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It is investment, not expense: the deduction actually claimed is elsewhere, and a large figure here can sit beside a small depreciation charge. Small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules skip item 49 entirely, so the column is missing for exactly the firms that write off most assets immediately.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return covers capital allowances, with label B the cost of non-intangible depreciating assets first deducted in the year, and the instruction states the small business entity exclusion at the top of the item.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) for which the partnership is claiming a deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Other depreciating assets first deducted' with the generic sentence twice, so a reader could mistake a cost of acquisition for a depreciation deduction.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Deductions - items 16 to 20
variable_description: The catch-all deduction line of the partnership return, item 18 label Q. The ATO defines it as "the total of any deductible losses and outgoings not already claimed by the partnership at any other items", and lists what typically lands there: tax-related expenses, losses on traditional securities, premiums to a non-resident insurer, gifts, political contributions, subscriptions and low-value pool depreciation. It sits outside the item 5 trading account, so it reduces net Australian income rather than business profit.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, GST exclusive where input tax credits were available, and one of the three components summed at item 19.
limitation: The heterogeneity is the point and the problem: a gift to a deductible gift recipient, an accountant's fee and a low-value pool write-off are indistinguishable inside the total. Debt deductions relating to foreign income are also pushed here from item 23, so the column is not purely domestic in substance.
rationale: Item 18 of the partnership return is other deductions, and the ATO instruction both defines label Q as a residual and enumerates the categories that fall into it.
evidence_quote: Show at label Q the total of any deductible losses and outgoings not already claimed by the partnership at any other items.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total other deductions' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which said nothing about the item being a residual outside the trading account.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: The residual expense line of the partnership's trading account, item 5 label N. The ATO defines it as "the total of all other business expenses for the income year which you have not included at labels P to M - for example, travel expenses", which makes it whatever is left after contractor, superannuation, cost of sales, bad debt, lease, rent, interest, royalty, depreciation, motor vehicle and repair costs are taken out. Accounting and legal fees are explicitly directed here rather than to the contractor label.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, GST exclusive where input tax credits are available, and the last of the labels totalled at label O.
limitation: It carries non-deductible amounts as well as deductible ones. Capital items, doubtful debt provisions and losses on asset sales are all told to sit here and then be added back at the expense reconciliation adjustment, so this number is not a deduction the partnership received.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines label N as the residual expense label and states which expenses are routed into it and which are added back later.
evidence_quote: Show at label N the total of all other business expenses for the income year which you have not included at labels P to M - for example, travel expenses.
