supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'All other expenses' and printed the generic sentence twice, hiding that non-deductible expenditure is deliberately parked in this line.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 9 Rent
variable_description: Rental property costs other than interest and capital works, at item 9 label H. The ATO asks for "the total of other deductible expenses incurred in earning rental income", which in practice means rates, insurance, agent commission, repairs and usually the decline in value of assets used in the property. Interest sits at label G and capital works at label X, so the three together are what net rent is calculated after.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, GST exclusive where the rent was a taxable supply, and reduced in advance by any thin capitalisation disallowance.
limitation: Because it absorbs everything except interest and capital works, it cannot be used to separate maintenance spending from holding costs. Depreciation on assets sent to a low-value pool is reported at item 18 instead, so a partnership with a pooled fit-out shows less here than it actually deducted against the rent.
rationale: Item 9 of the partnership return sets out the four rental labels, and the instruction defines label H as the residual deduction and names what is excluded from it.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the total of other deductible expenses incurred in earning rental income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other rental deductions' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say what the other rental deductions are or which costs sit outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: What the partnership paid to people connected with its partners, at item 45 label M. The ATO asks for "the amounts, including salaries, wages, commissions, superannuation contributions or allowances" paid to a relative of a partner, to another partnership in which a relative is a partner, and to shareholders, directors or beneficiaries of entities that are themselves partners. Payments to a partner are expressly excluded, because a partner cannot be an employee of the partnership.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the income year, drawn from and also included in the item 44 total salary and wage expenses figure rather than added to it.
limitation: It is a related-party disclosure, not a separate expense: double counting it with the salary and wage total overstates the wage bill. It also says nothing about how many people were paid, and section 26-35 can deny a deduction for the excessive part, so the amount reported is not necessarily the amount allowed.
rationale: Item 45 of the partnership return is payments to associated persons, and the ATO instruction lists the classes of recipient and states the overlap with item 44.
evidence_quote: Also, include the amounts of salaries and wages paid to an associated person, relative, principal, agent, related entity or associate entity at item 44 Total salary and wage expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Payments to associated persons' and the generic sentence twice, without warning that the amount is also inside the total wage figure.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: The part of a primary production distribution from another partnership that escapes the higher managed investment trust withholding rate, at item 32 label F. The ATO describes it as "the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as primary production income, that is, income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities". It is a carve-out from p_pp_ncmi_amt, and both must also appear inside the item 8 label A distribution.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of an amount reported elsewhere on the same return, tagged so that foreign investors in the chain are withheld at the concessional rather than the penalty rate.
limitation: It is a tagging line, not extra income; adding it to item 8 double counts. Only entities in a managed investment trust chain ever complete item 32, so a zero here means the partnership is outside that structure, not that its income failed the exclusion.
rationale: Item 32 of the partnership return breaks non-concessional MIT income down by source, and the ATO instruction assigns label F to the excluded-from-NCMI component of primary production partnership distributions.
evidence_quote: Show at label F the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw label 'PP - Distribution from partnerships - Excluded from NCMI' and the generic sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know NCMI is a withholding-rate concept or that the amount is already counted at item 8.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: Primary production income the partnership received from another partnership that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, at item 32 label E. The ATO defines NCMI as "MIT cross staple arrangement income, MIT trading trust income, MIT agricultural income, or MIT residential housing income", and label E as "the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as primary production income" - in practice, income attributable to agricultural land held for rent. Its presence marks the firm as sitting in a stapled or agricultural MIT structure.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the item 8 label A distribution, reported again at item 32 so the character of the income travels with it to the partners.
limitation: It is a characterisation of income already reported, so it must not be added to partnership income totals. It also does not measure tax paid: the consequence of the tag falls on foreign investors further up the chain through a higher withholding rate, not on this partnership.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 32 of the partnership return defines NCMI and assigns label E to the primary production partnership distribution component named by the DIL label.
evidence_quote: Show at label E the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'PP - Distribution from partnerships - NCMI' with the generic sentence twice, leaving the acronym unexplained and the double-count risk unflagged.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Primary production income this partnership received as a partner in another partnership, at item 8 label A. The ATO instruction is short: "Show at label A the amount of primary production income or loss distribution from other partnerships." Farming groups commonly run land-holding and operating partnerships in a chain, so a figure here usually means the reporting entity is one rung of such a structure rather than the operating farm itself.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year that may be a loss, flagged with an L on the form, and stated before the label S deductions that are netted against it.
limitation: It does not identify the paying partnership, so a group cannot be reassembled from this column alone. Any NCMI component of it is disclosed separately at item 32, and foreign source amounts are stripped out to item 23, so the label A figure is narrower than the total received.
rationale: Item 8 of the partnership return records distributions received from other partnerships and trusts, with label A the primary production partnership distribution.
evidence_quote: Show at label A the amount of primary production income or loss distribution from other partnerships.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Distribution from partnerships - PP' and the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish income received from income distributed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partnership's share of a trust's primary production net income, at item 8 label Z. The ATO asks for "the partnership's share of primary production income that has been included in the net income (for tax purposes) of a trust", counting income the partnership became presently entitled to whether or not it was received. Where the amount is positive the form also carries a trust type code beside it, distinguishing a deceased estate from a discretionary trading trust.
value_definition: A whole-dollar entitlement for the income year, which may be shown as a loss only when it forms part of an overall distribution of net income from the same trust.
limitation: Present entitlement rather than payment drives the figure, so it can be large in a year no cash moved. It is also a share of a tax-law amount, which can differ substantially from the trust's accounting distribution, and the trust itself is not identified.
rationale: Label Z of item 8 on the partnership return is the share of trust net income on the primary production side, defined by the ATO alongside the trust type code table.
evidence_quote: Show at label Z the partnership's share of primary production income that has been included in the net income (for tax purposes) of a trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Distribution from trusts - PP' and printed the generic sentence twice, which gave no hint that entitlement rather than receipt is what is measured.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partnership's own costs of holding its primary production interests in other partnerships and trusts, at item 8 label S. The ATO defines it as "the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts", and adds that "expenses incurred on behalf of the trust are not to be deducted by the partnership". Labels A, Z and S together give the net primary production amount from upstream entities.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, netted against the two primary production income labels rather than against trading income at item 5.
limitation: These are financing and holding costs of an interest, not farming costs, so adding this column to item 5 expenses to build a cost of production double counts the concept and misstates the farm. Prepayment and thin capitalisation rules may already have reduced the amount that reaches the label.
rationale: Label S of item 8 on the partnership return is defined by the ATO as the deductions relating to the primary production distribution labels A and Z.
evidence_quote: Show at label S the partnership's deductions for its own expenses relating to primary production distributions from other partnerships or its share of net income from trusts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Deductions relating to distribution - PP' and the generic sentence twice, without saying whose expenses they are or which income they attach to.

value_domain: Balance sheet amount in dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2010 instructions, 36 Proprietors' funds
variable_description: The partners' equity in the business, taken straight from the partnership's accounts. The ATO asks for "the net proprietors' funds from the accounting records of the partnership" and pins the arithmetic: "The amount shown at item 33 Total assets less the amount shown at item 35 Total liabilities equals the amount shown at K." It is the only net worth measure in the partnership return's key financial information block.
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance at the end of the income year, an accounting rather than tax figure, and able to be negative, in which case the form marks it with an L indicator.
limitation: The item was dropped from the partnership return: it appears in the ATO instructions up to 2012 and is absent from 2013 onwards, where key financial information stops at total liabilities. Any series built on this column ends there, and a run of empty years is a form change rather than firms losing their equity.
rationale: The 2010 partnership return instructions define item 36 label K and give the total assets less total liabilities identity; comparing the 2010, 2012, 2013 and later key financial information pages shows when the label was removed.
evidence_quote: Show at K the net proprietors' funds from the accounting records of the partnership.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Proprietors' funds' with the generic sentence printed twice, and gave no warning that the label ceased to exist on the return after 2012.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: The part of a non-primary-production partnership distribution that is carved out of the NCMI rules, at item 32 label J. The ATO defines it as "the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production", meaning income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities. The pair to it is p_pshp_npp_ncmi_amt, and both belong inside the item 8 label B distribution.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of an amount reported elsewhere on the same return, identifying income that keeps concessional managed investment trust withholding treatment.
limitation: It records an exclusion from a penalty rate, not an exemption from tax, and it is already inside item 8, so treating it as additional income overstates the partnership. Only entities within a managed investment trust chain complete item 32 at all, which makes the column empty for almost every business in the register.
rationale: Item 32 of the partnership return separates NCMI by source and production type, with label J the excluded-from-NCMI component of non-primary-production partnership distributions.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Non-PP - Distribution from partnerships - Excluded from NCMI' and the generic sentence twice, so neither the exclusion nor its narrow population was explained.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Taxation of financial arrangements - items 31 and 32
variable_description: Non-primary-production income from another partnership that is non-concessional managed investment trust income, at item 32 label I. The ATO defines the non-primary-production NCMI content as "cross staple income, trading trust income and residential housing income", and label I as "the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production". It is the clearest signal in the return that the firm sits inside a stapled infrastructure or build-to-rent structure.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the item 8 label B distribution, re-reported at item 32 so the character of the income passes down to the partners.
limitation: It is a tag on income already counted, not new income, and it measures character rather than any tax the partnership paid; the higher withholding falls on foreign investors upstream. The column also cannot separate the four kinds of NCMI from one another.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 32 defines NCMI and assigns label I to the non-primary-production partnership distribution component that the DIL label names.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the total NCMI amount distributed from partnerships categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Non-PP - Distribution from partnerships - NCMI' with the generic sentence twice and left the acronym and the double-count risk unexplained.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: What the partnership bought in as direct materials during the year, at item 40 label B. The ATO asks for "the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange, in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business". With opening and closing stock either side of it, this is the purchases term of the cost of sales identity rather than a deduction in its own right.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow of purchases over the income year, distinct from the stock valuations at items 39 and 41 that bracket it.
limitation: It is direct materials only, so it is not a measure of what the business spent with suppliers: services, subcontracting and overheads are elsewhere in item 5. A partnership still using the old simplified tax system accounting method shows only purchases it has paid for, which breaks comparability with accrual lodgers.
rationale: Item 40 of the partnership return is purchases and other costs, and the ATO instruction defines label B and notes the cash-basis variant for former STS taxpayers.
evidence_quote: Show at label B the cost of direct materials used for manufacture, sale or exchange, in deriving the gross proceeds or earnings of the business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Purchases and other costs' and printed the generic sentence twice, without saying that the figure is direct materials feeding a cost of sales calculation.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: What the partnership paid to occupy premises it does not own, at item 5 label H of the expenses column. The ATO defines it as "the expenditure incurred as a tenant for the rental or lease of land and buildings used in the production of income". Read against item 9, which is rent the partnership receives, the two labels tell opposite stories about the same firm's property position.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, GST exclusive where input tax credits are available, and split between the primary and non-primary production columns.
limitation: It covers land and buildings only. Equipment and vehicle leases are reported at the separate lease expenses label, so this cannot be used as a measure of total leasing, and a firm that owns its premises shows zero regardless of how much property it holds.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return holds the trading account expenses, and the ATO instruction restricts label H to premises rent paid as a tenant.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the expenditure incurred as a tenant for the rental or lease of land and buildings used in the production of income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Rent expenses' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate premises rent from equipment leasing or from rent received.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Upkeep of the partnership's plant and premises, at item 5 label M. The ATO defines it as "the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises", and expects capital items to be written back later: "Write back any non-deductible expenditure, such as items of a capital nature or amounts relating to private use of an item at label M, at item 5 Reconciliation items." It is one of the few direct indicators in tax data of whether a firm is maintaining its capital stock.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, before any tax adjustment, GST exclusive where input tax credits are available.
limitation: The figure mixes deductible repairs with capital improvements that are added back afterwards, so a spike can be a renovation rather than maintenance. Remedying defects that existed when an asset was bought is capital in nature, which means a firm's first year of owning second-hand equipment reads high here for reasons that have nothing to do with wear.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 defines label M and sets out the repair against capital improvement boundary that governs what is reported and what is written back.
evidence_quote: Show at label M the expenditure on repairs and maintenance of plant, machinery, implements and premises.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Repairs and maintenance' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that capital work can sit inside the number.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation - items 29 to 30
variable_description: Royalties the partnership paid offshore, at item 29 label E. The ATO instruction is to show "the royalty expenses paid to non-residents", and the amount is a subset of the total royalty expenses at item 5 label J rather than an addition to it. Because paying a royalty abroad triggers withholding tax and an International dealings schedule, this column marks a firm that licenses foreign intellectual property.
value_definition: A whole-dollar expense for the income year, reported in the overseas transactions item and repeated inside the item 5 royalty total after any reconciliation adjustment.
limitation: It does not say who was paid or in which country, and it is not deductible unless the withholding tax was remitted, so the reported amount is a claim rather than a settled deduction. Adding it to the total royalty expense figure double counts the same payments.
rationale: Item 29 of the partnership return covers overseas expenses, and the ATO instruction defines label E and states its relationship to item 5 label J.
evidence_quote: Show at label E the royalty expenses paid to non-residents during 2023-24.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Royalty expenses overseas' and printed the generic sentence twice, so the overlap with total royalty expenses was invisible.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business income and expenses - item 5
variable_description: Everything the partnership paid to use someone else's intellectual property, at item 5 label J. The ATO defines it as "the royalty expenses for the income year" and adds "Include royalties paid to residents and non-residents", which makes it the superset of the overseas-only figure at item 29 label E. Differencing the two gives a rough split between domestic and imported licensing.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accounting-system expense for the income year, split between the primary and non-primary production columns of item 5.
limitation: It is a payment for the right to use, not a measure of technology transfer: franchise fees, mineral royalties and software licences all land in the same line. Where withholding tax on a foreign royalty was not remitted the deduction is not allowable, so the label can overstate the deduction actually available.
rationale: Item 5 of the partnership return holds total royalty expenses at label J, and the instruction states that both resident and non-resident royalties belong there.
evidence_quote: Show at label J the royalty expenses for the income year. Include royalties paid to residents and non-residents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total royalty expenses' with the generic sentence twice and did not say that the overseas royalty column is a component of it.

value_domain: Country-by-country reporting entity indicator
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
variable_description: Whether the partnership declared itself a country-by-country reporting entity, at item 2 label G2. The ATO test is membership of a very large multinational group: "An entity is a CBC reporting entity if it is either a CBC reporting parent, or a member of a CBC reporting group, and one of the other group members is a CBC reporting parent with an annual global income of A$1 billion or more." A tick therefore identifies one of a few hundred entities in the country with global reporting obligations.
value_definition: A single flag rather than a graded code: one value marks a country-by-country reporting entity and every other response, including a blank, is treated as no response given.
limitation: Absence of the flag is not evidence of a small business, because it also covers an unticked box or a form version that predates the label; only a positive value carries information. The flag is also self-assessed at lodgment, and it is close to but not the same test as the significant global entity flag at label G1, so the two do not always agree.
rationale: Item 2 of the partnership return records business status and the two multinational flags, and the ATO instruction gives the country-by-country reporting entity definition and the A$1 billion threshold.
evidence_quote: Print X at label G2 if you were a country-by-country (CBC) reporting entity for the income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Country by country reporting entity' and the generic sentence twice, so it neither gave the threshold nor warned that a non-response looks identical to a no.

value_domain: Salary and wage reporting location code
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Where the partnership's wage bill was booked in its own accounts, not how big that wage bill was. The code box beside item 44 records the section "salary and wages were wholly or predominantly reported in": C for the expense component of cost of sales, A for all other expenses, B for both, and O for neither. It is the key that lets a reader work out whether labour cost is already sitting inside cost of sales at item 5 label E or inside all other expenses at label N.
value_definition: A single-character code taking the values C, A, B and O, mapped in the BLADE metadata to numeric codes with all other responses treated as invalid or missing.
limitation: It carries no dollars, so it cannot be used to measure labour cost; the amount is the separate item 44 figure. It is also a predominance judgment made by the lodger, so a business splitting wages evenly between cost of sales and other expenses may be coded either B or one of the single categories depending on who prepared the return.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 44 sets out the code table that determines where salary and wages have predominantly been reported, and the codes in the table match the DIL's valid responses one for one.
evidence_quote: Print in the CODE box the code from Table: Determine where salary and wages have predominantly been reported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Total salary and wage expenses action code' and the generic sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have expected dollars rather than a bookkeeping location code.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Reconciliation items and net income or loss - item 5
variable_description: The slice of the partnership's income that qualifies its individual partners for the small business income tax offset, at item 5 label V. The ATO defines it as "the partnership's assessable income from carrying on a small business, less deductions to the extent that they are attributable to that assessable income", combined across all its businesses. Only a partnership that is a small business entity completes it, so a value here is itself a turnover-threshold marker.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year. Where the partnership has no business income or deductions outside item 5 label S, the ATO says label V simply repeats the label S figure.
limitation: The population is truncated by the small business aggregated turnover threshold, so the column is blank for larger firms rather than zero, and comparisons across the size distribution are censored. Personal services income that is not from a personal services business, tax-related expenses and gifts are excluded, so it does not reconcile to net income from business.
rationale: The ATO instruction attached to item 5 of the partnership return defines net small business income, states who must complete it and describes the shortcut where label V equals label S.
evidence_quote: The net small business income is the partnership's assessable income from carrying on a small business, less deductions to the extent that they are attributable to that assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Net small business income' with the generic sentence twice and did not say that the column only exists for small business entities.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Depreciation still being claimed on assets first written down under the COVID-era Backing business investment concession, at item 49 label N. The ATO instruction is conditional on an earlier year: "If you used the Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation in 2019-20 or 2020-21 for one or more assets, show at label N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2023-24 for those assets." It is a tail measure, tracing the later-year cost of a stimulus decision taken in 2020 or 2021.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the current income year attributable to a defined cohort of assets, not to assets acquired in the year being reported.
limitation: The column exists only from the year after the concession was used and shrinks as the cohort depreciates away, so a decline measures the ageing of 2020 and 2021 assets rather than any change in investment behaviour. It also cannot be read as the value of the concession, since it is a claim in a later year, not the accelerated amount originally deducted.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return includes the subsequent-year Backing business investment label, and the ATO instruction ties it to assets first treated in 2019-20 or 2020-21.
evidence_quote: If you used the Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation in 2019-20 or 2020-21 for one or more assets, show at label N the amount of depreciation you are claiming in 2023-24 for those assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long DIL label and the generic sentence twice, without saying that the column refers back to a fixed cohort of assets from two specific years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Business capital expenditure the partnership is writing off over five years under the blackhole expenditure rules, at item 49 label K. The ATO asks for "the total of the partnership's deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997", which is the provision that lets a business deduct capital costs with no other home in the tax law: setting up or restructuring an entity, raising equity, and the costs of starting or ceasing a business. A value here is a reasonable marker of structural change in the firm.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for one income year, being one instalment of expenditure spread across five years rather than the expenditure itself.
limitation: It is one fifth of an earlier outlay, so it lags the event that caused it by up to five years and cannot date a restructure. The provision is a last resort by design, which means the same underlying cost may appear here for one firm and inside all other expenses for another depending on advice.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return carries the section 40-880 deduction at label K, and the ATO instruction identifies it by provision.
evidence_quote: Show at label K the total of the partnership's deductions allowable under section 40-880 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Section 40-880 deduction' and printed the generic sentence twice, which left the provision unexplained and the five-year spreading unmentioned.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Whether the partnership set its own depreciation lives rather than accepting the Commissioner's, at item 49 label C. The ATO frames the choice as "work out the effective life yourself (self-assess), or adopt the Commissioner's determination in Taxation Ruling TR 2022/1", and a yes means at least one asset was self-assessed. Because self-assessment usually shortens the life and brings deductions forward, the flag marks a firm taking an active position on its capital allowances.
value_definition: A two-state flag, Y for yes and N for no, with any other response treated as invalid or not given.
limitation: It is an any-asset flag, so one self-assessed laptop reads the same as a fully self-assessed plant fleet, and it carries no dollars. It is also missing rather than false for small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules, who are told to skip item 49 altogether.
rationale: Item 49 of the partnership return asks whether the effective life of any depreciating asset was self-assessed, and the ATO instruction states the yes and no conditions for label C.
evidence_quote: Yes - Print X in the Yes box at label C, as you have self-assessed the effective life of one or more of your depreciating assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the question text 'Have you self-assessed the effective life of any of these assets?' with the generic sentence twice, and did not say that one asset is enough to trigger it.

value_domain: Business status code (ceased, commenced, continuing)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business description and status - items 1 and 2
variable_description: Whether the partnership says it started, stopped or kept trading during the year, at item 2 labels B1 to B3. The ATO instruction is to "Print X at label B1, B2 or B3 to show the appropriate description for the status of the business", and it is the closest thing in the tax return to a self-reported entry and exit marker. It sits beside the industry code at item 1 and the multinational flags at labels G1 and G2.
value_definition: A single code with three substantive states, ceased, commenced and continuing, with any other response treated as invalid or not given.
limitation: It cannot record two events in one year: the ATO tells lodgers that "If more than one selection applies, select the first applicable option", so a business that both started and finished within the year reports only one status. A blank is also permitted when none of the descriptions apply, so absence is not evidence of continuity, and the field is a lodger's assertion rather than a registry event.
rationale: Item 2 of the partnership return records business status, and the ATO instruction gives both the three-way choice and the tie-breaking rule that limits it.
evidence_quote: If more than one selection applies, select the first applicable option.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Status of your business' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that a start and a cessation in the same year collapse to one code.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: The depreciation a small business partnership claimed on its general pool, at item 50 label B. Under the simplified depreciation rules assets above the instant write-off threshold go into one pool rather than being tracked individually, and the ATO directs the lodger to "Add up the general small business pool amounts" from the simplified depreciation worksheet and write the total here. It is the slower half of item 50, sitting beside the immediate deduction at label A.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, derived from a pool balance rather than from any single asset, and reported only by small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: Because the pool has no asset identity, nothing here says what was depreciated or when it was bought, and a pool balance below the write-off threshold can be deducted in full, producing a large one-off figure that is not new investment. The item is completed only by small business entities, so it is missing rather than zero for larger firms.
rationale: Item 50 of the partnership return is small business entity simplified depreciation, with label B the general pool deduction, and the ATO instruction states who completes the item and how the amount is derived.
evidence_quote: Complete this item only if the partnership is a small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Small business entity simplified depreciation - Deduction for general small business pool' with the generic sentence twice, without noting that the item is confined to small business entities.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported on the partnership tax return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return 2024 instructions, Business and professional items - items 37 to 53
variable_description: Assets a small business partnership wrote off in full in the year of purchase, at item 50 label A. The ATO names the label "Deduction for certain assets (costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold)", which makes this the instant asset write-off line of the return. Unlike the pool deduction beside it at label B, the whole cost is deducted at once, so the figure is close to a measure of that year's small-asset capital spending.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction for the income year, equal to the cost of the qualifying assets rather than to a decline in value, and reported only by small business entities using the simplified depreciation rules.
limitation: The threshold moved repeatedly, from $20,000 to $30,000, to unlimited temporary full expensing and back to $20,000, so the same firm buying the same asset falls in or out of this label depending on the year; a break in the series is policy, not behaviour. The item is also blank rather than zero for firms outside the small business rules.
rationale: Item 50 of the partnership return holds the two simplified depreciation deductions, and the ATO instruction names label A as the deduction for assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold.
evidence_quote: Transfer the deduction for certain assets at row a in Worksheet: Small businesses using simplified depreciation to item 50 - label A Deduction for certain assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Small business entity simplified depreciation - Deduction for certain assets' and the generic sentence twice, so the instant asset write-off and its shifting threshold went unmentioned.

value_domain: Count of distinct patent technology areas within Other Fields
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How broadly the business filed patents within the Other Fields technology grouping in the financial year. IP Australia describes scope variables as "the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year", and Other Fields holds just three of the 35 areas: furniture and games, other consumer goods, and civil engineering. A value of 3 means the firm filed across all of consumer products, furnishings and construction in one year.
value_definition: A whole number bounded at 3, counting distinct technology areas from the WIPO IPC concordance as adapted for IPLoRD, over the applications the applicant filed during the Australian financial year.
limitation: The ceiling of 3 makes it incomparable with p_filed_class_scope, which runs to 35, so a ratio of the two is not a diversity measure. It is also a count of areas, not of applications: a firm filing one patent that carries two classifications outscores a firm filing fifty in a single area.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines scope variables, states that patents have 35 classification areas grouped into five coarse areas, and lists the three areas that make up Other Fields in its Annex A concordance table.
evidence_quote: Scope variables are intended to indicate the breadth of an applicant's activity across multiple event streams in a given financial year and are used as a term to describe the number of classification areas in which an applicant conducts the activity in a given financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording about other fields technology area classes and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that Other Fields contains only three areas or what they are.

value_domain: Count of patent applications filed in a financial year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How many patent applications the business filed during the year within the Other Fields technology grouping. That grouping covers three areas: furniture and games, other consumer goods, and civil engineering. IP Australia defines the filed event stream as "rights filed during the financial year", so this is a flow of new applications, not a stock of patents held. It is the whole-number companion of p_other_filed_w_count, which shares jointly filed applications between applicants.
value_definition: A whole count of applications over the Australian financial year, classified by the WIPO IPC technology concordance as adapted for IPLoRD.
limitation: A patent can carry classifications in more than one coarse area, so the five coarse-area counts sum to more than the total filings and cannot be treated as a partition. A filing is also not an invention that reached the market: many applications lapse before grant, and this column says nothing about what became of them.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines count variables and the four event streams, and states that a patent right can sit in more than one coarse classification area simultaneously.
evidence_quote: Count variables are counts of the number of events of a certain kind or the number of rights in the stockpile of an applicant for an IP right.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording about total number of patents in the other fields technology and the generic sentence twice, so it did not warn that coarse areas overlap.

value_domain: IPLoRD patent technology area, Other Fields grouping
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: The single technology area the business filed most patents in during the year, restricted to the Other Fields grouping. IP Australia says modal variables "record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year", and within Other Fields the only possible answers are area 33 furniture and games, 34 other consumer goods, and 35 civil engineering. Unlike the counts beside it, this column is a label rather than a quantity.
value_definition: A character value naming one of three technology areas from the WIPO concordance as adapted for IPLoRD, taken over the applications filed in the Australian financial year.
limitation: A mode carries no weight behind it: two applications in one area and one in another produce the same value as two hundred against one hundred. The dictionary does not state how ties are resolved, so a year with an even split cannot be interpreted from this column alone.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines modal value variables and its Annex A table lists the three technology areas that make up the Other Fields grouping.
evidence_quote: Modal value variables record the most frequent variable type (using IPLoRD's simplified classification system for IP activity) for activity in a year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Most common other fields technology area class for all patents filed applications during the financial year' and the generic sentence twice, and pointed at an appendix without naming the three possible values.

value_domain: Fractional count of patent applications filed
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: The business's share of Other Fields patent applications filed in the year, splitting jointly filed applications between the applicants. IP Australia explains the weighting directly: "when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score", which keeps national totals correct when applicant records are added up. Comparing it with p_other_filed_count reveals how much of the firm's patenting is collaborative.
value_definition: A fractional count over the Australian financial year, less than or equal to the unweighted count, formed from sums of 1/n terms rather than whole applications.
limitation: The weight is 1/n on the number of applicants, not a share of ownership or of inventive contribution, so a junior partner and a lead firm on the same patent receive the same fraction. It also cannot be reconciled to grant outcomes, since a fraction of an application says nothing about whether that application succeeded.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines weighted count variables and gives the 1/n rule for jointly filed applications along with the reason for using them.
evidence_quote: For example, when an application is filed jointly by a group of n applicants, that application counts (1/n) towards each of the applicants' weighted count score.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the phrase 'number of patent applications fraction filed' unexplained and printed the generic sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know what the fraction was of.

value_domain: Count of distinct patent technology areas within Other Fields
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How many of the three Other Fields technology areas the business actually won patents in during the year, as opposed to merely applying in. The granted stream covers "rights granted during the financial year", and scope counts the distinct classification areas that activity touched. Set against p_other_filed_class_scope for the same firm, it shows whether the breadth of what was applied for survived examination.
value_definition: A whole number bounded at 3, counting distinct technology areas among the applications granted in the Australian financial year.
limitation: Grant lags filing by years, so the granted and filed scopes in the same row describe different cohorts of applications and should not be differenced as though they were a pass rate. The ceiling of 3 also makes it incomparable with the whole-of-patent scope variable, which runs to 35.
rationale: The IPLoRD data dictionary defines the granted event stream and the scope activity metric, and its Annex A table fixes the number of technology areas inside the Other Fields grouping.
evidence_quote: Granted - rights granted during the financial year
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the DIL wording about enforceable patent rights granted and printed the generic sentence twice, leaving both the bound of 3 and the filing-to-grant lag unstated.

value_domain: Count of patents granted in a financial year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLoRD2020) Data Dictionary, April 2021
variable_description: How many Other Fields patents the business was granted during the financial year. IP Australia uses grant to mean the point at which "a right is granted legally enforceable status by IP Australia", so this is the flow into the enforceable stockpile rather than a count of applications made. Grants add to the stock measured by p_other_le_count, and retirements take away from it.
value_definition: A whole count of rights granted over the Australian financial year, in the furniture and games, other consumer goods and civil engineering technology areas.
limitation: The grant relates to applications filed several years earlier, so pairing this year's grants with this year's filings measures nothing about success rates. Because a patent can carry classifications in more than one coarse area, the Other Fields grant count overlaps the other four coarse-area counts.

The figure is what full expensing would have allowed, which for an asset held part-year and part privately is less than what was paid for it, and firms that never became eligible or that used simplified depreciation report nothing at all.

The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label wording with the generic sentence printed twice, so a reader would have taken this for the cost of the assets rather than the deduction given up on them.

value_domain: Tax file number amounts withheld from interest, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 11 Gross interest
variable_description: Tax an investment body held back from the partnership's interest because no tax file number had been given to it, reported at item 11 label I. The ATO instruction is "Show at label I any TFN amounts withheld from gross interest where a TFN has not been provided to the investment body." The gross interest that the withholding was taken from sits beside it at label J, so the pair shows both the income and the penalty rate deduction taken at source.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, credited against the partners' tax rather than the partnership's, since a partnership is not itself a taxpayer. It is an administrative amount reported by the payer as well, and the ATO data matches it.

Almost every partnership reports nothing here even when it earns substantial interest, so the column cannot be used as a proxy for interest income or for financial assets.

The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Total business income, non-primary production column, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The partnership's gross trading income from everything other than farming, in the non-primary production column of item 5. The return splits business income into a primary production and a non-primary production column and the ATO says of the total row "Show the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H", which for this side means gross payments where an ABN was not quoted, foreign resident withholding payments, assessable government industry payments and other business income at label H. It is turnover before any expense, not profit.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, on the partnership's own accounting basis before the reconciliation adjustments made later at item 5. It excludes interest, dividends, rent, foreign income and trust distributions, which are reported at their own items.
limitation: It is not the firm's sales figure and does not match BAS turnover: the return is annual and tax-basis while the activity statement is quarterly and GST-basis, and a partnership carrying on both a farm and another business splits its income across this column and the primary production one on judgement, so the split can move between years without any change in activity.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the total business income row and lists the income labels feeding it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Total Business Income - NPP' with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what NPP means, what is inside the total, or why it will not reconcile with the activity statement.

value_domain: Total business income, primary production column, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: The partnership's gross farming income, reported in the primary production column of item 5. It is split out there because primary producers get concessional treatment elsewhere in the tax law. The ATO instruction for the total row is "Show the total of all income items at labels C, D, B, E, F, G and H", and on this side the components include livestock and produce sales worked out on the primary production worksheet and other business income at label G. A partnership with a non-zero value here is farming, fishing or forestry to some degree, whatever its registered industry code says.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, gross of all expenses, taken from the partnership's accounts. Livestock killed for rations, exchanged for goods or taken for private use are brought in here as other business income rather than left out.
limitation: It does not identify a farm business. The column is filled whenever any part of the income is primary production, so a small agistment or forestry sideline puts an amount here, and averaging, farm management deposits and livestock valuation elections mean the figure is not comparable across years for the same operation.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 5 sets out the total business income row and the primary production column that this variable takes. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only 'Total Business Income - PP' and the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what primary production means for the split or warned that the column marks any farming activity, not a farm.

value_domain: Personal services income included in business income, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: How much of the partnership's business income was really a reward for one person's effort or skill, at item 30 label A. The ATO instruction is "Write at A the total amount of income gained by you during the year that is PSI of one or more individuals that you have included at item 5 income labels", excluding exempt amounts and GST. It is a carve-out of income already counted at item 5, not extra income, and a large value relative to total business income marks a consultancy or professional practice rather than a trading business.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, self-assessed by the partnership as the personal services component of amounts it has already reported as business income. The matching deductions figure sits at label B on the same item.
limitation: It does not say whether the personal services income rules actually bit. That depends on the results test, the 80 per cent rule, a personal services business determination and the three self-assessed tests recorded in the neighbouring columns, so a partnership can report a large amount here and still be taxed normally.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 30 gives the label, its scope and its relationship to item 5. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Assessable gains from financial arrangements under Division 230, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Assessable gains the partnership brought to account under the taxation of financial arrangements rules, at item 31 label M. The ATO instruction is "Show at label M the partnership's total assessable TOFA gains from financial arrangements." The amount is a memorandum total: the same gains are already inside the income labels at items 5, 8, 11, 12, 14 and 23, so adding this to reported income double counts it.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, measured under the Division 230 methods, which include accruals and realisation, fair value, foreign exchange retranslation, hedging and reliance on financial reports.
limitation: It exists only for large or financial entities, so a zero usually means the rules do not apply rather than that no financial gains were made: the thresholds are $100 million aggregated turnover, $300 million of assets or $100 million of financial assets, and $20 million turnover for deposit-taking institutions and securitisation vehicles.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label and lists both the entities the rules reach and the other items where the same amounts appear. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

value_domain: Deductible losses from financial arrangements under Division 230, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Deductible losses the partnership brought to account under the taxation of financial arrangements rules, at item 31 label N. The ATO instruction is "Show at label N the partnership's total deductible TOFA losses from financial arrangements." Like the gains figure beside it, it restates amounts already claimed in the ordinary deduction labels, so the pair is best read as a disclosure of exposure to derivatives, debt and hedging rather than as new income or expense.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, worked out under the Division 230 tax-timing methods. Once an entity is inside the rules it stays inside them even if its turnover or assets later fall below the threshold.
limitation: Gains and losses are reported gross and cannot be netted into a meaningful position, because hedging elections mean an offsetting gain may sit in a different year or a different label. Elections under the rules are irrevocable, so two firms with identical arrangements can report very different amounts.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the label wording and the election and threshold rules that govern who reports it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.

supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label text with the generic sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished it from an ordinary expense or explained why netting it against the gains column is unsafe.

value_domain: Total assets on the partnership balance sheet, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Key financial information items 33 to 36
variable_description: The partnership's whole balance sheet asset side at year end, reported at item 34 label G. The ATO instruction is "Show at label G all of the partnership assets, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets, and all current assets from item 33 All current assets." It is a stock at one date, on accounting rather than tax values, and it is the only firm-size measure on the return that is not an income or expense flow.
value_definition: A dollar amount at the balance date, reported in the return's key financial information block alongside current assets, current liabilities and total liabilities. It nests the current assets figure at item 33 rather than sitting beside it.
limitation: It is not a valuation of the business. Assets are carried at book value, internally generated goodwill and brands never appear, revaluations are inconsistent between firms, and the key financial information items are not always completed with the care given to the income labels because nothing in the tax calculation depends on them.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 34 defines the label and its relationship to the current assets item beneath it. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label G all of the partnership assets, including fixed, tangible and intangible assets, and all current assets from item 33 All current assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Total assets' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said this is a year-end accounting stock, what it contains, or why it should not be read as firm value.

value_domain: Total expenses at item 5 of the partnership return, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business income and expenses item 5
variable_description: Everything the partnership deducted against business income in the year, summed at item 5 label O. The ATO instruction is "Show at label O the total of all expense items shown at labels P to N", which is the block running from foreign resident withholding expenses and cost of sales through superannuation, rent, interest, royalties, depreciation, motor vehicle, repairs and all other expenses. Total business income less this figure is the starting point for net business income, before the reconciliation adjustments that follow.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year on the partnership's accounting basis, with an L printed beside it when a negative cost of sales makes the total negative. Small business entities using simplified trading stock or depreciation rules substitute tax values in two of the components.
limitation: It is not deductible expenditure. Prepayments, leased car limits, hire purchase, non-compliant payments and thin capitalisation denials are all corrected later at the reconciliation label, so the tax deduction actually allowed differs from this number, and no split between primary and non-primary production is available on the expense side.
rationale: The ATO instruction names label O, the labels it totals and the accounting basis of the block. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label O the total of all expense items shown at labels P to N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total expenses' and the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said the figure is an accounting total that tax adjustments have not yet been applied to.

value_domain: Total income across the return's income items, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 14 Other Australian income and 15 Total of items 5 to 14
variable_description: The sum of every income item on the return, which on the partnership form is item 15, the total of items 5 to 14. The ATO instruction is "Show at item 15 the total of all Australian income", and an L is printed beside it where the total is a loss. It is broader than total business income because it also picks up trust and partnership distributions, rent, interest, dividends and other Australian income, and narrower than the firm's worldwide receipts because foreign income is reported separately at later items.
value_definition: A whole-dollar flow for the income year, signed: it can be negative when a business loss at item 5 exceeds the investment income items. It is a derived total rather than a separately reported quantity.
limitation: It is not taxable income and not turnover. Deductions at items 16 to 20 have not been taken off, foreign source income is outside it, and because a partnership is not itself taxed the amount is eventually distributed to partners, so it cannot be compared with a company's total income without allowing for that.
rationale: The data item wording describes a total of the items under the return's Income heading, which on the partnership return is item 15; the ATO instruction defines that total and its scope. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at item 15 the total of all Australian income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's parenthetical about items under the Income heading, which names no item and no form, together with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what is inside or outside the total.

value_domain: Total liabilities on the partnership balance sheet, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Key financial information items 33 to 36
variable_description: Everything the partnership owed at year end, reported at item 36 label J. The ATO instruction is "Show at label J all the partnership liabilities, including other creditors and deferred liabilities, such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans", and it includes the current liabilities already shown at item 35. Set against total assets at item 34 it gives the only gearing measure available on the return.
value_definition: A dollar amount at the balance date on accounting values, nesting rather than excluding the current liabilities figure. Trade creditors reported at item 43 are inside the current liabilities component.
limitation: It cannot separate related party debt from arm's length borrowing, which matters because a partnership's partners often lend to it, and it takes no account of guarantees or of assets pledged outside the partnership. Nothing in the tax calculation depends on the number, so it is less carefully prepared than the income labels.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 36 defines the label and what it must include. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label J all the partnership liabilities, including other creditors and deferred liabilities, such as loans secured by mortgage and long-term loans.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Total liabilities' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said it is a year-end accounting stock that already contains current liabilities.

value_domain: Deductions against personal services income, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: The expenses the partnership claimed against its personal services income, at item 30 label B. The ATO instruction is "Write at B the total amount of deductions against PSI included at item 5 expense labels." Like the income figure at label A it is a carve-out of amounts already reported at item 5, and the difference between the two is the net personal services income that may have to be attributed to the individual who earned it.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, self-identified by the partnership within its item 5 expense labels. Where the personal services income rules apply, adjustments to reverse denied deductions are made at the item 5 reconciliation items rather than here.
limitation: It is not the deduction the firm was allowed. Rent, mortgage interest, rates and land tax on the worker's residence, a second private-use car and payments to associates for non-principal work are specifically denied, so this number can include amounts later added back and cannot be treated as the cost of earning the personal services income.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 30 defines label B and sets out the categories of expense that the rules deny. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Write at B the total amount of deductions against PSI included at item 5 expense labels.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label wording, which refers to item 5 without explaining it, and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said these deductions may be denied or how they relate to the income label beside them.

value_domain: Total salary and wage expenses of the partnership, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: The partnership's whole wage bill for the year, at item 44 label L. The ATO instruction is "Show at label L the total salary, wages and other labour costs actually paid or payable to persons employed in the partnership's business", and it reaches across the return, picking up any wage component buried in cost of sales as well as allowances, bonuses, casual labour, directors' fees, leave and incentive payments. A code letter beside it records whether those wages were reported mainly in cost of sales, in all other expenses, in both or in neither.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year on a tax basis, accompanied by a single-letter code taking C, A, B or O for where the wages were predominantly reported. Contract, sub-contract, agency, service, management and consultant fees and superannuation are excluded from it.
limitation: It is not the firm's labour cost and not a headcount. Partners cannot be employees so their drawings are outside it, superannuation and contractors are outside it, and wages paid where the PAYG withholding obligations were not met are not deductible, so a firm using a labour hire model can run a large workforce and report very little here.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 44 defines the label, lists what is inside and outside it and explains the accompanying code. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label L the total salary, wages and other labour costs actually paid or payable to persons employed in the partnership's business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total salaries and wage expenses' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that partners, contractors and superannuation are all outside the total.

value_domain: Trust distribution excluded from non-concessional MIT income, non-primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: The part of a non-primary production trust distribution that escapes the non-concessional managed investment trust rules, at item 32 label L. The ATO instruction is "Show at label L the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as Non-primary production", and it explains that excluded amounts are "income from transitional arrangements or approved economic infrastructure facilities". The amount is also inside item 8 label R, so it flags the character of a distribution rather than adding to income.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, one of four trust-side non-concessional managed investment trust boxes split by primary and non-primary production and by whether the amount is inside or excluded from the concession-denying category. The labels exist only from the 2019-20 income year.
limitation: It cannot be added to the neighbouring non-concessional amount to recover the distribution: both are components of the item 8 figure, not additions to it. A blank means the trustee did not identify any excluded amount, which is not the same as the partnership having no trust income.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 32 gives the exact label and defines what excluded from non-concessional MIT income means. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label L the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the acronym-laden label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing expanded NCMI, said which of the four boxes this is, or noted the series begins in 2019-20.

value_domain: Non-concessional MIT income from trusts, non-primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Trust income of a non-primary production kind that carries the non-concessional managed investment trust label, at item 32 label K. The ATO instruction is "Show at label K the total NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as Non-primary production", and an amount is non-concessional if it is "MIT cross staple arrangement income, MIT trading trust income, MIT agricultural income, or MIT residential housing income". Tagging it this way denies the concessional withholding rate that managed investment trust distributions otherwise attract.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, sitting inside the item 8 label R distribution rather than adding to it, and paired with the excluded-amount box on the same row. Introduced with the stapled structures measures for income years from 2019-20.
limitation: It marks a character, not a cash flow the partnership can control: the tag depends on what the distributing trust reported to it. Cross staple income is the case the rules were built for, so the column is concentrated among a handful of infrastructure and property investors and is empty for almost every operating business.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines both the label and the four categories that make an amount non-concessional MIT income. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label K the total NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as Non-primary production.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the raw label and the generic sentence twice, so a reader could not tell what NCMI is, why it exists or which entities ever report it.

value_domain: Trust distribution excluded from non-concessional MIT income, primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: The primary production part of a trust distribution that the non-concessional managed investment trust rules leave alone, at item 32 label H. The ATO instruction is "Show at label H the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as primary production income", and the amount is also carried at item 8 label Z, the share of net income from trusts. Exclusion covers transitional arrangements and approved economic infrastructure facilities, so this box records agricultural trust income grandfathered out of the measure.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, the primary production counterpart of the non-primary production excluded box, and one of the four trust-side boxes at item 32. Available for income years from 2019-20 onward.
