The primary production classification follows how the distributing trust categorised the income, and MIT agricultural income that fails the transitional test is reported in the non-concessional box instead, so this column alone understates farming-related trust income.
rationale: The ATO instruction names label H and defines what excluded from non-concessional MIT income covers. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the total Excluded from NCMI amount distributed from trusts categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label and the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which of the four boxes it is, what exclusion means, or that the classification is the trustee's.

value_domain: Non-concessional MIT income from trusts, primary production, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Taxation of financial arrangements items 31 and 32
variable_description: Primary production trust income that is caught by the non-concessional managed investment trust rules, at item 32 label G. The ATO instruction is "Show at label G the total NCMI amount distributed from a trust categorised as primary production income", and the primary production example the ATO gives is "income attributable to agricultural land held for rent". It is the farming counterpart of label K and is likewise a component of the item 8 label Z distribution rather than an addition to it.
value_definition: A dollar flow for the income year, one of the four trust-side boxes introduced with the stapled structures measures for income years from 2019-20. MIT agricultural income is one of the four categories that make an amount non-concessional.
limitation: A value here does not mean the partnership farms anything. The tag attaches to rent from agricultural land held through a managed investment trust, which is an investment position rather than an operating one, and the amount depends entirely on the trustee's classification.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the label and the agricultural example that explains what primary production means in this context. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label G the total NCMI amount distributed from a trust categorised as primary production income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label alone with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what agricultural MIT income is or why it would appear in a business's tax record.

value_domain: Tax withheld from the partnership's income because it did not quote an ABN, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 6 Tax withheld
variable_description: Tax that payers held back from the partnership's own receipts because it failed to quote an Australian business number, at item 6 label T. The ATO instruction is "Show at label T the total of amounts withheld from income subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted", and the corresponding gross payments have to be declared at item 5 labels C and D. Withholding is at the top marginal rate, so an amount here is expensive and unusual.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, equal to the sum of the tax withheld boxes on the Non-individual PAYG payment summary schedule lodged with the return. It is a credit passed through to the partners, since the partnership itself is not taxed.
limitation: It only covers amounts withheld from the partnership directly. Any share of ABN withholding that reached it through another partnership or trust is reported instead at item 8, so the two columns must be read together, and neither says anything about tax the firm withheld from its own suppliers.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 6 defines the label and explicitly directs distributed shares to item 8 instead. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at label T the total of amounts withheld from income subject to withholding where an ABN was not quoted.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tax withheld where ABN not quoted' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said whose ABN was missing or how it differs from the share column on the same table.

value_domain: Share of an ABN withholding credit received through a trust or partnership, dollars
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, 8 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: The partnership's slice of tax that was withheld further up a chain of trusts or partnerships because no ABN was quoted there, at item 8 label C. The ATO instruction is "If the income shown at label A, Z, B, R or F includes any share of amounts that have had tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, show any share of credit for the tax withheld at label C." The failure to quote happened at the distributing entity, not at this business, which is what separates this column from the direct withholding figure at item 6.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, taken from the statement of distribution or trustee advice, which must disclose it separately. It is a credit attached to distributed income rather than to the partnership's own receipts.
limitation: It is evidence about a related entity's paperwork, not about this business. It cannot be added to the direct withholding column to get a firm-level compliance measure, and a partnership sitting in a long chain of trusts may receive a share without ever being able to identify which entity failed to quote.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 8 defines label C and ties it to the distribution labels it can arise from. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: If the income shown at label A, Z, B, R or F includes any share of amounts that have had tax withheld where an ABN was not quoted, show any share of credit for the tax withheld at label C.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label wording with the generic sentence twice, so a reader would have confused it with the firm's own ABN withholding at item 6.

value_domain: Yes or no answer to the specified countries question on the partnership return
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Overseas transactions or thin capitalisation items 29 to 30
variable_description: Whether the partnership moved funds or property to or from, or controlled assets in, any of the countries on the ATO's specified list, at item 29 label C. The question covers indirect movements "through another entity or country" and control that is only expected or indirect, so the threshold for a yes is deliberately low. The list of roughly forty-five jurisdictions includes Bermuda, the Cayman Islands, Hong Kong, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Singapore and Switzerland, so a yes is a flag for the ATO rather than an allegation.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. The specified country list is published in the return instructions and has changed between editions, so the meaning of a yes is not fixed across years.
limitation: It cannot distinguish tax planning from ordinary trade. Sending funds to a Singapore supplier, banking in Hong Kong and holding a Cayman Islands structure all produce the same Y, and because the list has been revised the same transaction can flip the answer between years without any change in the firm's behaviour.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 29 sets out the two questions behind the label and publishes the country list they refer to. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Did you send any funds or property to, or receive any funds or property from, any of the countries listed below?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Transactions with specified countries' and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which countries are specified or how broad the question is.

value_domain: Yes indicator for the personal services income unrelated clients test
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2020, item 30 Personal services income
variable_description: Whether the partnership self-assessed that it passes the unrelated clients test, one of three escape routes from the personal services income rules, at item 30 label E1. The ATO defines it: "You will meet the unrelated clients test in the income year if the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you", and the work must come from offers to the public such as advertising. Clients won through a labour hire firm or placement agency do not count.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. It is one of a set of self-assessed test indicators sitting beside the results test, the business premises test, the employment test and any personal services business determination.
limitation: It is a claim, not an entitlement. The test can only be self-assessed when no single client supplied 80 per cent or more of the individual's personal services income, so a Y from a firm that fails the 80 per cent rule is not effective without a Commissioner's determination, and the column records no such check.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 30 defines the unrelated clients test and the 80 per cent rule that governs when it may be self-assessed. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: You will meet the unrelated clients test in the income year if the individual doing the personal services work generates PSI from two or more clients who are not associated with each other, or with the individual, or with you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the three-word test name and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the test requires or that passing it is self-assessed and conditional.

value_domain: PAYG amount withheld from wages, activity statement label W2, dollars
value_source: ATO, Business activity statements: Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
variable_description: The tax the business took out of its own payroll for the activity statement period, at label W2. The ATO instruction is "Include at W2 the total amount you withheld from salaries, wages and other payments shown at W1", and W1 is the gross payments column beside it, so the two together give payroll and payroll tax withheld at the same frequency. It is the main type of withholding and is reported monthly or quarterly, which makes it the highest-frequency labour indicator in the BLADE tax data.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one activity statement period, left blank rather than zero-filled where nothing was withheld. Amounts withheld where no ABN was quoted go to W4 and investment and foreign resident withholding to W3, not here.
limitation: The largest employers are missing by design: a large withholder, meaning one that withheld more than $1 million in a past income year, completes only W1 and leaves W2 blank. It is also tax, not wages, so it moves with the tax scales and with employees' tax-free threshold and offset claims as well as with the payroll itself.
rationale: The ATO page for the activity statement PAYG withholding section defines label W2 and the large withholder exception. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Include at W2 the total amount you withheld from salaries, wages and other payments shown at W1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Amount withheld from salary, wages and other payments' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing identified the W2 label, distinguished it from W3 and W4, or warned that large withholders never report it.

value_domain: Instant asset write-off deductions claimed by a non-small business entity, dollars
value_source: ATO, Company tax return 2021 instructions, item 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The deduction a business too large to be a small business entity claimed by writing assets off immediately rather than depreciating them. The ATO instruction for the label is "Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available." The label belongs to the enhanced instant asset write-off that ran from March 2020 for businesses with aggregated turnover under $500 million and it was removed from the 2022 returns, so the series stops there.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, and a component of the depreciation deduction rather than an addition to it. Assets covered by temporary full expensing are reported at the temporary full expensing label instead of here.
limitation: It is not capital expenditure and not a complete write-off measure. Small business entities using simplified depreciation never report at this label, the threshold moved repeatedly between $1,000 and $150,000 over the life of the measure, and from the 2022 return the label was removed, so a zero after that year means the question stopped being asked.
rationale: The ATO capital allowances instruction defines this label in the same words as the BLADE data item, and the 2022 what's new page records its removal from the return. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Show at O the total amount you claimed at item 7F Deduction for decline in value of depreciating assets about assets costing less than the relevant instant asset write-off threshold for which an immediate deduction is available.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the label text with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said which businesses the label was for, that it duplicates part of the depreciation deduction, or that it ceased after the 2021 return.

value_domain: Yes or no answer to the effective life recalculation question
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2024, Business and professional items items 37 to 53
variable_description: Whether the partnership reworked the effective life of any depreciating asset during the year, at item 49 label D. The ATO asks "Have you recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets in 2023-24?" and notes that recalculation is sometimes optional and sometimes compulsory when the life in use is no longer accurate. It is a different question from the self-assessment indicator at label C, which asks whether the firm set the life itself instead of adopting the Commissioner's determination.
value_definition: A single character: Y for yes, N for no, and anything else invalid or missing. It applies to all depreciating assets and is asked only of firms outside the small business simplified depreciation rules, who skip item 49 entirely.
limitation: It says nothing about size or direction. One asset revised by a year and a whole fleet written down produce the same Y, the deduction effect is invisible, and small business entities using simplified depreciation never answer, so a blank is as likely to mean the firm is small as that it recalculated nothing.
rationale: The ATO instruction for item 49 states the question at label D and distinguishes it from the self-assessment question at label C. The BIT table carries parallel c_, i_, p_ and t_ columns on the same stems, which identifies the p_ family as the partnership tax return; the label wording and the reference to item 5 match the partnership return rather than the individual schedule.
evidence_quote: Have you recalculated the effective life of any of your depreciating assets in 2023-24?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form question and the Y/N codes with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing separated it from the self-assessment indicator or noted who never answers it.

value_domain: Total PAYG amounts withheld on the activity statement, label W5, dollars
value_source: ATO, Business activity statements: Pay as you go (PAYG) withholding
variable_description: All tax the business withheld from others during the activity statement period, the W5 total on its BAS. The ATO defines it arithmetically: "Include at W5 the total of W2 + W4 + W3", that is withholding from wages, withholding where a supplier did not quote an ABN, and other withholding such as investment distributions with no tax file number and payments to foreign residents. It is a liability the firm remits on behalf of other people, not tax on its own profit.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one activity statement period, monthly or quarterly, copied to the summary section of the statement. Gross payments at W1 are deliberately not included in the total.
limitation: It is not the business's own tax and not a payroll measure. Large withholders that withheld more than $1 million in a past year complete only W1 and leave W5 blank, and because W3 and W4 sit inside the total a firm with heavy supplier or investor withholding looks like a large employer.
rationale: The ATO page for the PAYG withholding section of the activity statement gives the composition of W5 and the large withholder exception.
evidence_quote: Include at W5 the total of W2 + W4 + W3.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pay as you go (PAYG) tax withheld' with the generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said which labels make up the total or that the biggest employers do not report it.

value_domain: ABS integration version stamp on the PAYG module
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: Which build of the ABS integration this PAYG row came out of, not anything about the business. BLADE is assembled by the ABS from administrative sources including "Pay as You Go (PAYG) summaries" and is rebuilt periodically, so the same reporting period can be present in more than one version with different linkage and cleaning applied. The same stamp appears on other modules as bas_version, which is how a researcher can tell whether two tables were drawn from the same build.
value_definition: An eight character alphanumeric code assigned by the ABS during integration. It is internal reference metadata with no published code list and no business meaning.
limitation: It is not a date, a reporting period or a data quality flag, and it cannot be ordered to give a vintage without ABS documentation. Filtering or grouping on it will silently drop or duplicate businesses whose records were reprocessed between builds.
rationale: No published documentation defines this field. The ABS BLADE page confirms the ABS integrates PAYG summary data into the asset and rebuilds it over time, which is what an integration version stamp would record; the reading is inferred from that and from the identical bas_version field on the activity statement table.
evidence_quote: The current BLADE asset contains data on all active businesses from 2001-02 to current
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'Integration version (internal ABS reference)' with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the field is a build stamp and unsafe to filter on.

value_domain: Days of paid bereavement leave provided by the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The number of days of paid bereavement leave written into an enterprise agreement covering this business, as coded by DEWR from the lodged agreement. It is a promise in a document, not leave anyone took, and it attaches to the agreement rather than to the firm, so a business covered by several agreements has several values. Coding of this item stopped for agreements made from 1 January 2011, when bereavement leave was folded into compassionate leave entitlements.
value_definition: A count of days, numeric, with 111111111 reserved for a quantity that varies or is unknown, including where leave is granted on a per occasion basis. Coded by DEWR from the agreement text rather than reported by the employer.
limitation: A blank after 2010 means the item was retired, not that the entitlement vanished, so the column cannot be used to track bereavement leave over time. It also says nothing about how many covered employees could realistically use it, since the agreement may set qualifying conditions the coding does not capture.
rationale: DEWR publishes the database description and states that the conditions collected are reviewed annually, which explains the field's start and stop and its agreement-level unit; the valid response text on the data item carries the pre-2011 coding rule.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about days being recorded with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the field was retired in 2011 or that the unit is the agreement rather than the business.

value_domain: Days of paid family carer's leave provided over and above personal leave
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Days of paid leave an agreement gives employees to care for a sick family member on top of their ordinary personal or sick leave. The distinction from personal leave is what the item is for: carer's leave drawn from the personal leave balance is the statutory minimum and is not counted here, so a value marks an above-award condition. DEWR codes it from the agreement text and the number of days is only recorded where the agreement specifies one.
value_definition: A count of days, numeric, with 111111111 standing for a varying or unknown quantity. It is coded per agreement, and the database holds conditions information for federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
limitation: It cannot be compared with total carer's leave available to employees, because the statutory entitlement inside personal leave is deliberately excluded. An absent value mixes agreements with no separate provision, agreements that provide it without quantifying it, and years in which the item was not coded.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database, its coverage of conditions since 1997 and the annual review of what is collected, which sets the unit of observation and the coverage limits for this item.
evidence_quote: The database contains wage information for all federal enterprise agreements since the introduction of enterprise bargaining in October 1991, and conditions information for all federal enterprise agreements approved since 1 January 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry reproduced the custodian's long definition and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said why the separation from personal leave matters or what a missing value can mean.

value_domain: Count of part-time employees covered by the agreement at lodgement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: How many part-time employees an enterprise agreement covered on the day it was lodged with the Fair Work Commission. It is a one-off snapshot taken at lodgement, not a payroll series, so it does not move as the workforce changes over the agreement's life, and it is reported by the parties to the agreement rather than measured. Read against the full-time and casual counts on the same record it gives the composition of the covered workforce at that moment.
value_definition: A numeric headcount, not a full-time equivalent, attached to one agreement. Around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement in the database and this is one of the general details captured at lodgement.
limitation: It is not the firm's part-time workforce. Employees outside the agreement's scope are not counted, a multi-employer agreement spreads its count across businesses, and because the figure is fixed at lodgement it becomes stale immediately: an agreement running four years reports the same number in each of them.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database and lists the number of employees covered among the general details recorded for each agreement, which establishes the unit and the point of measurement.
evidence_quote: There are over 180,000 agreements in the database. An average of 6,000 agreements are added each year, and around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line description with the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the count is frozen at lodgement or that it counts agreement coverage rather than the business's employees.

value_domain: Presence flag for a full-time to part-time switching clause
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement lets full-time employees move to part-time work, and back, at their own request. It is a flexibility provision recorded because the initiative sits with the employee: clauses that let the employer impose reduced hours are a different thing and are not what this flags. DEWR codes it from the agreement text as a presence indicator only.
value_definition: A one-sided flag: Y where the clause is present, and nothing recorded otherwise. There is no N code, so absence and non-coding share the same blank.
limitation: A blank cannot be read as no such clause. Because only Y is coded, agreements with no provision are indistinguishable from agreements coded before the item existed or coded incompletely, which makes any share calculated over blanks a lower bound rather than an estimate.
rationale: The DEWR page names flexibility arrangements among the conditions recorded for each agreement and explains that the conditions collected change over time, which is what makes the one-sided coding hazardous.
evidence_quote: The database also records details about conditions of employment contained within enterprise agreements
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's description and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing warned that the field carries only a Y and that blanks are ambiguous.

value_domain: Presence flag for a part-time hours loading clause, 2008-09 agreements only
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement pays part-time employees a loading on every hour worked, rather than only on hours beyond their rostered pattern. The item is unusual in that DEWR coded it only for agreements made in 2008 and 2009, so it is a snapshot of one bargaining round and not a series. A loading of this kind pushes part-time hourly pay above the full-time rate, which is why it was coded separately from ordinary penalty and overtime provisions.
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y where the provision is present, with nothing recorded otherwise, and coded only for agreements made in 2008 and 2009. It is one of roughly 200 items held for each agreement.
limitation: The column is empty for almost every agreement in the database, and that emptiness carries no information about the clause. Any comparison of firms on this field is really a comparison of which of them happened to lodge an agreement in a two-year window.
rationale: The valid response text limits coding to 2008-09 agreements, and the DEWR page explains that the conditions collected are reviewed annually so items do not span the full time series.
evidence_quote: The conditions collected about each agreement is reviewed annually so not all conditions data fields will span the full time series of the database.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description and code note with the generic sentence twice, so nothing explained why coverage is confined to one bargaining round or what a blank means.

value_domain: Minimum continuous hours in a single part-time engagement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: The shortest continuous shift an agreement allows a part-time employee to be called in for. It is a floor on shift length rather than on weekly hours, which is the protection that matters in retail, hospitality and care work where very short engagements are possible. DEWR codes it only where the agreement puts a number on it.
value_definition: A numeric count of hours per engagement, with 111111111 reserved for a varying or unknown quantity, coded from the agreement text. It is recorded once per agreement, not per employee or per classification.
limitation: It says nothing about how many hours a part-time employee actually gets. An agreement can set a generous minimum engagement and still offer few shifts, and where different minimums apply to different classifications the single coded value cannot represent them all.
rationale: The DEWR page establishes that these are conditions coded from lodged federal enterprise agreements at the agreement level, which fixes the unit and the source of the number.
evidence_quote: The Workplace Agreements Database (WAD) is maintained and operated by DEWR, and is the only one of its kind in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's conditional sentence with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing distinguished a minimum engagement from minimum weekly hours or explained the 111111111 code's effect on any average.

value_domain: Presence flag for a part-time hours regularity commitment
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement commits to stable and predictable hours for part-time employees. The devices coded include specified start and finish times, named rostered days, and changes to hours only by agreement. It captures predictability rather than quantity, so it sits beside the minimum engagement item rather than duplicating it. DEWR codes it as a presence indicator from the agreement text.
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y where such a commitment appears, with nothing recorded otherwise. It is one of the flexibility and rostering conditions coded for each federal enterprise agreement.
limitation: It reduces a spectrum of clauses to a single Y: a binding roster fixed in the agreement and a loose commitment to consult about changes are coded the same. With no N code, a blank cannot be read as an agreement that offers no predictability.
rationale: The DEWR page lists flexibility arrangements and conditions of employment among the details coded for each agreement, which identifies this as an agreement-level coded condition.
evidence_quote: The database also records details about conditions of employment contained within enterprise agreements
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's long parenthetical description and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is one-sided or that it measures predictability rather than hours.

value_domain: Presence flag for group-based performance pay in the agreement
value_source: DEWR, Workplace Agreements Database
variable_description: Whether the agreement offers a recurring performance payment to groups of employees, or to the whole workforce, for meeting targets. The group basis is the point of the item: it separates collective incentives such as site or company bonuses from individual performance pay, which is coded elsewhere in the database. It is a clause in the agreement, so it says a scheme exists, not that any payment was made.
value_definition: A one-sided flag taking Y where a group performance payment provision appears, with nothing recorded otherwise. It is coded per agreement, among roughly 200 items held for each.
limitation: It carries no amount, frequency or target, so a token annual bonus and a substantial gainsharing scheme look identical. Nothing records whether the targets were met, so the column cannot support any claim about performance pay actually received by employees of the business.
rationale: The DEWR page describes the database and the conditions coded for each agreement, including productivity provisions, which places this item and fixes its agreement-level unit.
evidence_quote: around 200 data items are recorded for each agreement
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the flag is one-sided, carries no dollar value and records a clause rather than a payment.

value_domain: IP Australia party role category on an IP right record
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID dataset, data.gov.au
variable_description: What part a named party played in an intellectual property right, grouping the finer party role into nine categories. The categories separate the people who own or seek the right from the people acting for them and the people acting against them: applicant, licensee and mortgagee are interests in the right, applicant_agent, opposition_agent and other_agent are attorneys and representatives, and opposition and non_use_applicant are challengers. Only rows in the applicant family should be treated as the business behind a filing when linking IP records to BLADE firms.
value_definition: A character value from a closed list of nine: applicant, applicant_agent, licensee, mortgagee, non_use_applicant, opposition, opposition_agent, other, other_agent. It generalises the more detailed party_role column on the same row.
limitation: It does not identify a business. An agent category names a law firm rather than the innovator, the same legal entity can appear under several categories on one right, and 'other' is a residual that carries no information, so counting parties without filtering on this column inflates any measure of firms holding intellectual property.
rationale: The IP RAPID dataset page identifies the product and its publisher and confirms it is the weekly successor to IPGOD, whose party tables use these role values; the category list itself comes from the data item's own valid response text.
evidence_quote: IP RAPID is a weekly updated version of IP Australia's open data product, previously released under the name IPGOD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the circular description 'The category into which the party_role falls' with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what the categories mean or which of them represent the business.

value_domain: Percentage of the R&D entity controlled by tax exempt entities
value_source: ATO, R&D tax incentive: refundable and non-refundable offsets
variable_description: How much of the company registering research and development activity is controlled by tax exempt entities, reported on its registration. The number decides which offset it can claim: the ATO says a company with aggregated turnover "less than $20 million and you are not controlled by any exempt entities" can claim the refundable offset, while one that is "controlled by exempt entities" gets the non-refundable offset regardless of size. A high value therefore usually marks a research entity sitting under a university, a hospital or another exempt body.
value_definition: A numeric percentage between 0 and 100, self-reported on the research and development tax incentive registration rather than assessed by the ATO. It measures control by exempt entities, not ownership by government or by non-residents.
limitation: It is not a public ownership share. Exempt entity status is a tax concept covering charities, some non-profits and various government bodies, so a company can be majority government owned and still report zero, and the figure is a claim on a registration form rather than a verified shareholding.
rationale: The ATO sets out the exempt entity control test that this percentage exists to answer, and states the consequence for the offset the firm receives.
evidence_quote: less than $20 million and you are not controlled by any exempt entities, then you can claim the refundable tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Percentage control held by tax exempt entities' with the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what an exempt entity is or why the percentage matters.

value_domain: Count of plant breeder's rights applications filed in the financial year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: How many plant breeder's rights applications this applicant lodged with IP Australia during the financial year. IP Australia describes the dataset as one that "leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year", so the row is an applicant-year and this is a flow within it. Each application is counted whole here, whatever the number of co-applicants, which is the difference between this column and the weighted count beside it.
value_definition: An integer count of applications for one applicant in one financial year. Plant breeder's rights cover new varieties of plants, fungi and algae and are one of four IP rights in IPLORD alongside patents, trade marks and designs.
limitation: It counts filings, not successful varieties: registration takes about two and a half years and an application may be withdrawn or refused, so this year's count says nothing about rights held. Plant breeder's rights are rare, so the column is zero for almost every business and cannot be used as a general innovation measure.
rationale: The IPLORD dataset page defines the product, its IPGOD source and its applicant-by-financial-year structure, which is what fixes the unit and the flow reading of the count.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line label with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the unit of observation is or that filings are not grants.

value_domain: Fractionally attributed count of plant breeder's rights applications filed
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: The applicant's share of the plant breeder's rights applications filed in the financial year, with each application divided among its co-applicants. Where the unweighted count gives a joint application to every applicant in full, this one splits it, so summing the weighted column across applicants recovers the true number of applications while summing the unweighted column does not. For a sole applicant the two columns are identical.
value_definition: A fractional count for one applicant in one financial year, so it takes non-integer values. It is the weighted companion of the plain filed count on the same row.
limitation: The split is by applicant count, not by contribution or by ownership share, so a breeder who did all the work and a nominal co-applicant receive the same half. It also cannot be compared with weighted counts for other rights without care, because the number of co-applicants differs systematically between plant breeder's rights and patents.
rationale: The data item describes an application fraction filed by the applicant, and the IPLORD dataset page establishes the applicant-by-year structure in which such a fraction is computed.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the word 'fraction' with no explanation and the generic sentence printed twice, so nothing said what the fraction is of or why a weighted count exists at all.

value_domain: Count of distinct plant genus classes among applications filed
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: How many different plant genus classes the applicant's filings of the year spanned, which is a breadth measure rather than a volume one. Plant breeder's rights are classified by the genus of the variety, so an applicant filing five apple varieties scores one while an applicant filing one apple, one wheat and one rose scores three. Read with the filed count it separates a specialist breeding programme from a diversified one.
value_definition: An integer count of distinct genus classes for one applicant in one financial year, bounded above by that year's filed count. Zero where nothing was filed.
limitation: Genus is a coarse unit, so it cannot show diversity within a crop: dozens of distinct wheat varieties collapse to one class. The measure also resets each financial year, so it describes that year's filings rather than the breadth of the applicant's whole portfolio.
rationale: The data item defines the column as the number of different genus classes filed in, and the IPLORD page fixes the applicant-year frame the count is taken over.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, which uses 'genuses classes' without defining it, and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what a class is or how the measure differs from a count of filings.

value_domain: Most frequent plant genus class among applications filed
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: The plant genus the applicant filed most often in during the financial year, given as a class code rather than a count. It answers what the breeder mainly works on, where the class scope column answers how widely. For an applicant with a single filing it is simply that filing's genus, so it is only informative alongside the filed count.
value_definition: A character class code for one applicant in one financial year, drawn from the plant genus classification IP Australia applies to plant breeder's rights applications. Empty where the applicant filed nothing that year.
limitation: A mode hides the distribution and gives no way to resolve a tie, so an applicant splitting its filings evenly across three genera is represented by whichever one the tie-break selected. It is not comparable with the technology class codes used for patents in the neighbouring columns.
rationale: The data item defines the column as the most common genus class for applications filed in the year, and the IPLORD page establishes the applicant-year structure that the mode is taken within.
evidence_quote: IPLoRD leverages IPGOD data to provide a history of an applicant's filings over time broken down by financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's phrase and the generic sentence twice, so nothing said the value is a genus code, that ties are unresolved, or that it is uninformative for single filers.

value_domain: Count of plant breeder's rights applications granted enforceable status in the year
value_source: IP Australia, Intellectual Property Longitudinal Research Data (IPLORD), data.gov.au
variable_description: How many of the applicant's plant breeder's rights applications became legally enforceable during the financial year. It is the grant flow, and it belongs to the year of grant rather than the year of filing, which matters because IP Australia says registration typically takes about two and a half years and depends on the plant type. A firm can therefore show grants in a year in which it filed nothing.
value_definition: An integer count of applications reaching enforceable status for one applicant in one financial year, counted whole regardless of co-applicants. It is a flow, unlike the legally enforceable stock column on the same row.
limitation: It cannot be divided by the filed count in the same year to get a grant rate, because the two refer to different cohorts of application. A zero is the normal case even for active breeders, since grants arrive in lumps years after the filing effort that produced them.

A business appears here only for the years an agreement of its own was in force, so award-reliant and individually contracted workplaces are absent by construction.

value_domain: Platinum grade of an exported ore or concentrate shipment (per cent)
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)

It sits with the copper, lead, nickel, tin, tungsten, zinc and tantalum percentage columns and the gold and silver grams-per-tonne columns, which together let contained metal be worked out from gross weight. It is a grade attribute of the consignment, not a quantity, so it is meaningful only on the mineral commodity codes that carry an assay.

The percentage is also the exporter's declared assay for one shipment and cannot be averaged across a year without weighting by shipment mass.

value_domain: Overseas port of discharge code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The first overseas port at which a firm's exported consignment is unloaded after leaving Australia. The ABS defines it as "the place where goods are unloaded from an aircraft or ship after it leaves Australia". It is the foreign end of the voyage, so it pairs with port_of_loading_ex, the Australian port the goods left from. It is not the same thing as the country of final destination on the same row, because a consignment can be discharged at a transhipment hub in one country and consumed in another.
value_definition: A six-digit international merchandise trade overseas port code. The ABS derives it from the five-character UN location code declared to Home Affairs and corresponds it to its own six-digit overseas port classification, so the code is a UN/LOCODE in origin but not in form.
limitation: It does not tell you where the goods ended up. Discharge at a hub such as Singapore or Rotterdam is common for onward shipment, so building an export destination series from this column instead of country_of_final_dest_ex overstates trade with entrepot economies.
rationale: The ABS concepts, sources and methods chapter defines the export port of discharge and states how UN location codes are corresponded to the six-digit overseas port classification the BLADE column carries.
evidence_quote: the place where goods are unloaded from an aircraft or ship after it leaves Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and pointed at an appendix the reader cannot open, with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never distinguished discharge from final destination.

value_domain: Australian port of discharge code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian port where a firm's imported consignment came off the ship or aircraft. The ABS treats this as the Australian end of an import voyage - "For exports, the Australian port is the port of loading and for imports the Australian port is the port of discharge" - so it is the import mirror of port_of_loading_ex. It describes the arrival point of the goods, not where the importing business is located or where the goods were eventually used.
value_definition: A three-digit international merchandise trade Australian port code, corresponded by the ABS from the five-character UN location code on the import declaration. The three-digit form is what makes it shorter than the six-digit overseas port codes on the same table.
limitation: The port of arrival is not the state of the market. Container traffic for the whole eastern seaboard clears through a handful of ports, so counting imports by discharge port attributes goods to the port state rather than to state_of_destination_im, which is the state where the goods are released from customs control.
rationale: The chapter states explicitly that the Australian port for imports is the port of discharge and describes the correspondence to three-digit Australian port codes, which matches the three-digit domain the BLADE data item list gives.
evidence_quote: For exports, the Australian port is the port of loading and for imports the Australian port is the port of discharge
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's sentence and an appendix reference with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so nothing told a reader the code is an ABS three-digit port code rather than a raw UN/LOCODE.

value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The Australian port from which a firm's exported consignment left the country. It is the port behind state_of_loading_ex, which the ABS defines as "the Australian state in which the goods are loaded onto an international carrier for export", and it is distinct from state_of_origin_ex, the state where production or the final stage of manufacture occurred. For a firm that trucks goods interstate to a deepwater port, the loading port and the production state disagree, and both columns are on the row.

supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording and cited an appendix, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never warned that the loading port is not the production state.

value_domain: Overseas port of loading code, ABS international merchandise trade
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Country, overseas port, state and Australian port
variable_description: The overseas port where a firm's imported consignment was put on the ship or aircraft bound for Australia. The ABS defines it as "the place where the goods are loaded onto an aircraft or ship for the purpose of being transported to Australia". It is the foreign end of an import voyage and pairs with port_of_discharge_im, the Australian arrival port. It is a shipping fact and is not the same as country_of_origin_im, which follows the rules of origin rather than the route.

rationale: The chapter gives the import port of loading definition verbatim and describes the six-digit overseas port coding that matches the domain the BLADE data item list states.
evidence_quote: the place where the goods are loaded onto an aircraft or ship for the purpose of being transported to Australia

value_domain: Australian postcode of the intellectual property applicant
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Postal Areas
variable_description: The postcode of the address an applicant gave IP Australia when filing, reduced to one value per applicant by taking the most common postcode on their filings. It locates the party named on the application, which for a firm is usually a head office or an attorney's office rather than the site where the invention or the design work happened. Overseas addresses are not given a postcode at all: they are set to 9999, and a full stop marks a missing value.

Postcodes are a delivery construct rather than a statistical geography; the ABS equivalent is the Postal Area, "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes".

An applicant that relocates, or that files some applications through an attorney and others directly, is collapsed to whichever postcode appears most often, so this column cannot be used to date a change of address or to split filings by site. Joining it to ABS geography also introduces approximation error, because Postal Areas do not match postal boundaries exactly.
rationale: The ABS Postal Areas page establishes what a postcode is in statistical terms and how it relates to the geography a BLADE user would join to, which is the fact the IP Australia data item list omits; the modal rule and the 9999 and '.' codes come from the BLADE data item list itself.
evidence_quote: Postal Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried IP Australia's own sentence with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the modal rule removes any address history or that postcodes are not an ABS geography.

supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's sentence about the JK prefix with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, so it never said the column is a bridge between releases rather than something about the firm.

value_domain: Weeks of paid primary care giver leave in an enterprise agreement
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: How many weeks of paid parental leave an enterprise agreement gives the primary care giver of a new child. Unlike most WAD columns this one carries a quantity rather than a yes flag, and the wording it is coded from varies: some agreements say maternity leave and some are gender neutral. Two sentinel values sit outside the count, 111111111 where the agreement leaves the quantity open and 222222222 where it sets no limit.
value_definition: A number of weeks, with 111111111 meaning varies or unknown and 222222222 meaning no limit. Because an enterprise agreement can only improve on the National Employment Standards, the figure is paid employer leave in addition to the statutory unpaid entitlement.
limitation: It is entitlement on paper, not leave taken. Nothing here says how many employees used the leave, at what rate of pay, or whether the firm's government-funded parental leave pay sits on top. The two sentinel codes must also be filtered out before any average is taken, or a single 'no limit' agreement will dominate the mean.

value_domain: Priority date of an intellectual property application
value_source: IP Australia, Patent Manual of Practice and Procedure, 5.6.1.1 Priority dates and filing dates
variable_description: The date from which a firm's application outranks any competing application for the same kind of right, which for patents can be earlier than the day it was filed. IP Australia states that "Under s43(1), each claim of a specification must have a priority date" and that the priority date is what novelty and inventive step are judged against, with the filing date as the latest possible priority date. It is the date to use when timing an innovation, because filing and grant both lag the point at which the firm secured its position.
value_definition: A calendar date written DD/MM/YYYY, one per application row across the patent, trade mark, design and plant breeder's right series that IPRAPID carries. The table's reference period runs from 1904-05, so dates far predate the tax and survey sources BLADE links to.
limitation: It is one date for a whole application, while the law attaches a priority date to each claim, so an application whose claims have different priority dates is flattened here. It also does not mean the right exists: a priority date is recorded for applications that lapse, are withdrawn or are refused, so counting priority dates counts attempts rather than granted rights.
rationale: The IP Australia patent manual gives the statutory basis and function of the priority date and explains its relationship to the filing date, which is the distinction the BLADE data item list leaves implicit.
evidence_quote: Under s43(1), each claim of a specification must have a priority date. The priority date of a claim is primarily of relevance when assessing the claim against the criteria of novelty and inventive/innovative step.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's one-line description with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said the priority date can precede filing or that it is recorded per application rather than per claim.

value_domain: Agreement clause flag, employee profit sharing
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: Marks an enterprise agreement under which employees share in company profits once a profit threshold or set of indicators is reached. It differs from the performance pay flags beside it because the trigger is the firm's result rather than the employee's or the team's output. The row is an agreement approved by the Fair Work Commission, so the flag attaches to a bargaining outcome and appears only while that agreement is on foot.
value_definition: A single-sided flag coded Y for yes, assigned by the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations from the agreement text. There is no companion no code, and no amount, share or threshold is recorded.
limitation: It does not measure profit sharing in the economy. Employee share and profit schemes are commonly set out in company policy or in a separate plan document rather than in the agreement, and those never reach this flag, so it undercounts the practice rather than measuring it.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page establishes that the row is a negotiated, Commission-approved instrument setting terms and conditions of employment, which is what limits the flag to provisions that were written into the agreement itself.
evidence_quote: Terms & conditions of employment
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's clause description with the generic no-value-list line as both value definition and limitation, so it never said the flag captures only agreement text and so undercounts profit sharing.

value_domain: Agreement clause flag, dismissal procedure, pre-2010 agreements
value_source: Fair Work Commission, Enterprise agreements
variable_description: Marks an agreement that sets out a process for dismissing an employee, and it is coded only for agreements made before 1 January 2010. The cut-off is a coding rule rather than a change in practice: after the Fair Work system took effect the statutory unfair dismissal regime made a bespoke agreement clause less common and the Department stopped coding it. Any series built on this flag therefore ends at the same date for every firm, whatever the agreement says.
value_definition: A single-sided flag coded Y for yes, valid only on agreements made before 1 January 2010 according to the BLADE data item list. Nothing is coded for later agreements, so the field is structurally empty over most of the table's 2001-02 to 2022-23 span.
limitation: A blank after 2009 means the item was not collected, not that the agreement lacks a dismissal procedure. Comparing the share of agreements with a dismissal clause before and after 2010 therefore measures a change in the coding frame and reads as though the practice vanished.
rationale: The Fair Work Commission page sets out the approval and content framework for enterprise agreements, and the data item list itself carries the pre-2010 coding restriction that governs how the flag may be used.
evidence_quote: Terms that exclude the NES
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's one-line clause description with the generic no-value-list line printed twice, and left the pre-2010 coding restriction in the valid-response text where a reader would not treat it as a break in the series.

value_domain: De-identified IP right application number (IP Australia IPRAPID)
value_source: ABS, BLADE data and legislation
variable_description: The de-identified application number of the intellectual property right on the other side of a link recorded in IP Australia's IPRAPID data. It is de-identified with the same key as s_an, so a value here joins straight back to the application-level IPRAPID tables and lets a filing be walked to its counterpart. IPRAPID is IP Australia's refreshed registry product covering patents, trade marks, designs and plant breeder's rights, which the ABS lists in BLADE from 1904-05 to 2024-25.
value_definition: An alphanumeric categorical identifier with no internal meaning, de-identified consistently with s_an so the two can be joined. The right type, filing date, status and owner live in the IPRAPID application tables, not in this column.
limitation: It is a key, not a count. A links table holds one row per link, so a filing with several counterparts appears several times and counting rows counts links rather than IP rights. The column also does not say what kind of relationship the link records, and IPRAPID's own dictionary is not published openly, so the direction of the link has to be established from the table rather than assumed.
rationale: The ABS page listing BLADE's data inclusions names IPRAPID as IP Australia's contribution and gives its reference period, and IP Australia's open data on data.gov.au shows the same registry organised as application-level tables per right type. Neither publishes the IPRAPID links table itself, so the meaning of the linked application number is inferred from the data item wording.
evidence_quote: Intellectual Property Refreshed Automated Product for Information 1904-05 to 2024-25
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the data item's own sentence and printed the generic no-value-list text as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which agency's registry this is, how far back it runs, or that a row is a link rather than a right.

value_domain: De-identified previous ABS agricultural unit identifier
value_source: ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22
variable_description: The de-identified unit identifier this agricultural business carried before its ABS agricultural unit identifier changed. That is what lets a holding be followed across collections. The population it belongs to is size-tested, not universal: businesses were in scope "if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater" (ABS, Agricultural Commodities, Australia methodology, 2021-22). The ABS carries the Agricultural Indicative data items in BLADE for 2010-11 to 2020-21.
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier, de-identified, taking the same form as the current agricultural unit identifier it supersedes. It is present where the ABS recorded a change of unit identifier for the holding and carries no information of its own beyond the link.
limitation: It cannot tell you why the identifier changed. A sale, an amalgamation, a split of the holding and an ABS reclassification of the statistical unit all look identical here. It also gives only one step back, so a holding whose identifier changed twice cannot be traced through both changes from this column alone.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the agricultural collection defines the population these units come from, including the activity and size test that decides whether a farm business is on file at all, and the BLADE data inclusions page gives the Agricultural Indicative data items their reference period.
evidence_quote: Businesses on the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Business Register (ABSBR) were in scope for the 2021-22 Rural Environment and Agricultural Commodity Survey if: they undertook agricultural activity, and the estimated value of their agricultural operations (EVAO) was $40,000 or greater
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the data item wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said that the agricultural population is cut at an EVAO threshold or that the column only ever reaches one identifier back.

value_domain: De-identified R&D Tax Incentive registration application identifier
value_source: Australian Government, business.gov.au, Apply for the R&D Tax Incentive
variable_description: The de-identified identifier of one application to register research and development activities under the R&D Tax Incentive. The company lodges it with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, and registration is annual and bound to the income year, since "The deadline to apply for the R&DTI is 10 months after the end of your company's income year" (business.gov.au), so a company that registers every year has a different identifier each year. The ABS carries RDTI Program data in BLADE for 2013-14 to 2020-21.
value_definition: A ten-character alphanumeric identifier, de-identified, with one value per registration application. It carries no income year, activity or dollar amount of its own; those sit in the other columns of the RDTI table and in the company's tax return.
limitation: A registration is a claim, not an audited fact, and it is not the offset. The company self-assesses that its activities meet the eligibility rules, and the money is claimed separately through the company return, so the presence of an identifier says a company registered activities, not that it received or kept an R&D tax offset. BLADE's RDTI coverage stopping at 2020-21 also means later years show no registrations regardless of what companies did.
rationale: The business.gov.au page for applying to the programme sets out that registering activities is an application to the department, made through its portal within ten months of the end of the income year, which is what the identifier counts; the ABS data inclusions page gives the years BLADE holds.
evidence_quote: The deadline to apply for the R&DTI is 10 months after the end of your company's income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the data item's own six-word label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which agency receives the application, that registration is annual and self-assessed, or that it is not evidence an offset was allowed.
